Positions of SCP-9517 and the Sun within the Milky Way

Special Containment Procedures: Due to its size and location, physical containment of SCP-9517 has been deemed both unnecessary and impossible. All astronomical instruments precise enough to detect SCP-9517 that are not currently under the direct control of The SCP Foundation have been equipped with automatic censors to erase evidence of the object’s existence and output mundane data. The radius, luminosity, and gravitational mass of SCP-9517 are to be measured and monitored for changes every six months.

Description: SCP-9517 is an oblate spheroidal area with a polar diameter of about 70.90 pc and an equatorial diameter of about 70.72 pc. It is located in the constellation Scorpio at RA: 17h 31m 4s, Dec: -37° 11' 21" in epoch J2000.0, at a distance of about 4.51 kpc from the Solar System.

The volume of SCP-9517 contains zero stars, and has an abnormally low interstellar medium density for its area, at 1.538×10-3 M☉ pc-3, contains comparatively lower amounts of elements other than hydrogen, at about 81.0% hydrogen, 18.8% helium, and 0.2% other elements, and has a dark matter density of about 1.114×10-3 M☉ pc-3.

Although there is no material separating SCP-9517 from the surrounding space, it possesses a discrete boundary at which objects entering face sudden resistance. This boundary is constantly receding at a rate of 36,400 km/h or 2.13 au/yr.

SCP-9517-1/-2: SCP-9517-1 and SCP-9517-2 are two frequency modulated radio signals captured from Horn Antenna 2 of Site 59 between January 29th and January 31st of 1934 while the antenna was pointed in the direction of the constellation Scorpio.

The radio signals transmitted recordings of a human or human-like voice speaking in an early Afroasiatic language. The first recording lasts for three minutes and thirty-one seconds and the second recording lasts for four minutes and twelve seconds.

Both recordings were initially stored on a twelve-inch record in the archives of Site 59, and have since been transferred to digital formats. No similar broadcasts have been received since January 31, 1934.

Addendum 9517.1: Below is a digital copy of the translation document of SCP-9517-1 and SCP-9517-2 by Foundation linguist Dr. Rosetta Stone. At the time the document was written, the broadcasts were designated Sco1-1934-1 and Sco-1934-2 respectively.

Level 3 clearance is required to access this file | Please input credentials:
Access granted

Since identifying the speeches as having the distinctive morphology of a Hamito-Semitic2 language, I have been working tirelessly to translate the two recordings into English by comparison with Egyptian and various early Semitic languages, as well as the modern Berber and Cushitic languages, with interpretation and inference as necessary.

Sco-1934-1:

Five days ago, the cavity reached our sun ring. The outer cosmic settlements that were in its path were consumed. That caused the panic to finally reach its peak. Suddenly, [unknown] workers would not come to work. Our plan to move against it was bad enough as it was, but almost half of our men abandoning us overnight sealed its fate. 1,193 call towers shut down in one day.

It was two days after it reached its first cosmic settlement that it reached its first world. Images started coming out before I had even woken up. I was woken up by my manservant who was in tears. He showed me everything. Do you know what that ravenous abyss does to a world? If it just swallowed everything in an instant, then it was all over, that would be a mercy. Instead it tugs at your life until your soul is stretched too thin for you to even think, then it just keeps pulling. We are at war with the waters themselves.

Two days ago, I decided to pull the entirety of my army. Nobody was surprised that I was the first to “surrender” as they put it as if it was some sort of shameful defeat. There is no shame in admitting defeat, and what I decided to do was not that. I see it as a different type of victory. The outcome seems to be the same in either case: everybody dies. At least if we do it my way we can give billions of innocent people a quick and painless end as opposed to being [unknown] alive.

Yesterday only 49 call towers were still open when I woke up. When I went to bed only 11 were. Half of our worlds were turned into [unknown]. Three of the others finally saw it my way. The rest had already given up the idea that they were heroes on a righteous quest to take back their world, but they still refused to take the obvious next course of action. I think that it is quite funny. I was always the sad one. Now, the waters are up to our necks and I am the one who still finds a reason to get up in the morning.

Today, there were only five open call towers when I woke up. I watched that number drop to four, then three, then, ours fell. That is why I am sending this the old way. Two more of the others came to my side. We only need one more. Do you know how much I dread that moment? Once that happens, the other six will just have to sit and watch as I set into motion a weapon that will tear our sun ring to shreds. As much as I envy the weakness it takes to resign yourself to such indecision, I do not envy the position that any of them are in right now. One of them makes up their mind and decides to rule our world a lost cause, then it is all over.

I have personally dubbed the incursion described in this broadcast "the Manowar" from the Greek word "μανός" meaning "sparse" or "thin." I am rather proud of that stroke of genius. Aside from that I have nothing to say that cannot wait until after the translation of the second message.

Sco-1934-2:

First I will tell you this: I am clearly not asking for permission to use the [unknown]. The only people with the power to make that decision have finished deliberating. If you are listening to this, you have to have already come to our sun ring and seen what happened. I just want to justify to you what I will have already done. If you were in our position, you would see that there was only one path.

You have seen the plans. I believe that you, or your intellect, already knows that they are right. I think you just wanted for there to be another way. I do not fault you for that. It is a noble goal, however futile your struggle was. If that is not the case, and the plans do not justify themselves to you, then I am sure that you at least have enough faith in the elders to trust that their judgements are sound. This weapon is more than enough to do the job. Just watch as physics does the work.

The reason I choose not to wait for your permission, or even your response, is because I do not know how much time there is to waste. It seems that when the cavity is not rooted to something, it can move incredibly quickly, and as the people of our worlds are killed, the time for it to uproot and begin moving again draws nearer. It could be outside of the effective range within three [unknown (unit of time?)]. Furthermore, I do not know how quickly after it reaches our world there will be nobody left to use the [unknown]. I fear that every moment I waste, the more likely it becomes that it is already too late to stop the cavity from spreading.

One thing I can say for certain is that our people are already doomed. The brief flicker that was our existence has already faded. At most, one in sixty of us are still alive, and that is a generous estimate from before we lost our call tower. I know how much you want us to live on. I know how much this weapon's mere existence is an insult to everything you believe in, but we are a moribund people. Denying us the peaceful cradle of extinction by our own hands would be an injustice of the highest degree.

Do not look upon our deaths as a senseless tragedy. Objectively, we were horribly unlucky and lost everything for no reason, but when this is all over, the cosmos will be a more just place for having gotten rid of the cavity, and this will at least have given us a chance to try out our new weapon against the real thing. For the first time, you will have actual data to show the kind of damage this thing can wreak. For the first time, you will see what it looks like to fill emptiness with emptiness. The thing that saddens me the most about dying here is that I will never get to see those numbers myself.

I am clearing a path for you. I am giving you everything you could ever ask for without you having to do any of the work, and thus you are greatly indebted to me. As your creditor, I see it fit to indenture you so that you may never rest again. There are more things that lurk at the edges of our sight, and although no two of such things are the same, I believe having some information is better than none. You are about to watch as the innards of an unknown animal are scattered across the sky, and it would be unbecoming of a scientist such as yourself to not rummage through its remains.

It is quite the gift to be able to hear a language that was probably spoken by humans thousands of years ago. Just one of the countless things I love about working at the foundation. Opportunities like this cannot be found anywhere else.

I wonder if the scientist this message was addressed to ever heard it. No matter how thorough our techniques are, some information may be forever beyond our reach. That saddens me somewhat, but that is life.

As for the main contents of the message, I believe it is worth keeping watch in Scorpio. It seems that the threat was neutralized, but I do wonder what remains of the “cavity” and the planetary system that it invaded. Considering we received this signal less than three decades ago, from our point in the galaxy we should be able to view its remains while they are still fresh in an astronomical time-scale.

— Dr. Rosetta Stone

Footnotes
1. Abbreviation for Scorpio; used in cataloguing astronomical discoveries.
2. Now more commonly known as Afroasiatic.

SCP-9529.raw_content:
SCP-9529, illustrated by Dir. Josie.

Item #: SCP-9529

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9529 is contained within the staff lounge. Flipping SCP-9529 vertically is prohibited.

Description: SCP-9529 is a domestic cat (Felis catus). The bottom half part of SCP-9529, comprising its four paws, half of its belly and the base of its tail, is missing. However, the interior of its abdominal cavity is invisible through the cross-section and the absence of its bottom body does not lead to any physiological problems.

SCP-9529 can walk with its two ears and tail tip, which function as its forepaws and hind paw. The structure of SCP-9529 is absolutely stable: the distance between the head end of its tail and the back end of its belly is always precisely 7.22 centimeters.

Appendix 9529.1:

On September 16th, 2025, Dir. Josie unintentionally traversed the gap of SCP-9529 and tripped it over. This immobilized SCP-9529 and prevented it from getting food for about 3 hours until it was rescued by Dr. Mozzarella.

Dir. Josie was soon punished with a one-week ban on cheese consumption.

NOTICE FROM THE FOUNDATION RECORDS AND INFORMATION SECURITY ADMINISTRATION

The following text is the oldest version of SCP-9537's documentation. Access links to updated and additional documents have been moved to the bottom of the page to encourage staff to read documents fully before proceeding to newer versions.

— Maria Jones, Director, RAISA.

Item#: 9537
Level3
Containment Class:
euclid
Secondary Class:
none
Disruption Class:
keneq
Risk Class:
danger
link to memo

Special Containment Procedures: The currently contained computerized instance of SCP-9537 is to be stored within a standard anomalous containment unit, with slight modifications. It is currently, and should stay as, a 15 x 10 foot room, with a 5-foot radius expanding from the center of the room marked with yellow and black caution tape. Cameras are to be installed in all four corners of the room and are only to be activated during visits to SCP-9537 and only analyzed by research personnel resistant to strong memetic effects.

During election seasons in the United States, not including the midterms, an exploratory commission between Task Forces;

  • Iota-10 "Damn Feds"
  • Mu-4 "Debuggers"
  • Mu-13 "Ghostbusters"
  • Eta-10 "See No Evil"
  • Epsilion-6 "Village Idiots" for Rural and Suburban cases of SCP-9537 exposure
  • Pi-1 "City Slickers" for Urban cases of SCP-9537 exposure

will be formed to contain possible manifestations of SCP-9537. Other Task Forces may be added depending on the manifestation's qualities.

Any testing with SCP-9537 is only to be authorized by the Memetic Effects Specialist currently assigned to SCP-9537. Any individual entering SCP-9537, for testing or otherwise, are to be adminstered political indentification tests before entering and every 15 minutes within the chamber. If the test identifies that alteration from SCP-9537 is present beyond acceptable parameters of the MES, the individual is to be removed from the chamber and given a memetic examination before being adminstered Class-C amnestics.

Description: SCP-9537 is divided into 3 parts;

Recovered instance of SCP-9537. No longer active

  • SCP-9537-A is a memetic effect and physical message initially perpetuated by SCP-9537-C, and maintained by the presence of SCP-9537-B. This effect alters the political views of the afflicted subject, and has been shown to alter infected individual's personalities under long terms of exposure, with only some individuals showing no sign of intensifcation. This intensifcation can only occur if -B is present within a 5-mile radius of the infected individual. If SCP-9537-B is removed from this radius, the infection will start to regress. Research has shown, however, that long-term and constant exposure to -A and -C can slow down the regression process, leading to certain infected individuals being unable to regress to a pre-infection state without the use of Class-C amnestics.
  • SCP-9537-B is the spectral presence of George William Poli. All manifestations of SCP-9537-A and -C are accompanied by the appearence of SCP-9537. Currently, the role of -B, outside of perpetuating the memetic effect of -B within already infected hosts, is unknown, and -B hasn't manifested since the containment of SCP-9537. During manifestations that contain multiple -C instances, sightings of -B have been recorded at both locations. However, any visual or auditory recording of -B have yet to be produced. Individuals who have been in the presence of -B have reported headaches, migranes, and temporary loss of senses, which have been attributed to -B attempting to transmit -A, though no documented infections have been attributed to -B alone.
  • SCP-9537-C is the vessel in which the previous parts (-A and -B respectively.) are transmitted. In 2006, SCP-9537 manifested a -C that it now uses as a main vessel, which is currently contained within Site-537. More can be read on its containment in Addendum 0-A. Over the years since it's discovery, both physical and historically, many forms of its vessel have been logged and have been put into Addendum 0-B. While each manifestation of -C is different, the one common factor amongst all vessels is the physical message that is a part of -A. Said message can be located below.
Access SCiPNET Email? One (1) new message!
Re:Project: Secular Democracy. Potential contamination issues with our project and SCP-9537

To: Memetics Effect Specialist Jack Horay
From: Project: Secular Democracy Lead Lori Sunderweather
Subject: Project: Secular Democracy, Potential contamination issues with our project and SCP-9537.

Hello! This is Lori Sunderweather, Project Lead for Secular Democracy.

We've attempted to reach you multiple times about possible contamination issues with our project and the currently contained SCP-9537. It is our priority to maintain a stable, fair, and unmodified political environment, and considering the anomalous properties of SCP-9537, we are worried that SCP-9537 might be able to effect the implementation of the project.

Our own Memetic Effects specialist is too worried about contamination, and would like to meet with you to discuss the possibility. However, if you aren't going to partake in a meeting, we will have to move forward with the project using precautions developed by our specialist. We hope you respond.

Thanks, Lore Sunderweather.

- Sent September 11, 2024

Discovery:

During the election cycle of 2000, reports of a compound of politically extreme individuals was created inside the Everglades. While normally, the only precaution that would've been taken was to increase security at the surrounding outposts and sites, it also came to the attention of the Foundation that this same compound had been contacting a local division of Marshall, Carter and Dark Ltd for help in the procurement of weaponized artifacts and anomalies, which led to a squad of Epsilion-6 "Village Idiots" being assigned to investigate the compound under the guise of the local electricity company trying to figure out why there was a increased power draw.

Field that borders on forest compound was constructed in.

Upon reaching the compound, Epsilion-6 Team Leader attempted to make contact with a member of the compound, which was not responded to. This continued 3 more times until Foundation Tactical Command allowed them to send in their stealth member, Hotel-7, into the compound to try and make visual contact with anybody inside. When Hotel-7 entered into the compound, they found that all the members committed mass suicide by a combination of poisoning, hanging and starvation. Hotel-7 then encountered SCP-9537-C and -A, which led to H-7 falling under the memetic affliction of SCP-9537-C. Tactical Command received vital monitoring information that Hotel-7 was experiencing the effects of -C, and gave the rest of the Village Idiots permission to make entry and retrieve Hotel-7. Before either Upsilon-4 "Sugar Pill" or Eta-10 "See No Evil" arrived, the manifestation of -A, -B, and -C then disappeared as the election ended.

Please see Addendum 0-A for how the object came under containment, 0-B for past instances of SCP-9537, and 0-C for the message itself.

Addendum 0-A, -B, -C: Containments

+ 0-A; Containment
- 0-A; Containment

During the end of the 2004 election cycle, SCP-9537 and its parts manifested into a computer within the defunct computer room of a church. This is one of the first Foundation recorded instances of SCP-9537-B appearing to make a difference in how SCP-9537-A and -C would affect others. Recovered messages from people who attended the church SCP-9537 was being held in appeared to have encountered a "holy spirit" that was encouraging them to go into the computer room of the church. During preliminary investigation by foundation agents, the section of the nearby populace who attended the church went missing, which launched an emergency inspection of the church to confirm the presence of a possible anomaly.

Currently contained instance of SCP-9537 before containment.

Due to the previous manifestations of SCP-9537, and apparently digital nature of the current manifestation, a JTF of Eta-10 "See No Evil", Epsilon-6 "Village Idiots" and Mu-13 "Ghostbusters" was formed to handle the emergency. On October 31st, the JTF was deployed with approval from Foundation Tactical Command to contain the possible anomaly and investigate the church. Upon arrival to the church, the JTF noted lights coming from within the church, alongside humming as they approached. Once they entered, they were welcomed in by the missing churchgoers. The memetic effects of SCP-9537 had converted the members of the church into extreme anti-governmental communists, leading to the formation of a independent commune city-state within the church itself.

After recording all possible data from the commune, members from Eta-10 and Mu-13 started to navigate to the computer room. Upon arrival, they found that the room was heavily guarded, and were prevented from entering. A member of Eta-10 attempted to sneak into the room through a alternate door, but was detected upon entering, leading to the affected individuals attacking JTF members. The JTF quickly evacuated the church, and Epsilon-6 deployed a strong aerosilized tranquilizer, which rendered the members inside unconscious, and additional support in the form of Alpha-45 "The Janitors" to transport the unconscious individuals to Site-14-M for memetic decontamination and amnestic treatment.

SCP-9537 was contained after the initial deployment of the tranquilizer, and contained within a standard memetic hazard container and transported to Site-537 for further testing under Jack Horay after inital database entry and testing at Site-56.

- 0-B: Previous Forms

Below is the Message that is contained within all manifestations of SCP-9537-A and -C

This traitorous American Government, under the guise of freeing us from a supposed parasitic monarchy is instead depriving us and every man on in this country from the light and blessings of our rightful government. If you want to reclaim the system you are owed, and the resources that follow it, then you must sabotage the traitors. Enter their ranks, confuse their morales, and collapse the disgusting rebels. Join the Crucible!

While the message has been viewed by a audience when it isn't memetically active to be barely convincing and "cringy", when memetically active, the meme has a 100% chance to activate in some way, even at a reduced power as was proven during the 56th election.

Addendum 1-A and -B; POI and Historical Analysis:

+ 2-A Person of Interest File
- 2-A Person of Interest File

Name: George William Poli.
DOB: Unknown exact. Around 1753.
DOD: December 16th, 1773

Possible painting depicting both Boston Tea Party and William's death. Verification underway.

Recovered chest from George Poli's room.

Description: According to historical texts and a personal journal belonging to Poli, George William Poli was a secret royalist during the colonial period before the Boston Tea Party. In response to the growing revolutionary movement within Boston and the surrounding city, Poli began a political party known as the Crucible. The purpose of the Crucible, according to his journal, was to disorient and disrupt revolutionary movements within Boston by creatiing too many view points for the movements to handle. However, historical records at the time indicate that the Crucible went largely unoticed by revolutionary movements. That said, records also indicate the first infections of SCP-9537 around the same time.

While the exact nature of how Poli was integrated into SCP-9537 as -B, or how SCP-9537 was created, during the annual Memetic Conference, the parahistorian assigned to SCP-9537 gave a possible theory. It should be noted that this hasn't be proven.

VIDEO LOG

DATE:8/15/24

NOTE: Full transcript and video can be requested from the Site-19 Archives.

[BEGIN LOG]

TIME: 00:00 Memetic Effects Specialist Jack Horay steps down from the stage as Parahistorian Lily Orman steps on.

TIME: 00:10 Lily places a binder onto the pedistal on the stage and begins speaking.

Lily Orman: As you may have noticed SCP-9537 comes bundled with a spectral presence, or, in more relatable terms, a ghost. While the memeticists assigned to this anomaly have yet to discover what the point of -B is beyond memetics, I feel that it is still important to compile a historical record of -B's existence.

TIME: 00:30 Lily switches to a slide of a painting of George William Poli.

Lily Orman: For all intents and purposes, Poli was a hidden royalist inside of a soon-to-burst kettle pot of revolutionary ideals and actions, and was very angered with that fact. Because of this, he created the Crucible, a political party centered around creating and promoting so many ideas that, in his hopes, would confuse the revolutionary waters of Boston. However-.

TIME: 01:00 Lily switches to a slide of a newspaper, the Boston Gazette, before it quickly zooms into a section dedicated to coverage of the Crucible. The section in the corner of the 4th page, and is only a paragraph long.

Lily Orman: It should be clear that it wasn't an exactly popular party.

TIME: 01:17 Chuckles come from the audience.

Lily Orman: That isn't to say that the Crucible had no members during its lifetime. At a minimum, going off of the first possible manifestation of SCP-9537, 5 members. This would lead us to the obvious of question of, how was SCP-9537 created? While there are many possibilities, this is the one our team working on SCP-9537 is currently researching.

TIME: 01:35 Lily switches to a slide of a artistic depiction of the Boston Tea Party.

Lily Orman: Unlike what many of you may have heard about the Boston Tea Party, there was in fact one casualty of the event. George William Poli. How he died is, well, entirely unknown to us, and seemingly was unknown to people of that time, as no newspaper reported a orbituary, and no documents recovered regarding the Crucible discussed his death. It is his death that we think he became a part of SCP-9537. However, like many anomalies, we do not have a full picture. The questions of how -C manifests or how -A was created remain unknown, and will likely end up being the same as many anomalies. Unknown.

TIME: 02:25 Appalause comes from the audience as Lily Orman steps down from the stage and █████ ████ steps up to announce that the intermission has begun.

[END LOG]

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9547 is to be monitored in communities with a high concentration of SCP-9547 triggers, such as Nexuses and Free Ports. In the case that an individual might be at serious risk due to SCP-9547, they are to be removed from the trigger whenever possible.

Information regarding SCP-9547 is to be disseminated to all Foundation personnel. Foundation agents and researchers are to be administered a standard issue SCP-9547 test kit along with the allergy tests that are administered at the time of employment. If a Foundation agent is expected to handle known SCP-9547 triggers that are outside of the ones tested for in the standard issue kit, they are to be tested for an SCP-9547 response to that trigger whenever possible.

Description: SCP-9547 is an anomalous immune response created when individuals come into contact with anomalous materials, hereafter referred to as "triggers". An individual that displays an SCP-9547 response to one trigger may not display it for others. While exact numbers are not known, it is estimated that SCP-9547 is displayed by around 2% of the human population.

The symptoms of SCP-9547 are similar to that of a non-anomalous allergen response, including sneezing, itchiness, rashes, and in cases of severe or extended exposure, anaphylactic shock.

While the symptoms of SCP-9547 mimic allergies, there are important differences between SCP-9547 and non-anomalous allergies. For example, there does not seem to be any hereditary or environmental correlation between individuals that display SCP-9547, and the factors responsible for SCP-9547 remain unclear. Additionally, SCP-9547 is considered to be more severe than non-anomalous allergies, as no effective treatments for acute SCP-9547 cases have been discovered. Epinephrine, for example, has no effect on SCP-9547. In most cases, removing the subject from the trigger is the best way to treat SCP-9547 symptoms.

Around 100 triggers for SCP-9547 have been confirmed, but many more are suspected to exist. Relevant examples of triggers include: amnestic and mnestic compounds, materials used in the production of Scranton Reality Anchors, and contact with many contained anomalies.1 It is important to note, many SCP-9547 triggers appear to be entirely inconsistent with each other. Besides an anomalous designation, it is unclear what properties are responsible for a material to be a SCP-9547 trigger. The mechanisms by which the body detects SCP-9547 triggers, and the reasoning for an immune response, are unknown.

SCP-9547 was brought to attention during a raid by MTF Epsilon-6, "Village Idiots", on the house of a Type Green reality bender. During a confrontation with the threat, officer Samuel Rodgers was forced to sustain direct contact with the target, and subsequently experienced a severe anaphylactic shock. This could have posed a severe threat to the team, but they were able to dispatch the threat quickly, and move Samuel Rodgers to safety, where he was able to recover.

Samuel Rodgers was not known to have had any major allergies at the time, so it was initially assumed that the response was due to the Type Green's effects, but that did not line up with the symptoms experienced by the other members of Epsilon-6. Later, the response was able to be replicated using reality benders under the employment of the Foundation. Samuel Rodgers' reaction is now known to be due to SCP-9547.

Because of the rarity of almost all triggers of SCP-9547, in addition to the difficulty to distinguish from non-anomalous allergies, SCP-9547 is considered to pose very little threat to the general population and the Veil.

However, SCP-9547 does pose a unique challenge to the Foundation. If undetected, an SCP-9547 response could pose a severe issue to any Foundation agent that is expected to remain in contact with anomalous conditions for an extended period of time, as was the case with Samuel Rodgers.

In order to prevent future issues related to SCP-9547, it has been deemed necessary to develop a standardized test in order to detect Foundation agents that display SCP-9547, to be issued alongside standard Foundation allergy tests. However, the exact triggers that are to be tested for in such a test have been debated. The Foundation has the capability to hypothetically test any individual for any of the known triggers of SCP-9547, but many of these procedures are expensive and impractical, particularly if the test is to be done at scale.

Addendum: On May 19th, 2007, a meeting was held with researcher Sandra Matthews, who spearheaded research on SCP-9547, conducted by Ethics Committee liaison Thomas Parnett. The goal of the meeting was to discuss how the Foundation might operate with SCP-9547 in mind, and how to prevent incidents like the one with Samuel Rodgers.

[Begin Transcript]

Matthews: Thank you for your time today. I recognize that SCP-9547 might remain a low priority for the Foundation, but I think it's extremely important that we prevent further incidents in the future.

Parnett: Of course. Admittedly, it was originally quite difficult to take the idea of an "allergy to SCPs" seriously, when I first read the case file. Well, until I read about the incident with the Epsilon-6 raid.

[Matthews laughs.]

Matthews: I've heard that quite a few times in the intervening months. If I'm being honest, I'm sort of glad that things went down the way they did. That could easily happen again, and with far greater consequences the next time. It's important that it drew attention. Otherwise, I might not have been sitting here with the knowledge that I have. In fact, Samuel Rodgers has been quite instrumental in our current understanding of SCP-9547. He has been a large ally, and I appreciate that he endured quite as many rashes as he did, for science.

Parnett: I don't think that either of us would have been sitting here if that didn't attract as much attention as it did. Some of the higher ups seem quite worried about all this.

Matthews: As they should be. I'm just glad that I've finally been able to get people to take it seriously.

Parnett: Well, anyways, could you explain more about these tests?

Matthews: Of course. It's the same logic as an ordinary allergy test. You prick someone with the allergen and see how big the bump is, in relation to a control, of course. As long as you're able to get a sample of the material that you want to test, it's trivial to test for an allergic reaction.

Parnett: I think you've made it clear that the Foundation should implement these tests across the board.

Matthews: Yes, I do believe that.

Parnett: Why is that? Don't you think that SCP-9547 is quite trivial? Why is it necessary that Foundation resources go toward this?

Matthews: SCP-9547 is often trivial, but it's not trivial in all cases. As we have seen, it can very well put someone's life on the line. Ignoring SCP-9547 means inviting the risk for a critical failure down the line, and that could be even more costly than these tests. If you can prevent an incident, it is in your responsibility to do so. I have worked to give the Foundation the means for that prevention, and I believe that they should move forward with that in mind.

Parnett: But you're aware that SCP-9547 test kits are far more expensive than normal allergy test kits?

Matthews: I am aware of that. I still believe the Foundation has the necessary resources to devote to this.

Parnett: Do you think that Foundation employment should be conditional on a negative test?

[Matthews shifts within her seat. She appears uncomfortable with the question.]

Matthews: …No. I don't think that should be the case. People should be denied employment only in a few extreme circumstances.

Parnett: Alright. Do you believe all triggers should be tested for?

Matthews: Well, certainly not all of them. Almost nobody would ever come into contact with some contained anomalies, for example. However, I would really like to reiterate that there are many triggers that should be tested for unconditionally. We can go over the details, and I have listed specific triggers I am concerned about in the report, but there should be about 26 triggers that everyone should be tested for. My sincere hope is that these tests don’t just become something that only a few high ranking officials get and no-one else. It's important that we don't risk the lives of our personnel just to save a few bucks.

Parnett: I think we could be in agreement of that. Please understand, I'm pushing you here because I know that these are the things that people will say.

Matthews: I am aware of that.

Parnett: Regardless, I think that should be enough for now. Thank you for your time, Dr. Matthews, and thank you for bringing this to the Foundation's attention, of course. I will try to convince the higher ups that resources should be dedicated to this.

Matthews: Thank you, Parnett. You are very welcome.

[End Transcript]

Following the meeting, SCP-9547 test kits were formalized and distributed to Foundation sites. Currently, the standard issue test kit for SCP-9547 contains a test for 12 known triggers. High ranking personnel, such as Site Directors or O5 council members, are issued a test kit for 59 known triggers. Following these events, Samuel Rodgers has been deemed unfit for his role, and has been removed from active duty.

Besides an anomalous designation, it is unclear what properties are responsible for a material to be a SCP-9547 trigger. The mechanisms by which the body detects SCP-9547 triggers, and the reasoning for an immune response, are unknown. SCP-9547 was brought to attention during a raid by MTF Epsilon-6, "Village Idiots", on the house of a Type Green reality bender. During a confrontation with the threat, officer Samuel Rodgers was forced to sustain direct contact with the target, and subsequently experienced a severe anaphylactic shock. This could have posed a severe threat to the team, but they were able to dispatch the threat quickly, and move Samuel Rodgers to safety, where he was able to recover. Samuel Rodgers was not known to have had any major allergies at the time, so it was initially assumed that the response was due to the Type Green's effects, but that did not line up with the symptoms experienced by the other members of Epsilon-6. Later, the response was able to be replicated using reality benders under the employment of the Foundation. Samuel Rodgers' reaction is now known to be due to SCP-9547. Because of the rarity of almost all triggers of SCP-9547, in addition to the difficulty to distinguish from non-anomalous allergies, SCP-9547 is considered to pose very little threat to the general population and the Veil. However, SCP-9547 does pose a unique challenge to the Foundation. If undetected, an SCP-9547 response could pose a severe issue to any Foundation agent that is expected to remain in contact with anomalous conditions for an extended period of time, as was the case with Samuel Rodgers. In order to prevent future issues related to SCP-9547, it has been deemed necessary to develop a standardized test in order to detect Foundation agents that display SCP-9547, to be issued alongside standard Foundation allergy tests. However, the exact triggers that are to be tested for in such a test have been debated. The Foundation has the capability to hypothetically test any individual for any of the known triggers of SCP-9547, but many of these procedures are expensive and impractical, particularly if the test is to be done at scale. **Addendum:** On May 19th, 2007, a meeting was held with researcher Sandra Matthews, who spearheaded research on SCP-9547, conducted by Ethics Committee liaison Thomas Parnett. The goal of the meeting was to discuss how the Foundation might operate with SCP-9547 in mind, and how to prevent incidents like the one with Samuel Rodgers. [[div class="blockquote"]] **[Begin Transcript]** **Matthews:** Thank you for your time today. I recognize that SCP-9547 might remain a low priority for the Foundation, but I think it's extremely important that we prevent further incidents in the future. **Parnett:** Of course. Admittedly, it was originally quite difficult to take the idea of an "allergy to SCPs" seriously, when I first read the case file. Well, until I read about the incident with the Epsilon-6 raid. //[Matthews laughs.]// **Matthews:** I've heard that quite a few times in the intervening months. If I'm being honest, I'm sort of glad that things went down the way they did. That could easily happen again, and with far greater consequences the next time. It's important that it drew attention. Otherwise, I might not have been sitting here with the knowledge that I have. In fact, Samuel Rodgers has been quite instrumental in our current understanding of SCP-9547. He has been a large ally, and I appreciate that he endured quite as many rashes as he did, for science. **Parnett:** I don't think that either of us would have been sitting here if that didn't attract as much attention as it did. Some of the higher ups seem quite worried about all this. **Matthews:** As they should be. I'm just glad that I've finally been able to get people to take it seriously. **Parnett:** Well, anyways, could you explain more about these tests? **Matthews:** Of course. It's the same logic as an ordinary allergy test. You prick someone with the allergen and see how big the bump is, in relation to a control, of course. As long as you're able to get a sample of the material that you want to test, it's trivial to test for an allergic reaction. **Parnett:** I think you've made it clear that the Foundation should implement these tests across the board. **Matthews:** Yes, I do believe that. **Parnett:** Why is that? Don't you think that SCP-9547 is quite trivial? Why is it necessary that Foundation resources go toward this? **Matthews:**  SCP-9547 is often trivial, but it's not trivial in all cases. As we have seen, it can very well put someone's life on the line. Ignoring SCP-9547 means inviting the risk for a critical failure down the line, and that could be even more costly than these tests. If you can prevent an incident, it is in your responsibility to do so.  I have worked to give the Foundation the means for that prevention, and I believe that they should move forward with that in mind. **Parnett:** But you're aware that SCP-9547 test kits are far more expensive than normal allergy test kits? **Matthews:** I am aware of that. I still believe the Foundation has the necessary resources to devote to this. **Parnett:** Do you think that Foundation employment should be conditional on a negative test? //[Matthews shifts within her seat. She appears uncomfortable with the question.]// **Matthews:** ...No. I don't think that should be the case. People should be denied employment only in a few extreme circumstances. **Parnett:** Alright. Do you believe all triggers should be tested for? **Matthews:** Well, certainly not all of them. Almost nobody would ever come into contact with some contained anomalies, for example. However, I would really like to reiterate that there are many triggers that should be tested for unconditionally. We can go over the details, and I have listed specific triggers I am concerned about in the report, but there should be about 26 triggers that //everyone// should be tested for. My sincere hope is that these tests don’t just become something that only a few high ranking officials get and no-one else. It's important that we don't risk the lives of our personnel just to save a few bucks. **Parnett:** I think we could be in agreement of that. Please understand, I'm pushing you here because I know that these are the things that people will say. **Matthews:** I am aware of that. **Parnett:** Regardless, I think that should be enough for now. Thank you for your time, Dr. Matthews, and thank you for bringing this to the Foundation's attention, of course. I will try to convince the higher ups that resources should be dedicated to this. **Matthews:** Thank you, Parnett. You are very welcome. **[End Transcript]** [[/div]] Following the meeting, SCP-9547 test kits were formalized and distributed to Foundation sites. Currently, the standard issue test kit for SCP-9547 contains a test for 12 known triggers. High ranking personnel, such as Site Directors or O5 council members, are issued a test kit for 59 known triggers. Following these events, Samuel Rodgers has been deemed unfit for his role, and has been removed from active duty. Special Containment Procedures: Containment has been delegated to the Federal Bureau of Investigation's Unusual Incidents Unit (UIU).

SCP-9550 at the time of discovery.

Description: SCP-9550 is a wooden-frame farmhouse located approximately 32 kilometres east of Des Moines, Iowa. The interior of SCP-9550 is insulated from baseline reality. Initially detected in 2012, ownership of the building was claimed by the UIU soon after its discovery by Foundation operatives.

Addendum 9550.1: On December 21st, 2025, embedded Foundation agents in the Des Moines area detected a large decrease in Hume1 levels near the location of SCP-9550. Local UIU operatives were immediately contacted to discuss the source of the decrease.

Interview Log 2025-12-21

Subject: Darren Macy (External, Unusual Incidents Unit)

Interviewer: Eleanor Zhang (External Affairs)

Location: Simple Clean Pasta, a Foundation-operated vegan restaurant in Des Moines

[BEGIN LOG]

[Zhang enters the private booth and sits down across from Macy.]

Zhang: Good afternoon, Macy.

Macy: Zhang. Thanks for meeting me.

Zhang: I seem to remember being the one who called you.

[Macy laughs.]

Macy: This is faster.

[Zhang glances down at the menu on the table.]

Zhang: Before we start, do you want to order anything? You look like you've had a long day.

Macy: Kid, you'd look like [expletive] too if one of your big brains cut his comms and ran off with your top-secret project. You reckon I could get a coffee here?

Zhang: I'll see if we can get you some on the way out.

Macy: Just make sure it's a real coffee. If it's got any of that plant stuff in it I don't want it.

Zhang: Don't coffee beans come from a plant?

Macy: You know what I mean.

Zhang: I'll let them know. Now, to business — Macy, the Foundation wants to know what's going on with that house of yours.

Macy: Trying to bail us out?

Zhang: I just meant the Foundation wants to know if you have everything under control. You mentioned an operative going rogue?

Macy: I'll tell you everything we know, Zhang, but before I do I'm gonna insist on one thing. I want this to be a joint operation. If you wanna help we won't turn it down, but this is our mess and we're gonna clean it up.

Zhang: Of course — the Foundation appreciates your support.

Macy: Great. Take these.

[Macy passes Zhang a pile of documents.]

Zhang: You're handing over your top-secret project?

Macy: Zhang, if there's anything in there that you don't already have a vastly superior version of, I'll eat my belt. God knows I'm not gonna find any other food in this place.

[Zhang begins to read the documents.]

Macy: We call it Last Resort: a safe house for the end of the world. Everyone knows that we're not gonna be the ones to stop the apocalypse when it happens. With Last Resort, at least if you [Macy points his fork at Zhang] or the gawkers — we're not picky — manage to stop whatever is bringing about the end times, there'll be something left of us.

Zhang: Was it operational?

Macy: We were getting there. [Macy sets his fork down.] Alright, you're gonna see two names.

Zhang: Your scientists?

Macy: Yep. Don't worry about Cantrell — he ran off years ago. Here. [Macy points to a line in the document Zhang is reading.] Bloodworth is the guy we care about. He shut off his comms and got in the house this morning. No idea what his plan is, but we think he set off that big energy drop you saw.

Zhang: Could you get Cantrell back?

Macy: No dice. Cantrell didn't just leave the project, he left this life. Mind-wipe, new identity, the works. Then he died anyway. Drove into a ditch in 2022 after we went through all that trouble.

Zhang: Unfortunate. Thank you, Macy. I'll have this passed along to the right people. Someone should be over in a few minutes with your coffee.

[Zhang stands up to leave.]

Zhang: And there's a McDonald's around the corner.

[END LOG]

Selected documents from the files provided by the UIU are available below.

+ PROJECT LAST RESORT
- Close

Summary: PROJECT LAST RESORT was proposed in 2007 following a suspected mass restructuring of reality2, with the goal of preserving the integrity of UIU leadership in emergency scenarios. The project was approved in 2008. Initial plans considered a location in Three Portlands, which were scrapped in favor of an independent structure wholly under UIU jurisdiction. Due to budget issues, work on the project was delayed until 2010 when Cyrus Bloodworth and Colin Cantrell were recruited. Construction of Last Resort, the core physical structure of PROJECT LAST RESORT, was completed in 2012.

Last Resort is completely isolated from normal reality, requiring any occupants of the structure to collectively reconstruct an internal material reality. Due to the coherency of intent required for this task, early work on PROJECT LAST RESORT was primarily focused on providing the necessary mental scaffolding to construct a stable internal reality. A stable internal reality for multiple occupants was achieved in 2016. Following this initial success, work on PROJECT LAST RESORT was suspended while funds were redirected to rebuilding ██████████ in ███████. During this period, Cantrell left the project. Work on PROJECT LAST RESORT resumed in 2023. Current work is focused on enabling on-demand entry to the structure.

+ Experimentation Record
- Close

Date: 09/30/20123
Occupants: Cyrus Bloodworth
Method: Bloodworth entered through the front door and imagined his childhood home.
Result: Successful. The internal reality was sustained for three hours before the occupant voluntarily exited through the front door.

Date: 10/01/2012
Occupants: Colin Cantrell
Method: Suspecting that he was unable to recall the details of his childhood home in sufficient detail, Cantrell entered through the front door and imagined his former dormitory at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
Result: Unsuccessful. The occupant was unable to maintain the required coherency of intent.

Date: 08/17/2014
Occupants: Cyrus Bloodworth, Colin Cantrell
Method: Bloodworth and Cantrell entered through the front door and imagined their shared college dormitory from their time at Deer College.4
Result: Partially successful. The internal reality was maintained for 23 seconds before destabilizing. Both occupants were transported onto the front porch of Last Resort upon the collapse of the internal reality. No lasting effects were reported.

Date: 08/26/2016
Occupants: Cyrus Bloodworth, Colin Cantrell
Method: Cantrell proposed an experiment to determine if the internal reality could be constructed based on a location that does not exist. Bloodworth and Cantrell entered and imagined the set of a local theater's production of the stage play Romeo and Juliet.
Result: Partially successful. The internal reality was constructed without incident. However, the internal reality contained elements of both the fictional setting of Romeo and Juliet and the set. The ensuing panic triggered the rapid destabilization of the internal reality. Bloodworth sustained major injuries that were treated upon his return.

Date: 08/27/2016
Occupants: Caden Attwood, Colin Cantrell, Ryan Giles, Gina Sawyer, Lewis Summers
Method: Cantrell proposed an experiment to determine if the stability of the internal reality depended on the number of occupants. All five occupants entered and imagined the interior of the local UIU office.
Result: Successful. A stable internal reality was maintained until all five occupants voluntarily exited. All occupants re-entered and repeated the experiment successfully.

Addendum 9550.2: Shortly after the initial meeting with the UIU, a Foundation containment team from Site-157 met with regional UIU operatives to form a joint containment team. A temporary containment site approximately 300 metres from SCP-9550 was established. Researcher Raphael Vidal was dispatched to assist the containment team and arrived at 03:00 local time on December 22nd, 2025.

Video Log 2025-12-22

Participants: Clarice Katz (Containment Team Lead), Raphael Vidal (Researcher), Darren Macy (External, Unusual Incidents Unit)

Location: SCP-9550 Containment Zone, Tent A

[BEGIN LOG]

[Vidal enters the tent, interrupting a meeting between Macy and Katz.]

Vidal: Hi.

[Vidal waves his right arm. A piece of tomato flies out of the sandwich he is holding and lands in the grass.]

Vidal: I'm Raphael Vidal. I do research with, well, mostly anomalies insulated from baseline reality, which is why they sent me here. I'm sorry for being late but when I was looking for the tent there were just so many and I ended up at Tent B but all they have in there is food and I was hungry — I get airsick so I couldn't eat on the plane — so I took a sandwich and then I remembered I was supposed to be here and—

Katz: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Vidal. Please take a seat.

Vidal: Ah — just thought you should know, I never got around to the whole doctorate thing. Don't worry, I know what I'm doing. I think.

Katz: Mr. Vidal, please sit down.

Vidal: Right.

[Vidal sits down. A piece of chicken falls out of his sandwich.]

Katz: I'm leading the Foundation side of this containment team. You can call me Captain Katz. This is Darren Macy of the Unusual Incidents Unit. He can catch you up to speed with what we've been discussing so far.

[Macy does not respond.]

Katz: Mr. Macy?

[Katz leans over to examine Macy.]

Katz: Mr. Macy, if you're beginning to experience any unusual effects from the anomaly—

Macy: I'm fine. [Macy waves them off.] So, Vidal, was it? Did you read the files we gave you?

Vidal: Yes. Was that everything? I thought it was some very interesting science. Nothing truly groundbreaking, of course — no offence, Mr. Macy — but you have to know that around here we don't necessarily expect a lot from the UIU.

Macy: If you're looking for more recent notes, they're gone. We think Bloodworth scrubbed them when he shut off his comms.

Vidal: Hmm.

Katz: Is something wrong? We had the files checked for cognitohazards before we sent them to you, but we can still have you assessed.

Macy: Have a little faith.

Katz: It's policy.

Vidal: No, it's not that, it's like when you're looking for a word and it's right there on the tip of your tongue. There's something I should remember — I just don't know what it is.

Katz: Is it important?

[Vidal shrugs.]

Vidal: Probably not?

Katz: If it's not important, it can wait.

Macy: Vidal, I'm about to fall asleep standing up and the faster we get this over with the faster we can all go home. You're up to speed on the house, so now let's get you up to speed on the plan. We wanna send a team into Last Resort to get Bloodworth out so we can question him. Before we do that, we wanna figure out what that big energy drop was and what he's trying to do.

Vidal: [chewing] Can I see the data?

Katz: I have the report here.

[Katz passes their laptop to Vidal. Vidal leans over to study the screen and sets his sandwich on the keyboard.]

Vidal: You said Bloodworth was experimenting with the entrance to Last Resort?

Macy: Yes. He'd had some successes, but without his notes there's not much else I can tell you. Couldn't make heads or tails of it.

Vidal: See this? [Vidal points at the screen, leaving a fingerprint.] It's an entrance drop. You know how when you open a door, there's this whoosh of air? Same idea, the Hume levels — that's reality energy to you, Macy — of our reality and the reality inside Last Resort are different, so you get this signature drop whenever someone tries to enter the internal reality. What we picked up is that same drop, just amplified enough that it reached our equipment.

Macy: Was that in the files we gave you?

Vidal: Probably? Point is, I think he's trying to bring someone in.

Katz: Thank you, Mr. Vidal. My chief concern is still safety. Can we risk a direct approach?

Vidal: Aren't you trying to get inside anyway? It's safe. The insulation goes both ways — the internal reality collapsing doesn't affect baseline reality, and baseline reality collapsing doesn't affect the internal reality. Well, I don't know about safe, you're still going to have to bust down the door of a house with an armed man inside — he's a scientist, but he's also FBI so I think it evens out. I'll let you handle that part.

Katz: Theoretically, but what about in practice? Mr. Vidal, with all due respect, you didn't even know about 9550 six hours ago.

Vidal: I've read the files and I've seen the schematics. This is science — I mean, it's anomalous science, but it's still science. It's safe.

Katz: In one of their experiments, Bloodworth sustained a major injury.

[Vidal opens his mouth to speak, but is cut off by Macy.]

Macy: Bloodworth got hurt because he and Cantrell were two young hotshot geniuses who decided to goof off. I agree with, uh, Vidal here. My team's ready when you are.

Vidal: Look at the screen, there's another—

[Vidal disappears from the camera feed.]

[END LOG]

Interview Log 2025-12-22

Subject: Cyrus Bloodworth (External, Unusual Incidents Unit)

Interviewer: Raphael Vidal (Researcher)

Location: SCP-9550

Notes: Recovered from Vidal's body camera after his return to baseline reality.

[BEGIN LOG]

[Vidal appears within SCP-9550's internal reality. The internal reality manifests as a college dormitory.]

Bloodworth: Hello.

Vidal: Wow. Total control over the entrance point — how did you solve that?

Bloodworth: I had nine years. And I wasn't the one who solved it, Colin, you did.

Vidal: What?

[Bloodworth pauses.]

Bloodworth: You don't remember.

Vidal: Sorry, this is a bit awkward but I think you kidnapped the wrong guy.

Bloodworth: Maybe. [Bloodworth gestures at the bed opposite to him.] Come, sit.

[Vidal does not move.]

Vidal: How is it this stable? I've never seen this room before.

Bloodworth: Nine years is a long time. Now, who do you think you are?

Vidal: I'm — I probably shouldn't tell you my name, not sure I even can — I'm a researcher for the Foundation.

Bloodworth: Good. What do you research?

Vidal: The same thing you do. Well, mostly. I usually work with anomalies that are insulated from baseline reality, but I have a really bad memory so I figure at some point they must have had me on a memetics project.

Bloodworth: And how do you like your coffee?

[Bloodworth holds out a coffee cup.]

Bloodworth: No milk, packet and a half of sugar because one is too bitter and two is too sweet. Am I right?

[Vidal backs away from Bloodworth.]

Vidal: Don't try to distract me. Everyone this side of the Veil saw that Hume drop when you went rogue and tried to bring someone here. Colin. Colin Cantrell? Why him?

Bloodworth: You want to know why?

Vidal: That's why I'm still here — if I wanted to leave you'd be in handcuffs by now.

Bloodworth: Sit down. Let me tell you a story.

[Vidal approaches the bed cautiously. He sits.]

Bloodworth: Do you know where we are?

Vidal: SCP-9550. Last Resort. I like Last Resort better, but don't tell them I said that.

Bloodworth: I mean this room.

Vidal: It looks like a dormitory. Give me a second, I'm trying to remember your file. MIT? No, that was definitely Cantrell. Deer College?

[Bloodworth nods.]

Bloodworth: This was my dorm for the first three years I was there. He was my roommate. God, for the first year I wanted to hate him. Do you know how many colours mould comes in?

Vidal: Not really? Green obviously, sometimes blue, and then there's that pink slimy stuff but I don't know if that's actually mould. Never really got into biology.

Bloodworth: At least twelve. We found a new one every month on his side of the fridge. But he was brilliant, and he didn't think it was weird that I took exactly enough occult coursework to graduate and not a single credit more.

Vidal: Then why go to Deer? I saw your work — any mundane institution would've been lucky to have you.

Bloodworth: My family. I'm from a line of — thaumaturges, Type Blues, witches, whatever. I was born with the family gift for it, but I've never liked things that can't be understood. Then Cantrell turned up.

Vidal: What was special about him?

Bloodworth: I think we had the same sort of screw loose. He was a classic child prodigy — when I met him he was sixteen and already had two degrees. But he was terrified of becoming the stereotype.

Vidal: I feel that. We start off so strong, end up on TV, earn a few degrees, and then bam! You turn 21 and fall off the face of the Earth.

Bloodworth: I wasn't quite the same, but I could relate. I needed to prove I deserved my name.

Vidal: And then?

Bloodworth: He talked me into doing our term project together. It was part magic, part science, all madness. That was the problem with Cantrell — he had this dangerous ability to make you feel like he knew what he was doing.

Vidal: There's no way that didn't end in a smoking crater. Ah, sorry, that's insensitive — I've been trying to work on that.

Bloodworth: No, you're right. It blew up. The building isn't there anymore, but it isn't quite a crater. They roped off the rubble and called it an art installation.

Vidal: What happened?

Bloodworth: I thought he understood it. He certainly thought he understood it. But that's the problem with this. [Bloodworth gestures around him.] Sometimes you get something that seems to follow rules, but it's all an illusion.

Vidal: There are always rules. We just don't always understand them in time.

[Bloodworth laughs. A brief silence elapses.]

Vidal: Can I ask? Was that how you got…

Bloodworth: Oh, you mean this?

[Bloodworth points to a faded scar on his face. It runs across his left eye and down to his chin.]

Bloodworth: Yes. And it was his fault. We both knew it was his fault. I was out for a week and by the time I woke up he'd already left. I didn't get to talk to him.

Vidal: I would've punched him in the face.

Bloodworth: Oh, I wanted to do that too. He didn't give me the chance.

Vidal: Didn't he come back? I thought you worked on Last Resort together.

Bloodworth: He did. I got to tell him I forgave him, and he got to apologise. And then — well, you've read the file.

Vidal: I'm sorry.

Bloodworth: Are you? [Bloodworth chuckles.] They told me he died in 2022. I didn't buy it, but I guess in a way they were right.

Vidal: So you think he's still out there somewhere? You still haven't told me why you wanted to bring him here.

Bloodworth: Tell me, Researcher…

Vidal: Vidal.

Bloodworth: Vidal, is there anyone in your life you would like to see again? One more time?

Vidal: I… no. I'm in the wrong line of work for that.

Bloodworth: No family? Friends?

Vidal: I have my work. I wish I could tell you about it — I think you'd like it — and now I sound like I don't appreciate what you've done, which isn't true. This really is some solid science, but it's so small — you could be doing so much more with this.

Bloodworth: I am. You'll see soon.

Vidal: Look, clearly you made a mistake and I'm sorry I'm not the person you wanted to see, but if you're not going to explain I'm just going to bust out of here. It was nice meeting you, Bloodworth. I hope they go easy on you.

Bloodworth: I didn't.

Vidal: What?

Bloodworth: You're not here by mistake. I wanted you here because there's always a chance this won't work, and I wanted to be able to say this just once. Goodbye, Colin.

Vidal: What—

[Vidal is ejected from the internal reality of SCP-9550.]

[END LOG]

Following Researcher Vidal's return to baseline reality, Darren Macy of the UIU provided the SCP-9550 containment team with additional documents.

+ Video Log: 09/21/2010
- Close

Video Log: 09/21/2010

Participants: Darren MACY, Colin CANTRELL, Cyrus BLOODWORTH
Location: Des Moines office
Notes: Recorded shortly after Colin Cantrell and Cyrus Bloodworth were recruited to join PROJECT LAST RESORT.

[BEGIN LOG]

[BLOODWORTH is seated at a table in the center of the room. MACY enters with CANTRELL trailing behind him.]

MACY: Bloodworth, I want you to meet Colin Cantrell.

[BLOODWORTH drops his coffee mug with a loud crashing sound.]

MACY: I see you've already met.

BLOODWORTH: Colin?

[MACY sighs.]

MACY: I don't have time for this.

[CANTRELL turns around and reaches for the doorknob. MACY grabs the doorknob first, holding the door shut.]

MACY: Both of you, shut up and listen to me. I don't know what your deal is with each other and I don't wanna know — don't tell me. What I do know is that it took me two years to find you two and I am not spending another two finding your replacements. You're gonna kiss and make up here and now or you can have it out in a holding cell. Who wants to go first?

[Silence elapses.]

MACY: Cantrell.

CANTRELL: I'm sorry. I should've said something or left a note at least or—

BLOODWORTH: I forgive you. I don't know if I should but I do. I'm glad to see you again, Colin.

[MACY claps his hands once.]

MACY: Great, now we can all move on. Cantrell, sit down.

[CANTRELL sits down.]

MACY: In front of you is the dossier on Last Resort. Before we start, I want you to know three things. One, yes, it is too late to back out. Two, we're on a shoestring budget. You're not gonna get a lot of things you want and most of the things you need you'll have to get yourself. Which brings me to three — we'll train you, but you don't fit the usual profile of an agent. I trust, given your backgrounds, that you are capable of defending yourselves. I'm supposed to tell you that you are under no circumstances allowed to use magic of any kind: no spells, no rituals, no psychic touches. But I need you two alive, so just make sure I don't hear about it. Understood?

BLOODWORTH: Yes.

[CANTRELL nods.]

MACY: Then I think this will work out just fine.

[END LOG]

+  Video Log: 09/19/2012
- Close

Video Log: 09/19/2012

PARTICIPANTS: Colin CANTRELL, Cyrus BLOODWORTH
LOCATION: An abandoned warehouse near Portland, Maine
NOTES: Recorded during a mission to retrieve materials for PROJECT LAST RESORT. This footage was originally deleted and recovered on 12/22/2025 with the assistance of the SCP Foundation.

[BEGIN LOG]

[CANTRELL and BLOODWORTH are tied together in the centre of a dimly lit room. A middle-aged woman stands facing them.]

UNKNOWN: Gentlemen.

CANTRELL: Who are you?

UNKNOWN: There will be time for introductions, but not now. My men were ready to shoot you where you stood — those who steal from me do not live to tell the tale. But I know who you are, and I know you are more valuable to me alive than dead. Whatever they're paying you, I have the means to pay you more. The UIU? You're both intelligent enough to recognize you deserve more than the UIU can give you. You don't need to be doing the dirty work of men far below—

[BLOODWORTH recites a thaumaturgical incantation, and the woman speaking freezes. CANTRELL slips out of his restraints and unties BLOODWORTH.]

CANTRELL: Couldn't have done that earlier? Like, when they were punching me?

BLOODWORTH: Yeah, but now we have video of her face — Macy's going to be over the moon. And it's not my fault you missed when you tried to shoot them.

CANTRELL: That's not fair, my aim isn't any worse than yours. I was just cold and that made me shiver and that made me miss.

BLOODWORTH: Here. Don't miss next time.

[BLOODWORTH shrugs off his jacket and tosses it at CANTRELL. It is several sizes too big for him.]

CANTRELL: I can't wear this back — they'll talk.

BLOODWORTH: They talk enough already. You still have what we came here for?

[CANTRELL produces a doorknob from his pocket.]

BLOODWORTH: Where's the rest of it?

CANTRELL: What, did you expect me to take the entire door? Only the doorknob is anomalous — that's the bit we want.

[BLOODWORTH and CANTRELL leave the room. BLOODWORTH briefly stops to look at the frozen woman before joining CANTRELL in the hallway.]

CANTRELL: If you're still thinking about her deal, I hate to break it to you but most people take getting their brain thaumaturgically shut off as a pretty solid no.

BLOODWORTH: You know she's right.

CANTRELL: About what?

BLOODWORTH: Come on, Colin, don't pretend you haven't thought about it. This is below you — you shouldn't need to be here, risking your neck to steal a [expletive] doorknob.

CANTRELL: Hey, that doorknob is a critical component of Last Resort.

BLOODWORTH: And speaking of Last Resort — I know you, Colin. I know you're not happy just building a nice spot for us to hole up in while the Skippers or the gawks or someone, anyone else actually saves the world.

CANTRELL: Then why knock her out?

BLOODWORTH: She's a second-rate anomalous goods dealer working out of a few abandoned warehouses. You can do better than that.

CANTRELL: What do you mean, 'you can do better than that?' If I'm leaving you're coming with me.

BLOODWORTH: You mean that?

CANTRELL: Of course.

[BLOODWORTH and CANTRELL advance down the hallway and approach a door.]

BLOODWORTH: It could be more.

CANTRELL: What?

BLOODWORTH: Last Resort. I've been thinking — say we figure it all out. Say we figure out a stable internal reality, arbitrary entry, everything. We could build more than a safe house. We could build a safe world.

CANTRELL: How?

BLOODWORTH: I saw your notes. You've done the math. As long as you can get them in, as long as the coherency remains high enough, there's no limit on the number of occupants.

CANTRELL: But we only have a few hundred agents — no, you're thinking bigger than that, you want to bring in more people, millions, billions—

BLOODWORTH: 7 billion souls, blissfully unaware of the horrors we've worked so hard to hide from them—

CANTRELL: They wouldn't know about the anomalous, so the world they'd construct wouldn't have any anomalies, but they'd never know the difference—

BLOODWORTH: And we could keep them all safe.

CANTRELL: But it wouldn't be real.

BLOODWORTH: Just because it's a world they made means it's not worth living in?

CANTRELL: Philosophy aside, there's no way it could work. There must be a limit, some threshold where the population is too high to maintain coherence or where the physical structure can't sustain the number of entries.

BLOODWORTH: At least think about it.

CANTRELL: Maybe an experiment or two, just to prove my point- whoa!

[A masked man emerges from around the corner. He raises his gun and shoots. The bullets are repelled by a thaumaturgical barrier generated by BLOODWORTH. CANTRELL returns fire. He misses.]

CANTRELL: Can't you turn off his brain?

BLOODWORTH: Can't you aim?

[CANTRELL discards his gun and strikes the masked man with a low-level thaumaturgical attack.]

CANTRELL: If Macy finds out about this he's going to kill us both.

BLOODWORTH: He won't. He needs your brain too much.

[BLOODWORTH ruffles CANTRELL's hair.]

CANTRELL: Hey!

BLOODWORTH: And Colin — if you wanted my jacket, you could've just asked.

[CANTRELL laughs and starts advancing along the hallway again.]

CANTRELL: Come on, let's find Giles and the rest of the team before they start mourning us.

BLOODWORTH: Mourning? Giles will be celebrating the day Colin Cantrell finally shut up.

[END LOG]

Video Log: 12/25/2015


Participants: Colin CANTRELL, Cyrus BLOODWORTH, Ryan GILES
Location: Des Moines office
Notes: Unofficial record created when Ryan Giles neglected to disable his body camera before attending the annual holiday social.

[BEGIN LOG]

[BLOODWORTH and CANTRELL approach GILES, who is standing near the punch bowl.]

BLOODWORTH: Giles, do you have a minute?

GILES: Sure.

CANTRELL: Whoa, what happened to you?

[BLOODWORTH sighs. GILES laughs.]

BLOODWORTH: Colin.

GILES: Hey, I'd want to know too. We were busting that ring out in Cedar Rapids and had a bit of a run-in with a werewolf. Want to see?

[GILES retrieves a printed photograph from his pocket.]

BLOODWORTH: Colin, is that Jeremy?

CANTRELL: No way, from applied thaumaturgy?

GILES: You went to school with a werewolf?

CANTRELL: He's only half.

GILES: Anyway, he got a nasty hit in on the way out. They think it'll scar, but if it ends up looking half as cool as yours, Bloodworth, I won't mind.

[CANTRELL stiffens.]

GILES: Sorry. I didn't…

BLOODWORTH: It's fine.

GILES: So, uh, what did you want to ask me about?

CANTRELL: I've been working on this theory about Last Resort — you remember Last Resort, right? This whole time we've been running with the idea that it's harder to construct the internal reality the more people there are. I have a theory that it's like averages — the more people you have, the less outliers matter — that is, it's actually easier with more people. We want to test this but there's only two of us so we need to bring in a few more agents from the area so I asked Macy for twelve agents which I did think was a bit ambitious since we probably can't even afford the gas to drive out the team in Wisconsin and—

[BLOODWORTH squeezes CANTRELL's shoulder.]

BLOODWORTH: Colin, breathe.

CANTRELL: And he told us we could use anyone we could get to agree. It's safe! I mean, it didn't completely work the first time, but it's safe. Promise.

GILES: You want me to be one of your guinea pigs?

BLOODWORTH: I wouldn't phrase it like that.

[GILES sighs.]

GILES: I want something in return. Hey, do you think you could teach me, like, a little spell? It doesn't have to be anything big, just something I can whip out at parties, you know?

BLOODWORTH: Macy won't like that.

GILES: Come on, I won't tell.

[CANTRELL looks around the area before giving BLOODWORTH a thumbs-up.]

BLOODWORTH: Okay, maybe a little one. But if Macy finds out, I'll make you regret it.

GILES: Deal.

[END LOG]

- Close

Video Log: 08/29/2016

Participants: Darren MACY, Colin CANTRELL, Cyrus BLOODWORTH
Location: Medical wing of the Des Moines office
Notes: Recorded shortly after Cyrus Bloodworth was injured during an experiment for PROJECT LAST RESORT.

[BEGIN LOG]

[BLOODWORTH is lying on a hospital bed in a private room. MACY and CANTRELL enter.]

MACY: Cantrell, I'm serious. You're not leaving until you talk to him.

[MACY leaves, closing the door behind him. CANTRELL tries the doorknob. It does not move.]

BLOODWORTH: I've been here for three days.

[CANTRELL does not reply.]

BLOODWORTH: You know, despite everything, you were my…

[BLOODWORTH sighs.]

BLOODWORTH: You mean something to me, Colin. Was it too much to hope you would visit me without Macy holding you at gunpoint?

[CANTRELL slowly approaches the hospital bed. He sits down in the provided chair.]

CANTRELL: Does it hurt?

BLOODWORTH: Not much. They have me on the good stuff.

[Silence elapses.]

BLOODWORTH: Colin, this wasn't your fault. The knife was my idea. We couldn't have known.

CANTRELL: No, it was. We built Last Resort — we set the rules. I shouldn't have agreed to this. I should've picked something else.

BLOODWORTH: Do you remember Deer?

CANTRELL: Of course I remember, Cyrus. I can't look at you and not remember.

BLOODWORTH: Is that why you won't look at me now?

[CANTRELL does not reply.]

BLOODWORTH: I forgive you, Colin.

CANTRELL: Stop.

BLOODWORTH: No, we need to talk about this. I put my heart and soul into that project and you blew it up. When I woke up and they told me you were already gone, I didn't know if I ever wanted to see you again. And then — call it fate, a stroke of luck, the statistical consequence of staying in this field — we ended up here.

CANTRELL: I said stop.

BLOODWORTH: And I got to tell you I forgave you, and you got to tell me you were sorry. Then we moved on, Colin, we were happy. So I'm telling you now like I told you then: I forgive you.

[CANTRELL covers his face with both hands.]

BLOODWORTH: Colin?

[CANTRELL removes a document from his jacket and sets it on BLOODWORTH's chest.]

BLOODWORTH: This… you're resigning?

CANTRELL: I'm sorry.

BLOODWORTH: Why?

CANTRELL: Because I did it again. I blew up the lab.

BLOODWORTH: This is different. I read the report — you got it stable and working. Give me another week and I'll be good as new. We're getting somewhere.

CANTRELL: The guys in charge don't think so.

BLOODWORTH: You know that money is tight. We'll get the funding back.

CANTRELL: When? In three years? Six?

BLOODWORTH: Colin, please. Remember the idea?

CANTRELL: What idea?

BLOODWORTH: Our plan to use Last Resort to save the world.

CANTRELL: Cyrus, it was never going to work.

BLOODWORTH: I think you're wrong. You just showed that the internal reality is more stable with more occupants. All we need to do is figure out arbitrary entry. Together, we could replace this world with the perfect world.

CANTRELL: You're insane. It's impossible — I don't know what I was thinking when I ran that experiment. Even if the internal reality could be stabilized we would never be able to get them all inside. We need the physical structure for insulation and there's no way it would hold up under that kind of load.

BLOODWORTH: I'll make it work. We can make it work. Isn't this what you said you wanted when you agreed to all this?

CANTRELL: I remember.

BLOODWORTH: You wanted a world without anomalies.

CANTRELL: That's not what I said. I said I wanted the world to be safe.

BLOODWORTH: A safe world is a world without anomalies. Please, Colin. I don't care about the funding — I think this is our chance. Are you in?

[CANTRELL turns so that he is facing away from BLOODWORTH.]

CANTRELL: I'm sorry.

BLOODWORTH: So, is this the encore? The lab blows up, I get hurt, you run away, and I never see you again?

CANTRELL: I'm sorry.

BLOODWORTH: I thought… if you wouldn't stay for me, you'd at least stay for this mission.

CANTRELL: Don't make this harder than it is.

BLOODWORTH: Please, Colin. The project needs you. I need you.

[CANTRELL attempts to leave. BLOODWORTH pulls CANTRELL by the wrist and he falls onto the hospital bed. CANTRELL is obscured for several seconds before he stands back up and moves towards the door.]

CANTRELL: I'm sorry. Goodbye, Cyrus.

[CANTRELL reaches for the doorknob again. It turns.]

CANTRELL: Prove me wrong.

[END LOG]
