Alexander: I'm not sure where you mean, Tolmony. I extended a hand to you, but now that I'm here, you're just—

[The scene changes abruptly. The hanger is now entirely empty, save for Dr. Tolmony and Alexander.]

Tolmony: If you think I'm going to just— sit there and let you lie through your fucking teeth, I—

Alexander: Tolmony, Tolmony. How determined are you to uphold these systems?

Tolmony: We both know you're being reckless with more lives than—

[Dr. Tolmony turns slightly as she's speaking and reaches toward a strap on her backpack.]

Alexander: Looking for this?

[Dr. Tolmony turns back to Alexander. He's holding a survival knife and has a slight grin.]

Alexander: Hm, do we have the same tastes in blade shape or is this not quite a coincidence, Tolmony?

Tolmony: Uh… Shit… Listen, I just—

Alexander: Hm?

[Dr. Tolmony lunges for Alexander and and attempts to pry the knife from his hand.]

[Alexander pushes Dr. Tolmony off of himself. He kicks her back to make space, though he isn't able to apply much force from their relative positions. Alexander then slashes at Dr. Tolmony as she stumbles back. Dr. Tolmony cries out in pain.]

[Dr. Tolmony holds up her hands and keeps her distance while Alexander brandishes the knife.]

Alexander: Not a fan of playing fair, are you? But you look like a scared kitten once things take a turn against you, Tolmony.

Tolmony: You know damn well this has never been a fair fight!

[Alexander steps closer.]

Alexander: Perhaps it hasn't been.

[Dr. Tolmony continues to backpedal. She backs up a bit, near the start of a window by the personnel door.]

[Alexander reaches up to his temple. Little immediately changes, but a pile of metal posts appears in a corner of the room along with some assorted spent rations and the lighting takes a slightly more orange hue.]

[Dr. Tolmony ducks pre-emptively, and in the next moment, Alexander swings the back end of the knife at where Dr. Tolmony was a moment ago.]

[Dr. Tolmony flees away from the window while Alexander steadies himself from the missed swing.]

Tolmony: Fucking bastard— Upper hand and that's how you want to make me go out!

[Dr. Tolmony moves for a corner of the room where she retrieves a metal post and brandishes it as a weapon.]

[Alexander approaches again. He grapples with the metal post while Dr. Tolmony uses it to fend him off. Dr. Tolmony strikes and prods at him quickly, and Alexander can't quite keep up with one hand occupied by the knife.]

[Dr. Tolmony catches Alexander's knife with the post, and he's forced to drop it to catch her swinging back at him again.]

Tolmony: Do you want to make that many people suffer?

[Now having Alexander disarmed, Dr. Tolmony begins to advance on her opponent. Alexander grows more confident in blocking and handling Dr. Tolmony's makeshift weapon.]

Alexander: Who's to say they will? You wouldn't be here if you were afraid to take a little leap of faith.

Tolmony: You're a fucking clown— Listen to yourself!

[Dr. Tolmony backs Alexander a short way across the room. His steps gradually near the patch of sunlight. He finally gets a good grip on Dr. Tolmony's blunt weapon, and she's only able to free it after a short back and forth over it.]

Alexander: And here you are attacking me with the first metal stick you find again. You don't learn, either, Tolmony.

Tolmony: Do I?

[Dr. Tolmony casts the post aside and rushes forward.]

[Dr. Tolmony shoves Alexander toward the patch of sunlight. He stops short of it with a pained grimace, and his back arches further with his momentum before he fully catches himself and darts away. An upright metal post is left behind him in the previously clear path he'd been shoved in. It clatters to the ground.]

Alexander: I think this has gone on enough, Tolmony. I'm sorry we couldn't find a middle ground.

Tolmony: What do you—

[Alexander hurls an empty tin can toward Dr. Tolmony. The camera's position shifts backward a short distance, and Dr. Tolmony's arms raise momentarily.]

Tolmony: A soup can? What are you— Wait— Hey!

[Alexander holds up a second pair of SCP-9669 and waves before reaching for his temple and vanishing from sight.]

Tolmony: Alexander, you fucking—

Tolmony: He just— He—

[There is silence for a moment. Dr. Tolmony backs toward a wall and slumps down.]

Tolmony: Goddamnit.

Tolmony: He fucking left me here. Just— Oh God.

[Heavy sniffles are heard that gradually turn to sobs.]

Tolmony: I knew something like this was going to happen. I'm so fucking— [Unintelligible]

[Dr. Tolmony begins to weep, though she only chokes out occasional, quieter sounds.]

Tolmony: Stop— No— Can't be heard— I'll… I'll figure—

Tolmony: I'm going to die here. Or worse.

[Dr. Tolmony sobs into her hands for nearly a half hour.]

Tolmony: Fuck.

Tolmony: What's even the point?

Tolmony: I guess I can— At least see how long I have. If nothing out there finds me.

[Dr. Tolmony removes her backpack and opens it. She sniffles, and her breathing grows more steady as she sorts through its contents.]

Tolmony: These are rations for probably, like…

Tolmony: I guess I have a month maybe, before I get to just sit here and starve myself— Starve myself and wait for something to— God fucking—

[Dr. Tolmony sighs.]

Tolmony: Okay. Just— Let's see what else we have.

Tolmony: Maybe the rations will last longer anyway. I've never been good at estimating these things.

Tolmony: The slash wound he gave me seems pretty superficial, luckily, but…

[Dr. Tolmony takes a piece of bandage from the roll in her backpack and applies it to herself.]

Tolmony: Should help, just in case.

[Dr. Tolmony breathes somewhat unsteadily for a moment.]

Tolmony: Shit, the knife, I have that.

[Dr. Tolmony moves forward and retrieves the survival knife from the floor.]

Tolmony: I don't think it's… really that much use right now anyway.

Tolmony: I guess opening the ration packs will be easier.

Tolmony: Maybe— Maybe Alexander will come back for me. If he sets off his plan and survives.

Tolmony: If I'm still alive by then. If he bothers to remember by then—

Tolmony: He wouldn't just— He wouldn't leave me here, would he?

Tolmony: I say that like he didn't try to kill me before.

[Dr. Tolmony takes a deep breath.]

Tolmony: I guess… Worst case scenario…

[Dr. Tolmony inspects the knife and turns it in her hand.]

Tolmony: There's worse ways to cut starvation short.

[Dr. Tolmony sighs.]

[EXTRANEOUS FOOTAGE REMOVED]

[Dr. Tolmony is quietly singing something to herself.]

Tolmony: …hope next time you'll stay…

Tolmony: …even just one more—

[Dr. Tolmony stifles a scream.]

Tolmony: Wait— I don't want— Please— I—

[Dr. Tolmony turns. A middle-aged man in a trench coat is knelt on one knee beside her. Subject is presumed to be PoI-0000, henceforth referred to as Nobody. Nobody wears an instance of SCP-9669. Further details of the subject's appearance are indiscernible due to the dim lighting of the room.]

Nobody: You have my apologies for my elusiveness thus far, Dr. Tolmony, and for the startle.

[Dr. Tolmony takes a moment to catch her breath.]

Tolmony: Er— Yeah, I— So you… You're that voice.

[Nobody nods.]

Nobody: You know who I am. It's not an easy prospect to show my hand, much less the rest of me.

Nobody: I've been around, though. I have my means. And I'm sure you'll trust that I have your best interests in mind.

Tolmony: Don't exactly have options outside of trusting you, but… What do you plan to do for me anyway? And… why?

Nobody: Dr. Tolmony, you're a brilliant woman. You've deduced the answer to the latter many times over.

Nobody: What Alexander is going to do is going to cause calamity even I cannot predict.

Nobody: But I'm not in a position to handle these things myself. I hope you'll understand.

Tolmony: Not— Not really. As in, like, why you can't, but uhm— I'd like to help. Uh, obviously.

Nobody: You can rack your brains to put my situation in an itemized list another time. Right now, just know I can't push anything far myself.

Nobody: But I can do something small and simple. Something like hand over these.

[Nobody removes his instance of SCP-9669 and holds it out to Dr. Tolmony.]

[Dr. Tolmony reaches out slowly to take them. She holds them and inspects them carefully.]

Tolmony: Do you just— Have some other mysterious way out?

Nobody: You and I both wish.

Tolmony: Then why— Why give these to me? Alexander's just— kicked my ass and slipped away every time I've tried to confront him. Am I really your best bet? That you'd leave yourself here of all places for that?

Nobody: Don't make it sound so bleak.

Tolmony: It feels it.

Nobody: This isn't self-sacrifice, Dr. Tolmony. I have faith you won't leave me here.

Tolmony: I mean— Obviously I wouldn't, but I need to stop him first.

Nobody: Then do it.

Tolmony: Yeah, that's gone so well for me so far…

Nobody: Dr. Tolmony, tell me what Alexander's end goal is.

Tolmony: He's going to that temple. Grabbing that tablet. And… I don't know how he plans to do it, but he wants to write something on it for himself.

Nobody: There you have it, don't you? Get there first.

Nobody: Stop playing fair, Doctor. He isn't, either.

[A moment passes in silence.]

Tolmony: You're sure you'll be alright here?

Nobody: Long as these rations last me. Keep the knife, though, and the bandages.

Nobody: Nothing out there will know I'm here. I can promise you that.

Tolmony: Okay. I'll— I'll come back.

Nobody: I know you will.

[Dr. Tolmony equips the instance of SCP-9669. She reaches one hand to her temple, and the scene abruptly changes.]

[The camera's view is of the inside of a near identical hangar, though it is in less of a state of disrepair. It still appears abandoned.]

[Dr. Tolmony stands and dusts herself off. She holds a survival knife in one hand.]

Tolmony: Okay… Okay.

Tolmony: Guess this is it, then.

[Dr. Tolmony suddenly looks down toward where the camera is pinned to her chest.]

Tolmony: I left this stupid thing on again, didn't I?

Tolmony: Well, I'll have a hell of a story to tell. Guess it doesn't hurt to save the moment.

[Dr. Tolmony walks to the window and looks outside. The tarmac is empty. Weeds grow through cracks in the asphault. The fence around the premeter only has a few portions still standing.]

Tolmony: But I guess this isn't the most interesting part to record.

[END LOG]


Mission Report Recovered from PR-D2

Operation: N/A
Date: 9/19/2025

Col. Abraham, reporting on an upcoming operation. And the state of things, I guess. To hell with it.

This Alexander fellow's gotten the Administrator's approval for something. Wants to go to Brazil somewhere. Says some deity there's going to become a really big problem if we don't go stuff it now.

Hell if I know how he's suppose to know that or why she believes him, but the Administrator's word still goes at the end of the day. And we all still like him anyhow, even if we've all started to notice holes in his stories.

Administrator probably knows the whole story. I'd hope so. She seems to trust him.

Guess we're really putting the command structure back in place. Maybe that should give me some hope.

Well, either way, we're off tomorrow. Gonna be a hell of a trip. Few enough of us here, we're all making a convoy to make a site near the location of interest our temporary base of operations. Can't spread ourselves any thinner.

Everyone seems in good spirits. I guess you get stuck hunkering down here so long, you're always going to look forward to a change of scenery. Especially now that we have the means to go out again and defend ourselves, to some extent.

This decrepit hangar's not much of a Site-01 anyway. I think the designation was supposed to make us feel more secure here. Nobody really bought it. Some nowhere hellhole how far out from the crater that used to be Dallas.

The only reason we survived this long is nothing almighty enough bothered to check.

Never thought this war would go on this long, but it never really was one, was it? I guess I just thought the apocalypse would've choosen its flavor by now.

Either we're luckier bastards than we thought or someone out there's keeping it waiting.

I'll leave this here. I'm not writing anything useful at this point. Marshal's nagging me to go help pack anyway.

Col. Abraham signing off.

Mission Report Recovered from PR-D2

Operation: Fuck
Date: Does it fucking matter?

It's Marshal. Abraham's dead. They're all fucking dead. That fucking bastard.

Few days ago we rode out to that fucking middle of nowhere temple to poke a hornet's nest because that snake told us to. He walks in alone. Takes that giant gun thing with him. We think he's just gotten a big head, but we figure it's a big head he's earned and let him go. Not like we're much use anyway.

Some fucking ancient god of who gives a fuck follows him back out. Walks right through all the fences and shit set up by whatever Foundation outpost however many years ago. And there's that piece of shit beneath him strolling out without a care.

That thing tore us apart. I think I'm the only one left. Guess it thought I was dead or my injuries would do it later. It just said "follow your promise" or something to him in this deep voice, and the traitor walks off and takes one of the only jeeps that wasn't trashed.

Don't know how long I waited, but I think whatever it was left or went dormant or just disappeared or I dont fucking know it was gone and I hopped in the first piece of junk I could make run and floored it.

I arrived a few minutes ago to 505, the shitty nowhere site we set up in for this whole clusterfuck. She's dead. The Administrator's fucking dead.

The ones who're left told me he walked in like nothing was wrong, asked to talk to her in private. Someone finally noticed something was up and barged in to find her on the ground and the window wide open.

Wish I'd have seen him leave. I'd have put a bullet in his head on the spot.

So if anyone's left out there to find our bodies when something or another wipes this shithole off the map, let my final tesimony be this: If you meet an Alexander Swath, put that fucker in the ground with the rest of us.

Camera Log Retrieved from Dr. Ross Tolmony (09)

Date: 10/03/2025
Start time: 07:22

⮞ Display Camera Log
⮟ Collapse Camera Log

[BEGIN LOG]

[The shape of a large, stone pyramid is visible in the middle distance. The sky is clear and blue. There are minimal signs of other people. Dr. Tolmony walks forward through thick foliage toward it.]

Tolmony: Christ. Never was an outdoorsman.

Tolmony: Okay. Okay.

Tolmony: I'm uh, in A2 right now. For the record. Long and not terribly interesting story how I got here. Learned how to ride a horse, I guess. Lot of headache mapping shit out through public transit between like four different realities.

[Dr. Tolmony uses a survival knife to cut through foliage in her way. Doing so often takes several successive batoning motions.]

Tolmony: But here we are. Didn't get eaten by anything out here on the way. Albeit it I cut it closer than I'd like with a huge snake… It doesn't matter.

[Dr. Tolmony approaches the base of the pyramid. She begins to climb a set of stairs toward the top.]

Tolmony: With any luck, nothing too bad's here in A2. And, uh, I guess I'm just banking on the deity in D2 not being home.

Tolmony: A bit late to go back now, so that's about as much of a plan as I have.

[Dr. Tolmony sighs and grumbles as she ascends the stairs.]

Tolmony: Maybe I should be more freaked out right now, but fuck it, right?

Tolmony: If I weren't capable enough… or lucky enough… I'd already be dead a few dozen times over.

[Dr. Tolmony brandishes her knife and runs a finger along either side of its edge to clean off portions of plant matter on it.]

Tolmony: Him or me. That's just what I have to remember, isn't it?

[Dr. Tolmony falls silent. She reaches the top of the pyramid and steps into an open plaza covered by a small stone structure. All four sides of the structure are completely open except for one. An altar sits against the singular wall. It is empty.]

[The scene abruptly changes. The sky becomes darker and is blanketed with circling thunderclouds. Foundation installations in states of disrepair or outright destruction litter the area. Many gates and security features are torn open from the inside. At the base of the pyramid, an assortment of totaled military vehicles are strewn throughout the area. Several corpses in tactical gear are visible.]

Tolmony: Christ, did he do this? Or did whatever was here just go for a stroll?

Tolmony: Well, whatever it is, I don't see it anywhere.

[Dr. Tolmony moves into a shadowed corner by the lone wall near the altar. A stone tablet now sits atop it.]

[Dr. Tolmony finds a place to hide behind a stack of metal supply crates in a dark corner. Most of the crates are dented in places.]

Tolmony: This is it… Now I just… Wait.

[EXTRANEOUS FOOTAGE REMOVED]

[The distant sound of an engine becomes audible before stopping some distance away.]

[Dr. Tolmony adjusts her posture slightly and prepares her knife. Her hands shake slightly.]

[Several minutes pass in silence.]

[Footsteps become audible and grow in volume.]

[Dr. Tolmony leans around the edge of the crates. Alexander is visible approaching the altar. His expression is unreadable in the low light.]

[Alexander looks around the room for a moment. He doesn't seem to notice Dr. Tolmony. He then approaches the altar.]

Alexander: Here it is. Finally.

[Alexander places one hand on the tablet.]

Alexander: Kept its end of the bargain. I kept mine. And here we are.

[Alexander reaches into his pocket and pulls out a small, handheld device with a stylized W on the side.]

Alexander: Thing's indestructible, I hear. But not tamper proof.

[Dr. Tolmony begins to step out of her hiding place. She moves as quietly as she can manage.]

[Alexander presses the device to the surface. It makes a buzzing sound then goes quiet.]

[Dr. Tolmony creeps closer.]

[Alexander wipes away the writings on the surface of the tablet, which vanish like indents in putty under his palm.]

[Alexander moves a finger to start writing something new.]

[Dr. Tolmony lunges toward Alexander with the knife raised.]

[Alexander shouts. Dr. Tolmony tackles him to the ground and plunges the knife into his side. She pulls it back out and swings it toward his neck, but he catches her by the wrist at the last moment.]

Alexander: Who the—

[Alexander rolls to the side and uses both hands to hold back Dr. Tolmony's knife-wielding arm. His expression changes to shock then a slight smile when he recognizes Dr. Tolmony.]

[Dr. Tolmony strains against him and moves her free hand to try to unsteady his grip.]

Alexander: Tolmony. I guess— You really didn't want to take my gamble, huh?

[Dr. Tolmony only grunts in frustration.]

Alexander: You had a second pair, then? Suppose I should've checked. Was wondering where those went.

Tolmony: No, Alexander. I just had— A bit of help.

[Dr. Tolmony suddenly moves back and uses the force of Alexander trying to push her arm away to stand and wrench her wrist free.]

[Alexander takes the opportuinty to push Dr. Tolmony back further and get to his feet. His posture is slightly hunched, and he's visibly bleeding from his side.]

[Alexander holds out a hand. He curls his fingers a few times, as if expecting something to happen, then looks up. Dr. Tolmony is moving for the tablet.]

Alexander: Wait a second—

[Alexander goes after her, but Dr. Tolmony reaches it first.]

[Dr. Tolmony reaches the tablet and takes it. She turns to face Alexander while backpedaling. She stops when her back hits solid stone in the nook between the wall by the altar and a rectangular stone pillar holding up the ceiling.]

[Alexander approaches Dr. Tolmony despite a noticable limp and reaches into his pocket.]

Alexander: Tolmony. What are you planning to do with that thing? Where do you think you can take it that I won't follow? You know it's indestructible.

[Alexander pulls a pistol from his pocket.]

Alexander: You can stop here, Tolmony. Hand it over.

Alexander: We've done a lot to each other, but if you drop the chase, you can go.

[Alexander holds up his pistol and steadies his aim on Dr. Tolmony.]

Alexander: You had a good run, really. You're tenacious. But your escapade ends here, Tolmony, one way or another. Consider your options.

Tolmony: Alexander, you know what that Wondertainment gizmo you bargained for does, but do you know why it was recalled?

Alexander: What are you—

Tolmony: Multiple building collapses when it was applied to loadbearing walls.

Tolmony: In other words, the things it's applied to— They become pretty fragile.

[Dr. Tolmony swings the tablet hard against the stone wall. It shatters to pieces.]

[Several seconds pass in silence.]

[Alexander lowers his weapon.]

[A moment passes. The wind howls.]

Alexander: Tolmony… Tolmony…

[Alexander laughs slightly.]

Alexander: Well, you got me.

[Alexander slumps to his knees and drops the pistol at his side.]

[A small pool of blood grows where Alexander kneels.]

[Dr. Tolmony relaxes her whiteknuckle grip on her knife. She lowers her weapon and moves forward.]

[Dr. Tolmony kneels beside Alexander and retrieves a roll of bandages from her pocket.]

Tolmony: Hey, here, uh.

[Alexander wordlessly removes his vest. He attempts to take off his buttonup shirt, though his movements appear weak.]

[Dr. Tolmony uses her knife to cut through the buttons and remove the shirt herself. She begins applying bandages to Alexander's wound.]

Alexander: That shirt wasn't cheap, you know.

[Alexander smiles and stifles a chuckle. Dr. Tolmony lets out a single laugh.]

[Dr. Tolmony finishes bandaging Alexander's side.]

Tolmony: You think this'll hold?

Alexander: I've lived through worse. Hurts like a bitch, though.

Tolmony: Er, yeah… Sorry about that.

Alexander: You could've done worse. I would've in your shoes.

Tolmony: Eh, I'm not sure about that. But whatever. It's— What's done is done, right?

Alexander: Not much I can do now.

[Dr. Tolmony sits beside Alexander.]

Tolmony: Yeah, uh… Guess this is it, isn't it?

Tolmony: This all went on so long, I… even at the end I wasn't sure I'd do it.

Alexander: Well, here you are.

Tolmony: Yeah. Yeah, here I am.

Tolmony: Our lives are fucked now.

Alexander: I see this as more of a neutral change, really.

Alexander: You weren't happy before anyway, were you?

Tolmony: No. No, I— I always just thought I wanted to settle down. Rest.

Tolmony: Feels like that ship has sailed. But I guess it did a long time ago.

[Alexander points at Dr. Tolmony's chest.]

Alexander: When you got that?

Tolmony: I mean, yeah, but not for the reasons you're probably thinking. I— You know how 81 is. Remote enough I could still live at home close to the site. Just had to take some precautions to protect the veil during my commute. I was never the most social anyway.

Tolmony: The weird hole in my chest happened from a lover. It, uh, wasn't from any world I know about. Pretty large, not really human, but it… cared.

Tolmony: I guess I'll spare you the details, but there was an unrelated breach, the uh, blackout incident, you probably heard of it.

Alexander: I was there for it, Tolmony. I was just in a different sector at the time.

Tolmony: Right, well… I took it home with me. Phalanx. It has a name.

Alexander: You loved this 'Phalanx' but still refer to them like an object?

Tolmony: That's just, uh, how it preferred being talked about, I guess.

Tolmony: Couldn't stay forever, though. It was just— I would've been implicated, so it…

Tolmony: Staged me aiding a patrol in recapturing it. Throw off the scent, I guess.

Tolmony: Haven't really felt… cared for much since.

Alexander: Hm. I assume you don't share that too much?

Tolmony: I'm a fan of not being executed, so, uh, yeah.

Alexander: I have my own regrets. With all of this.

Alexander: And I guess it was for nothing now.

Tolmony: What did you even… do?

Alexander: Those men down there are the same as the ones you were sitting with last time we met, Tolmony.

Alexander: This world was doomed anyway, so I…

Tolmony: Christ, man.

Alexander: The tablet doesn't lie, Doctor.

Tolmony: Well, it doesn't say anything now.

Alexander: I guess not.

Alexander: It's all I can do to make amends and move on. But I don't expect forgiveness here.

Alexander: I don't deserve it, either.

Alexander: Their Administrator was humanity's hope in this world. I put her down myself as my bargain to get that tablet.

Tolmony: Fuck. You really were hellbent on that plan.

[Alexander nods and bears a solemn expression.]

Alexander: I just wanted the still living worlds to be better ones. That's all.

Alexander: If the tablet is destroyed, and this world is still so… You know…

Alexander: Maybe I'll return when this injury's healed. I'm one guy, I can't fix this mess, but… Maybe I could get some people out of it.

Alexander: Not working with the Foundation anymore mind you, not that they would agree anyway after… Just, even under the circumstances of this world… I'd prefer to work individually.

[Alexander sighs.]

Alexander: You know what you're going to do now?

Tolmony: Well, first and foremost, I have someone to thank for my continued existence who's trapped in a hangar in D1 right now.

Alexander: Who's that?

Tolmony: Nobody.

Alexander: Hm?

Tolmony: As in, the guy named Nobody, the— You know what I mean. Don't act coy.

[Alexander nods.]

Alexander: I guess you'll want these, then?

[Alexander retrieves SCP-9669-2 from his pocket and hands it to Dr. Tolmony.]

Tolmony: Yeah. Uh, thanks.

[There's silence for a moment.]

Tolmony: I guess I have one other friend to pay a visit to as well. Not much better to do.

Tolmony: I'm going to need time to figure out where to even go after all this.

Alexander: If you'd like a hand keeping yourself somewhere safe, it's the least I can do after all I put you through.

Tolmony: Despite everything… I wouldn't mind staying in touch.

Alexander: I was half expecting someone from the Foundation to try hunting me down. Wasn't expecting that someone to be a friend by the end of things.

Tolmony: Well, take what you can get, right?

Alexander: All you can do.

[Several moments pass in silence.]

Alexander: Well, I've got enough gas to get us to the nearest town if we're lucky.

Alexander: Let's just…

Tolmony: Yeah. No use sitting here. You're gonna need stitches at the least.

Alexander: No kidding.

[Dr. Tolmony stands and offers Alexander a hand getting up.]

Tolmony: You can lean on me if you want. It's, uh, whole lot of steps to climb down.

[Dr. Tolmony coughs then looks down. She reaches to turn off the camera.]

[END LOG]


Dr. Tolmony was apprehended at a ranch in rural Oklaholma, PR-A1 on 10/08/2025 as part of a joint investigatory effort into Incident 9669-82225 by the Foundation and its counterparts in PR-A1 and PR-D3. Subject surrendered without incident and has offered testimony regarding her role in Incident 9669-82225 as well as several documents and video logs pertaining to it. Full interview and disciplinary hearing are to be conducted 10/11/2025 following comprehensive assessment.

SCP-9669-5 has been secured. Containment procedures for SCP-9669 are currently under review.

Addendum 9669.1010:

Dr. Tolmony was reported missing from her cell on the morning of 10/10/2025. The following is an excerpt of security footage from Dr. Tolmony's cell during the night prior.

Security Footage Log, Site-81 Detention Center

Date: 10/09/2025

[BEGIN LOG]

23:47 [Dr. Tolmony is seated in Cell A37.]

23:47 Unknown: Dr. Tolmony.

23:47 [Dr. Tolmony looks toward the camera's blindspot.]

23:48 Tolmony: Oh! You, uhm. Hey…

23:48 Unknown: All that, and you end up back here?

23:48 Unknown: Is this what you wanted, Doctor?

23:48 Tolmony: …I'm not sure where I am between being given an award and put back to work and being executed.

23:49 Tolmony: I think there's people higher in the chain who want to cover their tracks for enabling Alexander, though. They might uhm, one of them spoke to me about— I probably shouldn't say. You get the idea.

23:50 Unknown: And is that what you want? Will you be happy if you win that chance?

23:51 [Dr. Tolmony steps toward the camera's blindspot. most of her body becomes obscured from view.]

23:52 [Dr. Tolmony vanishes entirely.]

[END LOG]

Expect it to take over an hour to read. ]] [[table style="border: none; width: 100%;"]] [[row]] [[cell]] [[size 125%]]**Item #:** SCP-9669[[/size]] [[/cell]] [[cell style="text-align: right;"]] [[size 125%]]###996690|**Level 3/9669**##[[/size]] [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell]] [[size 125%]]**Object Class:** Safe[[/size]] [[/cell]] [[cell style="text-align: right;"]] [[size 125%]]###996690|**Classified**##[[/size]] [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] ---- [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] **Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9669-2 through -5 are kept in a standard secure storage locker in Room 08 of Site-81's Transplanar Research Sector. Routine usage of SCP-9669 for diplomatic and research purposes is to be carried out under supervision of the current acting lead of Site-81's Transplanar Research Sector. Foundation communications monitoring teams are to consider potential leads to the whereabouts of SCP-9669-6 a high priority. **Update 8/25/2025:** Remaining instances of SCP-9669 have been confiscated following Incident 9669-82225. Standard diplomatic and research activities are on hold. Access is restricted without direct appointment by the Incident 9669-82225 Investigatory Committee. [[include component:image-block |name=9kcon-Glasses-Edit.png |caption=SCP-9669-2 |width=40% |align=right]] **Description:** SCP-9669 denotes 6 identical pairs of cosmetic novelty glasses, designated SCP-9669-1 through -6. Instances of SCP-9669 have lenses with a variable but highly saturated tint. A small slider is present on the left temple of each instance of SCP-9669. When a subject wearing an instance of SCP-9669 adjusts the slider, the subject will exit local reality, coinciding with a shift in the hue of the lenses. This causes the subject to appear to instantaneously physically demanifest. Subjects who exit local reality via SCP-9669 appear instantaneously in another reality corresponding to the hue of the object's lenses. Manifestation exerts a retrocausal effect which leads the immediate surrounding topography of the destination to have a near identical layout to that of the subject's location in their previous reality. Relative location of the subject remains consistent between realities. If multiple subjects wearing SCP-9669 are present in the immediate vicinity of one another when a change in local reality occurs, all subjects are transported simultaneously. A total of 6 accessible realities have been observed through SCP-9669: ||~ **Designation**||~ **Corresponding Hue**||~ **Description**|| ||[[[competitive-eschatology-hub|PR-D2]]]||Red||Numerous anomalous entities, especially those with noted religious or cultural significance, have had their anomalous capabilities drastically amplified by unknown means. Human civilization significantly disrupted.|| ||[[[daybreak|PR-D1]]]||Orange||A reality-altering event has caused direct exposure to light from PR-D1's Sun to exert a liquefying property on organic life. Affected subjects retain limited sapience and attempt to expose other subjects to sunlight. Human civilization completely defunct.|| ||[[[aces-and-eights|PR-A2]]]||Yellow||Reality is temporally displaced 158 years in the past, but notable modern day figures and entities that are involved with the anomalous or are anomalies themselves have recognizable counterparts.|| ||[[[broken-masquerade-hub|PR-A1]]]||Green||An incident resulting in the complete spatial displacement of North Korea has led to the anomalous becoming widely known to the general public. Anomalous organizations continue operation publicly.|| ||PR-Prime||Blue||Local reality.|| ||[[[end-of-death-hub|PR-D3]]]||Violet||Reality has suffered a ΩK-Class ("End-of-Death") Scenario. Living animals in PR-D3 are unable to decease by any known means.|| SCP-9669-2 through -6 were received in a plastic case following [DATA EXPUNGED] on 02/08/2025 **Recovered Materials:** Since the acquiring of SCP-9669, contact has been made with variations of the SCP Foundation in PR-A2 and PR-D3. To mutually further research and aid in positive diplomatic relations, low-security documentation has been gradually shared between all three parties. Documents received in this way have included the files of SCP-173, SCP-2991, and SCP-3425 for comparison between versions in all 3 applicable realities as well as low-clearance internal reports and memos. As of writing, 2 pieces of recovered documentation have corresponded exactly to documentation acquired from SCP-1437. These documents respectively regard SCP-173 and SCP-3425. See Document 9669-Recovery-Comparison for further details. Several additional files without known counterparts have been acquired through mutual agreement from PR-A1 and PR-D3 or manual recovery from PR-D2, PR-D1, and PR-A2. A full database of recovered and exchanged files is available upon request from the current acting supervisor of the SCP-9669 project. Notable excerpts are included below. [[div class="blockquote"]] **Document:** Excerpt from Extended Experiment Log [[[scp-3984|3984]]]-D3 **Origin:** Provided by Foundation of PR-D3 ---- [[div class="email"]]  **Experiment Log 01** **Date:** 2020-09-14 **Experimenter:** Dr. Emily Young **Subject:** D-1190 **Procedure:** D-1190 was asphyxiated by manual strangulation from D-9981. **Results:** D-1190 struggled initially but stopped resisting after several minutes of strangulation. D-9981 was told to maintain grip for a further ten minutes. D-1190 recovered shortly afterwards with no lasting damage. [[/div]] [[div class="email"]]  **Experiment Log 06** **Date:** 2020-09-26 **Experimenter:** Dr. Emily Young **Subject:** D-1377 **Procedure:** D-1377 was restrained on an operating table. Subject's heart was surgically removed. **Results:** D-1377 expressed distress throughout the procedure until incapacitation following the severing of the superior venae cavae. Subject became largely unresponsive but remained conscious. After 24 hours, D-1377's heart was implanted back into the subject's body. Subject remained in a vegetative state for over a month. Subject has displayed decreased motor functions and recurring heart palpitations and has made no further recovery since. [[/div]] [[div class="email"]]  **Experiment Log 16** **Date:** 2023-12-07 **Experimenter:** Dr. Emily Young **Subject:** D-8028 **Foreword:** Through a joint effort between several thaumaturgical, psionic, and eigenweapons research departments, a tool designated Prototype-Omega-532 was developed. Its intended function is to cease and permanently prevent neurological activity in any entity it is fired upon. It is designed to counteract or circumvent over 3000 known forms of anomalous protections. **Procedure:** Prototype-Omega-532 was fired upon D-8028. The projection of effect passed directly through D-8028's cranium. **Results:** Prototype-Omega-532 was found to have no effect. **Notes:** Object has been placed into long-term low-risk anomalous storage. Project has been deemed a failure. [[/div]] [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Document:** LoI-9831-D2 **Origin:** Unknown Foundation installation approximately 60 miles south of Bauru, Brazil, PR-D2 ---- **Designation:** Location of Interest - 9831 **Description:** Location is a large stone pyramid located near Bauru, Brazil. LoI-9831 was not documented prior to 1997, when it received an abrupt influx of attention. LoI-9831 is constructed from cut limestone and displays great but indeterminate age. Its architecture doesn't clearly match any known indigenous culture of the region, and it bears no engravings or distinct markings on any surface, with the sole exception of LoI-9831-A. No known references to LoI-9831 exist in historical record. Further assessment pending. LoI-9831-A is a stone tablet approximately 0.75 meters in length. It is entirely indistinct save for the engraving in modern English, "Humanity's undoer will come. The key will turn." **Actions Taken:** Site-505 has been established a short distance from LoI-9831. The location's perimeter has been secured and fenced off under the guise of an archeological site. **Addendum 9831-Patmos:** [[div class="email"]] **Reported Activity:** A large, cloaked figure emerged at the top of LoI-9831. Site-505 has been evacuated. No further activity has been reported. Awaiting further instruction. [[/div]] ---- **Notes:** The described location of interest has been confirmed to exist in baseline reality. Location has been secured and tentatively designated LoI-9831. No apparent anomalous properties have been recorded. Response in case of indirect action or communication is at the discretion of the acting supervisor of the PoI-0000 Committee. **Relations:** Actions taken by PoI-0000 are wildly varying and appear personal in nature. See full documentation. [[/tab]] [[/tabview]] @@ @@ [[/div]] On 08/22/2025, SCP-9669-2 was reported missing from its secure storage locker outside of testing hours. Review of security footage suggests Dr. Tolmony retrieved the item at 21:28 the previous day, upon which she is presumed to have applied the anomaly and exited local reality. Investigation into the motivation of the theft is ongoing. Relevant documents are provided below. A full summary is currently pending a consensus statement from the Incident 9669-82225 Investigatory Committee. [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ Foundation Tip Line Submission **Date of Submission:** 7/14/2025 **Submitted by:** Dr. Ross Tolmony **Reason:** Potential theft of anomaly, Potential threat to security **Relevant Persons:** PoI-8765 **Relevant Anomalies:** SCP-9669 ---- [[div class="email"]] I have reason to suspect Alexander is plotting the theft of an anomaly. I passed him in the hall in Transplanar Research, and he dropped a sticky note from the inside of his coat. I glanced it when I picked it up to hand it back to him, and it mentioned finding out if Dr. Mesmur still worked at Site-76 in PR-D3. I thought it might've been something to do with our research that he was planning to bring up to us, but he never ended up saying anything. If it was related, it's not something I have the clearance to hear about, since we only have a couple brief mentions of her in our records. I mentioned it to my supervisor in case he was keeping personal notes containing classified data as per information protocol, but I was just brushed off. The week after, I saw him quietly exit the breakroom, but didn't see him enter when I'd been waiting outside on a coworker to get a report back to me for nearly an hour. I had a weird feeling about him, and I ended up stopping by his personal quarters after hours one night, now I'll accept reprimand for invasion of privacy, but I just felt I Okay, I don't have a good excuse for snooping, but I did find something. It was an elaborate write-up with multiple crudely drawn maps detailing some plan. As far as I could tell, everything was written in codewords, but there were clear parallels to our research, especially with several realities 9669 accesses having equivalents. Several files from the SCP-9669 project were kept with it, ranging from recovered SCP documentation to memos to a list of recalled Wondertainment products from A1. [[/div]] ---- **Notes:** Dr. Tolmony was reprimanded for inappropriate conduct following the review of this tip. On questioning, PoI-8765 explained that the so-called plan was a plot outline for a novel it had begun writing. PoI-8765 was reprimanded for multiple instances of failure to follow Foundation Information Protocol and returned to current duties following a weekend seminar to review information handling standards. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ Security Footage Log, Site-81 Transplanar Research Sector **Date:**8/22/2025 ---- [BEGIN LOG] //21:22 [Dr. Tolmony enters Corridor 73 toward Room 08.]// //21:23 [Dr. Tolmony enters Room 08 and approaches the door separating SCP-9669's secure storage locker from the rest of the room.]// //21:23 [The door opens, Dr. Tolmony enters, and the door shuts behind her.]// //21:24 [A quiet metal creak is audible, presumed to be the opening of SCP-9669's secure storage locker.]// //21:26// **Unknown:** Hesitant? To take that leap? //21:26// **Dr. Tolmony:** What? Who's there? I didn't— //21:26// **Unknown:** Hey, me too. But don't let the chance pass by you. I'll see you real soon. //21:27// **Dr. Tolmony:** Wait! Who are— were? //21:27// **Dr. Tolmony:** Fuck. Okay. //21:28// **Dr. Tolmony:** Here goes. //[No further activity is recorded.]// [END LOG] [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ Camera Log Retrieved from Dr. Ross Tolmony (01) **Date:** 8/23/2025 **Start time:** 03:17 ---- [[collapsible show="⮞ Display Camera Log" hide="⮟ Collapse Camera Log"]] [BEGIN LOG] **Tolmony:** Shit, alright, think I got this thing working. //[The camera is clipped onto Dr. Tolmony's front shirt pocket. Location identified as Dr. Tolmony's personal residence.]// **Tolmony:** Guess it's time to carry on the age old Foundation tradition of recording myself getting killed by my own stupidity. Christ, I shouldn't have— **Tolmony:** They always tell you the ones who follow protocol are the ones who have long careers. I've just made myself one of the ones who ends up on the wrong end of an incident report instead. **Tolmony:** Who am I even planning to show this to? Not like I can go back. Guess I've thrown my life away for some whim before. //[SCP-9669-2 is lifted past the view of the camera.]// **Tolmony:** Let's see if we can make it 2 for 2 on working out for me anyway. //[View abruptly changes to the interior of a wooden structure with identical dimensions to Dr. Tolmony's bedroom. The floor is soft earth.]// **Tolmony:** Fuck! That feels so weird. Okay. Okay. **Tolmony:** So now I can... Try to decipher what I wrote down from Alexander's plans, and... Stop him, I guess? How do I plan to...? **Tolmony:** This was fucking stupid. //[Several minutes pass in silence.]// **Tolmony:** I'm stuck at like 3 a.m. in some stranger's wood shed or something in another goddamn dimension... And frankly I need to fucking sleep. **Tolmony:** Don't see any point in walking around out there in the dark anyway. Better odds here than at my home back in Prime. It'll probably be crawling with agents in... Fuck. //[Some rustling is heard. The camera's position moves uneasily as Tolmony attempts to make herself comfortable.]// **Tolmony:** I guess this'll work. //[The view remains stationary for several hours.]// //[Motion is heard outside.]// **Tolmony:** Shit. //[A few seconds pass, then Tolmony stands.]// **Tolmony:** Alright, I... don't think that sounds too close... //[Tolmony moves to the door and opens it after several seconds.]// //[The door opens to a side yard. The structure is located between a house and a small barn. Several men walk down a dirt road several meters away. Only a few other homes are visible in the vicinity. Architecture of visible buildings is consistent with 1860's America, and most smaller surrounding structures appear to have been made unprofessionally.]// **Tolmony:** It's... so much weirder in person. //[Tolmony approaches the road.]// //[Buildings presumed to be a church and courthouse respectively are visible in the distance. A bell tolls from the church. At least a dozen other people are walking down the road ahead of Dr. Tolmony.]// [EXTRANEOUS FOOTAGE REMOVED] //[Tolmony is between wooden stalls of a small market. The steeple of the church is visible in the background. She approaches an unidentified man with an unkempt beard wearing flannel and overalls. He's sitting on a barrel in front of a stall.]// **Tolmony:** Uhm, excuse me, sir... **Unknown:** Yess'm? **Unknown:** Well, don't you look lost. Odd set of clothes you've got there. **Tolmony:** Yeah, I guess so. I'm uh, not from around here or anything. //[The man laughs for a moment.]// **Unknown:** Well, I coulda certainly told you that much. **Tolmony:** Know where I can grab a bite to eat and clear my head a little? //[The man points down the row of stalls.]// **Unknown:** You'll want to go down that way, take a left past the church. Diner down that way. Door'll be open. If Grace is workin' tonight, tell her Henry Fischer sent you. Might get a discount that way. **Tolmony:** Thanks, I uhm... I'll do that. **Unknown:** Ain't nothing. Maggie's still workin' the inn if you're stayin' in town tonight. She'll talk your head off, but she's a real nice lady. **Tolmony:** I'll keep that in mind. Have a— Have a good day, sir. //[The man chuckles slightly.]// **Unknown:** You too, little lady. Whatever you're lookin' for out here... I can't imagine what it is, but I hope you find it. **Tolmony:** Just passing through, I think. **Unknown:** Most are. //[Tolmony walks away from the man in the direction he indicated.]// [EXTRANEOUS FOOTAGE REMOVED] //[A small wooden building comes into view at the end of a dirt road. The doors are open, and several people are on a porch outside. Some sit in rocking chairs. Some lean on posts. A couple glance toward Tolmony, though they're too far away for anything to be audible from them.]// //[An audible sigh is heard from Dr. Tolmony.]// **Tolmony:** No one's going to watch this. No one's going to watch this, and I'm just going to die out here or be tracked down or— Ugh, fuck. Why did I have to— Alexander probably isn't even doing anything. Christ. **Tolmony:** I guess I'll just see where I can go from here. Maybe if I go back now and try to explain, I'll just— Maybe they at least won't kill me that way. **Tolmony:** Why am I still recording this? [END LOG] [[/collapsible]] @@ @@ [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ Camera Log Retrieved from Dr. Ross Tolmony (02) **Date:** 8/23/2025 **Start time:** 19:43 ---- [[collapsible show="⮞ Display Camera Log" hide="⮟ Collapse Camera Log"]] [BEGIN LOG] //[Tolmony is walking away from the diner alone.]// **Tolmony:** What the fuck? **Tolmony:** I mean, it was really helpful, but what the fuck? //[The bindings of Tolmony's notepad are visible at the bottom of the frame as well as a pencil moving quickly across it and pausing briefly when she speaks.]// **Tolmony:** I was just in the diner, having my meal, wondering what to even do with my life at this point, and I hear this— this voice. **Tolmony:** It tells me I just need to find my footing. That I can be independent, or something like that. **Tolmony:** I look around expecting to see some weird stranger with beard lice and a farmer's tan trying to give me advice, but I don't see anyone anywhere. No one else seems to hear it. A waitress even stopped to see if I needed anything, the way I was looking around. //[Tolmony's pencil stops moving and is lowered out of frame.]// **Tolmony:** I think I got it all down. All the important parts, at least. **Tolmony:** I guess I just needed my memory jogged a bit. The voice reminded me of that damn note I picked up when Alexander dropped it in the hall. Site-76. **Tolmony:** You're not supposed to know where these things are, but in A1 it's public knowledge. They screen a lot of the materials we get from there before handing it to us for that reason. I'm assuming most are rough equivalents since the other Site-81s definitely are. **Tolmony:** I'll be the first to admit I'm not completely sure where that falls on Alexander's plan, and I only really have notes and even rougher from memory copies of already rough outlines for where things are, but I can see if Site-76 lines up with any of the points he had marked. **Tolmony:** If it's at the start of his plan, perfect. Either way, I'll intercept him there and... I guess talk to him about it? Figure out what the hell is happening? I mean, what I gleaned sounded like he wanted to cause a world war or something, but he never seemed like a malicious guy. **Tolmony:** If he is doing something evil or dangerous or stupid or something, well, that'd make two of us for the last two, but I guess I could try to stop him... **Tolmony:** I'm going to get my ass kicked, aren't I? **Tolmony:** But at least I can do something... Or try to, I guess. [END LOG] [[/collapsible]] @@ @@ [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ Camera Log Retrieved from Dr. Ross Tolmony (03) **Date:** 8/23/2025 **Start time:** 23:35 ---- [[collapsible show="⮞ Display Camera Log" hide="⮟ Collapse Camera Log"]] [BEGIN LOG] //[Dr. Tolmony is in a small room, presumed to be at an inn in PR-A2. She is seated at a desk in front of a window. On the desk is her notepad and cellular phone. The latter is displaying a low battery warning.]// **Tolmony:** Just about have this copied... //[On Dr. Tolmony's phone is a list of Foundation sites and their locations that have been made public in PR-A1. She copies them onto her notepad with a pencil.]// **Tolmony:** Alright... Perfect. **Tolmony:** Dipped into PR-A1 to download their list of sites. Kinda weird to see it all public facing. Almost expected something nasty to show up on the screen and kill me for snooping... But here it all is. **Tolmony:** 76 lines up pretty nicely with what I think is the rough location Alexander had marked first. Guess that settles it. I'll find... some way to get there. **Tolmony:** Fucking Oklahoma. Not too far off, all things considered. //[Dr. Tolmony scoots her chair back from the desk.]// **Tolmony:** Guess I'll turn in for the night. I'll figure out what to do next in the— //[Dr. Tolmony quickly stands.]// **Tolmony:** What the fuck? //[Outside the window, a man in a brown coat holds up his hand and produces a flame spontaneously. A small crowd is gathered around him. Some appear unsettled. Other's applaud.]// **Tolmony:** Is he... They didn't have much in pyrotechnics in these times, did they? //[The flame grows and bends in unnatural ways with motions of the man's hand. This goes on for several minutes until he seems to finish the act by twirling his hand and causing the flame to soar upward in a long, twirling spiral before collapsing toward his hand and vanishing.]// //[The scene outside darkens. Faint lantern light is all that remains. The applause becomes practically a roar.]// **Magician:** Thank you! Thank you! It's been wonderful to perform for you ladies and gentlemen tonight. **Magician:** I'll be in town the week if any of you fine fellows want a chat. **Magician:** You can find me at the Allens'. They've generously allowed me to stay with them for the while. **Audience Member:** Bet it saves them some firewood! Hoo-wee, my folks been going through it like nothing else. Darn cold front. //[The magician smiles.]// **Magician:** My talents are practical as they are a spectacle! //[Dr. Tolmony sits back down, obscuring the scene outside the window from view.]// **Tolmony:** Damn. They just... //[One hand reaches up beside the camera, presumably to the anomalous hole in Dr. Tolmony's chest.]// **Tolmony:** I was so worried about... everything, I didn't even think about how everyone just accepted... this. **Tolmony:** I almost forgot it was there. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ Camera Log Retrieved from Dr. Ross Tolmony (04) **Date:** 8/30/2025 **Start time:** 09:07 ---- [[collapsible show="⮞ Display Camera Log" hide="⮟ Collapse Camera Log"]] [BEGIN LOG] //[Tolmony is seated in an empty subway carriage. Discarded takeout boxes and soda cans dot the floor.]// **Tolmony:** Okay, uh, nothing better to do, I guess? No one to overhear me right now. I may as well record things. If nothing else, I can look back on it. Not that I don't have a notebook. **Tolmony:** Took a minute to find anything to even charge this little camera with. Wasn't exactly a priority. **Tolmony:** I'm in A1 now. Nice being able to walk around without having to cover my chest. Stupid hole showing through clothes and all... I wish I could go back to taking it for granted. **Tolmony:** But anyway, I think I should be getting closer to Site-76 now. Infrastructure looks better here than it does in Prime. I passed a construction site, and it looked like they were levitating I-beams into place, so I guess that'd be why. Probably couldn't take a subway out of Phoenix where I'm from. **Tolmony:** Tulsa was not where Site-76 is located. Apparently the list I copied from was outdated. Someone finally noticed something was up and barged in to find her on the ground and the window wide open. Wish I'd have seen him leave. I'd have put a bullet in his head on the spot. So if anyone's left out there to find our bodies when something or another wipes this shithole off the map, let my final tesimony be this: If you meet an Alexander Swath, put that fucker in the ground with the rest of us. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ Camera Log Retrieved from Dr. Ross Tolmony (09) **Date:** 10/03/2025 **Start time:** 07:22 ---- [[collapsible show="⮞ Display Camera Log" hide="⮟ Collapse Camera Log"]] [BEGIN LOG] //[The shape of a large, stone pyramid is visible in the middle distance. The sky is clear and blue. There are minimal signs of other people. Dr. Tolmony walks forward through thick foliage toward it.]// **Tolmony:** Christ. Never was an outdoorsman. **Tolmony:** Okay. Okay. **Tolmony:** I'm uh, in A2 right now. For the record. Long and not terribly interesting story how I got here. Learned how to ride a horse, I guess. Lot of headache mapping shit out through public transit between like four different realities. //[Dr. Tolmony uses a survival knife to cut through foliage in her way. Doing so often takes several successive batoning motions.]// **Tolmony:** But here we are. Didn't get eaten by anything out here on the way. Albeit it I cut it closer than I'd like with a huge snake... It doesn't matter. //[Dr. Tolmony approaches the base of the pyramid. She begins to climb a set of stairs toward the top.]// **Tolmony:** With any luck, nothing too bad's here in A2. And, uh, I guess I'm just banking on the deity in D2 not being home. **Tolmony:** A bit late to go back now, so that's about as much of a plan as I have. //[Dr. Tolmony sighs and grumbles as she ascends the stairs.]// **Tolmony:** Maybe I should be more freaked out right now, but fuck it, right? **Tolmony:** If I weren't capable enough... or lucky enough... I'd already be dead a few dozen times over. //[Dr. Tolmony brandishes her knife and runs a finger along either side of its edge to clean off portions of plant matter on it.]// **Tolmony:** Him or me. That's just what I have to remember, isn't it? //[Dr. Tolmony falls silent. She reaches the top of the pyramid and steps into an open plaza covered by a small stone structure. All four sides of the structure are completely open except for one. An altar sits against the singular wall. It is empty.]// //[The scene abruptly changes. The sky becomes darker and is blanketed with circling thunderclouds. Foundation installations in states of disrepair or outright destruction litter the area. Many gates and security features are torn open from the inside. At the base of the pyramid, an assortment of totaled military vehicles are strewn throughout the area. Several corpses in tactical gear are visible.]// **Tolmony:** Christ, did he do this? Or did whatever was here just go for a stroll? **Tolmony:** Well, whatever it is, I don't see it anywhere. //[Dr. Tolmony moves into a shadowed corner by the lone wall near the altar. A stone tablet now sits atop it.]// //[Dr. Tolmony finds a place to hide behind a stack of metal supply crates in a dark corner. Most of the crates are dented in places.]// **Tolmony:** This is it... Now I just... Wait. [EXTRANEOUS FOOTAGE REMOVED] //[The distant sound of an engine becomes audible before stopping some distance away.]// //[Dr. Tolmony adjusts her posture slightly and prepares her knife. Her hands shake slightly.]// //[Several minutes pass in silence.]// //[Footsteps become audible and grow in volume.]// //[Dr. Tolmony leans around the edge of the crates. Alexander is visible approaching the altar. His expression is unreadable in the low light.]// //[Alexander looks around the room for a moment. He doesn't seem to notice Dr. Tolmony. He then approaches the altar.]// **Alexander:** Here it is. Finally. //[Alexander places one hand on the tablet.]// **Alexander:** Kept its end of the bargain. I kept mine. And here we are. //[Alexander reaches into his pocket and pulls out a small, handheld device with a stylized W on the side.]// **Alexander:** Thing's indestructible, I hear. But not tamper proof. //[Dr. Tolmony begins to step out of her hiding place. She moves as quietly as she can manage.]// //[Alexander presses the device to the surface. It makes a buzzing sound then goes quiet.]// //[Dr. Tolmony creeps closer.]// //[Alexander wipes away the writings on the surface of the tablet, which vanish like indents in putty under his palm.]// //[Alexander moves a finger to start writing something new.]// //[Dr. Tolmony lunges toward Alexander with the knife raised.]// //[Alexander shouts. Dr. Tolmony tackles him to the ground and plunges the knife into his side. She pulls it back out and swings it toward his neck, but he catches her by the wrist at the last moment.]// **Alexander:** Who the— //[Alexander rolls to the side and uses both hands to hold back Dr. Tolmony's knife-wielding arm. His expression changes to shock then a slight smile when he recognizes Dr. Tolmony.]// //[Dr. Tolmony strains against him and moves her free hand to try to unsteady his grip.]// **Alexander:** Tolmony. I guess— You really didn't want to take my gamble, huh? //[Dr. Tolmony only grunts in frustration.]// **Alexander:** You had a second pair, then? Suppose I should've checked. Was wondering where those went. **Tolmony:** No, Alexander. I just had— A bit of help. //[Dr. Tolmony suddenly moves back and uses the force of Alexander trying to push her arm away to stand and wrench her wrist free.]// //[Alexander takes the opportuinty to push Dr. Tolmony back further and get to his feet. His posture is slightly hunched, and he's visibly bleeding from his side.]// //[Alexander holds out a hand. He curls his fingers a few times, as if expecting something to happen, then looks up. Dr. Tolmony is moving for the tablet.]// **Alexander:** Wait a second— //[Alexander goes after her, but Dr. Tolmony reaches it first.]// //[Dr. Tolmony reaches the tablet and takes it. She turns to face Alexander while backpedaling. She stops when her back hits solid stone in the nook between the wall by the altar and a rectangular stone pillar holding up the ceiling.]// //[Alexander approaches Dr. Tolmony despite a noticable limp and reaches into his pocket.]// **Alexander:** Tolmony. What are you planning to do with that thing? Where do you think you can take it that I won't follow? You know it's indestructible. //[Alexander pulls a pistol from his pocket.]// **Alexander:** You can stop here, Tolmony. Hand it over. **Alexander:** We've done a lot to each other, but if you drop the chase, you can go. //[Alexander holds up his pistol and steadies his aim on Dr. Tolmony.]// **Alexander:** You had a good run, really. You're tenacious. But your escapade ends here, Tolmony, one way or another. Consider your options. **Tolmony:** Alexander, you know what that Wondertainment gizmo you bargained for does, but do you know why it was recalled? **Alexander:** What are you— **Tolmony:** Multiple building collapses when it was applied to loadbearing walls. **Tolmony:** In other words, the things it's applied to— They become pretty fragile. //[Dr. Tolmony swings the tablet hard against the stone wall. It shatters to pieces.]// //[Several seconds pass in silence.]// //[Alexander lowers his weapon.]// //[A moment passes. The wind howls.]// **Alexander:** Tolmony... Tolmony... //[Alexander laughs slightly.]// **Alexander:** Well, you got me. //[Alexander slumps to his knees and drops the pistol at his side.]// //[A small pool of blood grows where Alexander kneels.]// //[Dr. Tolmony relaxes her whiteknuckle grip on her knife. She lowers her weapon and moves forward.]// //[Dr. Tolmony kneels beside Alexander and retrieves a roll of bandages from her pocket.]// **Tolmony:** Hey, here, uh. //[Alexander wordlessly removes his vest. He attempts to take off his buttonup shirt, though his movements appear weak.]// //[Dr. Tolmony uses her knife to cut through the buttons and remove the shirt herself. She begins applying bandages to Alexander's wound.]// **Alexander:** That shirt wasn't cheap, you know. //[Alexander smiles and stifles a chuckle. Dr. Tolmony lets out a single laugh.]// //[Dr. Tolmony finishes bandaging Alexander's side.]// **Tolmony:** You think this'll hold? **Alexander:** I've lived through worse. Hurts like a bitch, though. **Tolmony:** Er, yeah... Sorry about that. **Alexander:** You could've done worse. I would've in your shoes. **Tolmony:** Eh, I'm not sure about that. But whatever. It's— What's done is done, right? **Alexander:** Not much I can do now. //[Dr. Tolmony sits beside Alexander.]// **Tolmony:** Yeah, uh... Guess this is it, isn't it? **Tolmony:** This all went on so long, I... even at the end I wasn't sure I'd do it. **Alexander:** Well, here you are. **Tolmony:** Yeah. Yeah, here I am. **Tolmony:** Our lives are fucked now. **Alexander:** I see this as more of a neutral change, really. **Alexander:** You weren't happy before anyway, were you? **Tolmony:** No. No, I— I always just thought I wanted to settle down. Rest. **Tolmony:** Feels like that ship has sailed. But I guess it did a long time ago. //[Alexander points at Dr. Tolmony's chest.]// **Alexander:** When you got that? **Tolmony:** I mean, yeah, but not for the reasons you're probably thinking. I— You know how 81 is. Remote enough I could still live at home close to the site. Just had to take some precautions to protect the veil during my commute. I was never the most social anyway. **Tolmony:** The weird hole in my chest happened from a lover. It, uh, wasn't from any world I know about. Pretty large, not really human, but it... cared. **Tolmony:** I guess I'll spare you the details, but there was an unrelated breach, the uh, blackout incident, you probably heard of it. **Alexander:** I was there for it, Tolmony. I was just in a different sector at the time. **Tolmony:** Right, well... I took it home with me. Phalanx. It has a name. **Alexander:** You loved this 'Phalanx' but still refer to them like an object? **Tolmony:** That's just, uh, how it preferred being talked about, I guess. **Tolmony:** Couldn't stay forever, though. It was just— I would've been implicated, so it... **Tolmony:** Staged me aiding a patrol in recapturing it. Throw off the scent, I guess. **Tolmony:** Haven't really felt... cared for much since. **Alexander:** Hm. I assume you don't share that too much? **Tolmony:** I'm a fan of not being executed, so, uh, yeah. **Alexander:** I have my own regrets. With all of this. **Alexander:** And I guess it was for nothing now. **Tolmony:** What did you even... do? **Alexander:** Those men down there are the same as the ones you were sitting with last time we met, Tolmony. **Alexander:** This world was doomed anyway, so I... **Tolmony:** Christ, man. **Alexander:** The tablet doesn't lie, Doctor. **Tolmony:** Well, it doesn't say anything now. **Alexander:** I guess not. **Alexander:** It's all I can do to make amends and move on. But I don't expect forgiveness here. **Alexander:** I don't deserve it, either. **Alexander:** Their Administrator was humanity's hope in this world. I put her down myself as my bargain to get that tablet. **Tolmony:** Fuck. You really were hellbent on that plan. //[Alexander nods and bears a solemn expression.]// **Alexander:** I just wanted the still living worlds to be better ones. That's all. **Alexander:** If the tablet is destroyed, and this world is still so... You know... **Alexander:** Maybe I'll return when this injury's healed. I'm one guy, I can't fix this mess, but... Maybe I could get some people out of it. **Alexander:** Not working with the Foundation anymore mind you, not that they would agree anyway after... Just, even under the circumstances of this world... I'd prefer to work individually. //[Alexander sighs.]// **Alexander:** You know what you're going to do now? **Tolmony:** Well, first and foremost, I have someone to thank for my continued existence who's trapped in a hangar in D1 right now. **Alexander:** Who's that? **Tolmony:** Nobody. **Alexander:** Hm? **Tolmony:** As in, the guy named Nobody, the— You know what I mean. Don't act coy. //[Alexander nods.]// **Alexander:** I guess you'll want these, then? //[Alexander retrieves SCP-9669-2 from his pocket and hands it to Dr. Tolmony.]// **Tolmony:** Yeah. Uh, thanks. //[There's silence for a moment.]// **Tolmony:** I guess I have one other friend to pay a visit to as well. Not much better to do. **Tolmony:** I'm going to need time to figure out where to even go after all this. **Alexander:** If you'd like a hand keeping yourself somewhere safe, it's the least I can do after all I put you through. **Tolmony:** Despite everything... I wouldn't mind staying in touch. **Alexander:** I was half expecting someone from the Foundation to try hunting me down. Wasn't expecting that someone to be a friend by the end of things. **Tolmony:** Well, take what you can get, right? **Alexander:** All you can do. //[Several moments pass in silence.]// **Alexander:** Well, I've got enough gas to get us to the nearest town if we're lucky. **Alexander:** Let's just... **Tolmony:** Yeah. No use sitting here. You're gonna need stitches at the least. **Alexander:** No kidding. //[Dr. Tolmony stands and offers Alexander a hand getting up.]// **Tolmony:** You can lean on me if you want. It's, uh, whole lot of steps to climb down. //[Dr. Tolmony coughs then looks down. She reaches to turn off the camera.]// [END LOG] [[/collapsible]] @@ @@ [[/div]] Dr. Tolmony was apprehended at a ranch in rural Oklaholma, PR-A1 on 10/08/2025 as part of a joint investigatory effort into Incident 9669-82225 by the Foundation and its counterparts in PR-A1 and PR-D3. Subject surrendered without incident and has offered testimony regarding her role in Incident 9669-82225 as well as several documents and video logs pertaining to it. Full interview and disciplinary hearing are to be conducted 10/11/2025 following comprehensive assessment. SCP-9669-5 has been secured. Containment procedures for SCP-9669 are currently under review. **Addendum 9669.1010:** Dr. Tolmony was reported missing from her cell on the morning of 10/10/2025. The following is an excerpt of security footage from Dr. Tolmony's cell during the night prior. [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ Security Footage Log, Site-81 Detention Center **Date:** 10/09/2025 ---- [BEGIN LOG] 23:47 //[Dr. Tolmony is seated in Cell A37.]// 23:47 **Unknown:** Dr. Tolmony. 23:47 //[Dr. Tolmony looks toward the camera's blindspot.]// 23:48 **Tolmony:** Oh! You, uhm. Hey... 23:48 **Unknown:** All that, and you end up back here? 23:48 **Unknown:** Is this what you wanted, Doctor? 23:48 **Tolmony:** ...I'm not sure where I am between being given an award and put back to work and being executed. 23:49 **Tolmony:** I think there's people higher in the chain who want to cover their tracks for enabling Alexander, though. They might uhm, one of them spoke to me about— I probably shouldn't say. You get the idea. 23:50 **Unknown:** And is that what you want? Will you be happy if you win that chance? 23:51 //[Dr. Tolmony steps toward the camera's blindspot. most of her body becomes obscured from view.]// 23:52 //[Dr. Tolmony vanishes entirely.]// [END LOG] [[/div]] [[div class="footer-wikiwalk-nav"]] [[=]] << [[[SCP-9668]]] | SCP-9669 | [[[SCP-9670]]] >> [[/=]] [[/div]]

An SCP-9676 instance orbiting Jupiter.

Special Containment Procedures: Foundation agents embedded in major space agencies are to ensure no information about the nature of SCP-9676 bodies is disseminated to the public.

Agents in relevant businesses are to monitor the capabilities of astronomical observation equipment planned to be available to the public, and ensure no device capable of detecting SCP-9676 instances' composition reaches market. All reports of asteroids with unusually green hues or low densities are to be suppressed.

Description: SCP-9676 is a form of exotic life, currently the only known organism to be naturally capable of growing and reproducing in a vacuum.

SCP-9676 instances are spherical, dark-green clumps of vegetative matter, varying widely in size: most instances are likely too small to be detectable with current observational equipment. However, the largest instance currently known has an estimated diameter of 18 kilometers. They derive energy from photosynthesizing sunlight, and gain biomass by extracting nutrients from dust and asteroids via an as-of-yet unknown process. Almost all SCP-9676 instances detected have been found in the Asteroid Belt, but a small number of individuals have been found as far from the sun as in the rings of Saturn.

Research into the biology, ecology, and potential dangers or uses of SCP-9676 is ongoing. Foundation liaisons within the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) have arranged for the Hayabusa2 craft to visit an SCP-9676 instance, designated SCP-9676-1-162173, and return a sample of it to Earth for analysis by a joint team of Foundation and JAXA scientists.

Update 06-12-2020:

Foundation-JAXA Joint Team Briefing Transcript
Persons Present: Dr. Archer Steward, Dr. Bridget Alex, Sgt. Aidan Lee, Dr. Miyo Hara

[BEGIN LOG]

Dr. Steward: Good morning, Dr. Hara. Please take a seat. As you are aware, you have been selected to work with our team to analyze the samples delivered by Hayabusa2 yesterday, as well as conduct follow-up research as needed. As you are no doubt also aware, this is highly classified. No information about any of this can be shared with anyone.

Dr. Hara: I'm honored to work with you on such a momentous discovery, but I'm afraid I still don't quite understand what requires your involvement here. Could we begin with that?

Dr. Steward: Ah, of course. You are familiar with our organization and its mission, yes?

Dr. Hara: I've read the brochure you gave me.

Dr. Steward: Good. While these organisms may currently appear harmless, they display multiple likely-anomalous properties. This is the first life we've seen in a vacuum, and until we understand how it works, we cannot risk exposing it to the public. Even if it is harmless, it is our organization's belief that publicly revealing the existence of any extraterrestrial life would cause more harm than good.

Dr. Hara: Any extraterrestrial life? How many-

Dr. Steward: I'm afraid that's classified.

Dr. Hara: Of course.

Dr. Steward: Anyway, introductions. I am Dr. Archer Steward, Foundation astrophysicist and leader of this team. This is Dr. Bridget Alex, Foundation xenobiologist.

Dr. Alex: Hello.

Dr. Hara: Dr. Miyo Hara, JAXA engineer.

Dr. Steward: Perfect. Sign here, please, and then shall we get started?

[END LOG]

SCP-9676 Initial Findings
The genome of SCP-9676 strongly suggests it belongs to phylum Chlorophyta. The outer cell walls are extremely tough, containing high concentrations of carbonate and silicate minerals. Long filaments extend from the surface. These filaments appear to be responsible for the digestion of rock and ice, but the chemical process responsible is likely anomalous. All attempts to observe or replicate it have failed. The chloroplasts are clearly modified as well. Investigation into the photosynthetic mechanism is ongoing.
Dr. Bridget Alex
Foundation Xenobiologist
Secure, Contain, Protect
From:
To:
CC:
Subject:
AStew@scp.int
BAlex@scp.int, MHara@temp.scp.int
none
Re:SCP-9676 Initial Findings

Huh, it's actually space algae. Assuming this isn't an ectoentropic process, our space algae would need to eat a variety of asteroids. Carbonate and silicate compounds are easy to find in asteroids, but they also need a fair amount of water. There are icy and hydrated asteroids in the Belt, but not enough to support such a large population of space algae, assuming they're just bouncing around out there.

P.S. We need a better name than the SCP number or "space algae". I get the feeling we will become quite closely acquainted with these by the time we're done.
Dr. Archer Steward
Foundation Astrophysicist
Secure, Contain, Protect
From:
To:
CC:
Subject:
MHara@temp.scp.int
AStew@scp.int, BAlex@scp.int
none
Re:Re:SCP-9676 Initial Findings

I suspect they have some kind of propulsion. If they were able to target and move towards water-containing bodies, these organisms could sustain themselves in an environment with a much lower concentration of them. This would also require some method of detecting water, but simple light or chemical sensors could lead one to water at long ranges.

As for your question, they are essentially just very large and tough marimo, are they not?
Dr. Miyo Hara
Guest
Secure, Contain, Protect

An SCP-9676 instance orbiting Jupiter.

Special Containment Procedures: Foundation agents embedded in major space agencies are to ensure no information about the nature of SCP-9676 bodies or existence of SCP-9676-2 is disseminated to the public.

Agents in relevant businesses are to monitor the capabilities of astronomical observation equipment planned to be available to the public, and ensure no device capable of detecting SCP-9676 instances' composition reaches market. All reports of asteroids with unusually green hues or low densities are to be suppressed.

All reports of a "Planet Nine" becoming detectable by advanced telescopes are to be suppressed and their originators amnesticized.

Description: SCP-9676 is a form of exotic life, currently the only known organism to be naturally capable of growing and reproducing in a vacuum.

SCP-9676 instances are spherical, dark-green clumps of vegetative matter, varying widely in size: most instances are likely too small to be detectable with current observational equipment. However, the largest instance currently known, designated SCP-9676-2, has an estimated diameter of 32,000 kilometers. They derive energy from photosynthesizing sunlight, and gain biomass by extracting nutrients from dust and asteroids via an as-of-yet unknown process. Almost all SCP-9676 instances detected have been found in the Asteroid Belt, but a small number of individuals are far enough from the sun to qualify as extreme trans-Neptunian objects

SCP-9676-2 is an exceptionally large instance of SCP-9676, currently the largest known single organism in existence. It is believed to be the object responsible for the theory that a distant ninth planet exists in the Solar System. It is currently located 221 AU away from the Sun. SCP-9676-2 is in the process of moving closer to the Sun at high velocity (estimates suggest its current speed is in excess of 200 kilometers per second, and increasing). This runs contrary to mathematical predictions of its orbit and is currently unexplained.

Research into methods of hiding or preventing SCP-9676-2's approach to the rest of the Solar System is ongoing.

Update 22-04-2021:

From:
To:

BAlex@scp.int, MHara@temp.scp.int

URGENT: SCP-9676-2

So, Planet Nine is real and it's a humongous marimo. What exactly do we do here? We can't stop it, because it's bigger than the Earth. We can't hide it, because it's bigger than the Earth. It also appears to be actively propelling itself towards us, so even if we did stop or hide it, we have no way of knowing what it would do after. And I don't think I need to explain why killing something that is, as I have said, bigger than the Earth, is not a feasible option. The good news is, we have about two decades before it becomes widely observable, assuming no major breakthroughs in commercially-available telescope technology. Any ideas, anyone?

P.S. Our collaboration has been extended, pending your signature, Dr. Hara. We have much to do now.
Dr. Archer Steward
Foundation Astrophysicist
Secure, Contain, Protect
From:
To:
CC:
Subject:
BAlex@scp.int
AStew@scp.int, MHara@temp.scp.int
none
Re:URGENT: SCP-9676-2
I do not as of yet have a solution for SCP-9676-2's approach, but I believe I have uncovered a key component of SCP-9676 biology. Our samples contain microscopic pockets filled with a mix of hydrogen and methane gases at fairly high pressures, which become more abundant in the deeper layers. I suspect that sufficiently-large instances have a hollow bladder in their center, filled with high-pressure gas. This would serve two purposes: it would allow instances to propel themselves by venting it in a controlled manner, and it would allow them to grow much larger than expected, as their gravity would be balanced out by the internal pressure of their bladders. This explains both the massive size and high speed of SCP-9676-2.
Dr. Bridget Alex
Foundation Xenobiologist
Secure, Contain, Protect
From:
To:
CC:
Subject:
MHara@temp.scp.int
AStew@scp.int, BAlex@scp.int
none
Re:Re:URGENT: SCP-9676-2

If your gas-bladder hypothesis is true, I believe I have a solution to SCP-9676-2. It is, in essence, an impossibly-large balloon. All we need to do is puncture a sufficiently-large hole in it. Depending on the exact pressure of the gas and physical properties of the outer shell, it's possible that it would deflate or even pop entirely.

Of course, the challenging part would be making something capable of piercing through it, but I believe the Foundation has the resources to do so. A long period of acceleration via gravitational assists and ion propulsion would be sufficient to deal catastrophic damage, given a sharp and tough enough tip.

I will attend to our agreement as my next order of business.
Dr. Miyo Hara
Guest
Secure, Contain, Protect
From:
To:
CC:
Subject:
AStew@scp.int
BAlex@scp.int, MHara@temp.scp.int
none
Re:Re:Re:URGENT: SCP-9676-2

If both of you are correct, and this gets off the ground, we would be simultaneously destroying a planet and killing the largest known organism. I don't know what the ethics are on that, but it'll certainly make us notable.

Of course, I don't have anywhere near the authority to approve something like that, but I'll submit an official proposal as soon as possible.
Dr. Archer Steward
Foundation Astrophysicist
Secure, Contain, Protect
