The resultant fragments show continued signs of life, and have been designated as new SCP-9676 instances.

Update 01-08-2030:

Foundation-JAXA Joint Team Debriefing Transcript
Persons Present: Dr. Archer Steward, Dr. Bridget Alex, Sgt. Michael Bayle, Dr. Miyo Hara

[BEGIN LOG]

Dr. Steward: Congratulations, both of you. We just popped a planet.

Dr. Hara: It was an honor, doctor.

Dr. Alex: Thank you.

Dr. Hara: So, is this where our collaboration ends?

Dr. Steward: The contract is up, and we have no further expectations for you. This is where we amnesticize you and let you continue your work at JAXA. However, my superiors have taken notice of your role in this achievement. Should you be interested, the SCP Foundation would be proud to have you. In an official status, that is. You have already worked with us longer than many.

Dr. Hara: I see… This is a truly great honor. I would-

Dr. Steward: No pressure to accept, of course. We have already taken plenty of your time. If you would prefer to be amnesticized and returned to civilian science, that is your choice.

Dr. Hara: …I will accept your offer. There is clearly more I can do.

Dr. Steward: Very well. Sign here, please.

[END LOG]

[[/div]] [[/div]] **Special Containment Procedures:** Foundation agents embedded in major space agencies are to ensure no information about the nature of SCP-9676 bodies is disseminated to the public. Agents in relevant businesses are to monitor the capabilities of astronomical observation equipment planned to be available to the public, and ensure no device capable of detecting SCP-9676 instances' composition reaches market. All reports of asteroids with unusually green hues or low densities are to be suppressed. **Description:** SCP-9676 is a form of exotic life, currently the only known organism to be naturally capable of growing and reproducing in a vacuum. SCP-9676 instances are spherical, dark-green clumps of vegetative matter, varying widely in size: most instances are likely too small to be detectable with current observational equipment. However, the largest instance currently known has an estimated diameter of 18 kilometers. They derive energy from photosynthesizing sunlight, and gain biomass by extracting nutrients from dust and asteroids via an as-of-yet unknown process. Almost all SCP-9676 instances detected have been found in the Asteroid Belt, but a small number of individuals have been found as far from the sun as in the rings of Saturn. Research into the biology, ecology, and potential dangers or uses of SCP-9676 is ongoing. Foundation liaisons within the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) have arranged for the Hayabusa2 craft to visit an SCP-9676 instance, designated SCP-9676-1-162173, and return a sample of it to Earth for analysis by a joint team of Foundation and JAXA scientists. ##red|**Update 06-12-2020:**## [[div class="blockquote"]] **Foundation-JAXA Joint Team Briefing Transcript** Persons Present: Dr. Archer Steward, Dr. Bridget Alex, Sgt. Aidan Lee, Dr. Miyo Hara ----- [BEGIN LOG] **Dr. Steward:** Good morning, Dr. Hara. Please take a seat. As you are aware, you have been selected to work with our team to analyze the samples delivered by Hayabusa2 yesterday, as well as conduct follow-up research as needed. As you are no doubt also aware, this is highly classified. No information about any of this can be shared with anyone. **Dr. Hara:** I'm honored to work with you on such a momentous discovery, but I'm afraid I still don't quite understand what requires your involvement here. Could we begin with that? **Dr. Steward:** Ah, of course. You are familiar with our organization and its mission, yes? **Dr. Hara:** I've read the brochure you gave me. **Dr. Steward:** Good. While these organisms may currently appear harmless, they display multiple likely-anomalous properties. This is the first life we've seen in a vacuum, and until we understand how it works, we cannot risk exposing it to the public. Even if it is harmless, it is our organization's belief that publicly revealing the existence of any extraterrestrial life would cause more harm than good. **Dr. Hara:** //Any// extraterrestrial life? How many- **Dr. Steward:** I'm afraid that's classified. **Dr. Hara:** Of course. **Dr. Steward:** Anyway, introductions. I am Dr. Archer Steward, Foundation astrophysicist and leader of this team. This is Dr. Bridget Alex, Foundation xenobiologist. **Dr. Alex:** Hello. **Dr. Hara:** Dr. Miyo Hara, JAXA engineer. **Dr. Steward:** Perfect. Sign here, please, and then shall we get started? [END LOG] [[/div]] ##red|**Update 09-02-2021:**## [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails start=-- |from= BAlex@scp.int |to= AStew@scp.int, MHara@temp.scp.int |cc=none |subject= SCP-9676 Initial Findings ]] The genome of SCP-9676 strongly suggests it belongs to phylum Chlorophyta. The outer cell walls are extremely tough, containing high concentrations of carbonate and silicate minerals. Long filaments extend from the surface. These filaments appear to be responsible for the digestion of rock and ice, but the chemical process responsible is likely anomalous. All attempts to observe or replicate it have failed. The chloroplasts are clearly modified as well. Investigation into the photosynthetic mechanism is ongoing. [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails end=-- |name= Dr. Bridget Alex |title= Foundation Xenobiologist |signoff= Secure, Contain, Protect |signoff-icon= https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/component:dynamic-emails/transparent.png ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails start=-- |from= AStew@scp.int |to= BAlex@scp.int, MHara@temp.scp.int |cc=none |subject= Re:SCP-9676 Initial Findings ]] Huh, it's actually space algae. Assuming this isn't an ectoentropic process, our space algae would need to eat a variety of asteroids. Carbonate and silicate compounds are easy to find in asteroids, but they also need a fair amount of water. There are icy and hydrated asteroids in the Belt, but not enough to support such a large population of space algae, assuming they're just bouncing around out there. P.S. We need a better name than the SCP number or "space algae". I get the feeling we will become quite closely acquainted with these by the time we're done. [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails end=-- |name= Dr. Archer Steward |title= Foundation Astrophysicist |signoff= Secure, Contain, Protect |signoff-icon= https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/component:dynamic-emails/transparent.png ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails start=-- |from= MHara@temp.scp.int |to= AStew@scp.int, BAlex@scp.int |cc=none |subject= Re:Re:SCP-9676 Initial Findings ]] I suspect they have some kind of propulsion. If they were able to target and move towards water-containing bodies, these organisms could sustain themselves in an environment with a much lower concentration of them. This would also require some method of detecting water, but simple light or chemical sensors could lead one to water at long ranges. As for your question, they are essentially just very large and tough marimo, are they not? [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails end=-- |name= Dr. Miyo Hara |title= Guest |signoff= Secure, Contain, Protect |signoff-icon= https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/component:dynamic-emails/transparent.png ]] ##red|**Urgent Update 21-04-2021:**## **A new revision of this document is available. ##blue|Changes are highlighted in blue.##** [[include :scp-wiki:component:anomaly-class-bar-source |item-number= 9676 |clearance= 3 |container-class= esoteric |secondary-class= cernunnos |secondary-icon= https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/component%3Aanomaly-class-bar/cernunnos-icon.svg |disruption-class= ekhi |risk-class= notice ]] @@ @@ [[div class="scp-image-block block-right"]] [[image :first alt="An image of a dark-green sphere in front of what looks like the planet Jupiter."]] [[div class="scp-image-caption"]] An SCP-9676 instance orbiting Jupiter. Almost all SCP-9676 instances detected have been found in the Asteroid Belt, but a small number of individuals are ##blue|far enough from the sun to qualify as extreme trans-Neptunian objects## ##blue|SCP-9676-2 is an exceptionally large instance of SCP-9676, currently the largest known single organism in existence. It is believed to be the object responsible for the theory that a distant ninth planet exists in the Solar System. It is currently located 221 AU away from the Sun. SCP-9676-2 is in the process of moving closer to the Sun at high velocity (estimates suggest its current speed is in excess of 200 kilometers per second, and increasing). This runs contrary to mathematical predictions of its orbit and is currently unexplained.## ##blue|Research into methods of hiding or preventing SCP-9676-2's approach to the rest of the Solar System is ongoing.## ##red|**Update 22-04-2021:**## [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails start=-- |from= AStew@scp.int |to= BAlex@scp.int, MHara@temp.scp.int |cc=none |subject= URGENT: SCP-9676-2 ]] So, Planet Nine is real and it's a humongous marimo. What exactly do we do here? We can't stop it, because it's bigger than the Earth. We can't hide it, because it's bigger than the Earth. It also appears to be actively propelling itself towards us, so even if we did stop or hide it, we have no way of knowing what it would do after. And I don't think I need to explain why killing something that is, as I have said, bigger than the Earth, is not a feasible option. The good news is, we have about two decades before it becomes widely observable, assuming no major breakthroughs in commercially-available telescope technology. Any ideas, anyone? P.S. Our collaboration has been extended, pending your signature, Dr. Hara. We have much to do now. Our samples contain microscopic pockets filled with a mix of hydrogen and methane gases at fairly high pressures, which become more abundant in the deeper layers. I suspect that sufficiently-large instances have a hollow bladder in their center, filled with high-pressure gas. This would serve two purposes: it would allow instances to propel themselves by venting it in a controlled manner, and it would allow them to grow much larger than expected, as their gravity would be balanced out by the internal pressure of their bladders. This explains both the massive size and high speed of SCP-9676-2. [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails end=-- |name= Dr. Bridget Alex |title= Foundation Xenobiologist |signoff= Secure, Contain, Protect |signoff-icon= https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/component:dynamic-emails/transparent.png ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails start=-- |from= MHara@temp.scp.int |to= AStew@scp.int, BAlex@scp.int |cc=none |subject= Re:Re:URGENT: SCP-9676-2 ]] If your gas-bladder hypothesis is true, I believe I have a solution to SCP-9676-2. It is, in essence, an impossibly-large balloon. All we need to do is puncture a sufficiently-large hole in it. Depending on the exact pressure of the gas and physical properties of the outer shell, it's possible that it would deflate or even pop entirely. Of course, the challenging part would be making something capable of piercing through it, but I believe the Foundation has the resources to do so. A long period of acceleration via gravitational assists and ion propulsion would be sufficient to deal catastrophic damage, given a sharp and tough enough tip. I will attend to our agreement as my next order of business. I don't know what the ethics are on that, but it'll certainly make us notable. Of course, I don't have anywhere near the authority to approve something like that, but I'll submit an official proposal as soon as possible. Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9678 being uncontainable, efforts are to be focused on identifying infected individuals and preventing them from coming into prolonged contact with critical infrastructure. This applies to civilians (e.g., nuclear power plant staff, pilots, air traffic controllers), military personnel (e.g., nuclear silo operators, ammunition depot staff), and Foundation employees (e.g., field operatives, containment specialists).

Systematic screening of individuals whose professions require proximity to critical infrastructure is mandatory and must be conducted annually.

If an infected individual is found occupying a high-risk position, UNLUCKY STAR Protocol (removal from such a position through subterfuge and engineered career setbacks) is to be enacted.

Description: SCP-9678 is classified as a stochastic field disruption that anomalously manifests in specific individuals (designated SCP-9678-1). The mechanism of selection remains unknown.

SCP-9678-1 instances carry a stochastic disruption charge (SDC) of high intensity, expressed as consistent patterns of statistically improbable adverse events (“bad luck”). Family and close friends absorb a small fraction of this charge, lessening its impact on the infected individual. This characteristic renders personal relationships especially important to SCP-9678-1, not only for charge distribution but also for the emotional support that mitigates stress caused by SCP-9678.

Social isolation of SCP-9678-1 has been observed to result in rapid SDC escalation, frequently correlating with severe equipment malfunctions in their proximity.

Accumulated SDC may, under certain conditions, undergo catastrophic discharge. These discharge events present as single, high-intensity anomalies rather than distributed low-level disruptions, often resulting in significant systemic failure or infrastructural compromise.

Research into the mechanisms governing SDC accumulation and discharge remains ongoing.

Addendum-01 : Incident log 9678-L1

Foreword: The following log details Operation PUNKLOVER via video transcription. The operation involved the investigation of a suspected Chaos Insurgency hideout located in an abandoned asylum, away from urban centers.

While the initial operational goals were not achieved, this prompted the Foundation to further investigate the events, which later revealed the existence of SCP-9678.

Exploration Video Log Transcript

Date: 10/08/2016

Exploration Team: Busters

Subject: Operation PunkLover

[BEGIN LOG]

The video begins as Agent Brooks (communications and technical specialist) turns the handle and opens a metallic door. His attempt at doing so quietly is defeated by the creak of the rusty hinges, followed by a loud metallic bang as the door falls from its frame.

The team responds with a collective eye roll directed at him except for Agent Holt (team lead).

Agent Holt: The asylum’s large. Maybe nobody heard that. Valdez (retrieval/containment), move ahead and demonstrate for the new recruit how to proceed quietly.
New recruit, stay back. Monitor your readings for anomalous activity, and try not to break anything. Everyone else, eyes open, mouths shut. Standard procedure.

Holt gestures toward the doorless frame.

The video feed shows a dilapidated interior, illuminated only by a few surviving lights. The team advances silently as Agent Brooks slowly waves a Foundation-issued multipurpose field scanner in a smooth arc. Several minutes pass without incident. Agent Marquis (weapons specialist) is seen looking over Agent Brooks’s shoulder several times, trying to glimpse his wrist computer’s readings, before Holt finally notices.

Agent Holt: Marquis, problem? New guy’s not doing his job right?

Agent Marquis: I don’t know boss, this place feels wrong, it’s like all my body is itching. Like that time in Amazonia, it co—

Agent Holt: New guy, are the readings nominal??

Agent Brooks: I might be new to this team, but this is my sixth OP, Holt. I know how this gear works. All readings are flat. Zero across the board.

Agent Vance: Yeah, and this is clearly not anomalous.

Vance points at a fluid on the wall. Closer inspection reveals the purple-red liquid flowing upward against gravity. The video feed from Agent Valdez slowly pans toward the ceiling, where the liquid collects into an eye the size of a fist, darting erratically left and right, then up and down.

Agent Marquis: That is what I thought, look at that, a Sarkic surveillance system!

Agent Marquis gestures toward the eye, moments before it explodes. His video feed shifts to Agent Rodrigue (silent operations specialist), whose suppressed rifle is seen emitting a faint trail of smoke.

Agent Rodrigue approaches Agent Brooks and secures his wrist to get a closer view of the display. Video feed confirms all readings remain nominal until physical contact, at which point the wrist-mounted scanner’s screen displays a brief glitch before resetting. This anomaly is not immediately noticed by the rest of the team. A red warning dot then activates, indicating a spike in Hume1 levels. Agent Rodrigue raises Agent Brooks’s arm to present the data to the unit.

Agent Brooks: What the hell, Rodrigue?

Agent Rodrigue points at the scanner’s display. Brooks appears visibly surprised and withdraws his arm.

Agent Brooks: The spike occurred the moment you touched it.

Agent Rodrigue slowly shakes his head.

Agent Holt: Stand down, Rodrigue. Brooks, report.

Agent Brooks: Hume levels are elevated beyond baseline. Whatever is present here, it’s significant.

(Holt stares at Brooks.)

Agent Holt: Anything else?

Agent Brooks: Negative. All other readings remain nominal.

Agent Holt: Relay to Overwatch.

Brooks attempts to establish contact with HQ using the long-range communications transceiver. No response is received.

Agent Brooks: The signal is scrambled. Could be anomaly interference or structural shielding. Either way, we have to get out if we want to re-establish contact with Overwatch.

Agent Holt: We’re leaving then. We need to report Sarkic activity.

Agent Brooks: Affirmative.

The team advances without incident for several minutes. Marquis, leading, halts upon opening a door.

Agent Marquis: I’m sure we took the exact same path on the way back. We never used a staircase.

His video feed confirms the presence of a staircase.

Agent Marquis: Yet here we are.

Agent Brooks: This makes no sense. If there was a spatial anomaly, the field scanner should have detected it.

Agent Vance: Maybe the equipment is compromised. Or maybe you don’t know how to use it.

Agent Holt: Vance…

Agent Vance: Just saying!

Agent Holt: Enough, Vance. I don’t want to hear any more of it. We’re moving up. The signal can’t be worse going higher.

Agent Valdez: Unless “up” leads down…

Agent Holt: Duly noted. Ascend one floor and reassess signal integrity.

The team arrive on the next floor. As the team progresses in a corridor, the remaining light bulbs still functioning briefly flare with intense brightness before popping one by one.

Agent Brooks: At least the floor hasn’t given up on us.

Agent Vance: Shut the fuck up, Brooks.

A loud cracking noise is heard as the video feeds collectively shift toward Agent Brooks. The floor gives way entirely, leaving the team incapacitated for several moments. As the team regains its footing, significant environmental changes become apparent: surfaces appear cleaner and the overall condition markedly improved. The only visible damage in the room, which appears to be a cafeteria, is the hole in the ceiling above them, from which they fell.

Agent Holt: Nothing broken?

The team confirm.

Agent Brooks: Hume levels have returned to normal values.

Agent Valdez: You are not going to like this, Brooks, but I think I understand what is going on. Look.

Agent Valdez slowly takes hold of the display on Agent Brooks’s wrist and presses the reset button. The screen shows elevated Hume levels along with temporal and spatial anomaly readings. Agent Valdez releases the display, and the values remain consistent for several moments before reverting to nominal. When Agent Valdez takes hold of the device again, the readings spike once more.

Agent Holt: Valdez? Explanation.

Agent Valdez: It’s not only the environment affecting the reading, I think Brooks himself is. I believe he’s suffering from some form of affliction. I heard rumors about him, that he was unlucky or whatever. But it is the first time I can see bad luck manifest so constantly and measurably. I bet that if he fired his gun right now, it would jam or blow up in your hand.

Agent Brooks: I have always had tough luck, but that is no anomaly.

Agent Valdez: Then maybe there is something here amplifying it. Anomaly or not, you are a liability.

Agent Holt: We can’t take chances. Give your equipment to Valdez and secure the cafeteria. You are staying here.

[END LOG]

Subsequent operation remained uneventful. Follow-up investigation yielded no confirmation of Chaos Insurgency or Sarkic presence; however, multiple indicators of spatial and temporal distortion were documented throughout the site.**

Unbeknownst to Agent Brooks, multiple family members and close acquaintances died mere hours before Operation PUNKLOVER. Analysis confirms this event directly corresponded with an extreme SDC spike.

Addendum-02 : Test log 9678-T

Foreword: Comprehensive background analysis confirmed a statistically significant clustering of adverse events in Agent Nathan Brooks' personal life. These include repeated failures of digital authentication systems, light bulbs breaking spontaneously upon activation, abnormally frequent vending machine malfunctions and repeated injury from falling objects (including three separate air conditioning units).

Tests T01 to T03 were carried out with the consent of Agent Brooks.

Test Designation: 9678-T01

Date: 10/12/2016
Subject: Agent Brooks (male, 34, former Field operative)

Procedure: Subject instructed to access a restricted Foundation portal requiring completion of a simple arithmetic CAPTCHA (“7 + 5 = ?”).
Result: Despite correct input (“12”), system rejected entry attempt with on-screen error: “Incorrect value. Try again.” Repeated attempts with correct input produced identical rejections. (See attached capture, Figure 9678-T05-A.)

Control: Technician attempted the same CAPTCHA on the same terminal immediately after Subject vacated.
Result: Accepted on first attempt; login successful.

Notes: This marks the first documented case of SCP-9678 influencing deterministic arithmetic validation.

example of consistent SCP-9678 manifestation

Test Designation: 9678-T02

Date: 10/12/2016
Subject: Agent Brooks (male, 34, former Field operative)

Procedure: Subject instructed to withdraw $20 from a standard ATM unit located at Site-404.
Result: Machine produced an error message, card was retained, and transaction was voided.

Control: Technician attempted same transaction immediately after.
Result: No error observed. Repeated several times with consistent success.

Notes: Event supports theory of computational state corruption.

Test Designation: 9678-T03

Date: 10/12/2016
Subject: Agent Brooks (male, 34, former Field operative)

Procedure: Subject instructed to fire his service weapon at the site’s shooting range.
Result: Weapon misfire, causing temporary blindness and minor burn injuries on the right hand of the subject.

Control: Technician attempted to fire the same weapon, using rounds from the same magazine.
Result: Target successfully hit.

Notes: Event considered baseline SCP-9678 manifestation.

Test Designation: 9678-T05

Date: 10/12/2016
Subject: D-91737 (male, 52, victim of numerous hit-and-run accidents)

Procedure: Test of blood samples to determine if any anomalous agent can be found.
Result: Sample mislabeled as “waste” and discarded prior to testing. No result.

Procedure: Test of blood samples to determine if any anomalous agent can be found.
Result: Blood sample tube accidentally broken before test could be conducted. No result.

Procedure: Test of blood samples to determine if any anomalous agent can be found.
Result: Subject resisted sampling procedure and required physical restraint. Analysis of acquired sample yielded no anomalous findings.

Notes: When questioned, D-91737 attributed his resistance to severe trypanophobia (fear of needles), reporting that he had reached his tolerance limit following the third venipuncture conducted that morning.

Test Designation: 9678-T07

Date: 10/12/2016
Subject: D-91797 (female, 23, previously employed as a “cooler”2 by multiple casinos in Las Vegas, suggesting awareness of SCP-9678’s effect by her employers)

Procedure: Subject instructed to access banking account through standard Foundation-issued laptop.
Result: Browser opens the page with no problem, then crashes as the subject enters credentials.

Control: A technician (holding an account with the same bank) attempted access using the same hardware.
Result: Technician unable to access the bank’s website. Subsequent testing confirmed worldwide service outages affecting the institution for several hours.

Notes: First documented case of a 9678-related event producing a direct negative effect on others. If this can be reproduced consistently, the potential for weaponization should be formally evaluated.

Test Designation: 9678-T08

Date: 10/18/2016
Subject: D-91866 (female, 32, history of multiple lightning strikes)

Procedure: Subject is tied to a pole during a storm. One meter away, a taller and more conductive lightning rod is installed (measurements confirm higher conductivity).
Result: Subject is struck by lightning nearly instantly.
Control: Lightning rod remains untouched.

Additional subject: D-91590 (male, 43, documented history of multiple lottery wins)
Procedure: D-91590 is tied to the same pole as D-91866 and left exposed.
Result: Lightning strikes the lightning rod, leaving the subjects completely unharmed for 14 minutes and 12 seconds. The lightning then strikes the subjects repeatedly, with the rod remaining untouched until the end of the storm.

Notes: Data suggests that close physical proximity to an SCP-9678-1 instance, sustained over a set period of time, can be sufficient to induce adverse outcomes—even in individuals otherwise characterized by statistically improbable “good fortune.”

Addendum-03 : Ethics Committee Review

The Ethics Committee has ruled against the proposed weaponization of SCP-9678 by employing SCP-9678-1 instances. The rationale is twofold:

1. Effective weaponization would necessitate total isolation of the instance and, in certain cases, the termination of their SDC-buffer. Such measures would create an institutional incentive to deliberately inflict suffering, rendering the proposal ethically unacceptable.
2. Weaponization offers no guarantee of reliable targeting. Owing to SCP-9678’s anomalous properties, the probability of collateral malfunction or operational backfire is assessed as unacceptably high.

Proposal closed. Further attempts at weaponization are prohibited.

Personal note: please, ensure Agent Brooks gets proper psychological care. Dr. Linburg, Ethics Committee.

This applies to civilians (e.g., nuclear power plant staff, pilots, air traffic controllers), military personnel (e.g., nuclear silo operators, ammunition depot staff), and Foundation employees (e.g., field operatives, containment specialists). Systematic screening of individuals whose professions require proximity to critical infrastructure is mandatory and must be conducted annually. If an infected individual is found occupying a high-risk position, **UNLUCKY STAR Protocol** (removal from such a position through subterfuge and engineered career setbacks) is to be enacted. **Description:**  SCP-9678 is classified as a stochastic field disruption that anomalously manifests in specific individuals (designated SCP-9678-1). The mechanism of selection remains unknown. SCP-9678-1 instances carry a stochastic disruption charge (SDC) of high intensity, expressed as consistent patterns of statistically improbable adverse events (“bad luck”). Family and close friends absorb a small fraction of this charge, lessening its impact on the infected individual. This characteristic renders personal relationships especially important to SCP-9678-1, not only for charge distribution but also for the emotional support that mitigates stress caused by SCP-9678. Social isolation of SCP-9678-1 has been observed to result in rapid SDC escalation, frequently correlating with severe equipment malfunctions in their proximity. Accumulated SDC may, under certain conditions, undergo catastrophic discharge. These discharge events present as single, high-intensity anomalies rather than distributed low-level disruptions, often resulting in significant systemic failure or infrastructural compromise.  Research into the mechanisms governing SDC accumulation and discharge remains ongoing. ++ Addendum-01 : Incident log 9678-L1 **Foreword:** The following log details Operation PUNKLOVER via video transcription. The operation involved the investigation of a suspected Chaos Insurgency hideout located in an abandoned asylum, away from urban centers. While the initial operational goals were not achieved, this prompted the Foundation to further investigate the events, which later revealed the existence of SCP-9678. If there was a spatial anomaly, the field scanner should have detected it.    **Agent Vance:** Maybe the equipment is compromised. Or maybe you don’t know how to use it.    **Agent Holt:** Vance…   **Agent Vance:** Just saying!    **Agent Holt:** Enough, Vance. I don’t want to hear any more of it. We’re moving up. Agent Valdez releases the display, and the values remain consistent for several moments before reverting to nominal. When Agent Valdez takes hold of the device again, the readings spike once more.// **Agent Holt:** Valdez? Explanation. **Agent Valdez:** It’s not only the environment affecting the reading, I think **Brooks** himself is. I believe he’s suffering from some form of affliction. I heard rumors about him, that he was unlucky or whatever. But it is the first time I can see bad luck manifest so constantly and measurably. I bet that if he fired his gun right now, it would jam or blow up in your hand. **Agent Brooks:** I have always had tough luck, but that is no anomaly. **Agent Valdez:** Then maybe there is something here amplifying it. Anomaly or not, you are a liability.   **Agent Holt:** We can’t take chances. Give your equipment to **Valdez** and secure the cafeteria. You are staying here. Notice: On October 2nd, 1973, an internal request to reclassify SCP-9680 as Explained was submitted, and was approved (See Addendum 9680.9). This document is currently being updated.


Item Designation: SCP-9680

Classification: Keter

Special Containment Procedures: Individuals affected by SCP-9680 failure are to be compensated with equivalent, nonanomalous seed stock from non-Méndez growers, under a cover story of "clearance stock." Following requests from Interim-Site 93 personnel, Foundation personnel that would like to attend funerals of SCP-9680 victims are permitted to do so, with prior approval for leave.

Archived Containment Procedures (preserved during reclassification): Produce and seed markets are to be monitored for sellers of SCP-9680. If found, seeds are to be confiscated, sellers are to be questioned regarding their purchase history of SCP-9680 to determine point of origin.1

Instances of SCP-9680 that have germinated, bloomed, or fruited are to be destroyed following sample collection.2

Growing sites containing SCP-9680 are to be quarantined until all potential pollen sources and deposits are confirmed safe, collected, or destroyed. Méndez company ties to known parabotanical threats are currently under investigation. Collected samples are to be returned to Sites 36 and 93 for thaumaturgic analysis. If SCP-9680 residual creation markers match those of known individuals in Foundation databases, investigations are to be launched.

SCP-9680 samples, a variety of wheat seeds named "Golden Goddess."

Description: SCP-9680 are specific packets of 30 different seed varieties from the Méndez Corporation. Species have been found to vary with no clear pattern or majority species, but primarily consist of food or textile crops (wheat, corn, cotton, sugarcane, etc.) SCP-9680 instances appear identical to nonanomalous equivalents sold by Méndez, but exhibit rapid growth patterns when planted. These extend to increased success not only in growth of planted seeds, but in seed production, pollen spread, and fruit production.

SCP-9680 instances have been sold in Northern India for the past three years. Instances have been found in small mandis3 in the states of Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh. Analyses by GoI-1469 and Foundation psychokinetic and thaumaturgical experts indicate an anomalous origin of recovered SCP-9680 instances.

Samples of all known varieties of SCP-9680 are currently in test growth chambers mimicking in situ conditions, in permanent Foundation sites located in the Middle East, due to personnel concerns.

The Méndez Corporation has shown no previous signs of anomalous activity as a major agricultural producer for the continental United States founded in, registered, and operating solely in Veil-compliant areas since incorporation. Addition to Foundation Groups of Interest may be considered.

SCP-9680 was first discovered by GoI-1469. Communication regarding SCP-9680's discovery can be found below, originally delivered as a letter that spontaneously manifested in Interim-Site 93's break room.

Given the history of positive collaboration with GoI-1469 and the importance of maintaining this relationship as the Foundation establishes presence in the Indian subcontinent, this letter and its contents were made top priority.

TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN AMONGST OUR NEW FRIENDS:

We have noticed a few problems that it may interest you to look at. We know we are asking something rather soon after you've come here. But as friends, we should help each other, no?

Those in mandis around here have been acting strange. Some farmers sell seeds they would need for future seasons with reckless abandon; come into money they could not have earned legally; grown new types of familiar plants that we have never seen before.

As is expected, we "ran point" as you all say, and collected some of these seeds. They do not taste different, look different, smell different.

Our psychic sweeps show nothing. Our tracers show nothing. Our strongest jadhus can find little more than the smallest of traces of magic. What we can find, it is most certainly nothing we are familiar with.

This scares us. It is our job to know these things. These people rely on us, as we rely on you now.

We do request your assistance in this case, with your technology to detect potential godly or magical influence. In return you will find us more than willing to help you with tasks associated.

You will also find some sweets with this message. Consider them a housewarming gift. Please keep in mind the kaju katli have cashews, for those with allergies. They are the white, diamond shaped ones.

Your dearest friends,
The House of The Naga

Addendum 9680.1 - January 1973

The sole local Mobile Task Force formed at the time, MTF Epsilon-65 ("Trishula") was dispatched. MTF E-65, at the time, primarily consisted of non-military personnel designed to supplement GoI-1469 forces. Members visited a mandi near a local Nexus, Jalandhar's Depths, for field research. GoI-1469 contacts met Foundation personnel there.

Foundation personnel concerns required a greater than expected GoI-1469 presence.

Field Personnel:

Junior Operative Santos: Environmental researcher specializing in counteroffensives against anomalous invasive species.

Lead Operative Wyle: Field director of MTF Epsilon-65.

Jadhughar Malkit Singh: Senior thaumaturgical expert of GoI-1469, specializing in parabotany, paraecology, and anthropology.

Baazighar Jashan Arora: Junior thaumaturgical expert of GoI-1469.

[Recording from Santos' body camera begins as the group walk towards the mandi. They are attempting to cross the street to a large group of tents.]

Arora: So! That's where it happens. The magic. Not, well, not actual magic, but the magic of food! Commerce! Food!

Singh: Arora, please behave.

Arora: Aw. I just want to show them. Have you two had a real, fresh mango? Or maybe some sugarcane? Sugarcane juice? Singh sahib, we never get anyone as new as them on our trips.

Wyle: Singh, it's fine. We'd love to, at some point.

Singh: Later, then. You're buying.

[A car speeds past them as they cross, nearly striking Santos.]

Santos: Fuck! Why are there so many people here?

Singh: Why are there birds in the sky?

Santos: Fine, I just— can't they drive normally, please? And the honking. My head.

Singh: This is normal. Please just keep your eyes open, people are always in a rush here.

Santos: No shit.

Singh: There are those who work in the city. They will be in a rush. You will see a lot of intermingling from stall to stall. They will be in a rush. You trade for what you don't have, and usually buy and sell enough to make a small amount of profit if those from the city come to buy from you.

Wyle: Variable rates? C’mon Singh, why spoil the surprise for us foreigners so soon?

[Singh smiles.]

Singh: That’s not the case officially, no.

[The group arrive. Sellers have their produce spread out on blankets on the floor, in large, haphazard piles. They hawk their wares at passersby.]

Seller 1: (translated from Punjabi) Brother! Three for five rupees! Better deal, you'll never see. Brother!

Santos: Christ.

A portion of the mandi.

Wyle: Watch your throat, Santos. Very nice and dusty here.

Santos: Heard. I’ll try my best not to keel over coughing.

Seller 2: (translated from Punjabi) Fresh mangos, juicy, sticky, so sweet you'll need to wash your hands soon! Fresh mangos here, get them, eat them now!

[Arora briefly leaves the group to head to the seller. After taking a few steps, he rejoins.]

Singh: I am told they should be in the back. Closer to the roads, you see. Many will come in wagons, carts, that sort of thing if they expect to be purchasing seeds.

Wyle: No little packets to be seen here. Is that usually a bulk purchase?

Arora: Yes! Usually farmers, if they need it. Not often though. We usually collect seeds.

Santos: We?

Arora: My family works the fields for a living. Not here. A village. Small one, near Tarn Taran. It's a quaint little thing. An acre at most, maybe? But I worked them too, before I came here and joined the House.

Singh: Where we found Arora, in fact. What a story that one was.

Arora: And for that, Singh-ji, I thank you. I don't think my back could have taken more nights crouching over the rows.

Seller 3: (translated from Punjabi) Seeds! Better than any seeds you've seen before. So many sacks! Many sacks! All of your choices for the next season, here!

[Singh holds up a hand, then gestures for the group to come near him as he moves to the side. Pulling them away from the seed seller, he speaks in a low whisper.]

Singh: That is the markings of the seeds we know. You will let Arora and I speak, and us alone. Please stay behind us.

[Arora enthusiastically nods, before looking back to Singh. Singh nods, and Arora approaches Wyle and Santos. He pulls them to the side to act as if they are looking at the seller's produce, while they converse in English.]

Wyle: It's fine if we talk this close?

Arora: Should be. There's not many English speakers here! We should just look like a tour guide and his little group, a sad group, but a group.

Santos: Can we focus, please?

Arora: So, these seeds. None of us recognize the company. Do you?

Wyle: I mean, yeah. They're a normal fruit company back in the States, like Bold, Sunny-Dayz, that kind of thing. Make good fruit cups since I was a kid.

Santos: And importantly, boss, they haven't been marked for doing anything particularly noteworthy or Veil-breaking. At least, not since we've been around.

Arora: Hm. We have our own producers, own companies. Odd that the Americans are trying to get in on it. We'd say it's fine that they're here, but reports are enough that people seem to be worried. Mostly the small farmers.

Wyle: I mean, it makes sense to me. They're big. At a big enough scale, I'd assume it adds up.

Arora: Wyle sahib, look at them. There is no scale here. Everyone knows each other, and everyone gets their seeds from each other, and grow their few crops.

Santos: And, like, that makes sense. It's a new market, duh. We're here too, because it's new to us too. No?

Wyle: She's right. I don't understand a bit of this. What have you all even found? At least, what have you found to warrant us coming out here? Not that I mind that, mind you. She might.

Arora: Nothing more than the equivalent of some wisps of smoke from a dying fire. Maybe the slightest scrap of a psychic signature. It's sneaky, too bloody sneaky.

Santos: It's how it works. You have the big fish, and the littler fish.

Arora: No, no it isn't! There's so many of these sellers, so many little relationships and friendships and differing preferences of who you buy from that it does not matter. The wealth is so spread out. There are no big fish.

[Arora coughs.]

Arora: They try. All they do is try.

Santos: Your first brush with a megacorp? I mean, sorry…?

Arora: No need to be, it's not like it's your fault or anything. Just, crops didn't use to be this big. This… strange.

[He picks up a mango from a nearby blanket, handles it, and gives it a sniff. At the same time, Singh returns.]

Singh: Find one you like?

Arora: No. All unripe. Big, the size of a ripe one, but unripe.

Singh: Hm. It is season.

Arora: I know. It's… gross, really. I can barely eat them. These new seeds have been disappointing.

Singh: If you’re done, I have information. Not a lot, but some. Simply a name or two.

Wyle: And d’you think that’s enough?

Singh: It will have to be. We can perform a minor divination, then notify you of our results.

Santos: Nothing about why?

[Singh shakes his head.]

Singh: I understand you may expect something different. We of the House apologize.

[Arora squeezes the mango, still in his hand.]

Arora: Look around you.

[He gestures widely.]

Arora: What could you hope to make from this? A few rupees?

[END LOG]

The following document was received the next morning, alongside a blank sheet of paper and a small package.

TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN AMONGST OUR NEW FRIENDS:


We have a name, a low-level employee, but a name nonetheless. We are told that he has come by in a truck, offered seeds to some local villages. If you'll permit us, we can attempt to locate him. It may take some time. To confirm, Méndez is the correct corporation?

In that case, we have a headquarters location; oddly close to Jalandhar's Depths. You will find it attached.

We also realize we forgot to send the sweets yesterday. Here are two boxes. Please remember the cashew content. We would hate to cause problems!

Your dearest friends,
The House of The Naga

Foundation thaumaturges returned the following document via basic conjure lines.

TO SINGH:

Fine with us. Go look for your man, and we'll contact Méndez as well. I’ll see if I can get us cleared for an in person op, preferably. I’ll be sure to let you know how it goes. Keep us updated as well.

Thank you for the sweets. They were delicious. Santos in particular enjoyed the laddu, I think the paper the box came with called it that? She’d never tell you, though, and don’t tell her I told you.

Wyle


Addendum 9680.2 - February 1973

The majority of those affected by SCP-9680 are currently stuck in debt to Méndez India. Loans that have been made to pay this debt are frequently predatory, and Foundation and GoI-1469 resources are currently addressing lenders responsible.

Following the above events, Santos and Wyle were dispatched to the Méndez India corporate headquarters, located in a small office building in Jalandhar, 2.5 km from a major entrance of Jalandhar's Depths. Upon entry, they were met by Méndez front desk personnel.

[Body cam footage begins with Santos and Wyle entering the front doors. The office resembles a well-lit corporate office, with a desk and a small waiting room. There is no receptionist. It is entirely quiet.]

Santos: So, uh. Nobody here, or…?

Wyle: Just be sure to have your weapons ready. Just in case, y’know. I know we're here for more of a corp negotation, but wouldn't hurt to have some decent trigger fingers right now.

Santos: Heard.

Wyle: Hello? Anybody home?

[A few seconds pass. No one responds.]

Former headquarters of Méndez India.

Santos: Well, okay. The water cooler's half empty, so there were at least some people here at some point.

Wyle: Yeah, yeah. I’ve seen weirder, so no assumptions Santos.

[There is a loud noise, like water through a pipe. Santos and Wyle turn to the source of the sound, a closed door behind the desk. Wyle gives Santos a nod. Both draw their weapons, standard anti-thaumaturgy sidearms.]

Wyle: Hello? Anyone there? Come out with your hands up!

Santos: Can we just get this over with, please?

[A man stumbles out of the room, hands up. He looks at the two nervously, before putting his hands behind his head. Wyle and Santos point their weapons at him.]

Williams: Hey! Hey! Don't shoot! I work here! I didn't do anything! I work here!

[Wyle makes a quick glance at Santos. Santos switches on her sidearm's thaumaturgical radar.]

Wyle: Your name?

Williams: Williams! Bennett Williams! I work for Méndez. We're just getting started, we've barely moved in, it's just me here at the office for now.

Santos: Nothing.

Wyle: Damn, really? Okay, Bennett. What do you do here?

[Williams looks to Wyle.]

Williams: I coordinate, or at least, am supposed to be one of the people coordinating fulfillment and distribution of our orders! But like I said, it's just me! I started like two weeks ago and they've been promising me it'll be more than just me, but I also handle HR, and I haven't been asked to onboard anyone! They don't even respond to my calls! I don't wanna be here.

Wyle: Do you have any weapons on you, Williams?

Williams: Weapons!? We just do our work here. Normal, non-criminal work. What the fuck are you talking about?

Wyle: Come around the desk. Slowly, please, keeping your hands up.

[Williams does so. Wyle gestures to Santos, who pats him down.]

Santos: Clean.

Wyle: Okay. Sit down. Let's talk.

Williams: Okay. What do you wanna know?

Wyle: About your bosses, immediate or otherwise.

Williams: I dunno 'em. Sorry.

Wyle: How the fuck did you get hired, then?

Williams: I was studying in Harvard, actually. Well, just graduating. Got offered a job with Méndez, which I never would have taken otherwise. I mean, who gives a shit about agro economics? But! I am never going to pass up all-expenses paid travel. Especially to India! All my classmates talked about how much being here changed them, taught them, you know?

Santos: But you… live here now? This isn't a temp thing?

Williams: Duh. Didn't pay for that either. Even get a cleaner to come through my place every so often, which is cray! It's just an apartment, nothing like what you'd expect for that kind of service, but still. Yay.

Wyle: Do you know anything about them?

[Williams fidgets.]

Williams: I know, well, we're Méndez! The foremost producers of fruit, vegetables, and assorted tubers in the United States! But- but I know what you want, sorry. Still a little shaky from the whole "gun-pointed-at-my-temple" thing. I should have a business card somewhere, wait—

[Williams begins to get up. Wyle gestures for him to sit down.]

Wyle: I'll get it. Where?

Williams: Rolodex there, top of the desk by the plant. Labeled "Central."

[Wyle thumbs through the cards, holding up one after a few seconds.]

Wyle: Lucky me. Last one left.

Santos: Nice. Can't say I've ever talked to a CEO before.

Wyle: Just a P.O. box of all things. Still better than nothing.

[Williams clears his throat.]

Williams: So, uh. Can I go now? Please? I have a lot of paperwork to get done. We've been doing seed buybacks. Y'know, get some money from whatever old-ass seeds they've been using. God, what a headache that is.

Wyle: Sure.

Santos: Careful, buddy. We know where you're at now.

Williams: If we last the season. Our numbers aren't the best right now. That's why we did this whole thing with these new varietals. Never heard of them, not that I'm all that familiar with plants in the first place, but it's supposed to be a test run here. You know, smaller market, if it goes well, we can debut them worldwide! God, the bonus I'd get.

Wyle: Man, fuck you.

[END LOG]

Addendum 9680.3 - March 1973

Following this, GoI-1469 members determined that the located Méndez employee had no knowledge or understanding of the nature of SCP-9680 after psychic evaluation. Other located employees had similar informational gaps.

At this time, the majority of those affected by SCP-9680 refused Foundation assistance in paying back loans, citing distrust of government entities following Indian pushes to change crop rotations to further industrialization.4

Given the nature of Méndez's operations, the potential of risk to civilians, and apparent nonanomalous operations, GoI-1469 contacts in the Indian government made inquiries to Méndez India's executives based on the contact information found on the card retrieved.

FROM THE DESK OF MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT KALYAN SINGH

TO: ISAAC EVES, Méndez India CFO
FROM: MP KALYAN SINGH

To whom it may concern:

I am MP Kalyan Singh, member of India's Parliament, covering the legislative area of Greater Jalandhar in which your company currently is registered. As a result, your practices are my purview and concern. As you may know, our district is an agricultural one. Approximately 55% of my constituents rely on farming for their livelihoods, and approximately two-thirds of that rely solely on that source of income.

We have been at risk of significant damage to this sector before, and it came at great cost to farmers and their family, and I urge you to please reconsider.

On that note, I am writing to request further information on the nature of the crops you are currently selling. Producers of seeds are concerned by unfair market practices by your company, and with the quality of the seeds themselves; these are varieties entirely unfamiliar to them, and to me as well. India, and Punjab especially, has had difficult encounters with invasive species before, and we are fearful these may prove to be a similar problem.

A formal request has been lodged at the last session to receive samples of your product for testing, and for a hearing. You will be called for a hearing, as will any other relevant members of your company. Expect formal papers in a few weeks at the latest.

We here welcome a stronger market, but not at the cost of our farmers. Tread lightly.

~ MP KALYAN SINGH

MÉNDEZ CORPORATION: LIVE FRESH, EAT FRESHER!

TO: MP KALYAN SINGH
FROM: ISAAC EVES, Méndez India CFO

To MP-Sahib;

I am Tiffany Elwes, Mr. Eves' secretary. Mr. Eves wanted me to tell you that the genetic code of our varieties is proprietary under Indian law, as well as in every other major world power's courts of law. As such, reverse-engineering, sequencing, or releasing samples will be impossible, and illegal under the law you uphold.

He also wanted me to let you know that no member of Méndez's C-Suite will be available for hearings. Schedules are packed, and cannot be moved at this moment. Additionally, you will find that request likely will not go anywhere, and he encourages you to spend your time on more fruitful endeavors.

Lastly, he wanted me to recommend you look at your portfolio. You may find a number of new stock options available to you. Ticker is MNDZ.

Best,
The Desk of Isaac Eves

After this, no response was received from Méndez executives in spite of repeated requests by MP Singh, Foundation personnel, and GoI-1469 contacts. Forced summoning of Mr. Eves or other Méndez executives was suggested, but struck down after deliberation due to risk of potential Veil breach. Concern was especially raised due to lack of knowledge of thaumaturgic capabilities employed by Méndez rendering traditional amnestics useless.

Addendum 9680.4 - April 1973

Despite attempts at market manipulation, SCP-9680 instances have continued to spread throughout the Indian subcontinent. Why Foundation and GoI-1946 preventative measures are ineffective is currently unknown.

Attached are GoI-1469 and Foundation communications regarding next steps.

TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN AMONGST OUR FRIENDS:

Our investigation of the trucks remains pointless. Just more cogs. More useless seeds that show traces of little more than dog piss and wisps of trace magic. We have taken the liberty to psychically wither what we can and save a few samples, but no more than the bare minimum.

Please tell us it fares better for you. We have received reports from some farmers in Malwa. They are not optimistic, and they could use some benefit.

Your dearest friends,
The House of The Naga

TO THE HOUSE:

This is our problem; we can't do a thing without causing an issue. Our higher-ups don't want us interfering without certainty. Could throw our whole operation here at risk, not just here, but in this whole country. Just growing pains of being new here, I suppose.

We've tried making requests, but official channels are as good as ignored. I'm sure they're shredding our letters as soon as they get them. We've tried marking them with some minor sigils to trigger if they're read, but have gotten no hits so far.

Wyle

TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN AMONGST OUR FRIENDS:

Have you any new information? Without any place for us to use our expertise, we are little more than vigilantes.

We have tried before to incorporate ourselves into matters that did not involve the magic or psychic. It did not go well.

Your dearest friends,
The House of The Naga

TO SINGH:


We're trying. Please be patient.

Wyle

Your friends,
The House of The Naga

What do you mean? We've grown them here, they're fine. Not here, at least, but in good enough simulations elsewhere. I can send for an update, but it might be a few days.

Please avoid psychokinetically blowing up any more trucks.

Addendum 9680.5 - May 1973

Lead Operative Wyle's statement was made prior to confirmation with Site personnel. Upon checks of test growths of SCP-9680, it was confirmed that nearly all specimens exhibited infection with an unknown fungal pathogen, different to each species. Fruit, if produced, was inedible and prematurely rotting. No viable seeds were produced across eight thousand potential germinating sites.

All fungal samples tested had no anomalous indicators.

Singh: —knew, you bastard!

Following this, a reclassification request was filed.

Below is the proposed description for SCP-9680-EX.

Description: SCP-9680-EX is the designation for over 45 varieties6 of nonanomalous, genetically modified seeds produced by the Méndez Corporation. These seeds were and are produced anomalously to increase the scale of production, but otherwise carry no anomalous effects.

SCP-9680-EX specimens have been prone to unique combinations of nearly 70 threats, including pathogens, pests, and intolerance to Indian climates.

Farmers planting SCP-9680-EX report the following:

  • SCP-9680-EX purchasing requiring the selling of heirloom seed storage, resulting in near-total depletion of seed stock
  • Disruption of seed production of mature specimens
  • Increased rates of disease, especially cancer, in those exposed to SCP-9680 fields due to increased pesticide usage.

SCP-9680-EX production is so widespread across the Indian subcontinent that attempts to curtail production or spread prove too great of a risk to Veil integrity. Foundation and GoI-1496 efforts are focused on harm mitigation. In spite of this, current trends continue.

3. Small grower produce markets, similar to farmer's markets.
4. It is widely accepted by now that these attempts as part of the "Green Revolution," while increasing the food produced, caused immense damage to farming populations and soil health.

6. Over a dozen have been introduced since original classification.

Species have been found to vary with no clear pattern or majority species, but primarily consist of food or textile crops (wheat, corn, cotton, sugarcane, etc.) SCP-9680 instances appear identical to nonanomalous equivalents sold by Méndez, but exhibit rapid growth patterns when planted. These extend to increased success not only in growth of planted seeds, but in seed production, pollen spread, and fruit production. SCP-9680 instances have been sold in Northern India for the past three years. Instances have been found in small //mandis// [[footnote]] Small grower produce markets, similar to farmer's markets. [[/footnote]] in the states of Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh. Analyses by GoI-1469 and Foundation psychokinetic and thaumaturgical experts indicate an anomalous origin of recovered SCP-9680 instances. Samples of all known varieties of SCP-9680 are currently in test growth chambers mimicking in situ conditions, in permanent Foundation sites located in the Middle East, due to personnel concerns. The Méndez Corporation has shown no previous signs of anomalous activity as a major agricultural producer for the continental United States founded in, registered, and operating solely in Veil-compliant areas since incorporation. Addition to Foundation Groups of Interest may be considered. SCP-9680 was first discovered by GoI-1469. Communication regarding SCP-9680's discovery can be found below, originally delivered as a letter that spontaneously manifested in Interim-Site 93's break room. Given the history of positive collaboration with GoI-1469 and the importance of maintaining this relationship as the Foundation establishes presence in the Indian subcontinent, this letter and its contents were made top priority. [[div class="blocknote"]] [[=]] [[size 120%]] **TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN AMONGST OUR FRIENDS:** [[/size]] [[/=]] We apologize for not going to you first. It's been worse. Much worse. Swarms upon //swarms// of pests. The fields are black with so many flies. Nothing is working. We took the liberty of telling Méndez first. In a... gentle way, of course. Have you come to find anything about these new seeds? [[>]] Your //dearest// friends, The House of The Naga [[/>]] [[/div]] [[div class="jotting"]] [[=]] [[size 120%]] **TO THE HOUSE:** [[/size]] [[/=]] We're so sorry to hear. Trust us, we're doing this as fast as we can. On the seeds - they're utterly normal. Different, in a genetic way, but utterly normal save for those same marks that we see. Exact same creator, exact same strength; which is to say barely any at all. We'll keep you updated. And what do you mean by "gentle"? [[>]] Wyle [[/>]] [[/div]] [[div class="blocknote"]] [[=]] [[size 120%]] **TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN AMONGST OUR FRIENDS:** [[/size]] [[/=]] You'll see. [[>]] Your //dearest// friends, The House of The Naga [[/>]] [[/div]] [[div class="jotting"]] [[=]] [[size 150%]] **OFFICIAL STATEMENT OF THE MÉNDEZ CORPORATION** [[/size]] [[size 120%]] **LIVE FRESH, EAT FRESHER!** [[/size]] [[/=]] ---- It has been brought to our attention that our SuperSeeds appear to have created some isolated problems with pests. We at Méndez are regretful for these problems experienced, and assure all our customers that this will not occur again. New, improved SuperDuperSeeds (trademark pending) will be distributed to these growers! Please report to your nearest Méndez representative. Additionally, affected growers can request new Bug-B-Gone pesticide from their representative, at minimal added cost! We also do not recommend assaulting your Méndez representative. Those found guilty will be charged to the fullest extent of the law. [[/div]] ------ [[=]] **Addendum 9680.7 - July 1973** [[/=]] ------ @@ @@ The following document and newspaper clipping were sent after a week of no response from GoI-1469 contacts. @@ @@ [[div class="blocknote"]] [[=]] [[size 120%]] **TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN AMONGST OUR FRIENDS:** [[/size]] [[/=]] We apologies for our silence. It has only been worse. So much worse. [[>]] Your friends, The House of The Naga [[/>]] [[/div]] The following has been translated from the original Punjabi. [[div class="jotting"]] [[div style="text-align: center"]] [[div class="unmargined" style="font-family: 'Cinzel'; font-size: 350%; margin: 2px 0 5px;"]] SAADA NEWS [[/div]] [[div class="unmargined" style="font-family: serif; font-size: 115%; border-top-style: solid; border-bottom-style: solid;"]] [[table style="border: none; width: 100%;"]] [[row]] [[cell]] VOL. 16, 10TH ISSUE [[/cell]] [[cell style="text-align: center;"]] JULY 18TH [[/cell]] [[cell style="text-align: right;"]] MERCHANTS ACCEPT NO REFUNDS [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] [[/div]] [[div class="unmargined" style="font-family: 'Anton'; font-size: 300%; margin: 2px 0 5px;"]] RASH OF SUICIDES PLAGUES PUNJAB [[/div]] [[div class="unmargined" style="font-family: 'Anton'; font-size: 215%; margin: 2px 0 5px;"]] RISK TO FOOD SUPPLY POSSIBLE, SAYS TOP POPULATION SCIENTISTS [[/div]] [[div class="unmargined" style="font-family:serif; font-size:120%;"]] //By Ali Das// [[/div]] [[/div]] [[div style="text-align:justify;"]] TARN TARAN - A plague of recent farmer suicides continue, with twenty suicides overnight reported from three villages in Tarn Taran District. All victims are farmers, causing villagers to worry that crops may go unharvested due to the sudden loss of manpower. Most were above the age of 50. Family of a number of the deceased raised concerns regarding long hours, exhaustion, and overwork. @@ @@ [[div_ style="opacity: .66"]] Some also mention potential crop failures, and the News can confirm all had purchased seeds from Méndez India, a branch of the well-known American farming corporation. Méndez India has recently been in the public eye for strong-arm tactics in local agriculture markets. For the victims of these tragedies, authorities have made all crematoriums and burial services fee-free. Local MPs and PM Kumar have expressed sympathies for the deceased. Obituaries that the News has received can be found on the following pages. [[/div]] @@ @@ [[div_ style="opacity: .33"]] Exact methods of suicide remain unknown, and will remain unpublished out of respect for the deceased. Authorities encourage those to utilize resources and talk to family as needed, and to ensure all firearms and pesticides remain locked and used in a safe manner as guidance dictates. [[/div]] @@ @@ [[div_ style="opacity: .11"]] This has not been enough for residents, some of whom claim the national government and PM Kumar have been paid by Méndez to look the other way. [SEE FARMERS, PAGE 4] [[/div]] [[/div]] [[/div]] @@ @@ @@ @@ [[div class="blocknote"]] [[=]] [[size 120%]] **Wyle:** [[/size]] [[/=]] We have cremated twenty across three villages. Three //adjacent// villages. They are //dying// with these crops. At their own hands. These pesticides are good for killing more than just //makhi.//  [[footnote]] Flies in Punjabi. [[/footnote]] You must do //something.// There must be //some// foul play at work that escapes us. Please. [[>]] Jadhughar Singh [[/>]] [[/div]] Foundation contacts sent the following communication immediately on behalf of MP Singh. [[div class="email"]] [[=]] +++++ FROM THE DESK OF MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT KALYAN SINGH [[/=]] [[div class="tofrom"]] **TO:** ISAAC EVES, Méndez India CFO **FROM:** MP KALYAN SINGH [[/div]] ------ To Mr. Eves; By operating in India, you have chosen to make yourself beholden to Indian laws. A summons must be accepted and followed through with by the summoned, or a designated representative. I'm sure you can find one of those to spare. You may have blood on your hands. ~ MP KALYAN SINGH [[/div]] [[div class="email"]] [[=]] +++++ MÉNDEZ CORPORATION: LIVE FRESH, EAT FRESHER! [[/=]] [[div class="tofrom"]] **TO:** MP KALYAN SINGH **FROM:** ISAAC EVES, Méndez India CFO [[/div]] ------ To Singh; Fine. Our geneticist is on the way. Expect him in by the next week; if adequate accommodations aren't arranged, you //will// feel it next election. You people are so annoying. Fuck //us,// I guess, for rushing things a little. Every second wasted is market potential lost. Isaac Eves [[/div]] ------ [[=]] **Addendum 9680.8 - August 1973** [[/=]] ------ It was determined that the geneticist in question, Symon Craft, is a thaumaturge-for-hire known to Foundation authorities. Given that Mr. Craft's known capabilities do not extend beyond low-level reality manipulation, GoI-1469 contacts were permitted to summon him to interim-Site 93. The following is an audio log of the session, automatically recorded due to volume reaching a threshold for potential safety concerns. [[div class="jotting"]] **Singh:** —//knew,// you bastard! **Craft:** Knew what? **Singh:** That these were doomed seeds! Never to grow properly! You want to //kill us,// to choke us! **Craft:** I'm not sure why I'm here in all honesty. Back up a little please. You're getting spit on my jacket. This is company issue. I only get the one. **Singh:** You— **Wyle:** Back up. Let me ask. **Craft:** Okay, before you waste more of my time, company time — ask Mr. Eves. Corporate says I'm not allowed to tell you, even if I knew. I don't. **Wyle:** You're fucking with us. **Craft:** Not at all. In fact, try me. Go ahead. Check if I'm lying. I don't know. I may be a //criminal,// but I can follow a contract for a job. **Singh:** Trivial. //[There is the sound of sparks, then silence. Then a gasp.]// **Wyle:** He's not, is he? **Craft:** //See?// I've been telling you for the last hour, I was hired //only// to duplicate. Not ask questions about the content, genetic material, or seeds themselves. **Singh:** This is all you are? **Craft:** Yep. Sorry. Just a, erm, "temp for hire" as some of you may put it. Crude, but apt. **Singh:** I... I thought you'd be //more.// He told us you were his geneticist. **Craft:** Méndez is sorry to disappoint. //[There is silence.]// **Craft:** We //are.// I can get that in writing. **Singh:** You //will// be hearing about this. About all of it. **Craft:** Haven't I already? And oh, about the... problems. Méndez wanted me to tell you that this recent swath of...commitments... is a regrettable incident. However, and I quote, "we cannot be held liable for any consequences of using products, such as our Bug-B-Gone pesticide, not as intended." **[END LOG]** [[/div]] @@ @@ [[div class="blocknote"]] [[=]] [[size 120%]] **TO WYLE:** [[/size]] [[/=]] They're out of seeds. Everyone's swapped over, and sold whatever heirlooms they had. There's //not enough.// What do they grow? [[>]] Jadhughar Singh [[/>]] [[/div]] [[div class="jotting"]] [[=]] [[size 120%]] **TO SINGH:** [[/size]] [[/=]] We don't know. We're reaching out now. [[>]] Wyle [[/>]] [[/div]] ------ [[=]] **Addendum 9680.9 - September 1973** [[/=]] ------ [[div class="email"]] [[=]] +++++ MÉNDEZ CORPORATION: LIVE FRESH, EAT FRESHER! [[/=]] [[div class="tofrom"]] **TO:** MP KALYAN SINGH **FROM:** ISAAC EVES, Méndez India CFO [[/div]] ------ To Singh; This morning marks the eighth time you've contacted us in the last 72 hours. Tiffany is tired of screening your calls. To be clear; what magic are you //talking// about? These are proprietary Méndez GMOs. Science. That's all it is. We dabbled in a little woo-woo to cut down on growing time and costs, sure, but they're utterly normal otherwise. Sorry for the losses. Nothing that a few more generations can't fix! Isaac Eves [[/div]] Following this, a reclassification request was filed. Below is the proposed description for SCP-9680-EX. [[div class="blockquote"]] **Description:** SCP-9680-EX is the designation for over 45 varieties [[footnote]] Over a dozen have been introduced since original classification. [[/footnote]] of nonanomalous, genetically modified seeds produced by the Méndez Corporation. These seeds were and are produced anomalously to increase the scale of production, but otherwise carry no anomalous effects. SCP-9680-EX specimens have been prone to unique combinations of nearly 70 threats, including pathogens, pests, and intolerance to Indian climates. Farmers planting SCP-9680-EX report the following: * SCP-9680-EX purchasing requiring the selling of heirloom seed storage, resulting in near-total depletion of seed stock * Disruption of seed production of mature specimens * Increased rates of disease, especially cancer, in those exposed to SCP-9680 fields due to increased pesticide usage. SCP-9680-EX production is so widespread across the Indian subcontinent that attempts to curtail production or spread prove too great of a risk to Veil integrity. Foundation and GoI-1496 efforts are focused on harm mitigation. In spite of this, ##blue|[*https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers%27_suicides_in_India#Punjabi_Farmers'_Suicides_in_India current trends continue.]## [[/div]]
