SCP-9690 was seen later the same day tearing a page from his notebook, and sliding it under the cell door when Dr. Faron passed through the area. At the time, Foundation staff couldn't identify or seek clarification as to what information was exchanged, as Dr. Faron was suspended the following day, and SCP-9690 refused to provide further information.

This note was later suspected to contain personal information, such as SCP-9690's home address prior to containment. Information that the Foundation previously had trouble discovering, due to the anomalous effects of SCP-9690.

Investigation Log: Nocturne & Cipher:

Date: 13/02/25

Notice: Having my clearance level restricted, and by extension losing my powers at work, I’ve had to get creative with my investigation. Kyrie gave me a note with an address on it, but didn't enlighten me as to what I'm here to find or do. He also neglected to tell me where he keeps the spare key…

And I guess being fired isn't much of a concern now, may as well go for it.

Kyrie, if you read this, I promise I’ll buy you a new front door. And maybe also some wine, assuming you don’t take the bottle upside my head.

- Demi

<Begin Log>

The beginning of this log was cut for brevity.

Demi: Fuck, kicking doors in is harder than it looks on those crime shows.

The exterior of Kyrie’s home is reminiscent of a French Chateau, built two stories high out in the countryside of… I better not leak his address. Anyway, the walls are made of a polished and sleek limestone, with large pillars supporting the ceiling and an intricate carved design in the oak door. Which is hanging off the hinges, currently.

Demi: Well, I’ll give it to you Ky, it’s a nice place…

The main hall is adorned with various bits of memorabilia from what I assume are Kyrie’s past personas. A tailored black and crimson suit from his first radio broadcast, an electric guitar which I guess was from his first attempt at being a rockstar, and naturally a Bechstein piano front and centre for the skylight to shine on.

Demi: Now just to find where you keep your less flashy stuff.

Going through the hall and into the main set of corridors, I eventually find my way to the basement. There’s nothing particularly special, it just looks like a basement, with maybe a catacombs style mood to it.

Inside his basement there’s a set of boxes tucked away in the back, holding old diaries, song lyrics, sheet music and one particular document of interest. A contract, with the Nocturne & Cipher insignia stamped on in very shiny ink.

Demi: Finally…

Five minutes of looking at legal terms on my phone.

Demi: Useless legal jargon… Couple fancy signatures… Oh here we are. “To the beneficiary who signs on the dot, their legacy shall be long remembered, so long as they cannot.”

[PAUSE]

Demi: Really, Ky? You fell for that? It’s like something out of a fairytale for god’s sake. Maybe I did put too much stock in him, actually.

I place the contract and all the other evidence relating to Nocturne & Cipher into my bag and head back upstairs.

Demi: Oh well, mission accomplished.

I look over at the obliterated front door.

Demi: I should get that fixed though.

<End Log>

Senior Leadership Meeting Regarding SCP-9690 and Project Mnemosyne:

Date: 23/02/25

Staff: Director Louis Valencia, Dr. Demi Faron

Subject: SCP-9690

<Begin Log>

SCP-9690 is sitting opposite Director Valencia and Dr. Faron, crossing his arms and staring with a flat expression.

Director Valencia: I didn’t let you in my office for you to glare at me the entire time.

Dr. Faron: Both of you, please, just listen to me. I’m not here to fight either of you.

SCP-9690: You’ve certainly changed your tune by a couple keys then.

Dr. Faron: Kyrie, I am really sorry about what happened between us before. That was wrong of me, and I apologize.

SCP-9690: You’re sorry? Do sorry people deface the homes of those they apologize to? Is that an apology in your eyes?

Dr. Faron: I know, going through your home without permission and… ransacking your basement wasn’t great, but it got me somewhere. I’ve looked into Nocturne and Cipher, and into your contract. That business went bust way back in the 70’s, and because of the terms binding you, we can void your contract. You could be free again.

SCP-9690 raises his eyebrow and huffs.

SCP-9690: You’re lying.

Director Valencia: He’s not, for whatever my opinion on the matter is worth to you.

Dr. Faron rubs the back of his neck and clears his throat.

Dr. Faron: The legal department believes that you’d have to give up on the thing that you signed for. You could be remembered by anyone, but you wouldn’t get the legacy you hoped of, either.

SCP-9690: Oh so there it is, the catch, the dagger beneath the cloak…

Dr. Faron: I really do appreciate that it’s asking you to abandon your life’s work, but it’s the best I’ve got at the moment.

SCP-9690 lunges forward and glares at Dr. Faron. Dr. Faron doesn't move.

SCP-9690: Your best isn’t enough, Demi! You can’t just fucking ask that!

Dr. Faron hesitantly reaches out for SCP-9690, but retracts it when SCP-9690 begins to tear up.

[Several seconds pass quietly.]

Director Valencia: We’ll move on to the next segment then.

Dr. Faron looks down at the floor for a few seconds while running his hand through his hair.

Dr. Faron: We can… attempt to do something else.

SCP-9690: Attempt what?

Dr. Faron: The Foundation has their own nomology team in the legal department, and if you were open to it… we could draft up a contract. You could sign, and we would do all we can to be fair.

[PAUSE]

Dr. Faron: I’d completely understand if you wanted to be done with all this and just… go live your life.

Director Valencia: To put it simply for you, Kyrie, you either keep your anomalous trait and stay at the Foundation with Demi, or we free you from your anomalous contract. If you were free, however, we would have to erase your memories of the past, and of Demi.

SCP-9690 cups his hands over his face and leans forward in his seat, tensing up and hyperventilating.

Dr. Faron places his hand on SCP-9690's shoulder.

Dr. Faron: If you agree to stay, I promise I will do all I can to make it worth it, and fair on you. You don't need to choose right this second.

SCP-9690: You would let me choose? Without anything shady?

Dr. Faron: Yes, I would. You’re the top priority.

[PAUSE]

Director Valencia: Or, you can stick with your current contract, and the world keeps turning.

SCP-9690 silently cries for several seconds.

SCP-9690: I don’t know… I just— I need time! Time to uhm, think…

Dr. Faron nods softly and stands up with SCP-9690, preparing to take him back to the containment area.

<End Log>

SCP-9690 Video Log #3:

Date: 29/02/25

Subject: SCP-9690

<Begin Log>

11:03PM: SCP-9690 is sat at a table in his containment chamber, holding the proposed contract in one hand, and a cup of tea in the other.

11:18PM: SCP-9690 remains in this position for fifteen minutes.

11:19PM: SCP-9690 picks up a pen from the table and brings the point to the contract, but does not write anything.

11:39PM: SCP-9690 repeats this action four more times over the next twenty minutes.

11:43PM: SCP-9690 stands up to brew another cup of tea, leaning forward on the counter while the kettle boils.

11:48PM: SCP-9690 pours the boiling water into their cup and stirs with a spoon.

12:07AM: SCP-9690 continues stirring and staring into the water.

12:08AM: SCP-9690 startles, before taking a sip of his tea and sighing. He leaves the mostly full cup on the counter.

12:10AM: SCP-9690 sits back down at the table and picks up the pen.

12:14AM: SCP-9690 looks to the piano on the other side of the room.

12:17AM: SCP-9690 takes several deep breaths, and begins to write on the contract.

<End Log>

Project Mnemosyne: Contractual Agreement between the SCP Foundation and SCP-9690:

Date: 11/03/25

Approved By: Director Louis Valencia

Signatory: SCP-9690

Outlined in the following agreement are the terms and conditions set forth by both parties. Any revisions to this agreement must be approved by both parties and signed by an administrative member of staff.

The full version of this agreement may be accessed through your on-site RAISA liaison.

SCP-9690 will be designated as a Class-IV (limited civilian) anomaly, and will receive the privileges and permissions associated with this rank, in accordance with the Ethics Committee Guidelines on Humanoid Anomalies.

SCP-9690 may:

• Transfer between Foundation facilities when not in active containment.
• Visit public areas with supervision from at least two Class-C personnel.
• Purchase any personal amenities through Foundation requisitions, provided that no individual item poses a security risk.
• Only participate in Foundation projects for a maximum of 50 hours per week.

In exchange for their new rank, SCP-9690 acknowledges:

• They must participate in Project Mnemosyne, and any operations it may involve.
• Their public identity will be changed once every ten years.
• They may not provide or disseminate information about the Foundation or its operations to non-Foundation personnel.
• That this agreement may only be negotiated once per full ten-year term of service.

Signed,

- Dr. Demi Faron, Head of R&D, Department of Paramedicine. Kyrie Morningstar

Video Log – Kyrie’s Residence:

Date: 27/03/25

Personnel: Dr. Demi Faron, Kyrie Morningstar

<Begin Log>

Kyrie leads Demi into the main hall of his home, where various bits and pieces of his past stage personas are on display.

Kyrie: Are you just going to stand there and ogle my belongings, or can I get some attention too? I got dressed up for you, you know, and if I’m correct… this isn’t your first visit.

Demi: Just appreciating the history. You’ve lived a hundred lives, and with all this lying about I might as well have a look-see. You’re certainly showing your true colours though, first night together outside of the site, and you’re twice as sassy already.

Demi walks over to a pile of boxes in the corner with strips of black leather and the point of some heels sticking out.

Demi: What’s in this one? The one marked ‘Absolutely Not’ in pink highlighter?

Kyrie: That would be the outfits from my 2004 tour of America. We do not speak of them, and guests certainly don’t look at them—

Demi: Noted. And this one? ‘We Made You”?

Kyrie: It’s all just old memorabilia from shows, tours, my radio days… Some things never made it onto the album, so to speak.

Demi: Is the violin real?

Kyrie: Of course it is, Demi. It's a Stradivarius, as a matter of fact. And come to think of that too, someone promised me a solo.

Kyrie turns away from the kitchen and gestures towards the violin while raising an eyebrow.

Demi: You mean you promised yourself that I’d do that?

[PAUSE]

Demi: After dinner, star.

Kyrie: I’m holding you to it.

Demi and Kyrie walk into the kitchen. Bell peppers, onions, garlic, chicken, andouille sausage and several other ingredients are placed neatly over the kitchen island.

Demi: So, what are we having, beautiful?

Kyrie: I—it’s jambalaya! Very rustic, and uhm… it’s very civilian.

Demi: Nothing wrong with comfort food, Kyrie. You could incinerate it, and it’d be leagues above the cafeteria food at work.

Kyrie: Uhm… do you promise? If I’m being honest, it’s been a few decades since I last cooked for someone, and it’s got me a bit nervous.

Kyrie picks up a knife and begins preparing the vegetables meticulously. Demi sits down at the kitchen table and watches.

Demi: Don’t worry about this lovely home cooked meal being your culinary master class. My eyes aren’t even on the food anyhow.

Kyrie: Ah—Well that’s lovely, I’m certainly uhm… thank you.

Demi stands up, pours some oil into the pan and turns the heat on, gracing his hand over Kyrie’s back as he steps beside him.

Demi: Really, star, relax. Do you want me to help out or just keep watching?

Kyrie: Go put on some music or something, please. Your lack of shame keeps taking me away from my knife skills.

Demi steps out of the kitchen and plays one of the vinyl records from Kyrie’s collection.

Demi: Spends months vying for my attention, finally gets it, too shy to handle all of this—

Kyrie: I heard that, espèce de salaud effronté!7

Demi: All you heard was your beautiful piano playing and that skillet.

Kyrie chucks the vegetables into the pan with a huff.

Demi: This is the piece you played when you first got your piano at the site. Is this your favourite or something?

Kyrie: I made it during a particularly lonely time back in the 90’s… It’s not the flashiest thing I’ve ever done, but something about it draws me in and keeps everything else out.

He stirs the vegetables with repetitive flicks of his wrist and movements of the pan, looking off out the window.

Demi: Oh, so you were trying to get me to leave you alone.

Demi returns to the kitchen, smirks, and places his hand on Kyrie’s lower back.

Kyrie: You are… absolutely impossible.

Kyrie washes the rice and puts it into the pot with some crushed tomatoes and chicken stock.

Kyrie: For one of these nifty “one-pot” meals, it’s easy to burn things.

Demi: To be fair, handsome, you’d do better if you were looking at the pot.

Kyrie pauses his stirring, his shoulders slumping just a bit.

Kyrie: I’m not used to being this… domestic, so I’m staring at the birds instead of the hawk gawking at me.

Demi leans forward and stands behind Kyrie, and wraps his arms around his waist.

Demi: I’m not watching you because I think you’ll fail, or you aren’t performing well enough. I'm watching because, after months of reports and sterile rooms, fighting with a shitbag of a boss, I finally get to see you. All those other times I got Kyrie the idol, the star. Now I get Kyrie, and some space to breathe and enjoy him.

Kyrie: Oh.

Kyrie is silent for a few moments, leaning back into Demi’s chest. He takes a breath and adds the sausage back to the pot, putting a lid on it.

Kyrie: Well… the star would like some wine, and I’d like to continue the hug. Dinner needs to simmer for a while.

Demi: Then we’ll have a drink and relax on the couch.

Demi guides Kyrie down onto the couch in the living room, then steps out to the kitchen to pour some drinks.

Kyrie: I promise I only keep good wine.

Demi: There were never any doubts. I knew from the start you liked a bit of spoiling.

Demi comes back into the room with two glasses of wine and places them on the table.

Demi: If it’s alright with you, I’d like to… chat about everything. That’s happened lately, I mean.

Kyrie: I suppose that’s fine, though I’m not excited for it.

Kyrie takes a large gulp of his drink, blinking a few times after.

Demi: That’s understandable. But let me start out by saying that I’m sorry. I’m really, sorry. The way I spoke to you before all that drama with Louis wasn’t acceptable, and I swear to you I won’t take that tone on again.

Kyrie: Your apology is accepted. I pushed at you at a vulnerable time, and I didn’t give you the effort you were putting in, so please don’t feel as if any of this is only on you.

Demi: I’m not upset about that anymore, Ky. I just wanted this… out, so we can move on without anything itching at us, you know?

Kyrie: Of course, no one wants any baggage, as they say.

Demi: Brilliant, we agree then.

Demi has a sip of his wine and runs a hand over Kyrie’s hair playfully.

Kyrie: Now about my door.

Demi: Okay that I think I’m justified in. Me tactically acquiring your contract saved our arses, and I fixed the door! Both necessary evils.

Kyrie: Oh, pour l'amour de tout ce qui est sacré,8what am I going to do with you?

Demi: I’ll make a point to learn French if I’m going to date you, thank you for the reminder my darling.

Kyrie props his head up in his palm, lying down on his side with his other hand on his hip after briefly flipping Demi the bird.

Kyrie: What do couples usually do in the downtime, Cher?

[PAUSE]

Demi: We could watch some of your old works while we wait for dinner?

Kyrie rolls over and slumps into the couch, closing his eyes.

Kyrie: Oh for… Close the curtains, Demi.

Demi: It’s been a long time coming, star. I’ll wake you up when dinner’s done.

<End Log>

Any pending works from a previous identity are to be released posthumously. All media coverage of a previous identity must cease after a maximum of five years after discontinuation. When touring Foundation facilities, SCP-9690 must be accompanied by one member of staff when not in active containment. The conditions outlined in SCP-9690’s contract with Dr. D. Faron[[footnote]]Level 3 medical researcher and head of Project Mnemosyne. [[/footnote]]dictate that any use of SCP-9690’s anomalous capabilities as medical treatment must be approved by Dr. Faron directly. ----- **##rgb(229, 214,157)|Description:##** SCP-9690 is a humanoid male of undetermined origin. Prior to Foundation capture, he was employed as a performer in the entertainment industry. **Key Characteristics:** • Exaggerated traits of albinism, causing SCP-9690 to present with a solid-white skin tone and a crimson hair colour. • A preference towards high fashion and extravagant clothing. • A Transatlantic accent with abnormal speech patterns. SCP-9690 exhibits a low-level cognitohazardous effect, targeting the hippocampus and neocortex regions of the brain. Acute exposure to SCP-9690 through any medium is associated with improved cognitive performance and memory. Individuals exposed to this effect will forget about SCP-9690 one-week post-exposure. Any memories unrelated to SCP-9690's person are unaffected. Chronic exposure appears to lessen the effects, allowing an individual to retain their memory of SCP-9690 for longer than one week. This has not been studied to the same extent as acute exposure, and is not confirmed as fact. Project Mnemosyne is being conducted by Dr. D. Faron, to determine how the anomalous traits of SCP-9690 can be used to improve the general memory and cognitive ability of humans. ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)|SCP-9690 Meeting with Dr. Demi Faron: Interview #1:##** **Date:** 12/02/24 **Staff:** Dr. D. Faron **Subject:** SCP-9690 **Notice:** Any audio recordings made by SCP-9690 have been attached to their relevant place within this document. Most recordings were made after the fact, and have been catalogued as insights into SCP-9690's emotional state. [[include :scp-wiki:component:audio-player-woed-source |unique-name= |audio-file= http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/scp-9690/ATWT%20-%20Kyrie%27s%20Dance.mp3 |background-color=rgb(22, 23, 33) |border-color=rgb(229, 214, 157) |border-radius=0.313rem |dropshadow-color=rgba(12, 12, 12, 0.15) |text-color=rgb(229, 214, 157) |icons-color=rgb(103, 80, 181) |player-color=rgb(229, 214, 157) |progress-color=rgb(103, 80, 181) ]] ----- **** //Dr. Faron enters SCP-9690’s containment cell. The area has been decorated with Art Nouveau furniture from the early 1900s, a bar with several types of spirits, and a large fireplace at the back wall of the room.// //SCP-9690 is lying across a chaise lounge in the centre of the room, nursing a glass of wine.// **SCP-9690:** A little young to be a doctor, are you not? //SCP-9690 stands from his chaise lounge and offers a handshake to Dr. Faron.// **SCP-9690:** I’m only winding you up. I’m Kyrie, cher[[footnote]]French for "Dear"[[/footnote]]. //Dr. Faron accepts the handshake with a slight pause and a smile. He places a project file down on the tea table.// **Dr. Faron:** Thank you kindly, uh, Kyrie… My name is Demi, by the way. **SCP-9690:** It’s a pleasure to meet, Demi. **Dr. Faron:** Do you mind if I have a seat? I'd be cheeky and reach for the kettle, but I haven't got much time today, unfortunately. **SCP-9690:** Be my guest, bon monsieur[[footnote]]French for "good sir"[[/footnote]]. We can get to know each other better another time. //SCP-9690 lies back down, and gestures to an ornate armchair opposite him.// **SCP-9690:** Your colleagues must love you though, surely. **Dr. Faron:** Colleagues being the key word... //Dr. Faron sits down opposite SCP-9690, looking at a row of albums made by SCP-9690 and smiling warmly.// **Dr. Faron:** I remember seeing one of your shows a few years ago in London. It was so beautiful, even my wallet was happy afterwards. **SCP-9690:** Hopefully it was worth it. I do aspire to leave an impression, and a pleasant one at that. A few human rights violations are all I receive in return... //SCP-9690 begins writing in his notebook. The pen tears through the paper at times.// **Dr. Faron:** Yeah, I uhm... understand coming here isn't a pleasant experience, but there could be something wrong with you. //SCP-9690 has another sip of wine, his expression subduing into a frown.// **SCP-9690:** Are you insinuating that I'm ill? //Dr. Faron stares past SCP-9690 for a few seconds, jolting slightly as his attention comes back to the conversation.// **Dr. Faron:** No! Of course not, it's just that— **SCP-9690:** In that case you won't mind me leaving, right doctor? You don't need a patient that hasn't got a problem. //SCP-9690 attempts to stand up, but Dr. Faron ushers him back into the seat.// **Dr. Faron:** Easy there, Kyrie, you can't leave yet. You have got a problem, it's just... not a typical one, so you’re staying. //SCP-9690 gently nudges Dr. Faron’s hand away, before dusting off his shirt and sighing.// **SCP-9690:** From where I'm sitting the only problem we have between us is you keeping me away from work. //SCP-9690 looks around, focusing on sheet music, albums, and his notebook.// //Dr. Faron frowns softly and sits up straight, leaning towards SCP-9690.// **Dr. Faron:** It's right to be upset, being in captivity, but we can work together. **SCP-9690:** In what way? If you wanted a backstage pass, you only needed to ask. //Dr. Faron raises his eyebrows for a few seconds, before giving an open palm gesture towards SCP-9690.// **Dr. Faron:** Should we do it business or casual? //SCP-9690 cocks an eyebrow for a moment, then relaxes into his seat, having a sip of his wine.// **SCP-9690:** You were in a rush, last I checked. Business for tonight only, doctor. //Dr. Faron leans back into his chair and sighs, cupping his hands over his face to mask a grin. His shoulders ease up and his posture softens.// **Dr. Faron:** I’ll cut it dry for you then. I could really benefit from someone of your abilit— talents, for a project of mine. If we harnessed your talents, I'm sure we could get you a stage anywhere in the world. [PAUSE] **Dr. Faron:** What would you like in return for a “yes”? **SCP-9690:** A better wine wouldn’t do harm. **Dr. Faron:** Be serious, answer the question. //SCP-9690 stares at the fireplace for several moments, bringing his hands together and rubbing circles on the inside of his wrist.// **SCP-9690:** I only want an audience... Even just an audience of one? **Dr. Faron:** Deal. //SCP-9690 sits up and shakes Dr. Faron’s hand with both of his own, offering an uneasy smile.// **SCP-9690:** Thank you… **** [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)|Kyrie's Notebook Entry #1:##** **Date:** 12/02/24 **Notes:** These notebook entries have been provided by SCP-9690 after 27/03/25, to provide additional context to personnel reading this document. ----- Oh, Kyrie, you absolute genius. That talk went right as rain for him, left with everything he wanted, and you're still stuck in the first act. When did you get so easy? I think you ought to relax on that fucking bottle if that's the performance you're putting up! Next time he's here, do better, or he'll have you lounge singing in the breakroom next... [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)|Director Louis Valencia Meeting with Dr. Demi Faron: Consult #1:##** **Date:** 19/02/24 **Staff:** Director Louis Valencia, Dr. Demi Faron ----- **** //Dr. Faron enters Director Valencia’s office and places a large folder onto his desk. I only assigned you this morning. //Both men pause for a second, before Director Valencia checks the date.// **Director Valencia:** Please don't tell me you came up with this in the couple minutes it takes to get from his cell to my office. **Dr. Faron:** Are you still not understanding how much better society could be with sharper minds? **Director Valencia:** It's easy to understand. Where me and you run into problems, however, is when we start talking about why you can't achieve that. **Dr. Faron:** And every time I get a bullshit answer about nature or ethics. **Director Valencia:** Our goal within the Foundation is to preserve nature. Tell me a downside to smarter research staff, or sharper task force units, or even just more organized janitors. **Director Valencia:** There isn’t one in that perfect scenario you keep imagining. //Dr. Faron leans forward and clasps his hands together tightly.// **Dr. Faron:** Do you know how fragile of a thing memory is? You’ve got kids, what if you forgot them tomorrow? It’s not likely to happen, but you’d be in pieces if it did. I can change that—stop that from happening to people! **Director Valencia:** They say a war against nature is inevitably a war against yourself. //Director Valencia cups his hands on the desk and softens his tone.// **Director Valencia:** Using an anomaly as a catalyst for your project, regardless of whether or not it's suited for the task, it's just... it isn't safe. **Dr. Faron:** And that’s a risk that I’m consenting to! So what if Kyrie’s anomalous? We have no issues wiping people’s memory, but when you want to help some poor old woman with dementia, or a veteran with Alzheimer’s, suddenly we’re tampering with the ‘natural’ balance too much— //Director Valencia clenches his hands together on the desk and glares at Dr. Faron.// **Director Valencia:** Demi, listen to me without arguing, this one time. You don’t know what he wants from you, we don’t know the extent of his anomalous nature, and I am not entertaining this conversation. Project Mnemosyne is not going any further, and if I find out about you continuing your research, you're going straight to a disciplinary. //Dr. Faron stands up from his chair and storms through the doorway.// **** [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)|SCP-9690 Meeting with Dr. Demi Faron: Interview #2:##** **Date:** 20/05/24 **Staff:** Dr. Demi Faron **Subject:** SCP-9690 ----- **** //SCP-9690 is sat at a piano, having played consistently for 10 minutes prior to Dr. Faron’s arrival. The fireplace is the only source of light in the room.// **Dr. Faron:** Enjoying yourself there? **SCP-9690:** Oh, it’s magnificent, cher! Bless you, really! //Dr. Faron sets up a blood draw kit beside the chaise lounge.// **Dr. Faron:** You’re still happy to do some tests? Maybe continue our chat from before while we’re at it? //SCP-9690 plays a key out of scale by mistake.// **SCP-9690:** Uhm, yes, yes of course. Just another minute of playing first... Sit and enjoy before you get any ideas about pricking me, doctor. **Dr. Faron:** No problem. //Dr. Faron sits down on the armchair present beside the chaise lounge, watching SCP-9690’s fingers glide over the keys and listening to the harmonies being played.// **Dr. Faron:** Y’know, I might not be as good as you with the arts, but I do pretty well with the violin. **SCP-9690:** What? You should’ve brought one! We could’ve played a duet together. **Dr. Faron:** Too much work to do, unfortunately, but I’m sure I’ll find the time for it someday. **SCP-9690:** Oh, but I know such a beautiful piece for the piano and violin! Of course, it’s a bit modern for my taste, it released in 2013, but you would love the experience… **Dr. Faron:** Very clever, now come on. Up you get. //SCP-9690 moves away from the piano and dramatically faints onto the chaise lounge, extending his left arm to Dr. Faron.// **SCP-9690:** Your lack of enthusiasm wounds me, Demi. Perhaps more than your instrument of misery will. **Dr. Faron:** Needles scare you that bad? **SCP-9690:** Well, they say that the average person has 7 true fears. I’ve known you a week and you’ve discovered one already. Gold star for you. **Dr. Faron:** Hopefully the next one isn’t blood. Why don’t you tell me more about your past? //Dr. Faron checks his watch briefly, then smiles at SCP-9690 reassuringly.// **SCP-9690:** I could bring myself to tell a little about the golden age, whilst you make an attempt on my life to make sure I've been getting my five-a-day. **Dr. Faron:** You’ve lived through a couple golden ages. You’re a very vintage… well, human. **SCP-9690:** The golden age of radio, Piqûre effrontée[[footnote]]French for "Cheeky prick"[[/footnote]]. //Dr. Faron takes SCP-9690’s wrist and wipes it with a sterile wipe.// //SCP-9690 kicks up in his seat and looks around the room with a slight frown.// **SCP-9690:** To set a scene, it was 1927, and I was a young star, not yet signed, making a lowly experience as a radio drama host on the evening broadcasts. Every night I would read different stories to the listeners, working through a novel over the week and doing one-offs on the weekends. Things got to a point where I started sleeping in the studio, practicing every waking hour and dreaming of the results when I slept. **Dr. Faron:** Sounds a bit pedestrian, compared to how you like to live now. //SCP-9690 turns his head away from Dr. Faron and rests his cheek in his free hand while scoffing.// **SCP-9690:** Eventually after countless nights slaving away for public entertainment, I was offered a deal with one of the bigger corporations in the entertainment industry. Noct— uhm, a corporation signed me on the 19th of June 1927, and from that day on my nightly broadcasts became a sensation, sweeping the airwaves and solidifying my position in the industry. [PAUSE] **SCP-9690:** On the condition that I kept up the pace... The passing of time doesn't do favours, though. //Dr. Faron leaves the needle inserted into SCP-9690’s arm, jotting down some notes on his pad.// **Dr. Faron:** Where did you find the time to eat during this schedule? Socialize? Even just resting, for that matter. //Both SCP-9690 and Dr. Faron glance over at some makeup on SCP-9690's table before looking back at each other.// **SCP-9690:** People started to recognize me in the local café, lounge players tried to imitate my voice, and anywhere I went I was the bee’s knees. I had an appetite for legacy, not Coq au Vin[[footnote]]A French casserole with chicken, braised in wine.[[/footnote]]. **Dr. Faron:** I had gathered as much, Kyrie. **SCP-9690:** Mm. Things grew sour, however, when my listeners started to tune in to other shows, and people stopped greeting me in person. At first, I thought I was just in a dry spell, and that it would wither away with time… I’m stuck here with you now, so it did not. I found other jobs over the years, but the world just kept turning regardless. //SCP-9690 rests his chin in his hand and looks out of the window at the stars.// **SCP-9690:** It’s been a never-ending performance ever since. //Dr. Faron takes the blood samples and places them inside of his bag. He stares at his hands for a few seconds before looking back at SCP-9690 and smiling warmly.// **Dr. Faron:** That was an interesting story, Kyrie. I’d love to hear the rest of that song, if you don't mind finishing it? [PAUSE] **SCP-9690:** Another time, cher… but thank you for listening. **** [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)| SCP-9690 Video Log #1:##** **Date:** 10/06/24 **Staff:** Dr. Demi Faron ----- **** **10:05PM:** //Dr. Faron brings a few cups of coffee into his office and takes a seat at his desk.// //Several materials and documents relating to SCP-9690 are pinned up or placed around the room. He places both on the table beside SCP-9690.// **Dr. Faron:** I bring gifts, assuming you want company today. **SCP-9690:** That’s to be decided, I’m particular about my coffee. **Dr. Faron:** I don’t know if it’s your favourite, but it’s expensive. **SCP-9690:** You’re a dear. //SCP-9690 takes the drink and sips it slowly, relaxing his slouched posture soon after.// **Dr. Faron:** I brought the coat in case you wanted a walk through the gardens. **SCP-9690:** A walk? Alright then. **Dr. Faron:** As you wish your majesty. //SCP-9690 rolls his eyes a bit, before both men exit the room and walk towards the site gardens.// **SCP-9690:** I really did mean it, you know. ‘The audience of one’ bit? **Dr. Faron:** I never doubted it. **SCP-9690:** Don’t leave me out in the cold, Demi. **Dr. Faron:** I gave you a coat! You'd make an excellent florist. **Dr. Faron:** I don’t want you bored while we have our conversation, so please, enjoy the scenery. **SCP-9690:** Merci, cher. //SCP-9690 sits quietly for a few minutes, admiring the flower display and fiddling with the fur of his coat.// **SCP-9690:** May I... tell you a little more about my past? Tonight’s all about you. //SCP-9690 readjusts his position on the bench, leaning back into the support with a sigh.// **SCP-9690:** Like any half-decent story, there’s a question or idea that’s raised that eventually needs an answer or conclusion. For this story, that idea is “be careful what you wish for.” A wish and a need aren’t the same, and though this story was so long ago... I haven't told it until today. //Dr. Faron turns to face SCP-9690 and pays rapt attention to him.// //SCP-9690 takes a deep breath and squeezes his hands together.// **SCP-9690:** Looking at it in hindsight, knowing some of the strangeness that exists in this world now, I think my contract was shady. Ever since signing, it's like every time I'm mentioned, people's minds switch to a dead channel. **Dr. Faron:** We can help you, Kyrie. I don’t mean to be rude, but it’s just… //SCP-9690 wipes at his eyes with the back of his hand, taking down the remainder of his wine in a single gulp.// **SCP-9690:** I can't delude myself into thinking you can help, if there’s a chance you can’t. [PAUSE] **Dr. Faron:** I swear, Kyrie. I will not let you down. //SCP-9690 tenses up, before looking down and bringing a shaky arm around Dr. Faron's shoulders. They remain in this state for several moments.// **SCP-9690:** Thank you, Demi. [PAUSE] **Dr. Faron:** You’re welcome. **** [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)| Nocturne & Cipher RAISA Report:##** **Date of Recording:** 13/03/1915 **Release Date:** 03/12/24 **Group of Interest:** GoI-739 "Nocturne & Cipher" **Case Number:** 10-192-017 ----- Nocturne & Cipher were a front organization operating in the entertainment industry, funded by unknown investors from the early 1910s--1927. Their business practices revolved around entrapping artists and performers in agreements that were ironic or paradoxical in nature. The proposed benefits of these agreements were often honoured for a set period of time, before support from Nocturne & Cipher was ceased, and artists became stuck in a cycle fuelled by their intentions at the time of signing. It is currently unknown if contracts with Nocturne & Cipher may be voided, as few reports have been verified since their discovery, and no new reports have been filed since 1927. A tagline from 1926 was recovered from a radio broadcast: “Make Your Wish! We’ll Be Waiting.” [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)| SCP-9690 Video Log #2:##** **Date:** 10/01/25 **Subject:** SCP-9690 ----- **** **7:05PM:** //SCP-9690 is seen pacing around the room, with a stiff posture and his arms folded.// **7:06PM:** //Some stray crimson hairs are noted on the table SCP-9690 usually sits at.// **7:07PM:** //The fresh bottle of wine delivered the previous morning is now half empty.// **7:11PM:** //SCP-9690 looks up at the clock above the fireplace.// **SCP-9690:** Where the fuck is he? **7:13PM:** //SCP-9690 looks through the window to the site courtyard for a few seconds.// **SCP-9690:** It's been six days for fuck's sake... You have to come tonight... **7:14PM:** //SCP-9690 places his ear to the entrance of his room.// //SCP-9690 remains still for 30 seconds.// **7:15PM:** //SCP-9690 steps away from the door and begins pacing around the room again.// **SCP-9690:** I'm sure he's just... running a little late! There must be some heavy paperwork, an urgent meeting, his car blew up and he can't get to work... And maybe also some wine, assuming you don’t take the bottle upside my head. - Demi ----- **** //The beginning of this log was cut for brevity.// **Demi:** Fuck, kicking doors in is harder than it looks on those crime shows. //The exterior of Kyrie’s home is reminiscent of a French Chateau, built two stories high out in the countryside of… I better not leak his address. Which is hanging off the hinges, currently.// **Demi:** Well, I’ll give it to you Ky, it’s a nice place… //The main hall is adorned with various bits of memorabilia from what I assume are Kyrie’s past personas. I’m not here to fight either of you. **SCP-9690:** You’ve certainly changed your tune by a couple keys then. **Dr. Faron:** Kyrie, I am really sorry about what happened between us before. That was wrong of me, and I apologize. **SCP-9690:** You’re sorry? Do sorry people deface the homes of those they apologize to? Is that an apology in your eyes? **Dr. Faron:** I know, going through your home without permission and… ransacking your basement wasn’t great, but it got me somewhere. I’ve looked into Nocturne and Cipher, and into your contract. That business went bust way back in the 70’s, and because of the terms binding you, we can void your contract. You could be free again. //SCP-9690 raises his eyebrow and huffs.// **SCP-9690:** You’re lying. **Director Valencia:** He’s not, for whatever my opinion on the matter is worth to you. //Dr. Faron rubs the back of his neck and clears his throat.// **Dr. Faron:** The legal department believes that you’d have to give up on the thing that you signed for. You could be remembered by anyone, but you wouldn’t get the legacy you hoped of, either. **SCP-9690:** Oh so there it is, the catch, the dagger beneath the cloak… **Dr. Faron:** I really do appreciate that it’s asking you to abandon your life’s work, but it’s the best I’ve got at the moment. //SCP-9690 lunges forward and glares at Dr. Faron. Dr. Faron doesn't move.// **SCP-9690:** Your best isn’t enough, Demi! You can’t just fucking ask that! //Dr. Faron hesitantly reaches out for SCP-9690, but retracts it when SCP-9690 begins to tear up.// [Several seconds pass quietly.] **Director Valencia:** We’ll move on to the next segment then. //Dr. Faron looks down at the floor for a few seconds while running his hand through his hair.// **Dr. Faron:** We can… attempt to do something else. **SCP-9690:** Attempt what? **Dr. Faron:** The Foundation has their own nomology team in the legal department, and if you were open to it… we could draft up a contract. You could sign, and we would do all we can to be fair. [PAUSE] **Dr. Faron:** I’d completely understand if you wanted to be done with all this and just… go live your life. **Director Valencia:** To put it simply for you, Kyrie, you either keep your anomalous trait and stay at the Foundation with Demi, or we free you from your anomalous contract. If you were free, however, we would have to erase your memories of the past, and of Demi. //SCP-9690 cups his hands over his face and leans forward in his seat, tensing up and hyperventilating.// //Dr. Faron places his hand on SCP-9690's shoulder.// **Dr. Faron:** If you agree to stay, I promise I will do all I can to make it worth it, and fair on you. You don't need to choose right this second. **SCP-9690:** You would let me choose? Without anything shady? **Dr. Faron:** Yes, I would. You’re the top priority. [PAUSE] **Director Valencia:** Or, you can stick with your current contract, and the world keeps turning. //SCP-9690 silently cries for several seconds.// **SCP-9690:** I don’t know… I just— I need time! Time to uhm, think… //Dr. Faron nods softly and stands up with SCP-9690, preparing to take him back to the containment area.// **** [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)| SCP-9690 Video Log #3:##** **Date:** 29/02/25 **Subject:** SCP-9690 ----- **** **11:03PM:** //SCP-9690 is sat at a table in his containment chamber, holding the proposed contract in one hand, and a cup of tea in the other.// **11:18PM:** //SCP-9690 remains in this position for fifteen minutes.// **11:19PM:** //SCP-9690 picks up a pen from the table and brings the point to the contract, but does not write anything.// **11:39PM:** //SCP-9690 repeats this action four more times over the next twenty minutes.// **11:43PM:** //SCP-9690 stands up to brew another cup of tea, leaning forward on the counter while the kettle boils.// **11:48PM:** //SCP-9690 pours the boiling water into their cup and stirs with a spoon.// **12:07AM:** //SCP-9690 continues stirring and staring into the water.// **12:08AM:** //SCP-9690 startles, before taking a sip of his tea and sighing. He leaves the mostly full cup on the counter.// **12:10AM:** //SCP-9690 sits back down at the table and picks up the pen.// **12:14AM:** //SCP-9690 looks to the piano on the other side of the room.// **12:17AM:** //SCP-9690 takes several deep breaths, and begins to write on the contract.// **** [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)|Project Mnemosyne: Contractual Agreement between the SCP Foundation and SCP-9690:##** ----- **Date:** 11/03/25 **Approved By:** Director Louis Valencia **Signatory:** SCP-9690 Outlined in the following agreement are the terms and conditions set forth by both parties. Any revisions to this agreement must be approved by both parties and signed by an administrative member of staff. The full version of this agreement may be accessed through your on-site RAISA liaison. ----- SCP-9690 will be designated as a Class-IV (limited civilian) anomaly, and will receive the privileges and permissions associated with this rank, in accordance with the Ethics Committee Guidelines on Humanoid Anomalies. SCP-9690 may: • Transfer between Foundation facilities when not in active containment. • Visit public areas with supervision from at least two Class-C personnel. • Purchase any personal amenities through Foundation requisitions, provided that no individual item poses a security risk. • Only participate in Foundation projects for a maximum of 50 hours per week. In exchange for their new rank, SCP-9690 acknowledges: • They must participate in Project Mnemosyne, and any operations it may involve. • Their public identity will be changed once every ten years. • They may not provide or disseminate information about the Foundation or its operations to non-Foundation personnel. • That this agreement may only be negotiated once per full ten-year term of service. Signed, - Dr. Demi Faron, Head of R&D, Department of Paramedicine. Kyrie Morningstar [[/div]] ----- [[div class="blockquote"]] **##rgb(229, 214,157)|Video Log – Kyrie’s Residence:##** **Date:** 27/03/25 **Personnel:** Dr. Demi Faron, Kyrie Morningstar [[include :scp-wiki:component:audio-player-woed-source |unique-name=secretparty (only words, no numbers) |audio-file= http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/scp-9690/ATWT%20-%20Fall.mp3 |background-color=rgb(22, 23, 33) |border-color=rgb(229, 214, 157) |border-radius=0.313rem |dropshadow-color=rgba(12, 12, 12, 0.15) |text-color=rgb(229, 214, 157) |icons-color=rgb(103, 80, 181) |player-color=rgb(229, 214, 157) |progress-color=rgb(103, 80, 181) ]] ----- //Kyrie leads Demi into the main hall of his home, where various bits and pieces of his past stage personas are on display.// **Kyrie:** Are you just going to stand there and ogle my belongings, or can I get some attention too? I got dressed up for you, you know, and if I’m correct… this isn’t your first visit. **Demi:** Just appreciating the history. You’ve lived a hundred lives, and with all this lying about I might as well have a look-see. You’re certainly showing your true colours though, first night together outside of the site, and you’re twice as sassy already. //Demi walks over to a pile of boxes in the corner with strips of black leather and the point of some heels sticking out.// **Demi:** What’s in this one? The one marked ‘Absolutely Not’ in pink highlighter? **Kyrie:** That would be the outfits from my 2004 tour of America. We do not speak of them, and guests certainly don’t look at them— **Demi:** Noted. And this one? ‘We Made You”? **Kyrie:** It’s all just old memorabilia from shows, tours, my radio days… Some things never made it onto the album, so to speak. **Demi:** Is the violin real? **Kyrie:** Of course it is, Demi. It's a Stradivarius, as a matter of fact. And come to think of that too, someone promised me a solo. //Kyrie turns away from the kitchen and gestures towards the violin while raising an eyebrow.// **Demi:** You mean you promised yourself that I’d do that? [PAUSE] **Demi:** After dinner, star. **Kyrie:** I’m holding you to it. //Demi and Kyrie walk into the kitchen. Bell peppers, onions, garlic, chicken, andouille sausage and several other ingredients are placed neatly over the kitchen island.// **Demi:** So, what are we having, beautiful? **Kyrie:** I—it’s jambalaya! Very rustic, and uhm… it’s very civilian. **Demi:** Nothing wrong with comfort food, Kyrie. You could incinerate it, and it’d be leagues above the cafeteria food at work. **Kyrie:** Uhm… do you promise? If I’m being honest, it’s been a few decades since I last cooked for someone, and it’s got me a bit nervous. //Kyrie picks up a knife and begins preparing the vegetables meticulously. Demi sits down at the kitchen table and watches.//                                                                                           **Demi:** Don’t worry about this lovely home cooked meal being your culinary master class. My eyes aren’t even on the food anyhow. **Kyrie:** Ah—Well that’s lovely, I’m certainly uhm… thank you. //Demi stands up, pours some oil into the pan and turns the heat on, gracing his hand over Kyrie’s back as he steps beside him.// **Demi:** Really, star, relax. Do you want me to help out or just keep watching? **Kyrie:** Go put on some music or something, please. Your lack of shame keeps taking me away from my knife skills. //Demi steps out of the kitchen and plays one of the vinyl records from Kyrie’s collection.// **Demi:** Spends months vying for my attention, finally gets it, too shy to handle all of this— **Kyrie:** I heard that, espèce de salaud effronté![[footnote]]French for "You cheeky bastard!"[[/footnote]] **Demi:** All you heard was your beautiful piano playing and that skillet. //Kyrie chucks the vegetables into the pan with a huff.// **Demi:** This is the piece you played when you first got your piano at the site. Is this your favourite or something? **Kyrie:** I made it during a particularly lonely time back in the 90’s… It’s not the flashiest thing I’ve ever done, but something about it draws me in and keeps everything else out. //He stirs the vegetables with repetitive flicks of his wrist and movements of the pan, looking off out the window.// **Demi:** Oh, so you were trying to get me to leave you alone. //Demi returns to the kitchen, smirks, and places his hand on Kyrie’s lower back.// **Kyrie:** You are… absolutely impossible. //Kyrie washes the rice and puts it into the pot with some crushed tomatoes and chicken stock.// **Kyrie:** For one of these nifty “one-pot” meals, it’s easy to burn things. **Demi:** To be fair, handsome, you’d do better if you were looking at the pot. //Kyrie pauses his stirring, his shoulders slumping just a bit.// **Kyrie:** I’m not used to being this… domestic, so I’m staring at the birds instead of the hawk gawking at me. //Demi leans forward and stands behind Kyrie, and wraps his arms around his waist.// **Demi:** I’m not watching you because I think you’ll fail, or you aren’t performing well enough. I'm watching because, after months of reports and sterile rooms, fighting with a shitbag of a boss, I finally get to see you. All those other times I got Kyrie the idol, the star. Now I get Kyrie, and some space to breathe and enjoy him. **Kyrie:** Oh. //Kyrie is silent for a few moments, leaning back into Demi’s chest. He takes a breath and adds the sausage back to the pot, putting a lid on it.// **Kyrie:** Well… the star would like some wine, and I’d like to continue the hug. Dinner needs to simmer for a while. **Demi:** Then we’ll have a drink and relax on the couch. //Demi guides Kyrie down onto the couch in the living room, then steps out to the kitchen to pour some drinks.// **Kyrie:** I promise I only keep good wine. **Demi:** There were never any doubts. I knew from the start you liked a bit of spoiling. //Demi comes back into the room with two glasses of wine and places them on the table.// **Demi:** If it’s alright with you, I’d like to… chat about everything. That’s happened lately, I mean. **Kyrie:** I suppose that’s fine, though I’m not excited for it. //Kyrie takes a large gulp of his drink, blinking a few times after.// **Demi:** That’s understandable. But let me start out by saying that I’m sorry. I’m really, sorry. The way I spoke to you before all that drama with Louis wasn’t acceptable, and I swear to you I won’t take that tone on again. **Kyrie:** Your apology is accepted. I pushed at you at a vulnerable time, and I didn’t give you the effort you were putting in, so please don’t feel as if any of this is only on you. **Demi:** I’m not upset about that anymore, Ky. I just wanted this… out, so we can move on without anything itching at us, you know? **Kyrie:** Of course, no one wants any baggage, as they say. **Demi:** Brilliant, we agree then. //Demi has a sip of his wine and runs a hand over Kyrie’s hair playfully.// **Kyrie:** Now about my door. **Demi:** Okay that I think I’m justified in. Me tactically acquiring your contract saved our arses, and I fixed the door! Both necessary evils. **Kyrie:** Oh, pour l'amour de tout ce qui est sacré,[[footnote]]French for "for the love of all that is sacred"[[/footnote]]what am I going to do with you? **Demi:** I’ll make a point to learn French if I’m going to date you, thank you for the reminder my darling. //Kyrie props his head up in his palm, lying down on his side with his other hand on his hip after briefly flipping Demi the bird.// **Kyrie:** What do couples usually do in the downtime, Cher? [PAUSE] **Demi:** We could watch some of your old works while we wait for dinner? //Kyrie rolls over and slumps into the couch, closing his eyes.// **Kyrie:** Oh for… Close the curtains, Demi. **Demi:** It’s been a long time coming, star. I’ll wake you up when dinner’s done.     SCP-9696: Floods
    by: Merehrab

    ⚠️ Content warning: Depictions of institutional transphobia and queerphobia, misogyny, and transmisogyny.

⚠️ content warning

An SCP-9696-1 instance pursuing Agent Glendale, 1927.

Item #: SCP-9696

Object Class: Thaumiel

Special Containment Procedures: Knowledge of SCP-9696’s existence must not be disseminated to personnel below Level 6 clearance. A file summarizing the stage one effects of SCP-9696-1 is to be inserted in this slot for lower clearance levels. Should an unauthorized member of personnel access this file, they are to be detained and interrogated at Site-01, and amnesticized of their experience accessing the SCP-9696 file.

Any instances of SCP-9696-1 that are captured by video surveillance systems within Foundation sites are to be filtered by AIC algorithms, and O5-8 is to be directly notified of these newly manifested instances. Subjects affected by SCP-9696-1 are to be monitored for any irregular developments of the anomaly, but are otherwise not to be contained or informed of the anomaly affecting them.

O5-8 is declared the main supervisor of the SCP-9696 project.

Description: SCP-9696 is the merging of the SCP Foundation with the concepts of normalcy and the status quo within the noosphere.1

Through this conceptual merging, the concept of normalcy within the Foundation is preserved, preventing any major, noticeable deviations2 from occurring in personnel who are not within the bounds of normalcy as defined by the consensus of the O5 Council. This effect creates an implicit amplification of personal fulfillment with their work at the Foundation, a stronger connection to the collective ideals of the Foundation and society within personnel as opposed to self-identity, and a drive toward the fulfillment of the core mission of the Foundation, that being the preservation of normalcy.

Personnel who are majorly affected by SCP-9696 are of minority status, existing outside of the normalcy sphere in the collective human consciousness. SCP-9696 pulls these individuals into being a part of this sphere, amplifying their preexisting aspirations for working with the Foundation and their preexisting rejection of traits that would otherwise not fit the concept of normalcy. This takes form via the adoption of normative ideals onto non-normative cultures and identities, for example the adoption of monogamy and matrimony on sexually deviant identities and relationships. It is believed that this makes the SCP Foundation the sole arbiter of the concept of normalcy, as defined by the O5 Council.

SCP-9696-1 is an unintended secondary effect of SCP-9696. SCP-9696-1 is the concept of drowning manifested in material reality. SCP-9696-1 targets a rare number of individuals affected by SCP-9696, physically manifesting in the form of unnatural flooding conditions, imperceptible to the eye and only affecting the specific target of the anomaly.

SCP-9696-1 has three stages:

Stage One: Subjects report feeling tightness in their chests, and symptoms similar to anxiety. On rare occasions, some of their clothes appear to be wet from an unknown source. The majority of subjects fall under this stage.

Stage Two: Symptoms of anxiety gradually increase, leading to feelings of dread of the future and catastrophizing. Subjects cough for intermittent periods, and in some cases display difficulty breathing and chest pain.

Stage Three: Subjects are fully incapacitated. Water is present in their lungs, and they are unable to be resuscitated regardless of any method used. Subjects remain alive, however, and occasionally convulse and choke from the effects of SCP-9696-1. Only a few individuals have been recorded suffering from stage three effects.

SCP-9696-1 is perceivable via video and photographic imaging, as flooding conditions within the area that the targeted subject occupies. The water level can rise or lower depending on the severity of the effects of SCP-9696-1 for each subject affected. Subjects affected by the anomaly are not entirely within the sphere of SCP-9696,3 and the only treatment found to suppress its effects is to further push them into the sphere.4 This can be done via mundane means such as organizational inclusivity initiatives and other incentives, primarily to assist them in refraining from acts against the ideals of SCP-9696.

Discovery: SCP-9696-1 was discovered on 1925/01/06, when Junior Researcher Charles Gomez became the first recorded stage three subject of the anomaly. Soon after, more affected subjects were documented and observed, with initial investigation resulting in no concrete findings, due to a lack of information and knowledge of conceptual anomalies.

SCP-9696 was officially documented on 2000/03/03, after an advancement of understanding of the noosphere and travel/manipulation of noospheric space had led to a greater demand for the Foundation to further tighten its grip on the Veil. The conceptual merging was developed by a clandestine team of researchers and engineers formed by order of the O5 Council to develop a symbiotic relationship between the concepts of the SCP Foundation and normalcy. After the project concluded, it was discovered that SCP-9696-1 had been created retroactively by the installation of SCP-9696. This was found after analyzing the area where SCP-9696 was created, revealing that the two anomalies possessed the same noospheric signature, and that by creating SCP-9696 both anomalies were entwined with the Foundation since its inception. The retroactive installation of SCP-9696 was expected; the installation of 9696-1 was not anticipated.

Addendum 9696.1: Examples of Affected Subjects of SCP-9696-1

The following is a list of affected SCP-9696-1 subjects, and actions taken to lessen the severity of the effects of the anomaly for each subject.

Subject Description Actions Taken
Evelyn Denver Junior researcher at Site-19, stage one subject. Reclusive, and interacts with her peers sporadically. Claims to not have depressive symptoms during therapy sessions, however it has been noted that she always has taken a day off during the 14th of February each year. Through examining civilian files, the subject has a restraining order against her ex-boyfriend Ed Brubeck. In interviews Brubeck claims that Denver had left him due to “not really giving me any affection at all” and “being an absolute bitch.” Well, it was clear to me that this attitude was due to a traumatic event of some sort, likely the reason for the restraining order. Trauma can do many things to the human brain. Even if that isn’t the reason, I could make it appear that way. So I switched her therapist to one who specializes in difficulties with intimacy and emotional distress, and it seems to have worked so far. She is going out more, and her symptoms are dropping dramatically. I’ll still keep an eye on her, I don’t think it’s over for her quite yet. -O5-8
Michelle Adams Technician at Site-15, stage two subject. Takes 5 mg of oral estradiol per day as documented in medical records. Has been criticized for being too “aggressive,” “loud,” “childish” and “hysterical” by peers. She has filed multiple claims of unacceptable behavior from fellow technicians in the past. These claims include alleged spreading of false rumors of her being abusive towards others, alleged threats to keep her quiet about misconduct, and alleged social ostracism and being barred from conferences and other events. This one raised some interesting questions. How does one make someone like Michelle be accepted with the very obvious fact that she defies just about every social norm that we embrace as a society? Well, the answer is quite simple. When you cross the gender binary, you’re merely moving from one box to the other. So I did my best for her to fit in that box, so she’ll settle in with those expectations. It’s been a bit of a struggle, considering how adamant she is on keeping the attributes that make her a pariah among her peers, which also quite frankly makes her difficult to work with. But all will be solved in time. -O5-8
Alyx Kelley Zoologist employed at Site-58, stage one subject. According to medical records, they were found to have ambiguous genitalia at birth, but later were assigned as female. After birth, their genitalia was surgically modified to resemble female organs. Presents themselves as androgynous, expressing themselves with combined feminine and masculine traits. Has stated in therapy sessions that they feel like they “don’t belong here, no matter how hard I try.” It was a bit difficult to find the angle of approach here, but eventually it became obvious to me. They already present themselves the way that we think when we hear the word ‘non-binary,’ don’t they? As for their other concerns about themselves, that’s covered by their therapy, which I made sure to be as accessible to them as much as I reasonably could. -O5-8
Sasha O’Neil Containment specialist from Site-42, stage two subject. Is in a romantic relationship with researcher Roxanne Saunders, according to HR records. Keeps her hair short and has consistently been seen wearing suits and formal attire. Had once requested a change in personal identification, but later backtracked. Interviews with Saunders reveal that O’Neil was convinced by Saunders that her masculine presentation was merely the result of the way she views herself as a lesbian. These just get more and more perplexing, huh? Well, I don’t have much to say about this one in particular. I remember that one recent movement a few years ago that pushed the idea that women can be strong, they can be confident, they don’t have to necessarily be feminine to be a woman. As normalcy is redefined, we must always remember to protect that consensus no matter which form it takes, and purge that which doesn’t follow it. -O5-8
Cameron Pritchett Senior researcher at Site-17, stage one subject. Confirmed to be married to Mitchell Pritchett, another researcher stationed at the same site. Was promoted after a push for diversity and inclusivity incentives in 2013, with an added bonus to his salary. Participated in many organizational initiatives to further prioritize inclusion of LGBT staffers. It has been noted that Pritchett had strongly opposed the inclusion of gender-neutral bathrooms, and called for an indication of a person’s assigned sex in their personnel IDs along with their preferred identity. This one speaks for itself. Cameron desires to feel included, which makes my job much easier. After all, regardless of who you are, we are all united in our mission to protect normalcy. He worked hard to prove that he deserves to be recognized as much as we all do, so I gave him what he wanted. As for the other bits, some may oppose such things, but it’s a common culture there at that site, and it’s not exactly in my purview to challenge that. -O5-8
John Blake Stage three subject. Was the former security chief at Site-35, before he succumbed to the effects of SCP-9696-1. Not much information is known about him, as he had kept most of his personal information private, never sending any documentation to the relevant HR representative, except for documents that are necessary for eligibility of employment. Father to Emily Blake, a security officer stationed at Site-35. Currently in storage at an undisclosed location. It’s a shame, what happened to him. He was very competent and did the most he could to protect those under his watch. It’s also a shame that his daughter will never know what truly happened to him, but that’s just how things are in this line of work. I could’ve helped him, had the reason for how 9696-1 was affecting him be revealed to me, but that was his decision to make. A shame, really. -O5-8

Addendum 9696.2: O5 Meeting 9696/727272

The following is the transcription of the 2015/04/15 meeting between O5-8 and O5-1 regarding the state of SCP-9696 and its continued existence.

<Begin Log>

O5-8 enters the meeting room, and sits in his chair, crossing his arms. O5-1 can be seen across from him, looking at the SCP-9696 file.

O5-8: You know what I’m getting sick of? Those goddamn ‘wet floor’ signs that keep showing up in the hallway when I try to walk in here. It’s getting ridiculous at this point.

O5-1 ignores him.

O5-1: Good afternoon, Eight.

O5-8: Afternoon.

O5-8 sighs.

O5-8: This is even more ridiculous. It’s been what, the third meeting in three months?

O5-1: Yes. Is there a problem?

O5-8: Why yes, there is. You’re being paranoid again.

O5-1: I’m having reasonable concerns.

O5-8: 9696 is working perfectly. Our grip on normalcy is stronger than ever. The morale of our personnel is even higher. Everyone is happy! Is that concerning to you?

O5-1: You know precisely what my concerns are.

O5-8: Go on, then. Enlighten me.

O5-1 pushes the file closer to O5-8, and taps on a picture of SCP-9696-1.

O5-8: Oh, that? That’s nothing.

O5-1: That’s nothing? There’s permanent suffering from this, and that’s nothing?

O5-8: …This matters to you now?

O5-1: These aren’t anomalies, Eight. These aren’t numbers on a graph.

O5-8: I don’t see why that’s relevant.

O5-1: This is not a sacrifice worth having.

O5-8: We’ve sacrificed worse. We have to sacrifice what’s necessary for the greater good. That’s what we are.

O5-1: But this isn’t calculated for a noble cause. All of this can be entirely avoided.

O5-8: I never get why you’re so worked up over this. It’s not like the total number of stage threes is in the thousands, or the hundreds, or even the dozens.

O5-1 stifles a cough.

O5-1: Look, Eight. Are we able to get rid of it?

O5-8: The merging?

O5-1: The floods.

O5-8: We can’t. I had the brightest minds working day after day so that we could manipulate the noosphere to excise it, and it wouldn’t budge. Nothing I could do.

O5-1: Then what’s the point of all this? How is any of this necessary for our mission?

O5-8: How is it necessary— Are you hearing yourself? We are bound to the concept of normalcy, and that means we get to decide how that’s defined for everyone else. This is what we all wanted, isn’t it?

O5-1: Yes. But that’s not what concerns me.

O5-8: 9696 is too significant of an asset for us. Why should we disable ourselves entirely to help a few precious personnel?

O5-1: Because the cons outweigh the pros by a landslide. You don’t even know how many risks there are with this thing. It might not even be helping us in the long run, and we’d never know.

O5-8 scowls.

O5-8: And how might that be the case, exactly? Our personnel are happier and more productive when they’re collaborating with each other to fulfill our prime directive. It’s not like we’re changing personality traits and turning them all into a bunch of drones. It takes what’s already there, and amplifies it. They want to be here, they want to feel like they’re part of something bigger than them, that they’re doing what’s best for the world. I see this as a boon for not only our mission but for our personnel who help make it happen.

O5-1: Fritz always told me that we should be standing shoulder to shoulder, holding our shields up to defend the human race from what lies beyond what we can comprehend. Not this.

O5-8: But we are, aren’t we? We’re defending ourselves from any threats to our natural order, and in turn, we defend humanity from those same threats.

O5-1: That’s not the same thing, and you know it.

O5-8: Tell me why, then. If your way is so much better, then go on and tell me.

O5-1 looks down at the file, and stares at it in silence for a few moments, before looking back up at O5-8.

O5-1: I can’t say that we shouldn’t have advanced to where we are now, but back when we started this thing all we had to do was lock them up and that was that. It made no difference who they were and where they were from, they defied the natural laws that govern our reality. They had to be taken in.

O5-1: But now we have nonexistent departments and ones which I wish we didn’t have. We can put our grubby fingers into the human mindscape like that.

O5-1 snaps his fingers in emphasis.

O5-1: And as we keep growing, so does the threat that we contain.

O5-8: I see your point.

O5-1: There has to be a better way than this, Eight. I can’t keep dealing with this. I can’t keep seeing us having to constantly one up ourselves to keep our grip from slipping. It’s all slipping from my fingers like sand.

O5-8: Then let me handle it.

O5-1: How can I trust you to not step out of line?

O5-8: You trusted me with all of this. Without me, the gears of our working machine would not be turning as smoothly as they are now. Believe me, I can handle it.

O5-1: Can you say that to the personnel who are drowning as we speak?

O5-8 shrugs.

O5-8: They knew the risks. They chose this path, so they did this to themselves.

There is silence. O5-8 picks up the file and examines it.

O5-1: Say that again?

O5-8: Well, it’s simple. Those outside the collective are pulled in because that’s what they desire, and those who resist drown. Again, it’s merely an amplification of what’s already there.

O5-1: But it can’t—

O5-8: This is how it’s always been. Who wouldn’t want to belong to a community that’ll make them feel safe, that’ll accept them with open arms? This is what all our personnel are striving for. No one ever wants to be an outsider.

O5-8: And those who drown, well they shouldn’t have brought it on themselves. They knew the risks when they made their decision to join us. In fact, we may now have our greatest loyalty detection method yet.

O5-1: We already have a panopticon. That’s all we need.

O5-8: I see nothing that could be a better option to what we have.

O5-1: There has to be another way.

O5-8: There isn’t. Let me tell you something. You want to go back to the days when we had white picket fences and happy families and communities that accepted each other, right? None of this chicanery. What do you think I’ve been doing this whole time?

O5-1: Well, I—

O5-8: Mankind must not go back to hiding in fear. That’s what Fritz said, correct? We can’t hide in fear from what we don’t understand. We have to live in a sane and normal world.

O5-1: Yes. That’s what he said at our first meeting.

O5-8: People are afraid out there. They’re afraid of dangerous people who aren’t what they expect. People like Michelle, one of my cases, they endanger what we’re supposed to protect. It’s not only the anomalies anymore.

O5-1: That’s not in our purview.

O5-8: I know it isn’t. But I’ve been doing my best to prevent this from affecting us. If we can’t be bothered to protect normalcy from within our ranks, then what are we even doing?

O5-8: They need us, Aaron. They need me to help them. They want to be seen, they want to be accepted. That’s how I save them from drowning, one small step after another so that we can be a big happy family. Or at least something to that effect.

O5-1: This isn’t what my world was like.

O5-8: We have to take the world as it is, not as you’d like it to be. I think it’s about time you get with the program.

O5-1 stares at the man across from him in silence.

O5-1: I only wanted peace. I only wanted people to feel safe. Safe from the anomalies. Safe from what they’re afraid of.

O5-8: They’ll be safe. They won’t have to worry about anything anymore. Because we are the Ark to spare them all from the floods. We’ll be their guiding hand to lead them as we always have.

O5-1: This cannot continue. There’s too many risks.

O5-8: Guess we’re at another stalemate, then.

O5-8 pauses.

O5-8: But between you and me, this isn’t our decision to make.

O5-1: What do you mean?

O5-8: You’re the leader, but that doesn’t mean you make the decisions. 9696 encompasses the entire scope of our organization, we can’t simply solve your concerns with a back-and-forth like this.

O5-1: You want a vote.

O5-8: Yes. With everyone else. It can either go my way and everything can continue as expected, or we can do your way and tear it all apart from the ground up.

O5-1: These meetings are only between us for a reason. You know how heated they can get. There’s no telling what would happen if I brought this to the table.

O5-8: And I’m guessing our continued standstill is preferable to you?

O5-1: Well, no, but—

O5-8: Then we need a vote. A decision will eventually be reached, and then we can finally move on to more important things.

O5-1 considers what has been spoken.

O5-1: Fine. We’ll have a vote.

O5-8 grins.

O5-8: Knew I’d get somewhere with you eventually, you ol’ coffin-dodger.

O5-8 stands up and pushes in his chair.

O5-8: Regardless of what decision is reached, I have faith that we will persist, and our world will continue to thrive on one condition: everything being as it should be.

O5-8 exits the meeting room, and closes the door behind him.

O5-1: Is this how things should be? For your sake, Eight, I hope it isn’t.

O5-1 coughs for a prolonged period, and a few drops of water are expelled from his throat. He does not appear to notice.

<End Log>

As of 2025/09/20, SCP-9696 is expected to continue operating at maximum efficacy.

Footnotes
1. The dimension of all concepts or ideas that are known by humanity, and the sum of all human consciousness.
2. Such as expressions of identity, culture, and other actions that act against normative ideals in society.
3. Or are those who retain ideals and convictions against the primary mission of the Foundation.
4. That is, to further be pushed into the ideals of normalcy.
