[-] RUNNING CREDENTIALS…

WARNING: THE FOLLOWING FILE IS LEVEL 4/9714 CLASSIFIED

ANY ATTEMPT TO ACCESS THIS FILE WITHOUT LEVEL 4/9714 AUTHORIZATION WILL BE LOGGED AND WILL LEAD TO IMMEDIATE DISCIPLINARY ACTION.

On 7/10/1991, D-Class personnel testing involving SCP-9714 was approved. New expedition guidelines incentivized closer examination of SCP-9714's relocation process, namely the possible existence of an extradimensional pocket space. Following SCP-9714's materialization in Roskeeragh Point, Mullaghmore, IE, on 7/14/1991, Test 9714-01-03 commenced posthaste.

The following is a video log transcript of recovered footage from Test-9714-01-03, recorded roughly over a two-month period. Irrelevant footage has been excluded.

Test 9714-01-03 Video Log Transcript

Initial Date: July 14, 1991 13:06

Testing Equipment:

  • Two (2) chest-mounted cameras
  • Two (2) implanted GPS trackers
  • One (1) radiation detector
  • Two (2) backpacks with standard survival gear
  • Two (2) bedrolls
  • Four (4) month ration and water supply

D-Class Personnel:

  • D-7485-OW: Oisín Winslow (involuntary manslaughter)
  • D-0291-CH: Courtney Harper (conspiracy, narcotrafficking)
<BEGIN LOG>

0291-CH: So, what? We just wait here? Do they really expect us to just stand around all day? It's been hours.

7485-OW: Wait and observe.

0291-CH: Observe what? This whole building's empty. There's nothing here.

[7485-OW does not respond.]

0291-CH: Yeah, okay. I get it. Fuck me, I guess.

7485-OW: You really think I know? You think those labcoats have told me anything? Don't be an idiot.

0291-CH: No, I don't. I don't think you know jack shit. Just my luck, getting paired up with an absolute pr—

[A loud bell sound interrupts 0291-CH, followed by an intense tremor that knocks both subjects to the floor. SCP-9714 in its entirety seems to rumble and shift, kicking up dust and dirt. However, no structural damage occurs. Over time, the tremor gradually subsides until SCP-9714 is once again still. Both subjects stare at each other, visibly distressed and confused.]

0291-CH: What just happened?

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

7485-OW: It's… water. I think.

0291-CH: But it's black as oil. Jesus, where the hell are we?

[Both 7485-OW and 0291-CH crowd the entryway into SCP-9714. The exterior space is no longer Roskeeragh Point. Instead, a still-water sea extends in all directions, stopping short at SCP-9714's foundations. The horizon is featureless with the black water blending into a dark-hued sky, dotted with unknown stars and constellations.]

7485-OW: It’s so quiet. There’s no wind or anything.

0291-CH: How does a whole building just up and move?

7485-OW: I'm pretty sure that's what we're supposed to figure out.

[0291-CH looks up, revealing the only prominent light source present is the lamp atop SCP-9714.]

0291-CH: Well, if they're looking for us, at least we're easy to spot.

[7485-OW doesn't respond, preoccupied as he gently dips his hand into the black water. It flows over his skin with little cohesion, gliding right off.]

0291-CH: I guess we should look around the place. See if anything else has changed.

7485-OW: Yeah, we probably should.

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[Both subjects are in one of SCP-9714's empty rooms, unpacking their Foundation-supplied backpacks and unrolling their bedrolls.]

0291-CH: So what did you do?

7485-OW: What?

0291-CH: What did you do? You know. What got you in the orange jumpsuit?

7485-OW: Oh. You know it’s taboo around the 89 block to ask about that sort of thing.

0291-CH: We’re not exactly at the Site though, are we?

[7485-OW does not immediately respond, focusing on his backpack.]

7485-OW: I… Manslaughter.

0291-CH: Damn, really? You killed a guy?

7485-OW: I’m not going to talk about it.

0291-CH: Alright, I won’t pry. Was just being curious.

7485-OW: What about you?

0291-CH: Me? Drug trafficking. They claimed I was part of a big morphine and narcotic distribution ring up in Chicago.

7485-OW: Claimed? You’re saying you didn’t do it?

0291-CH: Well, I ain't confessing to shit while I've got a literal camera on my chest.

[7485-OW laughs.]

7485-OW: Then why did you even bring this stuff up?

0291-CH: Just trying to start a conversation.

7485-OW: Poor subject choice then.

0291-CH: I will say I’m surprised they didn't convict on the money laundering charges.

7485-OW: You laundered money?

[0291-CH leans his head closer to the camera, speaking into it directly.]

0291-CH: Hell. No. Still surprised though.

[Both subjects briefly go quiet, focusing on their task.]

0291-CH: They're coming for us. We're not stuck here. Right?

[7485-OW looks up and opens his mouth to say something but ultimately does not respond.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[Both subjects are sleeping in their respective bedrolls. The room is silent. 0291-CH adjusts in his sleep, shifting the camera view towards the room's open doorway. In the hall beyond, a brief shadow is captured, moving out of view. The shadow's shape is unable to be determined. 2 minutes later, a very faint, distant chiming sound is heard.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[7485-OW is cupping his ear against a wall, listening intently.]

7485-OW: Do you really not hear that?

[0291-CH is leaning against the same wall. A low rhythmic hum, barely distinguishable from the ambience, rattles through SCP-9714.]

0291-CH: Wait… A little, yeah. What is that?

7485-OW: I don't know. I noticed it last night. It's stronger towards where the tower is.

0291-CH: No way to get to the tower…

7485-OW: It's kind of comforting.

0291-CH: It's fucking unsettling is what it is. This place is weird enough without white noise shit coming through the walls.

[7485-OW shoots 0291-CH a glare but says nothing.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[0291-CH is looking through a window on SCP-9714's second floor. 7485-OW can be seen outside SCP-9714's entrance, standing knee-deep in the surrounding black water sea. He is staring towards the direction of the light room atop SCP-9714's tower. 0291-CH watches silently for 7 minutes before eventually walking away.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[Both subjects are eating rations. 0291-CH is watching 7485-OW. 7485-OW is eating very slowly, often examining and flexing his hands.]

0291-CH: Do you think we’re alone?

7485-OW: What?

0291-CH: Do you think we’re alone here?

[7485-OW hesitates.]

7485-OW: Yes. I think we’re alone.

0291-CH: No you don't.

7485-OW: Excus—

0291-CH: What's so interesting in the lamp room? See someone up there?

7485-OW: I don't know what you're talking about.

0291-CH: I'm not an idiot. They told you something, didn't they? Before we got here. You know what we're supposed to be looking for.

7485-OW: No one has told me anything.

0291-CH: You're… lying to me.

7485-OW: Why the fuck would I be lying to you?

0291-CH: They're watching us, aren't they? Are you in on it?

[7485-OW stares in silence before abruptly standing up, tossing his half-eaten ration to the floor and leaving the room altogether.]

0291-CH: Winslow… Winslow!

[7485-OW does not respond.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[7485-OW begins to scream without warning, waking 0291-CH.]

0291-CH: Agh! What?! What's happening?!

7485-OW: The light! It's—the man in the boat! It's— it's…

0291-CH: Winslow! What the fuck?

7485-OW: I… I was… I'm sorry. I was dreaming.

0291-CH: Shit, man. What is wrong with you?

[7485-OW, now sitting against the wall, doesn't immediately respond.]

7485-OW: I don't think we're going home.

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[0291-CH is wandering SCP-9714 alone. His ear is close to the wall.]

0291-CH: Courtney, damn it, what are you looking for? You stupid asshole. You tool. Volunteer, they said. Knock some time off your sentence, they said. God, why is it so bright in here?

[0291-CH continues to speak to himself as he traverses SCP-9714. The faint low humming in walls gradually becomes more noticeable.]

0291-CH: It's here. It's got to be here. There's got to be something I'm supposed to find. You fuckers wanted us to find something. Why put us in concrete coffin to bumfuck nowhere? Tell me what I'm supposed to find. Just tell me. Please, please just tel—

[0291-CH is cut short as he trips to the floor. He tumbles down hard, grunting in pain. Looking back, his foot is caught on a bent floorboard, awkwardly angled against the base of the wall.]

[Once recuperated, 0291-CH crawls over to this floorboard and feels around it, testing its strength. It slides in place easily. Carefully, he pulls the floorboard away from the wall, opening a gap. Hidden in the floor is a simple iron lockbox with a handle over the lid. 0291-CH slightly hesitates before lifting the box out from the gap.]

[0291-CH silently examines the lockbox, feeling its edges, before undoing the latch. The lockbox is filled with white molluscan shells. Cradled within these shells is a small golden apple. 0291-CH plucks the apple and examines it. Crudely carved into the apple are outlines of Earth’s landmasses, forming a makeshift globe, as well as a single word in Ogham letters: Goidte.6]

[Without another word, 0291-CH hides the apple away into his jumpsuit pocket.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

7485-OW: They're not coming for us, Courtney. They don't even know where we are.

0291-CH: Don't say that. You don't know that.

7485-OW: They can't get to us. We're somewhere they can't get to.

0291-CH: They can, Winslow. They can. They have to. They need our cameras. They— they need to see what we've seen.

7485-OW: We're in a tomb. We're in a tomb at the bottom of the world and we're not getting out!

0291-CH: Why would they send us in here? For what? They don't get anything if they don't find us!

7485-OW: They don't have to! We don't come back and that's that. We're a fucking tax write-off!

0291-CH: We're going to be found. We're getting home. They know we're here. They've been watching us.

7485-OW: They gave us enough food to last for months! They don't know where we are!

[0291-CH grabs the radiation detector sitting beside his bedroll and hurls it at 7485-OW. It barely misses, smashing against a wall.]

0291-CH: You don't know, damn it! You don't—

[0291-CH’s exclamations sputter short, stunned into silence. 7485-OW follows 0291-CH’s gaze. The wall has cracked where the radiation detector impacted. A dark red fluid, akin to blood or sap, is slowly seeping through the cracks.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[Both subjects are erratically yelling at each other, stomping and circling around the room. Their shouts are incoherent and angry. This continues for 12 minutes.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[0291-CH is sleeping in his bedroll. 7485-OW is not. Instead, he is sitting up with his back against the wall, watching 0291-CH sleep. He appears to be whispering to himself, but his words are indiscernible. After 20 minutes, something unheard seems to draw 7485-OW’s attention. He silently stands up from the wall and exits the room. 3 minutes later, a creaking sound like an opening door is heard.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[0291-CH wanders SCP-9714, searching the rooms. 7485-OW is absent.]

0291-CH: Winslow? Fuck man, where’d you go?

[Each floor is empty, and 7485-OW is nowhere to be found. As time goes on, 0291-CH begins to search more frantically, shouting from room to room, running through SCP-9714’s empty spaces, until eventually reaching the ground floor once again.]

0291-CH: God damn it! Winslow?! Stop fucking with me man!

[0291-CH reaches SCP-9714’s entrance corridor. Like all the other rooms, it is seemingly empty, barren of any notable detail. He goes to shout again, but something catches his attention. In the wall on the far side, there is a previously undiscovered door. It is constructed to blend seamlessly into the wall, unable to be noticed while closed, but it is now open, revealing a short hallway.]

[0291-CH hesitates, glancing towards SCP-9714’s entrance, but he eventually goes through the open door. The hallway beyond snakes forward and opens up towards a small archway, leading to SCP-9714’s tower. 0291-CH approaches this archway and enters the tower proper.]

0291-CH: Okay…

[Inside the tower, a cast iron staircase spirals upwards along the walls, presumably towards the light room above. Flickers of light beam over the cracks in the ceiling, and the walls are blank and featureless. And dangling in the center of the space, high off the ground, a mummified corpse is strung by its feet from a rope. It appears to be a man, dressed in tattered naval clothes. Its flesh is black and taut, and budding flowers are placed where its eyes should be.]

0291-CH: Winslow?

7485-OW: [distant, barely audible] —ere.

[0291-CH proceeds to climb the spiral staircase. As he climbs, he watches the hanging corpse, refusing to look away from it, until reaching the top. The staircase ends at a small metal platform, presumably the service platform. Rotating optics and vents clutter the space, as well as pipes that seem to lead to a fuel tank powering the machinery. One of the pipes appears loose. A ladder to the side leads up to a hatch in the ceiling. Carefully, 0291-CH mounts the ladder and opens the hatch.]

[The hatch opens into the light room. The room is small and bright with the lamp shining in the center, shielding a rotating bulb beaming through the Fresnel lens and the outer storm panes. The lamp hums with a distinct rhythm, deep and rumbling. Standing off the central pedestal, staring into the lamp and bathed in its light, is 7485-OW.]

7485-OW: I'm up here.

0291-CH: Jesus! What the fuck? Did you not hear me running through the whole place?

[0291-CH goes to fully enter the room but hesitates. In 7485-OW's offhand, he is holding a weapon. A sort of bayonet, its blade rusted brown with dried blood. 7485-OW notices 0291-CH's hesitation and chuckles.]

7485-OW: This? It was blocking the door downstairs. Must've come loose.

0291-CH: Yeah?

7485-OW: Makes you think what must've happened to the guy who put it there.

[0291-CH does not immediately respond.]

0291-CH: I'm thinking the stiff hanging from the ceiling downstairs paints a good enough picture. How long have you been up here?

7485-OW: For a while. Needed a place to think. The light just feels safe, doesn't it?

0291-CH: Yeah. Sure… Safe from what?

7485-OW: There's a pit beneath the water.

0291-CH: What?

[7485-OW does not respond.]

0291-CH: Okay… I'm just gonna… You stay up here for a bit.

[0291-CH closes the hatch and climbs back down to the service room, leaving 7485-OW alone above. He stands still briefly, staring at the ceiling.]

0291-CH: Fuck me…

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

[0291-CH is crouched by a wall, moving the golden apple between his fingers. He is intently watching the doorway. 7485-OW can be faintly heard talking in another room. His words are indiscernible, but a separate voice can be heard. The two are conversing.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage]

[0291-CH detaches his chest-mounted camera and begins to address it directly.]

0291-CH: I don’t know if you are listening. Damn it, you better be listening. You need to get me out of here. I am in danger, and if there’s one thing I know you assholes hate, it’s losing resources. I am your resource. You’ve seen Winslow. You’ve seen how he hasn’t left the tower in days, how he’s losing his fucking mind. He has a weapon. Put two and two together, you heartless pricks! If you don’t get me out, he’s going to snap. He’s going to kill—

7485-OW: No one is listening, Courtney.

[The camera's view jolts, revealing 7485-OW standing in the room's doorway.]

0291-CH: No, that's not…

[The two subjects stare at each other in silence.]

[Skipping irrelevant footage.]

0291-CH: —therfucker! Get off me!

[The two subjects are wrestling each other on the floor. 7485-OW is seemingly intent on harming 0291-CH, attempting to stab 0291-CH with the bayonet. 0291-CH fights back, kicking 7485-OW off and throwing him into a nearby wall.]

0291-CH: Manslaughter my ass, you lunatic!

[0291-CH scrambles off the floor and sprints away through SCP-9714's empty rooms. 7485-OW can be heard grunting and yelling from behind. 0291-CH eventually reaches SCP-9714's entrance and seems to struggle on where to run next. He stares out to the black sea outside, ready to leave SCP-9714 entirely, but a shout from 7485-OW pulls him back, choosing the tower instead.]

[0291-CH runs into the tower. The mummified corpse still dangles overhead. Without hesitation, 0291-CH begins to hurriedly climb the spiral staircase, but stumbles halfway up. Looking back, 7485-OW has caught up and had grabbed 0291-CH by the foot. 7485-OW stands over 0291-CH and raises the bayonet up high.]

7485-OW: I won't let it take me! I am going home! Not you! Me!

[7485-OW lunges forward, but 0291-CH manages to roll over out of the way. Unable to control his momentum, 7485-OW trips and tumbles over the staircase railing, plummeting to the floor below and landing with a crack.]

[0291-CH stands and looks over the railing. 7485-OW is face down on the floor, unmoving.]

0291-CH: [panting] Oh my God. Holy shit. That's what you get, you lousy fucker!

[0291-CH pulls back from the railing and continues up the stairwell. Upon reaching the service platform, he spots the loose pipe and quickly goes to rip it free. He does so quickly with one strong pull, and without hesitation, begins to climb the ladder towards the ceiling hatch.]

[Entering the light room, 0291-CH positions himself in front of the lamp and holds the pipe up like a baseball bat. The lamp's hum pulses loudly.]

0291-CH: If you think I'm just going to let you get away with what you've put me through.

[0291-CH proceeds to swing the pipe into the lamp, shattering the Fresnel lens. He continues to swing, again and again, crashing through glass and metal mechanisms that burst with dark red fluid. Each hit breaks the lamp further, its rhythm sputtering, until the bulb within shutters with a whimper and the light goes out.]

0291-CH: Feed on that, you piece of shit!

[With one final hit, 0291-CH tosses the pipe to the floor, stained red. The light room has gone dark. 0291-CH laughs to himself, spitting at the broken lamp, before retreating back down the hatch. Walking down the stairwell, the tower has gone dark too, and completely quiet. 0291-CH continues to softly laugh, until approaching the ground floor. In the dark, 7485-OW stirs, but 0291-CH does not notice.]

[Nearly reaching the hall towards SCP-9714's entrance, 0291-CH suddenly yelps in pain, tumbling to the floor. Looking back, 7485-OW is grunting and propping himself up with the bayonet, now bloody from 0291-CH's freshly cut Achilles tendon. Frantically, 0291-CH attempts to crawl away. 7485-OW inches slowly behind him.]

[Upon reaching the entrance room, 0291-CH turns one more time. 7485-OW is now standing over him, once again raising the bayonet high.]

0291-CH: Oh God, please! Ple—

[7485-OW interrupts 0291-CH's pleas, driving the bayonet through his neck. Over the next 3 minutes, 7485-OW idly watches 0291-CH choke on his blood.]

7485-OW: This is my way out. My way home. Mine.

[7485-OW limps away and exits SCP-9714, wading into the surrounding water outside until completely submerged and out of view.]

[0291-CH's camera continues to record for roughly 14 continuous hours. Minimal activity and ambience are detected across the remaining footage, until the end of this runtime. 2 minutes before the camera's automatic shutdown, an unknown presence is heard approaching from behind. Sounds similar to scraping metal and chimes accompany this entity.]

[The scraping sounds intensify as the camera's perspective moves backwards along the floor, until getting caught on a loose floorboard. The camera becomes detached, rolling over into a resting position. 0291-CH's corpse is captured being dragged out of view into the main tower of SCP-9714. Briefly before the recording's conclusion, Earth's moon can be seen shining through a window.]

<END LOG>

Test-9714-01-03 concluded upon SCP-9714's remanifestation in Roskeeragh Point on 9/18/1991. Of the testing equipment recovered from SCP-9714, both GPS trackers and one chest-mounted camera still remain unaccounted for. Neither D-0291-CH or D-7485-OW have been recovered, and SCP-9714’s lamp is notably still functional.

The following two-sided document was also discovered alongside the remaining testing equipment.

Hark! Hark Manannán, son of the Sea, over-king of Tuath Dé, hark! Bid our father Oirbsiu to sweep the world ‘neath foam and salt. Grind the bones of men ‘til silt for apple trees. Bellow! Bellow, drown the wealth of mystery with slime, to choke, to engorge ye! ‘Til seven coral-tine sabers slash seven Fomorian gullets. Bilge do creep, simmer the flesh, bloated with the hours drawn near. Rise! Rise, Gilla Decair, course over thee, call thee home. We are lost! We are lost here, trapped! Seven lands long stolen by seven tribes of men. Buried by mound, by tomb. Feed! Feed, for death is your nectar. Breath is your wine. Bone is your ambrosia. Carve your crescent door for thee, cutting the path to thee in little stars. By moonlit marrow the door be opened! We are Fair! Just and Forgotten! To any man, any time, any god ‘neath black waves of sky. Steal back what was stolen. Our Birthright! Ár Domhan!7 Salvation, we cry! Salvation! Salvation!

The Riders of the Sidhe

Addendum 9714-2: All future expeditions involving SCP-9714 have been suspended until further notice. Testing involving experimental methods to prevent SCP-9714 manifestations have been approved.

Footnotes
1. The use of KIP emitters has been shown to increase the timeframe until SCP-9714's dematerialization by a factor of seven.
2. Translated from Irish Gaelic to: "The light feeds"
3. Sea of Crises
4. Now present-day Haiti
5. Sea of Nectar
6. Translated from Irish Gaelic: “Stolen”
7. Translated from Irish Gaelic: “Our Earth”

SCP-9714.raw_source: ==== [[include :scp-wiki:component:preview text= Beckon us home oh Light on the water, Fomorian tomb. ]] ===== [[include :scp-wiki:theme:black-highlighter-theme]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:dynamikron]] [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:classified-bar-woed |lv=3 |item=9714 |oc= Keter |lang=EN ]] ---- [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block name=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/35/%D0%9C%D0%B0%D1%8F%D0%BA_%D0%90%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%B2%D0%B0.jpg | caption=SCP-9714 on 6/23/1989, near Cape Aniva, Sakhalin Oblast | align=center | width=100% ]] ---- **Special Containment Procedures:** Due to the sporadic nature of SCP-9714 materializations, permanent physical containment of SCP-9714 is impossible. Monitoring Stations 23-RA and 64-US are to dedicate allocatable resources towards detecting global and/or localized electromagnetic distortions and elevated gravitational abnormalities. MTF Epsilon-7 ("Pendulum Pushers"), alongside Site-89's Department of Statistical Prediction, is tasked with surveying data provided by the previously mentioned monitoring stations and predicting possible SCP-9714 manifestations. In the event of an identified SCP-9714 materialization, a standard on-site containment perimeter is to be immediately established with KIP emitters and spatial dampeners surrounding SCP-9714 at intervals of 7m. [[footnote]]The use of KIP emitters has been shown to increase the timeframe until SCP-9714's dematerialization by a factor of seven.[[/footnote]] See Document 9714-CS-45 for an updated list of approved cover stories by region. Should SCP-9714 directly materialize within any major population center or in a region with a population density greater than 300 persons/km^^2^^, Code Broadway amnestic and media manipulation procedures are to be enacted until SCP-9714's dematerialization. **Description:** SCP-9714 is a lighthouse. Its construction consists of a circular concrete tower standing at 31.2m, topped by a light room with Fresnel lens and painted in horizontal black and white bands. Attached to SCP-9714's base is a nine-story building presumedly designed to house lighthouse operators or other appropriate personnel. SCP-9714 is capable of autonomous relocation, vanishing from one position and subsequentially reappearing in another at seemingly random intervals. Materializations can occur months or years apart with SCP-9714 vanishing to unknown locations. The process behind its transportation is currently unknown. However, intense localized surges of electromagnetic radiation are measured whenever SCP-9714 materializes in a location, as well as minor gravitational disruptions. SCP-9714 can theoretically materialize in any given location, either on Earth's surface or in interplanetary space. Since its discovery, SCP-9714 materializations have been recorded in at least 147 separate locations. Historical evidence alludes to an indeterminate number of positions prior to discovery. Given the scope of its anomalous properties, it is unclear whether SCP-9714 directly relocates to another location following a dematerialization or if it enters a separate space outside of reality. **Discovery:** On 2/17/1986, SCP-9714 manifested within Site-███, materializing along the site's security perimeter. SCP-9714 remained at this location for 2 months and 11 days before dematerializing, reappearing 4 months later near Daisetsuzan National Park, Hokkaido. Two casualties were reported following a temporary containment breach of SCP-████ directly caused by SCP-9714's disruption. +++++ **Supplemental Materials:** > Following its discovery, historical documentation of SCP-9714 and other related records have since been retroactively compiled. Compilation is ongoing. [[tabview]] [[tab County Meath, IE - 1985]] On June 14th, 1985, a previously undiscovered section of the //Brú na Bóinne// monument complex was unearthed by anthropology students visiting from Trinity College Dublin. This section consisted of a pair of passage tombs branching from the dominating Knowth structure, as well as a separate cruciform chamber. An archaeological operation, funded by the college, was swiftly approved. During this operation, artifacts and pieces of megalithic art displaying anomalous properties were unearthed and soon brought to the Foundation’s attention. The following is a partial catalogue of relevant objects recovered by on-site Foundation investigators and archeologists. See Document 9714-Trinity-7B for the complete list. ---- [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block-peppo |name=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/31/Neolithic_Horse_Carved_on_Stone_%2819597160620%29.jpg |caption=SCP-9714-BB-1 |width=300px ]] **Object Designation:** SCP-9714-BB-1 **Description:** A depiction of a horse carved into stone. Originally inlaid within an overhead sill stone. **Anomalous Properties:** Any person making physical contact with SCP-9714-BB-1 for an extended period experiences a visual hallucination of being in a large empty field of burnt flowers. Subjects describe the field extending in all directions amidst a featureless horizon. After approximately 7 minutes of contact, a towering structure identified as SCP-9714 materializes nearby, unleashing a stampeding herd of horses towards the subject’s position. These horses trample the subject until physical contact with SCP-9714-BB-1 ceases. The hallucination lacks any tactile elements, but affected subjects have been shown to suffer injuries consistent with the hallucination following continued exposure. ---- **Object Designation:** SCP-9714-BB-4 **Description:** Molluscan shell ornaments (bivalves and gastropods). Some are strung together into necklaces and headpieces. **Anomalous Properties:** Upon wearing or incorporating the ornaments into clothing, the wearer will begin to experience acute anemia and photophobia over a 7-hour period. These symptoms appear gradually and have yet to be documented causing permanent bodily harm. The affected wearer will also develop a severe irrational fear of bright light akin to heliophobia, suffering nausea, irregular heartbeat, and panic attacks around concentrated beams of light in particular. These conditions can last up to two weeks after removing SCP-9714-BB-4. ---- **Object Designation:** SCP-9714-BB-5 **Description:** Jadeitite axehead. A punctured hole through the tip. **Anomalous Properties:** When left idle, the phrase "Fothaíonn an solas[[footnote]] Translated from Irish Gaelic to: "The light feeds" [[/footnote]]," written in Ogham letters, is anomalously carved into any given surface within a 0.3m proximity to the axehead. The phrase will repeat itself until the entire surface is inscribed, only ceasing with SCP-9714-BB-5's removal. There seems to be no restriction to the type of surface affected: wood, stone, metal, and flesh. ---- [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block-peppo |name=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/26/2019-06-07_06-22_Irland_131_Br%C3%BA_na_B%C3%B3inne%2C_Knowth%2C_Megalithic_Tombs.jpg |caption=SCP-9714-BB-7 |width=300px ]] **Object Designation:** SCP-9714-BB-7 **Description:** Megalithic art. Serpentiform and spiral motifs, depicting a possible central obelisk or tower with a hole at its precipice. **Anomalous Properties:** Any person directly observing SCP-9714-BB-7 over a period exceeding 14 minutes will suffer impulses to draw blood from their wrists. These impulses gradually increase in severity with affected observers resorting to the use of their teeth or fingernails should no other method be present. Upon inflicting a sufficient wound, the observer will attempt to trace the motifs on SCP-9714-BB-7 with their blood. During this period, the observer will experience a full hallucination involving all sensory inputs, including tactile and emotional elements. Affected observers perceive themselves at the foot of a spiral staircase inside SCP-9714. The staircase is comprised of silver tree branches and budding golden apples. Climbing this staircase, the observer enters SCP-9714's light room, wherein their surrounding environment floods into a vast black sea. The observer experiences the sensation of drowning, reporting symptoms similar to acute respiratory distress syndrome and hypothermia, as they are submerged beneath the water. Swarms of hands have been described as pulling the observer down. Before complete submersion, the observer sees a golden boat autonomously drifting over the water with an obscured figure at its helm. The hallucination ends upon the affected observer either completing their outline of SCP-9714-BB-7, being forcibly removed from SCP-9714-BB-7’s proximity, or suffering hypovolemic shock. [[/tab]] [[tab Luna - 1976]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block-peppo |name=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f2/Ghost_Crater_in_Southern_Mare_Crisium%21_%28LROC166_-_Ghostcrater_context%29.png |caption=Mare Crisium (11.1° N, 59.7° E) |width=300px ]] On August 9th, 1976, at 15:04:12 UTC, //Luna 24//, the 24th probe of the Luna programme, launched from Baikonur 81/23 on the third Soviet mission to return lunar soil samples from the Moon.  The probe, based on the Ye-8-5 spacecraft body, entered lunar orbit on August 14th, and its lander reached the volcanic plains of Mare Crisium[[footnote]] Sea of Crises [[/footnote]] on August 18th at 06:36 UTC. The mission lasted 12 days, 14 hours and 51 minutes, returning with 170.1g of lunar samples on August 22nd. //Luna 24// was on the lunar surface for roughly 23 hours. At 17:27 UTC, August 18th, the lander's radiation detector registered an abnormal level of surface radiation originating west by southwest of its position. This elevated radiation was mapped as a reflection from an object foreign to the lunar surface. The orbital's stereo photographic imaging system, in tandem with the lander, automatically captured images of this radiation's estimated origin. A structure, now identified as SCP-9714, was pictured, albeit minimally. No photos following the //Luna 24// mission have since revealed SCP-9714's continued lunar presence. All images pertaining to SCP-9714 have since been archived by the Foundation. See Document 9714-Crisium-4C for the complete image registry. Among the returned samples, water and organic material was detected. Closer examination revealed 0.5% human bone tissue by mass, as revealed in infrared absorption spectroscopy. [[/tab]] [[tab Waco, TX - 1947]] In the early hours of September 16th, 1947, the body of Suzanne Abernathy was discovered in Cameron Park, off of Lawson Point Dr, by the park’s groundskeeper. The body displayed polytrauma consistent with a fall from height, including significant calcaneal fractures, fractures of the neck and femur, and spinal cord injuries. The coroner’s report suggested the injuries required a fall from a height of 25m or greater, but no such elevation was present in Cameron Park. Following a full police inquiry, no foul play was discovered. Abernathy’s death was ruled a suicide, citing her history of "mental instability." The following is a report of Abernathy’s psychological assessment. Prior to her death, Abernathy had been a registered patient at the local Oceans Behavioral Hospital. Its cargo consisted of luxury goods including sugar, spices, and rum. Five months later, on August 7th, the ship arrived at the port of Bayonne. Its cargo was relatively intact, but of its initial crew of 44 men, at least 7 members were missing and unaccounted for. The exact number is still unknown. Considering its late arrival by two months, the //Culverin// was originally thought lost at sea before its reappearance, and upon its return was immediately decommissioned and scrapped for lumber and other construction materials. Many of the ship's official records, including captain's logs, detailed cargo and crew manifests, and trade ledgers, were either lost or destroyed during its decommission. Following the audit and liquidation of SRS Trading in 1990, a cache of previously unlisted records and artifacts, including records regarding the //Culverin//, was rediscovered and brought to the attention of Foundation investigators. Among these records, the personal log of Jean-Marc De Verley, the //Culverin//'s second officer, was recovered and translated. Two poor souls were lost overboard as those final waves engulfed the deck, presumed drowned. They were able seamen, I believe. Leroux and that young Dutch man. [The other officers and I] can only explain so many times that the ship is already halfway across the Atlantic. Turning back would be pointless. It is the same distance to port no matter the direction we take. Not that our answers satisfy them, but for the moment, they remain loyal and compliant. > > We're to hold a service later this evening for the men lost. It feels unnecessary. We all know what this job entails. But I understand the reason for it. We diverted our course to meet it. > > Dawn turned to day, we grew closer, and the light's source was not a ship. A chamber of gilded glass and metal sits atop it, the light beaming brightly from within. And instead of masonry or even timber, the whole tower and the extension at its base is made of strange stone almost smooth to the touch. I know very little of such matters, but it doesn't seem a thing built up or put together. More like the stone was already there, and the rest was built into it. > > I can only presume it to be a lighthouse, but it is unlike any I have seen and in a place it shouldn't be. Who built such a thing, and how? > > Some of the men and officers, the captain and I included, went over to search it. It is even more peculiar up close, but we found nothing. All the rooms were empty and the light at the top could not be reached. The tower itself had no entrance. Only solid walls. If anyone had been there, all traces of them were gone. The way the others looked at us as we returned tell me they do not entirely believe our claims. I don't blame them, but I don't know how to convince them either. We're all in the dark. > > I feel an unease as the tower's shadow drifts over the ship. We continue our course to La Rochelle in a few hours' time. I fear there aren't too many sensible men on this ship. > > I've raised my concerns with the captain, advocating for swift action. If we don't smother this in the crib, it will grow like a cancer. I only hope that I'm wrong. > //Monday, 28th April// > ---- > I do not understand it. Dubois is adamant that our course has not shifted these last few days. That the ship has moved in a singular, straight direction. He has even proved it with his instruments and star charts; there is no denying. > > Why then is the lighthouse, at this very moment, off our port bow? > > It is the same tower; I am sure of it. The same spinning light, the same smooth stone, the same empty rooms. Even the mound of rock it stands upon is the same. But how? Perhaps we are truly lost, going circles, or perhaps there is simply more than one out here. > > I do not know what to think. What theory to grasp. For now, I only want off this God forsaken ship. > > As expected, the crew is frantic. They're demanding answers, and the captain cannot seem to come up with one good enough. That superstitious talk is running rampant now. The lighthouse's reappearance unnerves me like everyone else, but omens? Curses? Do these men even hear themselves? I fear what they might do with their minds absent of sense. > > For now, the captain has ordered we stay put. Perhaps it is the right decision, but it feels ill-advised. If only to think of what to do next. > > The lighthouse's shadow is trailing over the ship again, crossing over my cabin. They flinch each time the tower's light flashes through the windows. > > I'm not sure what we shall decide. Giving into the crew's demands is foolish. We're in a tomb at the bottom of the world and we're not getting out! > > **0291-CH:** Why would they send us in here? For what? They don't get anything if they don't find us! > > **7485-OW:** They don't have to! We don't come back and that's that. We're a fucking tax write-off! > > **0291-CH:** We're going to be found. We're getting home. They know we're here. They've been watching us. > > **7485-OW:** They gave us enough food to last for months! They don't know where we are! > > //[0291-CH grabs the radiation detector sitting beside his bedroll and hurls it at 7485-OW. It barely misses, smashing against a wall.]// > > **0291-CH:** You don't know, damn it! You don't— > > //[0291-CH’s exclamations sputter short, stunned into silence. 7485-OW follows 0291-CH’s gaze. The wall has cracked where the radiation detector impacted. A dark red fluid, akin to blood or sap, is slowly seeping through the cracks.]// > > //[Skipping irrelevant footage.]// > > //[Both subjects are erratically yelling at each other, stomping and circling around the room. Their shouts are incoherent and angry. This continues for 12 minutes.]// > > //[Skipping irrelevant footage.]// > > //[0291-CH is sleeping in his bedroll. 7485-OW is not. Instead, he is sitting up with his back against the wall, watching 0291-CH sleep. He appears to be whispering to himself, but his words are indiscernible. After 20 minutes, something unheard seems to draw 7485-OW’s attention. He silently stands up from the wall and exits the room. 3 minutes later, a creaking sound like an opening door is heard.]// > > //[Skipping irrelevant footage.]// > > //[0291-CH wanders SCP-9714, searching the rooms. 7485-OW is absent.]// > > **0291-CH:** Winslow? Fuck man, where’d you go? > > //[Each floor is empty, and 7485-OW is nowhere to be found. As time goes on, 0291-CH begins to search more frantically, shouting from room to room, running through SCP-9714’s empty spaces, until eventually reaching the ground floor once again.]// > > **0291-CH:** God damn it! Winslow?! Stop fucking with me man! > > //[0291-CH reaches SCP-9714’s entrance corridor. Like all the other rooms, it is seemingly empty, barren of any notable detail. He goes to shout again, but something catches his attention. In the wall on the far side, there is a previously undiscovered door. It is constructed to blend seamlessly into the wall, unable to be noticed while closed, but it is now open, revealing a short hallway.]// > > //[0291-CH hesitates, glancing towards SCP-9714’s entrance, but he eventually goes through the open door. The hallway beyond snakes forward and opens up towards a small archway, leading to SCP-9714’s tower. 0291-CH approaches this archway and enters the tower proper.]// > > **0291-CH:** Okay… > > //[Inside the tower, a cast iron staircase spirals upwards along the walls, presumably towards the light room above. Flickers of light beam over the cracks in the ceiling, and the walls are blank and featureless. And dangling in the center of the space, high off the ground, a mummified corpse is strung by its feet from a rope. It appears to be a man, dressed in tattered naval clothes. Its flesh is black and taut, and budding flowers are placed where its eyes should be.]// > > **0291-CH:** Winslow? > > **7485-OW:** //[distant, barely audible]// —ere. > > //[0291-CH proceeds to climb the spiral staircase. As he climbs, he watches the hanging corpse, refusing to look away from it, until reaching the top. The staircase ends at a small metal platform, presumably the service platform. Rotating optics and vents clutter the space, as well as pipes that seem to lead to a fuel tank powering the machinery. One of the pipes appears loose. A ladder to the side leads up to a hatch in the ceiling. Carefully, 0291-CH mounts the ladder and opens the hatch.]// > > //[The hatch opens into the light room. The room is small and bright with the lamp shining in the center, shielding a rotating bulb beaming through the Fresnel lens and the outer storm panes. The lamp hums with a distinct rhythm, deep and rumbling. Standing off the central pedestal, staring into the lamp and bathed in its light, is 7485-OW.]// > > **7485-OW:** I'm up here. > > **0291-CH:** Jesus! What the fuck? Did you not hear me running through the whole place? > > //[0291-CH goes to fully enter the room but hesitates. In 7485-OW's offhand, he is holding a weapon. A sort of bayonet, its blade rusted brown with dried blood. 7485-OW notices 0291-CH's hesitation and chuckles.]// > > **7485-OW:** This? It was blocking the door downstairs. Must've come loose. > > **0291-CH:** Yeah? > > **7485-OW:** Makes you think what must've happened to the guy who put it there. > > //[0291-CH does not immediately respond.]// > > **0291-CH:** I'm thinking the stiff hanging from the ceiling downstairs paints a good enough picture. How long have you been up here? > > **7485-OW:** For a while. Needed a place to think. The light just feels safe, doesn't it? > > **0291-CH:** Yeah. Sure… Safe from what? > > **7485-OW:** There's a pit beneath the water. > > **0291-CH:** What? > > //[7485-OW does not respond.]// > > **0291-CH:** Okay… I'm just gonna… You stay up here for a bit. > > //[0291-CH closes the hatch and climbs back down to the service room, leaving 7485-OW alone above. He stands still briefly, staring at the ceiling.]// > > **0291-CH:** Fuck me… > > //[Skipping irrelevant footage.]// > > //[0291-CH is crouched by a wall, moving the golden apple between his fingers. He is intently watching the doorway. 7485-OW can be faintly heard talking in another room. His words are indiscernible, but a separate voice can be heard. The two are conversing.]// > > //[Skipping irrelevant footage]// > > //[0291-CH detaches his chest-mounted camera and begins to address it directly.]// > > **0291-CH:** I don’t know if you are listening. Damn it, you better be listening. You need to get me out of here. I am in danger, and if there’s one thing I know you assholes hate, it’s losing resources. //I// am your resource. You’ve seen Winslow. You’ve seen how he hasn’t left the tower in days, how he’s losing his fucking mind. He has a weapon. Put two and two together, you heartless pricks! If you don’t get me out, he’s going to snap. He’s going to kill— > > **7485-OW:** No one is listening, Courtney. > > //[The camera's view jolts, revealing 7485-OW standing in the room's doorway.]// > > **0291-CH:** No, that's not… > > //[The two subjects stare at each other in silence.]// > > //[Skipping irrelevant footage.]// > > **0291-CH:** —therfucker! Get off me! > > //[The two subjects are wrestling each other on the floor. 7485-OW is seemingly intent on harming 0291-CH, attempting to stab 0291-CH with the bayonet. 0291-CH fights back, kicking 7485-OW off and throwing him into a nearby wall.]// > > **0291-CH:** Manslaughter my ass, you lunatic! > > //[0291-CH scrambles off the floor and sprints away through SCP-9714's empty rooms. 7485-OW can be heard grunting and yelling from behind. 0291-CH eventually reaches SCP-9714's entrance and seems to struggle on where to run next. He stares out to the black sea outside, ready to leave SCP-9714 entirely, but a shout from 7485-OW pulls him back, choosing the tower instead.]// > > //[0291-CH runs into the tower. The mummified corpse still dangles overhead. Without hesitation, 0291-CH begins to hurriedly climb the spiral staircase, but stumbles halfway up. Looking back, 7485-OW has caught up and had grabbed 0291-CH by the foot. 7485-OW stands over 0291-CH and raises the bayonet up high.]// > > **7485-OW:** I won't let it take me! I am going home! Not you! Me! > > //[7485-OW lunges forward, but 0291-CH manages to roll over out of the way. Unable to control his momentum, 7485-OW trips and tumbles over the staircase railing, plummeting to the floor below and landing with a crack.]// > > //[0291-CH stands and looks over the railing. 7485-OW is face down on the floor, unmoving.]// > > **0291-CH:** //[panting]// Oh my God. Holy shit. That's what you get, you lousy fucker! > > //[0291-CH pulls back from the railing and continues up the stairwell. Upon reaching the service platform, he spots the loose pipe and quickly goes to rip it free. He does so quickly with one strong pull, and without hesitation, begins to climb the ladder towards the ceiling hatch.]// > > //[Entering the light room, 0291-CH positions himself in front of the lamp and holds the pipe up like a baseball bat. The lamp's hum pulses loudly.]// > > **0291-CH:** If you think I'm just going to let you get away with what you've put me through. > > //[0291-CH proceeds to swing the pipe into the lamp, shattering the Fresnel lens. He continues to swing, again and again, crashing through glass and metal mechanisms that burst with dark red fluid. Each hit breaks the lamp further, its rhythm sputtering, until the bulb within shutters with a whimper and the light goes out.]// > > **0291-CH:** Feed on that, you piece of shit! > > //[With one final hit, 0291-CH tosses the pipe to the floor, stained red. The light room has gone dark. 0291-CH laughs to himself, spitting at the broken lamp, before retreating back down the hatch. Walking down the stairwell, the tower has gone dark too, and completely quiet. 0291-CH continues to softly laugh, until approaching the ground floor. In the dark, 7485-OW stirs, but 0291-CH does not notice.]// > > //[Nearly reaching the hall towards SCP-9714's entrance, 0291-CH suddenly yelps in pain, tumbling to the floor. Looking back, 7485-OW is grunting and propping himself up with the bayonet, now bloody from 0291-CH's freshly cut Achilles tendon. Frantically, 0291-CH attempts to crawl away. 7485-OW inches slowly behind him.]// > > //[Upon reaching the entrance room, 0291-CH turns one more time. 7485-OW is now standing over him, once again raising the bayonet high.]// > > **0291-CH:** Oh God, please! Ple— > > //[7485-OW interrupts 0291-CH's pleas, driving the bayonet through his neck. Over the next 3 minutes, 7485-OW idly watches 0291-CH choke on his blood.]// > > **7485-OW:** This is my way out. My way home. //Mine.// > > //[7485-OW limps away and exits SCP-9714, wading into the surrounding water outside until completely submerged and out of view.]// > > //[0291-CH's camera continues to record for roughly 14 continuous hours. Minimal activity and ambience are detected across the remaining footage, until the end of this runtime. 2 minutes before the camera's automatic shutdown, an unknown presence is heard approaching from behind. Sounds similar to scraping metal and chimes accompany this entity.]// > > //[The scraping sounds intensify as the camera's perspective moves backwards along the floor, until getting caught on a loose floorboard. The camera becomes detached, rolling over into a resting position. 0291-CH's corpse is captured being dragged out of view into the main tower of SCP-9714. Briefly before the recording's conclusion, Earth's moon can be seen shining through a window.]// > +++++ Test-9714-01-03 concluded upon SCP-9714's remanifestation in Roskeeragh Point on 9/18/1991. Of the testing equipment recovered from SCP-9714, both GPS trackers and one chest-mounted camera still remain unaccounted for. Neither D-0291-CH or D-7485-OW have been recovered, and SCP-9714’s lamp is notably still functional. The following two-sided document was also discovered alongside the remaining testing equipment. > {{**Hark! Hark Manannán, son of the Sea, over-king of Tuath Dé, hark! Bid our father Oirbsiu to sweep the world ‘neath foam and salt. Grind the bones of men ‘til silt for apple trees. Bellow! Bellow, drown the wealth of mystery with slime, to choke, to engorge ye! ‘Til seven coral-tine sabers slash seven Fomorian gullets. Bilge do creep, simmer the flesh, bloated with the hours drawn near. Rise! Rise, Gilla Decair, course over thee, call thee home. We are lost! We are lost here, trapped! Seven lands long stolen by seven tribes of men. Buried by mound, by tomb. Feed! Feed, for death is your nectar. Breath is your wine. Bone is your ambrosia. Carve your crescent door for thee, cutting the path to thee in little stars. By moonlit marrow the door be opened! We are Fair! Just and Forgotten! To any man, any time, any god ‘neath black waves of sky. Steal back what was stolen. Our Birthright! Ár Domhan![[footnote]] Translated from Irish Gaelic: “Our Earth”[[/footnote]] Salvation, we cry! Salvation! Salvation!**}} [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block-quoted name=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/6c/%22The_Riders_of_the_Sidhe%22_John_Duncan_1911_McManus_Galleries%2C_Dundee_%282%29.jpg|caption=//The Riders of the Sidhe//|link=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/6c/%22The_Riders_of_the_Sidhe%22_John_Duncan_1911_McManus_Galleries%2C_Dundee_%282%29.jpg|width=500px|align=center]] [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] **Addendum 9714-2:** All future expeditions involving SCP-9714 have been suspended until further notice. Item #: SCP-9724

Object Class: Safe Neutralized

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9724 has displayed no anomalous properties following Event-9724-A. As such, no further containment procedures are necessary.

+ Show Archived Containment Procedures
- Close

SCP-9724 has been bought by a Foundation front and declared condemned. All windows have been boarded up in order to more effectively conceal SCP-9724's anomalous properties. Access to the property is to be dissuaded by force if necessary. SCP-9724-1 is to be monitored for any changes in demeanor.

Description: SCP-9724 refers to a small abandoned house situated at the outskirts of Hammond, Indiana. The dwelling shows signs of deterioration, with severe structural damage present throughout the building. A rusted plaque near the house's entrance is thought to have at one point displayed an inscription, although the original text is illegible. The building contains three rooms, including a storage unit and the room that housed SCP-9724-1 at the time of discovery. The structure contains no windows or natural lighting sources.

SCP-9724's main anomalous property is a mild mind-altering effect that makes any non-baseline individual see their own reflection in every surface, including opaque and non-mirrored materials. Debriefing suggests that the reflection is always slightly altered, although the specifics vary. These alterations cause distress to the individual. The effect breaks down around SCP-9724-1, showing instead reflections of the entity.

SCP-9724-1 is an amorphous and undifferentiated mass of human tissue weighing approximately 150 kilograms. Psychoforensic analysis has found that it at one point was conscious, although the entity possesses no capacity to communicate. The area surrounding SCP-9724-1 displays a Hume reading below that of baseline reality.

Discovery: SCP-9724 was first discovered during a review of anomalous structures in old Foundation records, which led to the discovery of SCP-9724-1. Foundation operatives quickly secured the area and searched the building. Following a search of the building, several documents thought to be related to SCP-9724-1 were found in the house's storage room, although the environmental conditions have rendered most of the documentation illegible. Relevant documentation is filed under Addendum-9724-A.

SCP-9725.raw_content:
Canon Hub » The Alchemy Department Hub / What A Wonderful World Hub » SCP-9725

A sample of SCP-9725-1 in its dried state.

Item #: SCP-9725

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: Knowledge of SCP-9725 is limited to personnel with Level-4 and above clearance.

SCP-9725-1 is to be kept in a high-security anomalous object locker. No experiments involving the object are to take place without the approval of both Director Diaghilev and Doctor Everwood.

Description: SCP-9725 are the steps necessary for the creation of homunculi. A digital replication is available for viewing in Attached Document 9725-A.

SCP-9725-1 is a light-colored clay used in the creation of humanoid homunculi originally created by Dr. Wondertainment. The object's anomalous properties are not activated unless a specific ritual involving the use of various aethers is performed.

Attached Document 9725-A The following is a digital replication of SCP-9725, with steps and information redacted to prevent the replication of SCP-9725-1.

PRODUCT FORMULA ARCHIVE

This is a bit of a bizarre experiment, but I think we've finally managed to get it to work, and we hope this will be the start of a wonderful idea. I sincerely hope you can enjoy your own experiments in this same line whenever you feel comfortable doing so.

MIXTURE INGREDIENTS

  1. One hair of a unicorn
  2. A miner's inch of morning dew
  3. ██████████████
  4. A whiff of whimsy
  5. A spark of thought
  6. An acorn from the woods without words
  7. Twenty pounds of clay powder
  8. ██████████████████████
  9. One young somatic essence
  10. A breath of Air Aether to give life
  11. A splash of Water Aether to give shape
  12. A billow of Fire Aether to hold form
  13. A name, because no being should be without a name

This amount will yield enough base for 20 units.

First, assemble the ingredients in a █████ bowl. Mix the solution with Water Aether, then breathe in the Air Aether once shaped. Next, blast it with Fire Aether to ensure it holds shape for about an hour and give them 15 minutes to cool off. When sufficiently cooled, Air Aether must be applied to finish it off. Once done with Aethers, simply give your newfound friend a name and they shall spring to life!

Remember, only make one at a time. The base does not go bad, so take as long as you like to think on who and what you want to make. A life is a life, no matter whose it is.

- Cornelius

DEPARTMENT OF MISTEREERING INTERNAL ARCHIVAL USE ONLY

Addendum 9725.01: With the approval of the Cross-test Committee, SCP-9725 project lead Dr. Everwood proposed a joint effort between the Alchemy Department and the GoI-386 Research Department to better understand SCP-9725 via the execution of its instructions in creating a homunculus (prospectively SCP-9725-2). Director Diaghilev agreed to a meeting for the purpose of exploring the potential project.

<BEGIN LOG>

[Diaghilev enters the conference room. Everwood stands to meet him.]

Everwood: Director.

Diaghilev: Doctor.

Diaghilev: You know, I've given your proposal a bit of thought. Even did a bit of research into what a "Little Mister" is.

Everwood: Oh? What do you think?

Diaghilev: Of all the uses one could have for a homunculus, anomalous children's entertainment is not one that I envisioned. This Wondertainment person must be quite the specialist in their field if the Foundation has taken an interest in children's music.

Everwood: There's more to it than that. There are all sorts of anomalous toys and other such things that Wondertainment makes. Plus they have a pocket dimension city called Wonder World tee-ehm.

Diaghilev: Wonder World tee-ehm? Why did I just say 'tee-ehm' after saying 'Wonder World' tee-ehm? Oh. Davai.

Everwood: We don't know for sure yet, but we believe it may have to do with some sort of anomalous trademark.

Diaghilev: Anomalous trademark, what th— No. Anyway, back to the matter at hand, I don't know if you're aware, but homunculi are not easy to create and require a very specific set of—

Everwood: Instructions? Yes, I know. And I have them right here. [Everwood reaches into their bag and produces a manilla folder. They then slide it along the table to Diaghilev.]

Diaghilev: Oh. I see you came prepared.

[Diaghilev opens the folder and reads through Document 9725-A. He scoffs.]

Everwood: That doesn't sound good.

Diaghilev: What kind of blithering idiot wrote these instructions? They completely misnamed the Aethers! And these ingredients. A whiff of whimsy? A miner's inch of morning dew? These aren't real measurements, much less real ingredients.

Everwood: Except they are real ingredients.

[Everwood reaches into their bag again and produces a second manilla folder, which they slide across the table to Diaghilev. Diaghilev opens the folder with a sigh and reads the contents of the document.]

Diaghilev: So apparently a whiff of whimsy is the delight of a child, and the morning dew is actually morning dew. At least obtaining a unicorn hair isn't a challenge nowadays. How… creative. Where would we even get a child?

Everwood: We have Researcher James in my department.

Diaghilev: I… what? You have a child in your department?

Everwood: He's six years old.

Diaghilev: Fine. I'm willing to accept that you have a child in your department that researches an anomalous children's band and the company that manipulates them. But how do you know all of this is accurate?

Everwood: Remember Wonder World tee-ehm?

Diaghilev: How could I forget?

Everwood: We offer amnesty programs for citizens who want to leave Wonder World tee-ehm and enter the non-anomalous world. In exchange for information on their employer, we set them up with everything necessary to survive on the outside. We had a recent Wonder University flunky approach our department with knowledge on how to make the Misters, which were discontinued in the early 90's.

Diaghilev: Wonder… University.

Everwood: It's like a normal university except it teaches the history of the Wondertainment brand and its lines of products, economi—

Diaghilev: I don't need a full explanation.

[Diaghilev sighs. There is a five-second silence.]

Everwood: So…?

Diaghilev: This all seems quite ridiculous, Doctor.

Everwood: Doctor Wondertainment as a whole is a bit ridiculous but I don't let that take away from my enjoyment of learning more about it.

Diaghilev: And you understand that alchemy is not a toy to be played with, yes? It's a force to be respected. A single errant aether could kill you in an instant.

Everwood: Believe me, I understand. I pored over your research before contacting you. But you're the only one that can help me, Director.

Diaghilev: I am not certain you fully grasp how momentous the creation of a homunculus is. It is not something that any Alchemist simply just creates.

Everwood: Then wouldn't you want to be known as the Alchemist who created one?

[There is a brief silence.]

Diaghilev: Even if I were to agree, I feel as if this agreement is a bit stacked in your favor. What do I get out of this deal?

Everwood: Aside from the recognition of being the Alchemist who created a homunculus for the Foundation? I don't know. What would you want?

Diaghilev: I want equal research rights to the homunculus. I've never had the chance to study one up close and this would be an excellent opportunity for me and my research.

Everwood: Deal.

Diaghilev: Very well. You will have your homunculus, Doctor.

Everwood: Thank you. Sincerely. I can't wait to see what we learn.

<END LOG>

Addendum 9725.02: Following the meeting between Doctor Everwood and Director Diaghilev, efforts to obtain the necessary components to create the homunculus were undertaken by the Procurement and Liquidation Department. After the acquisition of all necessary components, a meeting between both parties was organized to discuss the fine details of the project. The meeting took place in Doctor Everwood's office in Site-55's Wondertainment Research Wing.

<BEGIN LOG>

[Diaghilev enters the office. Everwood stands to greet him. James continues to play with a toy truck in the corner of the room.]

Everwood: Hello and welcome to my humble little corner of Site-55.

Diaghilev: Greetings.

[The two shake hands.]

Everwood: That over there is Researcher James. James, come say hi to Director Diaghilev.

[James looks up from his truck and waves to Diaghilev. Diaghilev approaches him and kneels.]

Diaghilev: Hello, young man. It's nice to meet you.

James: You're old.

[Diaghilev frowns and stands up.]

Everwood: James, that's very rude. You shouldn't say that to people. I'm sorry, Director.

Diaghilev: How do you get anything done with a child in the office?

[The group sits down.]

Everwood: He has his days. Plus, it's useful to have a child on staff when most of the anomalies you deal with only work with children. Anyway, I heard from Helen that you finally got everything together for SCP-9725, and all we need to do now is put it together. How exciting!

Diaghilev: That is correct. Well, mostly correct. There is still one thing we haven't discussed.

Everwood: Oh?

Diaghilev: I've been doing my own research on these Little Misters of yours. They all apparently have names that designate their anomalous property. Is that not right?

Everwood: That's right.

Diaghilev: Well, one of the necessary ingredients is a name.

Everwood: That's correct. I've been putting off coming up with a name, to be honest.

Diaghilev: Fret not, Doctor. I have a suitable name for the resulting homunculus.

Everwood: Do tell.

Diaghilev: Mister Diaghilev.

[James slams his truck against the ground and mimics an explosion.]

Everwood: Eh… I dunno about that.

Diaghilev: Oh come on now. It's perfect.

Everwood: If the name dictates its anomalous properties, don't you think it's a little dangerous to give a homunculus the ability to perform Alchemy?

Diaghilev: Exactly! That's why it's perfect. It will help me with my work as I study it.

Everwood: What if it doesn't want to help you and it instead uses its alchemic prowess to breach containment?

Diaghilev: I can handle myself around a treacherous opponent.

Everwood: Okay, new rule; no naming the homunculus after ourselves. Not only is it egotistical, but it's also sure to create some unforeseen problems for us down the line.

[Diaghilev folds his arms and rolls his eyes.]

Diaghilev: Very well. Then what do you propose?

Everwood: I was thinking something along the lines of 'Mister Wondertainment'.

[James rolls his truck along the ground and makes 'vroom' noises as it moves.]

Diaghilev: I disagree. What if the homunculus picks up the properties of Doctor Wondertainment and breaches containment using its thaumaturgical and alchemical properties?

Everwood: Hmm. The way I imagined it, it was more along the lines of the concept of the knowledge of Doctor Wondertainment, but I suppose we can't afford to leave that up to interpretation. We need something simple.

Diaghilev: Not to mention that for all we know, this Doctor Wondertainment is also an Alchemist. They did make this homunculus, after all.

Everwood: That's a good point. Maybe we need something simpler.

Diaghilev: For what it's worth, I agree with the idea that we need something simple.

[James puts down his truck and approaches them.]

Everwood: Not now, buddy. We're a little busy.

James: Why not call him Mister Safe?

Diaghilev: Safe?

James: Like Safe, Yoo… Yoo… Yooklid, and Keter.

[Everwood and Diaghilev look at one another.]

Everwood: I… I think that could work.

Diaghilev: This kid is smart. You have a bright future ahead of you, young man.

Everwood: So are we settled on Mister Safe?

Diaghilev: It sounds agreeable to me.

<END LOG>

Addendum 9725.03: On 20/05/2022, the ritual to create the homunculus outlined by SCP-9725 was carried out by Director Diaghilev in Site-55's Experiment Chamber 22-Alpha. Present alongside Diaghilev was Doctor Everwood, Junior Alchemist Arturo Genuomo, and Researcher James. The following is a log of recorded interaction while attempting to create SCP-9725-2.

<BEGIN LOG>

[Diaghilev and Genuomo stand in front of a table containing the requisite materials placed near the center of the testing chamber. They are shoveling clay from a container onto the ground. Everwood sits behind the blast doors with James. Everwood is writing in their notebook and James is playing on his Nintendo Switch.]

Diaghilev: I can't remember the last time I had to do physical labor. My back hurts.

Genuomo: It's not so bad, Director. Soon we will be done and we will have created our very own homunculus!

Everwood: Sorry I can't help. Arm. [Everwood points to their stump.]

Diaghilev: Worry not, Doctor. We are almost done anyway.

[The two continue shoveling for two minutes, at which point Diaghilev stops and approaches the other materials.]

Genuomo: Alright. That should be the last of it.

Diaghilev: Thank goodness. And now for the easy part.

[Diaghilev turns to the table and begins dumping the pre-measured ingredients onto the clay.]

Diaghilev: And that was the last of the morning dew. Now, all we need is the whiff of whimsy. James, if you would be so kind?

[James looks up from his Switch and stands. He turns to face Everwood.]

Everwood: Go on, buddy. We need you in order for this to work.

[James exits the observation room and enters the testing chamber. ]

[There is a ten-second silence.]

Diaghilev: Well then. Do your thing, Mister James.

James: What am I supposed to do?

Genuomo: Be amazed, I suppose.

James: I don't get it.

Everwood: You're gonna have to do something to wow him.

Genuomo: I got this. My little cousins loved this back when I used to live at home.

[Genuomo approaches James and performs a finger trick, appearing to have removed his finger.]

Genuomo: Eh? Eh?

Diaghilev: What on earth are you doing, Arturo?

Everwood: You're going to have to try harder than that. He's used to playing with Wondertainment toys so you're really going to have to knock his socks off.

Diaghilev: How are we meant to compete with a person whose entire purpose is to make children's toys? We're kind of out of our depth here.

Everwood: I could go get something from the lab and see if it inspires some awe in him.

Genuomo: I have an idea. You could demonstrate your alchemic prowess for him, Director. That's sure to wow anyone.

Diaghilev: No. Alchemy is not a toy.

James: What is alchemy?

Diaghilev: It is the weaving of the Aethers which bind reality together. To mess with alchemy is to mess with life itself.

James: I want to see mister old man do alchemy.

Everwood: His name is Director Diaghilev, James.

James: Director Di… Die… Dieolov. I want to see Director Dieolov do alchemy.

Everwood: Diaghilev. Di-a-ghi-lev. Diaghilev. Try again, buddy.

James: Die… Dia… Diahay… Diaghilev.

Everwood: Thank you. Director?

Diaghilev: No.

Genuomo: Well, he is going to see you perform it anyway once we get him to produce the whimsy. So I figure why not give him a taste of it?

[Diaghilev sighs and palms his face.]

Diaghilev: Very well. But only once. And if that doesn't work, Doctor Everwood will go up to their lab and find a toy for him to play with.

Everwood: Deal.

Diaghilev: Stand clear. Also, Arturo, move the table while you're at it.

[James moves back towards the observation room. Genuomo shuffles the table formerly holding SCP-9725-1 and the other materials out of the way and places it against the corner of the testing chamber.]

Diaghilev: Now pay attention, James, because I am only going to do this once.

[Diaghilev closes his eyes and moves his arms in a circular motion, then extends his right hand forward. He forms a fist.]

Diaghilev: Ignis!

[A plume of flame extends from Diaghilev's fist. It winds around his arm and shoulders, then extends to the other arm before extinguishing itself against the ground.]

[James begins clapping excitedly.]

James: Whoa! Cool!

[A purple wisp manifests overhead James. It quickly moves through the glass window of the observation room and into the testing chamber before suddenly swerving down towards the pile of materials in the middle of the chamber. The pile begins glowing with a similar purple aura.]

Everwood: I think it worked! Quick, Director Diaghilev!

[Diaghilev turns to face the mixture and proceeds to douse it with Aequeous Aether. The mixture begins to coagulate into SCP-9725-1.]

Genuomo: My turn!

[Genuomo heats SCP-9725-1 with Igneous Aether, causing it to become semi-solid.]

Diaghilev: What's next, Doctor?

Everwood: We need to let it cool so we can shape it.

Genuomo: How long?

Everwood: An hour.

James: Alchemy is so cool! I want to be an alchemist.

Diaghilev: If only it were that easy, my child.

Everwood: So we have an hour to kill. Is anyone down for a game of cards?

Diaghilev: What's your poison?

James: 52 pick-up!

Everwood: No.

James: Go Fish?

Everwood: Poker. I love you, James, but I'm tired of playing 52 pick-up and Go Fish with you.

James: Aw…

[Diaghilev and Genuomo approach the observation room. SCP-9725-1 glows in the background.]

Genuomo: Count me in.

Diaghilev: Me too.

James: Can I play?

Everwood: Eh, sure. We'll teach you.

[One hour of extraneous video feed expunged.]

[James shows his cards to Everwood. They nod and whisper in his ear.]

James: Full house!

Everwood: Two pair.

Genuomo: Ace high.

Diaghilev: [Grumbling.] One pair.

Everwood: Heh.

[Genuomo's phone alarm begins to ring. He pulls it out of his pocket and turns it off.]

Genuomo: I think it's about time.

Everwood: Alright, I will I get down to shaping it then.

[Everwood rises from their chair and enters the testing chamber. They take off their lab coat and toss it towards the table in the corner.]

Diaghilev: Whoa, wait a minute there, Doctor. You're not just going to touch it without some sort of protection, are you?

Everwood: This is a Doctor Wondertainment product. The company wouldn't hurt anyone, do you have any idea how bad that would be for business?

Diaghilev: If you are so confident, then by all means go ahead.

[Everwood approaches SCP-9725-1 and begins molding it with their hand.]

Everwood: You know, I took a pottery class back when I still had my other arm and I gotta say, molding this is much easier than molding normal clay. It's like it knows what I want to do with it.

James: Can I try?

Everwood: No, James. Stay over there.

James: Aww…

Diaghilev: So what are you trying to shape it into, Doctor?

Everwood: The most average person one could imagine.

[SCP-9725-1's purple glow extends to Everwood for the duration of the molding process. They continue to mold SCP-9725-1 until it assumes a vaguely humanoid shape. Everwood steps away from SCP-9725-1 and the purple glow fades from them. Notably, they are not dirtied from sculpting SCP-9725-1 and their clothes remain in the same condition as they were prior to engaging with it.]

Everwood: That's about as good as I'm gonna get it. Gotta say I'm impressed with myself.

Diaghilev: So now I assume it is our turn to breathe life into it.

Genuomo: I'm ready if you are, Elder.

Everwood: Let me get out of here first if you don't mind.

[Everwood moves away from SCP-9725-1 and enters the observation room with James in tow after grabbing their lab coat.]

James: Why won't you let me have fun? Meanie.

Everwood: It sounds like someone doesn't want to play video games when this is all over.

James: No! I want to play video games! Please!

Everwood: Don't worry kiddo, it was just a joke. You can still play video games when we're done with SCP-9725. Just behave, okay?

James: I promise.

Diaghilev: Ready, Arturo?

Genuomo: Ready, Elder.

[Genuomo and Diaghilev both take a deep breath and blast SCP-9725-1 with Aeronous Aether. SCP-9725-1 begins stirring.]

Unknown: What is my name?

Everwood: Your name is Mister Safe!

[There is a blinding flash of light. Video recording cuts. Diaghilev, Genuomo, Everwood, and James exclaim in surprise.]

[There is a ten-second silence.]

Unknown: Uh… Why is everyone stari—

[The cameras of the experiment chamber fail.]

<END LOG>

SCP-9725-2


Item #: SCP-9725-2

SCP-9725.

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9725-2 is currently contained within former Experiment Chamber 22-Alpha. The room has been furnished with standard humanoid containment chamber objects. In addition to these furnishings, SCP-9725-1 is permitted a television and non-internet capable game devices. Researcher James is currently permitted to visit SCP-9725-2 in its cell so long as he is supervised by at least one Level-2 personnel.

Description: SCP-9725-2 is a humanoid male of average build, 1.5 m in height. Though it is able to move freely within its containment chamber, SCP-9725-2 is unable to leave the room in any capacity, nor has it displayed the desire to do so since containment began. SCP-9725-2 displays no other anomalous qualities, though it was made via anomalous means utilizing SCP-9725 and SCP-9725-1. A tattoo reading "Mr. Safe, from Little Misters ® by… The Foundation?!" appears on its left bicep.

Addendum 9725-2.01: The following is an audio log of an interview carried out with SCP-9725-2 immediately upon manifestation.

Interviewed: SCP-9725-2

Interviewee: Doctor Everwood

Note: The interview was recorded on Doctor Everwood's personal tape recorder, as the testing chamber's cameras malfunctioned.

<BEGIN LOG>

Everwood: Okay, we should be recording now. Hello! If you could please state your name for the record?

SCP-9725-2: Mr. Safe. But you know that already, didn't you? You named me, after all.

Everwood: Well, yes, but it's just standard procedure. I think. I don't get to do a lot of humanoid interactions. What is your purpose, Mister Safe?

SCP-9725-2: I dunno. You made me. If anyone should know my purpose it would be you.

Everwood: Okay. Okay, uh… Do you feel like leaving where you are right now? Maybe going back to Wonder World tee-ehm?

SCP-9725-2: Not really.

Everwood: Okay, good. So you know about Wonder World tee-ehm?

SCP-9725-2: No. All I know is I was made by the Foundation and I don't want to leave this place. Whatever that means. What's the Wonder World tee-ehm?

Everwood: I uh, I'm not sure I can disclose that. Yeah, no. I won't disclose that. If you wouldn't mind waiting here for a moment?

SCP-9725-2: Sure. I don't feel like doing anything else anyway.

[There is a slight rustling sound and footsteps.]

Everwood: I think we succeeded in making a Safe class anomaly.

Diaghilev: If it is to be trusted.

Everwood: Fair enough. We need to find out if it can even leave. I'll go talk to— Where is James?

[There is a slight rustling sound.]

Everwood: James! Get back here right now!

James: But I thought he might like my Switch.

SCP-9725-2: I do like this Switch. I like photographing these strange creatures. You said they were called 'Pokémon'?

Everwood: Get back, James. It could be dangerous.

James: But his name is Mr. Safe. How could he be dangerous?

SCP-9725-2: It's true. I don't want to breach containment.

Everwood: How does it know about containment?

Diaghilev: It knew about the Foundation earlier. I assume it is just as much a part of it as we are due to the circumstances of its creation.

Everwood: Right then. Give him back his Switch and come with me, please.

SCP-9725-2: Okay.

James: Look, I took a picture of a Gengar!

SCP-9725-2: Fascinating.

[There is a slight rustling and multiple pairs of footsteps.]

Everwood: Alright. Here we are at the door to the observation room. Mister Safe, if you would, please follow me through the door.

SCP-9725-2: But I don't want to.

Everwood: Oh come now. Surely you want to, uh, eat something? We have a canteen where all the protocol-compliant anomalies eat. Maybe you'll make some friends.

SCP-9725-2: Friends and food do sound nice, but—

Everwood: Exactly! So come on, follow me through the door.

SCP-9725-2: I told you, I don't want to leave.

Diaghilev: I wonder what is keeping it in here? Perhaps it is some sort of advanced alchemical ward?

Everwood: I think it has more to do with the fact that we named him Mister Safe and Safe class objects don't breach containment. At least not normally.

James: Look, I took a picture of a Clefairy. It's not my favorite, but it's still pretty cool I think.

SCP-9725-2: What an interesting pink creature. It reminds me of the Gengar you found earlier. Are they related?

Everwood: I guess we're going to have to turn this room into its containment chamber. Shouldn't be too hard to retrofit, I don't think. And it's bigger than a regular containment chamber, so Mister Safe really lucked out here.

James: Can I keep coming down here to show him the Pokémon I take pictures of? And show him my other games? He seems cool.

SCP-9725-2: Please? Can he come to visit me? I want to learn more about these "Pokémon".

Everwood: We'll put in a request for it. How does that sound?

SCP-9725-2: Does that mean no?

James: That means maybe.

SCP-9725-2: Oh, that reminds me. I have something to give you, doctor person. I think you're a doctor. You have a lab coat on, so I think it's a safe bet to assume you are one.

Everwood: I am a doctor, yes. What do you have for me?

SCP-9725-2: Here you go.

[There is a slight rustling as Doctor Everwood places the recording device in their lab coat pocket.]

Everwood: Oh boy. That's not good.

<END LOG>
