Item #: 9878

Profile of mask found at SCP-9878-2

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: Under agreement with the local government, the Foundation is to maintain stewardship over SCP-9878. Personnel are to turn away civilians and specifically track historians of Anglo-Saxon or Germanic history and ensure they do not approach any SCP-9878 sites. When government liaisons request it, they are to be granted access to SCP-9878 for sanctioned uses, as outlined in the Bucher Accords.

Under no circumstances are personnel to intercede in government use of SCP-9878. If they feel uncomfortable in their role, they may request reassignment outside the region.

Description: SCP-9878 are a series of thaumaturgically and necromantically active Anglo-Saxon archaeological sites. They are also distinguished by their exceptionally well-preserved condition. Their anomalous properties may only be utilised by certain individuals; it is not known what criteria are used in the selection, but it is known that Prime Minister █████ qualifies for the use of all SCP-9878 instances.

SCP-9878-1 is a church, dated to ca. 500 AD, whose graveyard has been emptied. Each grave has been unearthed, and the remains are scattered across the pews. When eligible individuals enter the main building, these remains answer questions regarding the presence, layout, and opinions of religious groups within four hundred and forty-four miles. Extensive use of this ability has been key to the monitoring of sectarian sentiment across the region. Unfortunately, the object possesses no ability to affect this sentiment, and violence has only deepened over time.

SCP-9878-2 is a burial-mound of an undetermined individual. It is filled mostly with various fairly mundane grave-goods, but contains one major anachronism. Much like the Sutton Hoo site, it contains a ship as its centrepiece; this ship is a nineteenth-century tea clipper. Within the hold is a stock of tea, which refills whenever the craft is unoccupied. Drinking this tea induces strong feelings of nationalism and patriotism, which last up to six months. The government possesses a reserve which it historically exported to splinter-states, with a focus on royalist holdouts such as █████████.

SCP-9878-3 is a scriptorium, which contains several hundred books written and illuminated in the monastic Anglo-Saxon style. The particular books vary between visits, but are generally late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century European and especially British literature. Modern English written at a designated lectern will be duplicated in bureaucratic centres across the country, providing a prompt and efficient method to disperse laws, decrees, and news. █████ expresses some discomfort at the prospect of erasing regional linguistic differences by forcing conformity to his own standardised English, but considers effective information-delivery more important.

SCP-9878-4 is a palace, strongly resembling reconstructions of Winchester Castle as it existed during the time of Alfred the Great. Before its entrance is a plinth, upon which lies a Bible whose contents have been altered. Instead of containing the typical Biblical narrative, its pages are filled by repetitions of the phrase þām þe fylgeþ1. When an eligible individual seats themselves upon SCP-9878-4’s throne, they may issue commands which are unequivocally obeyed. █████ has historically been hesitant to wield this power, believing it to be an overextension of his authority, but made extensive use of it during 1948-1950 to achieve unification.

The sites are located as follows:

SITE LOCATION
SCP-9878-1 Countryside outside Srikaranpur, Rajasthan
SCP-9878-2 The Sundarbans, West Bengal
SCP-9878-3 Poona, Maharashtra
SCP-9878-4 Outskirts of Hyderabad

SCP-9878.raw_source: [[include :scp-wiki:info:start]] **SCP-9878:** Here is the Giver of Gold **Author:** [[*user whenwerewe]] [*https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/whenwerewe Here's my page!] [[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] **Item #:** 9878 [[include component:image-block name=http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/scp-9878/mask.jpg|caption=Profile of mask found at SCP-9878-2|width=150px]] **Object Class:** Safe **Special Containment Procedures:** Under agreement with the local government, the Foundation is to maintain stewardship over SCP-9878. Personnel are to turn away civilians and specifically track historians of Anglo-Saxon or Germanic history and ensure they do not approach any SCP-9878 sites. When government liaisons request it, they are to be granted access to SCP-9878 for sanctioned uses, as outlined in the Bucher Accords. Under no circumstances are personnel to intercede in government use of SCP-9878. If they feel uncomfortable in their role, they may request reassignment outside the region. **Description:** SCP-9878 are a series of thaumaturgically and necromantically active Anglo-Saxon archaeological sites. They are also distinguished by their exceptionally well-preserved condition. Their anomalous properties may only be utilised by certain individuals; it is not known what criteria are used in the selection, but it is known that Prime Minister █████ qualifies for the use of all SCP-9878 instances. SCP-9878-1 is a church, dated to ca. 500 AD, whose graveyard has been emptied. Each grave has been unearthed, and the remains are scattered across the pews. When eligible individuals enter the main building, these remains answer questions regarding the presence, layout, and opinions of religious groups within four hundred and forty-four miles. Extensive use of this ability has been key to the monitoring of sectarian sentiment across the region. Unfortunately, the object possesses no ability to affect this sentiment, and violence has only deepened over time. SCP-9878-2 is a burial-mound of an undetermined individual. It is filled mostly with various fairly mundane grave-goods, but contains one major anachronism. Much like the Sutton Hoo site, it contains a ship as its centrepiece; this ship is a nineteenth-century tea clipper. Within the hold is a stock of tea, which refills whenever the craft is unoccupied. Drinking this tea induces strong feelings of nationalism and patriotism, which last up to six months. The government possesses a reserve which it historically exported to splinter-states, with a focus on royalist holdouts such as █████████. SCP-9878-3 is a scriptorium, which contains several hundred books written and illuminated in the monastic Anglo-Saxon style. The particular books vary between visits, but are generally late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century European and especially British literature. Modern English written at a designated lectern will be duplicated in bureaucratic centres across the country, providing a prompt and efficient method to disperse laws, decrees, and news. █████ expresses some discomfort at the prospect of erasing regional linguistic differences by forcing conformity to his own standardised English, but considers effective information-delivery more important. SCP-9878-4 is a palace, strongly resembling reconstructions of Winchester Castle as it existed during the time of Alfred the Great. Before its entrance is a plinth, upon which lies a Bible whose contents have been altered. Instead of containing the typical Biblical narrative, its pages are filled by repetitions of the phrase //þām þe fylgeþ//[[footnote]]trans. “To he who follows”.[[/footnote]]. When an eligible individual seats themselves upon SCP-9878-4’s throne, they may issue commands which are unequivocally obeyed. █████ has historically been hesitant to wield this power, believing it to be an overextension of his authority, but made extensive use of it during 1948-1950 to achieve unification. The sites are located as follows: ||~ SITE ||~ LOCATION|| || SCP-9878-1 || Countryside outside Srikaranpur, Rajasthan || || SCP-9878-2 || The Sundarbans, West Bengal || || SCP-9878-3 || Poona, Maharashtra || || SCP-9878-4 || Outskirts of Hyderabad || [[div class="footer-wikiwalk-nav"]] [[=]] << [[[SCP-9877]]] | SCP-9878 | [[[SCP-9879]]] >> [[/=]] [[/div]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] > **Filename:**mask.jpg > **Author:** Chris Daw/Axle Arts > **License:** CC BY-SA 4.0 > **Source Link:** https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sutton_Hoo_Helmet_maquette_-_detail.jpg [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]

SCP-9880.raw_content:
The light is preserved.

URGENT NOTICE FROM THE EMERGENCIES DIVISION

FOR DIRECTOR NOAH TORRENT: As per NORMALITY PROTOCOL 6-14, and due to your role as the director of Site-188, you are currently in charge of maintaining baseline reality for the city of Québec and the majority of its metropolitan area.

SCP-9880 was activated on all selected settlements and will not deactivate until the end of the ongoing threat. The city and the 516.92 km2 of land surrounding it are currently contained. You are currently the only member of your settlement who was made aware of the existence of SCP-9880 and the current situation.

Any order given by you concerning the settlement will be followed by Division members. You are charged to ensure the current attributes concerning the city must remain factual throughout its containment, and that any deviation must be corrected:

  • a population of around 650,000;
  • the city is located near the Saint Laurent River;
  • French is the dominant language, with a strong English presence;
  • a visible minority population of 32.8% at maximum;
  • hockey is the most popular sport;
  • Site-188 is the main SCP Foundation Site and the fourth biggest facility throughout Canada.

We count on you for the light to be preserved.

Item: SCP-9880

Object Class: K-Thaumiel

Special Containment Procedures: Emergencies Division personnel are to ensure containment of their respective settlements at all costs. Containment efforts should focus on transportation of water, food, and medical supplies into the settlement, protection of the settlement from outside forces, and misinformation programs directed at settlement residents, including other Foundation personnel.

No Division member is to interact directly with citizens of a settlement. If citizens or Foundation personnel learn of the ongoing scenario, they are to be administered amnestics as soon as possible. If there is a shortage of amnestics, termination or recruitment within the Emergencies Division is recommended.

YEAR 1

The Division told me I have to keep a journal of everything I do during the year. It's supposed to reassure me and the Division. Sure.

The citizens are unaware, as they should be. I've maintained many narratives to ensure that none get out of the city: lengthy permits, health clearances, or forms that are mysteriously delayed or denied. Some complaints are made, but nothing major. I think that dome is brainwashing them to think everything is alright.

Site-188 isn't changing much, really. They all work for the Division now, even if they are unaware of it. The only big change is the arrival of new anomalies to study and contain within the facility. But even so, they do their best to get the job done, as always.

The Division doesn't tell me much about the outside. All I know is that they have selected agents from all over the world sent to search for the anomalies necessary to resolve the situation. I tried to ask them how long it would take, but they replied that it depended. When I asked them what it depended on, they replied, “Everything.” I don't know whether I should feel reassured or terrified. I still don't know much, really. Despite being charged with taking care of the supposed "light", they keep me in the dark.

One Division member came to me not long ago. I think he was part of the medical transport team. He asked me if he could join the settlement as a citizen. I don't know what the procedure is for those kinds of things, or if I'm the one in charge of creating the procedures, so I've said that I'll allow him after a certain amount of work. Whatever that means.

Status:

  • A population of ~620,000
  • The city is located near the Saint Laurent River
  • French is the dominant language, with a strong English presence
  • Visible minority population of 31.3%
  • Hockey is the most popular sport
  • Site-188 is the main SCP Foundation Site and the fourth biggest facility throughout Canada

The light is preserved.

Description: SCP-9880 is a blend of 13 major thaumargic rituals, 76 memetic manipulations, 189 various micro-rituals, and 10^7 liters of water, creating a spherical dome reaching both above and below ground. The size of the dome adjusts itself to the size of the contained settlement.

Once activated, it is impossible for every living being to physically or anomalously enter or leave the area affected by SCP-9880. Physical force does not affect the dome's durability, and use of any thaumaturgy will have no effect either, no matter the amount of EVE energy accumulated. Souls' ritual, or any ritual that may remove one's spirit from a body, is superfluous, as even sentient ectoplasmic matter will be contained by the dome.

Thaumaturgic Passport

The inner layer of SCP-9880 possesses a memetic effect that alters perception of the world outside the dome, ensuring that no environmental damage is visible, no anomalous phenomena are apparent, and the sky remains blue during daytime and full of stars during night. This layer also induces a lack of engagement with anything outside of the affected location, with any individual viewing SCP-9880's inside surface feeling a sudden disinterest in leaving. These effects can be overcome by individuals with high Cognitive Resistance Values and are rendered ineffective for every Division member with the Antimeme-023 inoculation.

The only way to counter the physical presence of the dome is with the use of a Thaumaturgic Passport, which takes the form of a pin shaped like the Foundation's logo. Once the nature of the passport's use is revealed to the person wearing or holding the pin, they are able to pass through the dome's thaumaturgical barrier without difficulty.


YEAR 8

That new "Duty Points" system I've created, which is supposed to "dictate who may join the city as citizens depending on what prowess and years of service they have given for the Division," seems to be working. But it's far from perfect.

That kid I talked to years ago came to me again. I barely recognized him. He seemed much older, and he had a large scar running down his face. He told me that he could join the Québec colony now because this was what he had been promised after years of service and accumulating enough Duty Points. I told him I couldn't. The city's minority population already reached its maximum, and any new arrivals would upset the status quo. I told him I was sorry and suggested he ask me again in a few months, and we'll see if the numbers have changed.

Apparently, that same kid later assaulted and fatally injured a senior official member of the Emergencies Division to acquire the Thaumaturgic Password, granting him unauthorized access to the settlement. He actually managed to enter the city. That kid is in my city, hiding from his duty, with a key to let others in. I can't believe this.

They assured me that his name and previous achievements for the Division were removed from the DEEPWELL archive and that he will be forgotten in our next life. That's not enough. I need him out of my city. I need him terminated.

The city is not going strong. I've maintained the narrative that we're going through a severe economic depression. The stats are not good either. I suspect that other members of the Division are admitting people into the city without my knowledge. I alone should take care of the light.

Status:

  • A population of ~550,000
  • The city is located near the Saint Laurent River
  • Both French and English are the dominant languages
  • Visible minority population of 36.1%
  • Hockey is the most popular sport
  • Site-188 is the main SCP Foundation Site and the fourth biggest facility throughout Canada

The light is preserved.

SCP-9880 was created by the Emergencies Division at the request of the Department of Continuity prior to the current K-class crisis. The purpose of SCP-9880 is to contain a surviving remnant of normalcy in a situation where most or all of the world is affected by a K-class scenario, or a similar situation where baseline reality is no longer the foundational reference point. SCP-9880 activates automatically as soon as the Foundation detects that more than 75% of humanity on Earth has perished or been affected by an anomalous phenomenon. The contained settlements are maintained to ensure the following;

  • The original idea of a world under Veil is maintained, with no alteration, once the K-class scenario is resolved.
  • No other civilization created after the K-class scenario will take over normalcy as we once knew it.1
  • Foundation personnel inside the settlement may work in a healthy environment.
  • Foundation personnel helping the Division may be granted full amnestic treatment and subsequent reintegration into the settlement as veiled citizens under certain conditions.
Footnotes
1. Any other post-K-class new civilization not maintained by the Division must be terminated.

YEAR 16

I've allowed a few citizens who are really insistent on leaving to let them do so. It hurts the stats, but at least they'll be helping the Division from the outside.

I've also elevated the Duty Points necessary to join the settlement again. A group of Division members has protested against this and even refused to work. I expected this. The Division confirmed later that the traitors had been terminated, and their identities were removed from DEEPWELL. They shall be forgotten.

I've heard that Québec is the last settlement of America. The last one fell due to "mismanagement." I knew it. My city is the strongest. The only one worthy to be kept.

I say that, but with each passing day, I fear that it is less and less the city I know.

No one in the city is aware of the millions dead outside. No one is aware of the dome currently surrounded by dead bodies. No one is aware of the many I've killed myself. No one is aware of reality. I wish I could have taken amnestics when there were still some left. I wish I could be ignorant again. I wish I could be normal like all of them.

Status:

  • A population of ~300,000
  • The city is located near the Saint Laurent River
  • No dominant languages
  • Visible minority population of 41.1%
  • Most popular sport is unknown
  • Site-188 is the main SCP Foundation Site and the second biggest facility throughout Canada

The light is preserved.

Citizens inside the settlements are to remain reassured that their world is not at end, and that there is no reason for them to leave the place. This is maintained by Veil.aic, the Artificial Intelligent Conscript in charge of information within the contained settlements.

Veil.aic possesses a high memory storage to maintain a detailed profile of all inhabitants present in the settlement, as well as an intelligent Voice Impostor system that can imitate all related Profiles stored in memory. The main function of the AIC is to call and respond in the voice of relatives and acquaintances of the settlement's population. The AIC is also charged with maintaining fake international news of an under-Veil outside world through artificially generated images.

Foundation facilities located in the settlements are to study anomalies related to the current K-class scenario with the objective of developing countermeasures. Only high-ranking personnel are to be aware of the reality of the situation. This measure is intended to preserve operational stability and ensure that staff continue to function in a controlled, low-stress environment, unburdened by awareness of the broader collapse. Veil.aic is tasked with generating and distributing falsified Foundation documentation of various Foundation facilities across the world to maintain the appearance that external conditions remain stable.

YEAR 27

A large famine. That's the current narrative, and the closest to the truth I've ever allowed into the city. People are starving to death, and the few with enough strength to try and find a better place elsewhere will be met with disappointment. Or a bullet to the head if they don't join the Division.

That's what "normalcy" is, right? That's the only way to explain this hell. But this isn't supposed to be hell. This is supposed to be the last memory of our world. But how can one see this place and think "this is the world I once knew." I sure don't. It's not right. Yet it should be, cause that's all we have left.

The other Foundation agents of Site-188 don't bother with their work anymore. They're too occupied spending time with their friends and families. I don't even know if the ones I love are still alive. I don't want to know. At least I can afford this ignorance.

I've asked the Division when it will be over. Last time, they said a "few" years. Has it not been more? Has it not been enough? They haven't answered me. They no longer respond to any of my messages or orders. It has been a long time since I last saw food and all other necessities being transported to the city. I'm scared they might have given up on this place. They've left us to die slowly while they bother with the more important parts of this doomed world.

Wait, that's what it's all about, isn't it? We're waiting for the end of the world to end? We're conscient enough to admit that the end is here, yet we're stupid enough to think that there's a chance for us. To think that the past'll remember us. But we're not supposed to think. We're all supposed to have joined the dead long ago, rotting among all other corpses decorating the world we once knew.

But we're not dead.

No. We have to keep working. We have to keep hoping for a better time. For a better world. They've given up on us, but we won't. Not until.

Not until.

Status:

  • A population of less than 100,000
  • The city is located near the Saint Laurent River
  • No dominant languages
  • No visible minority
  • Most popular sport is unknown
  • Site-188 is the main SCP Foundation Site and the biggest facility throughout Canada

The light is preserved.

Once the K-class scenario is resolved and Earth is confirmed to be mostly habitable and non-hostile, SCP-9880's effects on the settlements will be lifted. The remaining members of the Emergencies Division will rejoin the Foundation. All individuals listed who assisted the Division in any way during the crisis will be rewarded. Their strength, courage, or sacrifice will be honored by being recorded in the Foundation's database.

It will be the duty of citizens and Foundation personnel to reconstruct normalcy as we once knew it, using all necessary tools. The light will shine once again, because of you.


YEAR ███

"One pair of every animal," said God to Noah, "the flood will come, and only your ark and its occupants will survive. Everything else of flesh I have created will die. Choose carefully who lives, as I believe you to be righteous."

As expected, the flood arrived, and every other life not present on the boat perished. The world Noah once knew came to an end, and now all he had to do was wait for the new one he was promised.

After 150 days, God did not remember Noah. However, being the righteous man he was told to be, Noah showed patience. Every day after taking care of each creature on board, he looked through a window of the wooden vessel, hoping to see the water subsiding and the land slowly showing its skin again. But the heavy rain decorating the horizon outside did not alter, not yet.

After 300 days, God did not remember Noah. A glimpse of doubt he expressed, which he immediately repressed, as he knows to trust the word of God. The animals, however, became agitated. Some of them have started fighting, others have lost hope and reason. Still, Noah believed in God's judgment, no matter what it might be.

After 500 days, God did not remember Noah. Doubt was no longer a glimpse but an ubiquitous fear. Had he somehow misunderstood God? Had he saved the wrong animals? Had God suddenly changed his mind? He continued to look out the window, wondering if there was even any land left beneath the water. The rations left on the boat slowly became rare. Half of the boat's occupants have been used to feed the other half. Noah himself had to taste some of the creatures he promised a new world to, and he hated himself to know they tasted delicious. He was the only one who still waited for the flood to end.

After 1000 days, God did not remember Noah. But Noah wished dearly he could forget about God. The rations on the boat have long been no more. All passengers have killed each other in the hope of a few more spells of existence in this dying world. In the end, Noah and one of the two mice were the last animals to survive. When he finally found it hidden behind a plank of wood, he grabbed and squeezed its little body firmly within a fist. The cries of the rodent echoed within the enormous hollow boat until it had no more air to scream. Noah swallowed his very last meal whole. Then, he remained still in the middle of his creation, his body moving along the flow of the sea outside. The ark still stood after the years gone by, but no boat, no matter how strong, could last an eternity. Noah promised himself to show silence until the very end. He knows not to break this promise.










After 100,000 days, God might have remembered Noah. But there was no one left to tell.




















Status:

  • Population of 1
  • The city is located near hell, heading towards
  • Silence is dominant
  • No one visible present
  • Site-188 is the only SCP Foundation Site

And the light was snuffed out.

Item #: SCP-9883

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9883 is contained within Office C-1013 at Site-███, formerly assigned to Dr. Daniel Koehl. Both the room's window and door are fitted with mesh screens1 scaled to SCP-9883. The window is to remain open at all times; this requirement is suspended when exterior temperatures fall below 15 °C, at which point the door is to remain open instead. During these periods, personnel are advised to check for written complaints regarding food scarcity. The ceiling of Office C-1013 has been coated with matte black paint to improve the legibility of such inscriptions.

The use of chemical pest-control agents harmful to arachnids is prohibited within Site-███.

ADMINISTRATIVE DIRECTIVE

Effective immediately, Dr. Daniel Koehl is prohibited from accessing Office C-1013.

Following Incident 9883.01, Dr. Koehl was determined to be emotionally compromised. He made repeated threats to terminate SCP-9883 and attempted to intimidate Site Security with an improvised weapon: right shoe.

This directive has been included here for operational clarity.


First observed word written by SCP-9883

Description: SCP-9883 is a specimen of Pholcus phalangioides2 exhibiting basic cognitive functions sufficient to comprehend rudimentary literacy and formulate simple concepts. This capacity has been expressed through the formation of silk letters (approximately 10 cm in height) constructed from repeated thread layering. The entity has been marked by a blue dot on its abdomen, distinguishing it from non-anomalous specimens on site.

SCP-9883 was first identified in Office C-1013 by Dr. Daniel Koehl, when he found the word “HELLO” inscribed along the ceiling's edge. Subsequent observation confirmed it as the source.

Current theory attributes the anomaly’s development to residual thaumaturgic radiation3 originating from experiments with ██████, conducted two floors below the office.

Addendum.01:

Containment Adjustment Log

Summary:
Over a 6-month period, Dr. Daniel Koehl submitted multiple requests to modify Office C-1013 in order to “optimize SCP-9883’s communicative potential.”

Below is an abridged record of relevant actions and outcomes.

Request: Repainting of ceiling in matte black to improve visibility of silk inscriptions.
Decision: Denied. Office C-1013 not recognized as containment environment.

Follow-up: Request to reclassify Office C-1013 as containment environment.
Decision: Approved.

Follow-up: Repainting of ceiling in matte black.
Decision: Approved. Work completed personally by Dr. Koehl after hours.

Follow-up: Reservation of standard mobile interview equipment.
Decision: Approved.

Results: Interview unsuccessful. SCP-9883 repeatedly layered “TOO LIGHT.”

Request: Reduction of light intensity within Office C-1013.
Decision: Approved. Pending submission of Form E-19.

Follow-up: (3) (re)submission(s) of Form E-19.
Decision: Approved. Estimated installation delay: 4–6 weeks.

Follow-up: Dr. Koehl was reminded the use of adhesive materials to obscure Site lighting systems is non-compliant, regardless of duration or intent.
Decision: Assigned mandatory refresher on Site fire safety standards.

Follow-up: Reservation of standard mobile interview equipment.
Decision: Approved. Only audio instruments.

Results: Interview unsuccessful. SCP-9883 refused to engage, citing “NO ENOUGH BUG.”

Request: Contacted Site Animal House directly for allocation of small-scale insect breeding unit to ensure consistent prey availability.
Decision: Denied. SCP-9883’s research priority does not warrant dedicated feeding infrastructure.

Follow-up: Contacted Mrs. Ana Wyss4 for informal guidance regarding fly-breeding equipment.
Decision: Approved. On the basis of personal discretion and prior acquaintance.

Follow-up: Disposal request for said equipment submitted the same week.
Decision: Approved.

Request: Verbal request to open window of Office C-1013 to increase air circulation and natural feeding opportunities.
Decision: Approved. Contingent on installation of a mesh screen preventing SCP-9883 containment breach.

Follow-up: Attending staff recommended consultation with Psychological Services.
Decision: Declined.

Follow-up: Package containing mesh screen intercepted at mailroom after being traced to unapproved vendor.
Decision: Returned to sender.

Follow-up: Custom apertured-mesh screen ordered from Facilities.
Decision: Denied. Custom alterations unsupported.

Follow-up: Dr. Koehl’s subsequent messages were redacted for language inconsistent with Foundation standards of professional conduct.

Addendum.02:

Incident 9883.01

Date: 08/09/2022

Summary: Personnel in the courtyard beneath Office C-1013 reported agitated shouting emanating from the office. Security was dispatched to the scene. Dr. Daniel Koehl was removed from the office and referred for psychological evaluation. The following Security footage was later reviewed.

VIDEO LOG

Date: 08/09/2022
Note: Dr. Daniel Koehl had repositioned the security camera in violation of Site regulations to provide an upward-facing view of the ceiling. SCP-9883’s silk inscriptions have been transcribed.

[BEGIN EXCERPT]

Dr. Koehl: “TOO COLD.” Too cold? You’ve got to be kidding me. I spend three months. Three months! Getting that mesh installed so you could have your precious window open and feed off natural insects, because God forbid a lady settles for farmed prey. Weeks of forms, risk assessments, containment waivers, and for what? So you can tell me you’re cold?

SCP-9883: FIX

Dr. Koehl: Fix. Oh, of course. Of course, fix. That’s what I do, isn’t it? You decide something’s wrong, and I fix it. What’s next? You'll want me to hunt down suitable bachelors for your eggs?

[SCP-9883 consumes the letters “C_LD”.]

SCP-9883: TOO LOUD

Dr. Koehl: “TOO LOUD,” she says. Now I'm too loud… [Laughs, voice cracking] You know what’s loud? The sound of my spine compressing as I crouch to make you a custom mesh out of fishing line because Facilities “doesn’t support custom apertures!” And it doesn’t stop there, no no no. Because Her Highness can’t stand standard site bulbs, so I had to do it all in near darkness, giving myself eyestrain every other day!

SCP-9883: MEAN

Dr. Koehl: I’m mean? You’re the most thankless, selfish, ungrateful arthropod I’ve ever met! Do you have any idea what admin’s been saying? Six months and not a single usable datum! Because every time I haul the interview equipment down here, you’re either too busy feeding, weaving, or thinking up some new demand for your personal butler!

[SCP-9883 retreats to its web.]

Dr. Koehl: Don’t you turn your abdomen on me! We’re finishing this conversation! You nitpick me all day, but the moment I point something out about you-

[SCP-9883 flings a silk-wrapped cocoon toward Dr. Koelh. It lands 2 cm off-center. An extended silence follows. Both SCP-9883 and Dr. Koehl remain motionless.]

Dr. Koehl: Did you just…

[Dr. Koelh reaches down, removes his right shoe, and raises it toward the ceiling.]

Dr. Koehl: Two can play at that game, 9883. And believe me, the odds are not in your favor anymore.

[Security personnel is heard knocking outside the office door.]

Security Officer: [Muffled] Dr. Koehl? Everything alright in there?

Dr. Koehl: Perfectly fine! Conducting an interview! Productive as ever!

Security Officer: [Muffled] Copy that, sir. We just had some noise complaints-

[Security enters the room, freezing mid-step.]

Security Officer: …Sir.

Dr. Koehl: What!

Security Officer: Sir, I’m gonna need you to put the shoe down.

Dr. Koehl: She started it! Check the ceiling! She’s mocking me! That little pest!

Security Officer: Alright, let’s-let’s take a breather outside the room, sir.

[Officers approach Dr. Koehl. He brandishes the shoe towards them.]

Dr. Koehl: No! You’ve got it backwards! She’s the anomaly, not me!

[There's a brief struggle between Security and Dr. Koehl. Security restrains Dr. Koehl and escorts him from the room.]

Dr. Koehl: I’ll put you in a jar! You here me? With the rest of your web-spinning colleagues, so you can enjoy baseline spider behavior! And if you make it through peer-review, I’ll take you to the pond, and feed you to the ducks! I’ll dangle you over the water by your own silk, like a little eight-legged teaba-

[Security and Dr. Koehl exit. The door remains slightly ajar. SCP-9883 descends on a silk thread, appearing to observe him being escorted down the corridor.]

[END EXCERPT]


Post-Incident Note: This exchange constitutes the most extensive display of communicative behavior ever recorded from SCP-9883, yielding the most significant data since its initial cataloguing. SCP-9883’s research priority has been accordingly upgraded.

Despite the progress achieved, Dr. Koehl will not be credited for these advancements due to conduct exhibited during the Incident. Administrative directive enacted. Disciplinary review ongoing. Estimated delay: 2–3 weeks.


SCP-9883

Footnotes
1. Woven barrier which filters by size.
2. Daddy long-legs or Cellar spider
3. Energetic byproducts of reality-altering phenomena, able to cause spontaneous anomaly formation in susceptible environments.
4. Staff member assigned to the Site Animal House

[[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:info-cw]] **Item #:** SCP-9883 **Object Class:** Safe **Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9883 is contained within Office C-1013 at Site-███, formerly assigned to Dr. Daniel Koehl. Both the room's window and door are fitted with mesh screens[[footnote]]Woven barrier which filters by size.[[/footnote]] scaled to SCP-9883. The window is to remain open at all times; this requirement is suspended when exterior temperatures fall below 15 °C, at which point the door is to remain open instead. During these periods, personnel are advised to check for written complaints regarding food scarcity. The ceiling of Office C-1013 has been coated with matte black paint to improve the legibility of such inscriptions. The use of chemical pest-control agents harmful to arachnids is prohibited within Site-███. [[div style="border:solid 1px #999999; background:#f1f1f1; padding:5px; margin-bottom: 10px;"]] [[=]] ++++ ADMINISTRATIVE DIRECTIVE Effective immediately, Dr. Daniel Koehl is prohibited from accessing Office C-1013. Following Incident 9883.01, Dr. Koehl was determined to be emotionally compromised. He made repeated threats to terminate SCP-9883 and attempted to intimidate Site Security with an improvised weapon: //right shoe//. This directive has been included here for operational clarity. [[/=]] [[/div]] @@@@ [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-features-source |slide-revealer=--] |float=true |align=right |width=100% |left-url=https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/scp-9883/Silk-Base.png |right-url=https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/scp-9883/Silk-Highlight.png |slider-start-percent=95 |slider-color=white |slider-circle-size=1.875rem |alt1=alt|alt1-text=Spider web on ceiling with the word "HELLO" vaguely written nearby. |alt2=alt|alt2-text=Spider web on ceiling with the word "HELLO" highlighted in read nearby. |add-caption=true |caption=First observed word written by SCP-9883 ]] **Description:** SCP-9883 is a specimen of //Pholcus phalangioides//[[footnote]]Daddy long-legs or Cellar spider[[/footnote]] exhibiting basic cognitive functions sufficient to comprehend rudimentary literacy and formulate simple concepts. This capacity has been expressed through the formation of silk letters (approximately 10 cm in height) constructed from repeated thread layering. The entity has been marked by a blue dot on its abdomen, distinguishing it from non-anomalous specimens on site. SCP-9883 was first identified in Office C-1013 by Dr. Daniel Koehl, when he found the word //“HELLO”// inscribed along the ceiling's edge. Subsequent observation confirmed it as the source. Current theory attributes the anomaly’s development to residual thaumaturgic radiation[[footnote]]Energetic byproducts of reality-altering phenomena, able to cause spontaneous anomaly formation in susceptible environments.[[/footnote]] originating from experiments with ██████, conducted two floors below the office. **Addendum.01:** [[div class="blockquote"]] [[=]] **Containment Adjustment Log** ---- **Summary:** Over a 6-month period, Dr. Daniel Koehl submitted multiple requests to modify Office C-1013 in order to //“optimize SCP-9883’s communicative potential.”// Below is an abridged record of relevant actions and outcomes. [[/=]] ---- **Request:** Repainting of ceiling in matte black to improve visibility of silk inscriptions. **Decision:** //Denied//. Office C-1013 not recognized as containment environment. **Follow-up:** Request to reclassify Office C-1013 as containment environment. **Decision:** //Approved//. **Follow-up:** Repainting of ceiling in matte black. **Decision:** //Approved//. Work completed personally by Dr. Koehl after hours. **Follow-up:** Reservation of standard mobile interview equipment. **Decision:** //Approved//. **Results:** Interview unsuccessful. SCP-9883 repeatedly layered //“TOO LIGHT.”// ---- **Request:** Reduction of light intensity within Office C-1013. **Decision:** //Approved//. Pending submission of Form E-19. **Follow-up:** (3) (re)submission(s) of Form E-19.   **Decision:** //Approved//. Estimated installation delay: 4–6 weeks. **Follow-up:** Dr. Koehl was reminded the use of adhesive materials to obscure Site lighting systems is non-compliant, regardless of duration or intent. **Decision:** Assigned mandatory refresher on Site fire safety standards. **Follow-up:** Reservation of standard mobile interview equipment. **Decision:** //Approved//. Only audio instruments. **Results:** Interview unsuccessful. SCP-9883 refused to engage, citing //“NO ENOUGH BUG.”// ---- **Request:** Contacted Site Animal House directly for allocation of small-scale insect breeding unit to ensure consistent prey availability. **Decision:** //Denied//. SCP-9883’s research priority does not warrant dedicated feeding infrastructure. **Follow-up:** Contacted Mrs. Ana Wyss[[footnote]]Staff member assigned to the Site Animal House[[/footnote]] for informal guidance regarding fly-breeding equipment. **Decision:** //Approved//. On the basis of personal discretion and prior acquaintance. **Follow-up:** Disposal request for said equipment submitted the same week. **Decision:** //Approved//. ---- **Request:** Verbal request to open window of Office C-1013 to increase air circulation and natural feeding opportunities. **Decision:** //Approved//. Contingent on installation of a mesh screen preventing SCP-9883 containment breach. **Follow-up:** Attending staff recommended consultation with Psychological Services. **Decision:** //Declined//. **Follow-up:** Package containing mesh screen intercepted at mailroom after being traced to unapproved vendor. **Decision:** //Returned to sender.// **Follow-up:** Custom apertured-mesh screen ordered from Facilities. **Decision:** //Denied.// Custom alterations unsupported. **Follow-up:** Dr. Koehl’s subsequent messages were redacted for language inconsistent with Foundation standards of professional conduct. [[/div]] **Addendum.02:** [[div class="blockquote"]] = **Incident 9883.01** ------ **Date:** 08/09/2022 **Summary:** Personnel in the courtyard beneath Office C-1013 reported agitated shouting emanating from the office. Security was dispatched to the scene. Dr. Daniel Koehl was removed from the office and referred for psychological evaluation. The following Security footage was later reviewed. [[div class="blockquote"]] = **VIDEO LOG** ---- **Date:** 08/09/2022 **Note:** Dr. Daniel Koehl had repositioned the security camera in violation of Site regulations to provide an upward-facing view of the ceiling. SCP-9883’s silk inscriptions have been transcribed. ---- [BEGIN EXCERPT] **Dr. Koehl:** //“TOO COLD.”// Too cold? You’ve got to be kidding me. I spend three months. Three months! Getting that mesh installed so you could have your precious window open and feed off //natural insects//, because God forbid a lady settles for farmed prey. Weeks of forms, risk assessments, containment waivers, and for what? So you can tell me you’re cold? **SCP-9883:** FIX **Dr. Koehl:** Fix. Oh, of course. Of course, fix. That’s what I do, isn’t it? You decide something’s wrong, and I fix it. What’s next? You'll want me to hunt down suitable bachelors for your eggs? [SCP-9883 consumes the letters //“C_LD”//.] **SCP-9883:** TOO LOUD **Dr. Koehl:** //“TOO LOUD,”// she says. Now I'm too loud... //[Laughs, voice cracking]// You know what’s loud? The sound of my spine compressing as I crouch to make you a custom mesh out of fishing line because Facilities //“doesn’t support custom apertures!”// And it doesn’t stop there, no no no. Because Her Highness can’t stand standard site bulbs, so I had to do it all in near darkness, giving myself eyestrain every other day! **SCP-9883:** MEAN **Dr. Koehl:** //I’m// mean? //You’re// the most thankless, selfish, ungrateful arthropod I’ve ever met! Do you have any idea what admin’s been saying? Six months and not a single usable datum! Because every time I haul the interview equipment down here, you’re either too busy feeding, weaving, or thinking up some new demand for your personal butler! [SCP-9883 retreats to its web.] **Dr. Koehl:** Don’t you turn your abdomen on me! We’re finishing this conversation! You nitpick me all day, but the moment I point something out about you- [SCP-9883 flings a silk-wrapped cocoon toward Dr. Koelh. It lands 2 cm off-center. An extended silence follows. Both SCP-9883 and Dr. Koehl remain motionless.] **Dr. Koehl:** Did you just... [Dr. Koelh reaches down, removes his right shoe, and raises it toward the ceiling.] **Dr. Koehl:** Two can play at that game, 9883. And believe me, the odds are not in your favor anymore. [Security personnel is heard knocking outside the office door.] **Security Officer:** //[Muffled]// Dr. Koehl? Everything alright in there? **Dr. Koehl:** Perfectly fine! Conducting an interview! Productive as ever! **Security Officer:** //[Muffled]// Copy that, sir. We just had some noise complaints- [Security enters the room, freezing mid-step.] **Security Officer:** …Sir. **Dr. Koehl:** What! **Security Officer:** Sir, I’m gonna need you to put the shoe down. **Dr. Koehl:** //She started it!// Check the ceiling! She’s mocking me! That little pest! **Security Officer:** Alright, let’s-let’s take a breather outside the room, sir. [Officers approach Dr. Koehl. He brandishes the shoe towards them.] **Dr. Koehl:** No! You’ve got it backwards! She’s the anomaly, not me! [There's a brief struggle between Security and Dr. Koehl. Security restrains Dr. Koehl and escorts him from the room.] **Dr. Koehl:** I’ll put you in a jar! You here me? With the rest of your web-spinning colleagues, so you can enjoy baseline spider behavior! And if you make it through peer-review, I’ll take you to the pond, and feed you to the ducks! I’ll dangle you over the water by your own silk, like a little eight-legged teaba- [Security and Dr. Koehl exit. The door remains slightly ajar. SCP-9883 descends on a silk thread, appearing to observe him being escorted down the corridor.] [END EXCERPT] [[/div]] **Post-Incident Note:** This exchange constitutes the most extensive display of communicative behavior ever recorded from SCP-9883, yielding the most significant data since its initial cataloguing. Item #: SCP-9886

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9886 is to be contained in an S-class humanoid containment cell at Site-234, and is to be perpetually sedated outside of testing. Any tests involving interaction between SCP-9886 and Dr. Joseph Hadley require approval from the Research Lead and the Site Director.

X-ray taken of the arm of SCP-9886

Description: SCP-9886 is an ersatz-class biological construct which superficially resembles Dr. Joseph Hadley, an employee of the Foundation stationed at Site-234. SCP-9886 is physically identical to Dr. Joseph Hadley, with the exception of several modifications:

  • The epidermis of the subject is more elastic than that of a normal human, resulting in skin folds resembling the effects of cutis laxa. The skin also lacks many sensory neurons, including nocireceptors.
  • Needle-like protrusions extend from the bones of the subject. These protrusions break through the skin of the subject in several locations around its body, including the hands, forearms, ribcage, and spine, and it has been observed using them as weaponry. The average bone density of the subject is also abnormally high, resulting in greater overall durability.
  • The subject has displayed an anomalously rapid healing response; all observed flesh wounds have scarred in less than two seconds, and any skeletal damage has been repaired in less than four minutes.

SCP-9886 has never displayed any capacity for communication or emotion during containment. It has shown a singular focus on terminating Dr. Joseph Hadley, and has shown no interest in any activities except ones which would allow it to achieve that goal.

Addendum-1: Discovery

Foreward: The following details the series of events leading up to the discovery and containment of SCP-9886.
Involved Persons:

  • Dr. Joseph Hadley: A specialist in applied thaumaturgy and an employee of the Foundation. Currently assigned to Site-234.
  • PoI-5329: A Karcist of GoI-281. They have demonstrated proficiency in multiple forms of biological manipulation, including flesh-sculpting and virus mutation.

Background: Operation White Glen
The following is a compilation of information from operation White Glen deemed relevant to SCP-9886. To view the full report for operation White Glen, see document PSTOP-29834-DRF.

On 25/03/2023, Foundation surveillance determined that a Neo-Sarkic sect of GoI-28 led by PoI-5329 had developed in a village near Perry, Oklahoma. Further investigation revealed that the entire population of the village had been infected with an anomalously aggressive virus. A temporary containment zone, designated as TCZ-648, was established under the control of MTF Beta-72 in order to determine the threat posed by the sect and prepare for permanent containment. A research team, led by Dr. Mira Talwar, was also assigned to the zone to assist the task force. This team was composed of anomalous virologists, experts in Sarkic anomalies, and thaumaturgic specialists, including Dr. Joseph Hadley.

Shortly after a squad from MTF Beta-7 entered the village, PoI-5329 released several hundred vermin from multiple buildings around the village, including rats, mice, rabbits, crows, and nutria; these animals were suspected and later confirmed to have been infected with the anomalous virus. The animals attempted to exit the village and spread into the surrounding woodlands, with several members of the team commenting that they appeared to be moving in the general direction of nearby population centers. Through a joint effort between MTF Beta-7 and several members of the research team, the operatives were able to thaumaturgically contain the infected animals while Dr. Joseph Hadley enacted a ritual to eradicate the virus from all subjects in the containment zone.

After the village was sterilized, the inhabitants were investigated for connections to GoI-28 and amnestics were administered. PoI-5329 could not be located in the aftermath. Following this operation, Dr. Joseph Hadley was transferred to Site-234 for the purpose of developing thaumaturgic containment strategies for high-risk anomalies.

Recovery Timeline
06/07/2025: A webcrawler reported that PoI-5329 was spotted in the background of an image taken in Union Grove, AL, USA. A surveillance team was sent to the town to investigate.
09/07/2025: The surveillance team reported no evidence of GoI-28 activities in the town, but found PoI-5329 on a road leading into the surrounding woodlands. The surveillance team utilized a UAV to covertly track the position of PoI-5329 and reported that they had moved to an abandoned house approximately 5 kilometers east from the town. The surveillance team was ordered to keep watch over the building and report any movements while a strike team from MTF Beta-7 was organized to enter the property and secure PoI-5329.
10/07/2025: After the surveillance team confirmed that PoI-5329 had not been seen leaving the building, the strike team entered the property. They noted that there were signs of occupation on the ground floor, including recently used bedding and multiple statuettes of mutated animals made from bone. Upon entering the basement, the team reported that the ground under the building was composed of an organic substance resembling intestinal lining, and that a cyst-like structure, approximately 3 meters in diameter and filled with a light-yellow liquid, grew from the floor in the center of the basement. After the team moved closer to investigate, SCP-9886 forced open the cyst from the inside and moved to attack the closest team member. SCP-9886 was able to pierce the team member's protective gear and inflicted fatal puncture wounds to their chest and throat before being sedated by the rest of the team. After a complete search of the property, PoI-5329 could not be located. The strike team incinerated the building following the operation.

Item #: SCP-9886

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9886-1 is to be contained in an S-class humanoid containment cell at Site-234. SCP-9886-1 has requested perpetual sedation when outside of testing, which may be granted at the discretion of the Research Lead. Interaction between SCP-9886-1 and SCP-9886-2 must not occur; to explain this, a cover story that SCP-9886-1 is extremely hostile towards SCP-9886-2 is to be maintained.

SCP-9886-2 is not to be contained at this time, and instead is to be allowed to perform the normal duties of SCP-9886-1. SCP-9886-2 is to be monitored for any changes in behavior, and both the Research Lead and Site Director are authorized to call for the containment of SCP-9886-2 if it is deemed necessary. In this event, SCP-9886-2 is to be held in a B-class humanoid containment cell at Site-234.

SCP-9886-2 must not have access to any information on this page. A false version of this document must be maintained which supports the cover story that SCP-9886-2 is non-anomalous and SCP-9886-1 is a biological construct.

X-ray taken of the arm of SCP-9886-1

Description: SCP-9886 refers to two anomalous entities. SCP-9886-1 is Dr. Joseph Hadley, an employee of the Foundation who was previously stationed at Site-234. SCP-9886-1 displays multiple signs of biological manipulation:

  • The epidermis of the subject is more elastic than that of a normal human, resulting in skin folds resembling the effects of cutis laxa.
  • Needle-like protrusions extend from the bones of the subject. These protrusions extend through the muscles and skin of the subject, severely inhibiting mobility.
  • The cartilage in the joints of the subject has been severely degraded, resulting in effects similar to advanced osteoarthritis.
  • The subject has displayed an anomalously rapid healing response; all observed flesh wounds have scarred in less than two seconds, and any skeletal damage has been repaired in less than four minutes.
  • The subject has displayed a strong resistance to multiple forms of medication, including analgesics and amnestics.

SCP-9886-2 is an ersatz-class biological construct which appears identical to SCP-9886-1 prior to transformation. SCP-9886-2 has displayed accurate recall of all information SCP-9886-1 had before its transformation, and behavioral analysis has shown that it will respond nearly identically to SCP-9886-1 in all tested situations. All internal and external analysis of SCP-9886-2 have confirmed that its physical form is consistent with a non-anomalous human body, including in brain function. Based on this information and discussions with specialists in biological manipulation, it is the current opinion of the Research Lead that SCP-9886-2 sincerely believes itself to be Dr. Joseph Hadley.

SCP-9886-2 has presented multiple illnesses, which it has not displayed knowledge of. These illnesses include:

  • Situs inversus
  • An abnormally high blood pressure (160/100)
  • Pulmonary fibrosis
  • Advanced chronic kidney disease
  • Advanced coronary artery disease

It is predicted that SCP-9886-2 will expire from these illnesses in less than a year if medical action is not taken. No plans for medical action are currently under consideration.

Addendum-1: Discovery

Note: Multiple sections of this addendum are identical to the previous version. Differences have been marked in blue.
Foreward: The following details the series of events leading up to the discovery and containment of SCP-9886.
Involved Persons:

  • PoI-5329: A Karcist of GoI-283. They have demonstrated proficiency in multiple forms of biological manipulation, including flesh-sculpting and virus mutation.

Recovery Timeline
06/07/2025: A webcrawler reported that PoI-5329 was spotted in the background of an image taken in Union Grove, AL, USA. A surveillance team was sent to the town to investigate
09/07/2025: The surveillance team reported no evidence of GoI-28 activities in the town, but found PoI-5329 on a road leading into the surrounding woodlands. The surveillance team utilized a UAV to covertly track the position of PoI-5329 and reported that they had moved to an abandoned house approximately 5 kilometers east from the town. The surveillance team was ordered to keep watch over the building and report any movements while a strike team from MTF Beta-7 was organized to enter the property and secure PoI-5329.
10/07/2025: After the surveillance team confirmed that PoI-5329 had not been seen leaving the building, the strike team entered the property. They noted that there were signs of occupation on the ground floor, including recently used bedding and multiple statuettes of mutated animals made from bone. A cyst-like structure, approximately 3 meters in diameter and filled with a light-yellow liquid, grew from the center of the basement. After the team moved closer to investigate, the outer layer of the cyst spontaneously disintegrated and revealed SCP-9886-1. SCP-9886-1 immediately requested to be terminated, which the team leader denied. SCP-9886-1 then attempted to take the weapon of the nearest team member, prompting them to sedate it for containment. After a complete search of the property, PoI-5329 could not be located. The strike team incinerated the building following the operation.
11/07/2025: SCP-9886-1 was given a pre-containment interview. During this interview, it claimed that it was Dr. Joseph Hadley, and that it had been abducted on the night of 03/06/2025. It was able to accurately answer all questions asked regarding Dr. Joseph Hadley, including his date of birth, the date he was hired by the Foundation, his FIN5, and the contents of multiple classified tests he was involved with. SCP-9886-1 and SCP-9886-2, who had previously been believed to be Dr. Joseph Hadley, were both given full-body analyses; SCP-9886-2 was told the procedure was a standard medical check. These analyses were led by Dr. Sophia Edwards, a biological researcher with a specialization in Sarkic anomalies. During the analyses, it was confirmed that SCP-9886-2 was artificially created via biological manipulation, and that SCP-9886-1 was Dr. Joseph Hadley.

Following the analyses, it was determined that SCP-9886-1 would not be able to fulfill its responsibilities due to its current state. As such, it was decided that SCP-9886-2 would be allowed to continue performing the duties of SCP-9886-1 while a permanent solution was developed by Dr. Sophia Edwards.

Addendum-2: Meeting Transcriptions

Meeting 9886-A

Foreward: The following is a transcription of a meeting reviewing project proposal 9886-XLJ-E.
Participants:

  • Dr. Carlos Ruiz: Research Lead assigned to SCP-9886
  • Dr. Sophia Edwards: Sarkic anomaly expert and primary author of 9886-XLJ-E
  • Junebug.aic: Artificially intelligent conscript responsible for automatic transcription

[BEGIN TRANSCRIPTION]

Dr. Ruiz: Alright, I've read through this once, but there are a few details I want to cover. How about you walk me through it and I'll ask questions as they come up?

Dr. Edwards: Very well. We have three real options on how to handle SCP-9886. The first is to contain both anomalies and provide medical treatment as necessary. This would directly and unambiguously follow the Foundation's mission statement, but would likely be very expensive.

Dr. Ruiz: Would they still be able to work?

Dr. Edwards: Given the extreme medical issues they present, I'd expect both of them will require some form of perpetual medical intervention before too long. Once that happens, I doubt they'll be able to do much.

[Dr. Ruiz writes something down on a notepad.]

Dr. Ruiz: Alright. What's the next option?

Dr. Edwards: The next idea would be to "fix" SCP-9886-2 and keep SCP-9886-1 contained. The main issue is that the biology of the simulacrum isn't particularly receptive to being fixed. Many of its diseases don't have any mundane medical solutions; we'd only be able to slow its decline.

Dr. Ruiz: What about using thaumaturgy?

Dr. Edwards: Thaumaturgic solutions are risky as well. The simulacrum is effectively a collection of mismatched animal cells that have been tricked into keeping a human shape. Any changes we try to make could cause it to…collapse, basically.

Dr. Ruiz: I'm not sure I understand; I was under the impression it's basically human. Is that not the case?

Dr. Edwards: It is, but…it's like if you made a table by nailing the different parts together, and someone else made a visually identical copy by carving the entire thing out of a single piece of wood. They both might function the same, but if you needed to replace a table leg because it was rotting, you'd have to handle that in two very different ways. SCP-9886-2 wasn't made by modifying an existing person, it was made from scratch using available biological material; that's what makes it an ersatz-class construct. As a result, there are subtle differences between it and a normal person regarding its genes and cells. All of our standard healing rituals are based on a regular human's anatomical and genetic structure; although we could try to modify them to account for the simulacrum's differences, I'd say the chances of success without significant complications are very low.

Dr. Ruiz: I see. I guess now would be a good time to bring up another question I have about SCP-9886-2. It is my understanding that it has behaved exactly like Joe in every test we've thought of, correct?

Dr. Edwards: Yes.

Dr. Ruiz: So externally, they're the same. But what about internally?

Dr. Edwards: I'm not sure what you mean by, "internally". We've already discussed its biology.

Dr. Ruiz: I mean internally, as in, in its head. Is it actually sapient, or is it just a mimic? I know it has the correct brain matter, but what about beyond that?

Dr. Edwards: Ah.

[Both sit silently for a moment.]

Dr. Edwards: That's…a difficult question to answer. If I've learned anything studying biological anomalies, it's that there isn't really anything "special" about our neurons and synapses from a purely physical standpoint; they're just chemistry that produces an interesting result. As such, it can be difficult to draw a line between "real" sapience and a very good mimicry; many things we consider to be anomalous intelligences came from someone trying to create an imitation of consciousness and doing too well. The best I can give you is that from a physical perspective, SCP-9886-2 appears to have all the necessary components for sapience.

Dr. Ruiz: What about beyond the physical?

Dr. Edwards: I'm not a theologist; I can't tell you if it has a soul.

[Both sit silently for a moment. Dr. Ruiz writes something down on a notepad.]

Dr. Ruiz: Alright. What's our third option?

Dr. Edwards: I believe that it may be possible to undo the anomaly effecting Dr. Hadley via a thaumaturgic sculpting. The simulacrum was created using Dr. Hadley as a…blueprint, of sorts. We may be able to decompile the anomaly to retrieve that blueprint and use it to return Dr. Hadley to his original state. This option is best, by my view.

Dr. Ruiz: You said you could "decompile" SCP-9886-2? What does that mean?

Dr. Edwards: Thaumaturgic shredding.

Dr. Ruiz: Hmm. That sounds…very fatal.

Dr. Edwards: Yes.

[Dr. Ruiz rubs his chin with his hand.]

Dr. Ruiz: I know you've reversed some Sarkic biological manipulations in the past, but I've never heard of this. Is it something you use often?

Dr. Edwards: No. Normally, the workings are amateur enough that we can pick them apart fairly easily. Undoing them is just a matter of…finding a loose thread to pull.

Dr. Ruiz: But this one isn't?

Dr. Edwards: No. It's actually been bothering me for a while. It's too finished.

Dr. Ruiz: What do you mean, too finished?

Dr. Edwards: Well, we interrupted the Karcist, right? Which means that no matter how good they are, there should be some signs of incomplete work, something they started but couldn't finish because we caught them. But there aren't, all the workings are complete; the threads are tied too nicely.

Dr. Ruiz: What's your point?

[Both sit silently for a moment.]

Dr. Edwards: I'm not sure how much you know about Neo-Sarkism, but that disease the Karcist created at the TCZ was likely as much of a religious icon as it was a weapon. It was an…avatar of unconstrained life, caring only for itself and feeding on anything too weak to stop it. So when Joseph killed everything except what we had contained, it was more than just an attack; it was like a form of heresy.

Dr. Ruiz: Okay. So they get mad at Joe, abduct him, and try to turn him into another weapon, right? But we get in the way?

Dr. Edwards: Maybe. But…what if this is what they wanted to happen?

Dr. Ruiz: This?

[Both sit in silence for a moment.]

Dr. Edwards: Joseph trapped something that was made to be free. So if the Karcist wanted revenge, it makes sense they would want to trap him back, right? And who better than us to keep him alive and contained for as long as possible?

Dr. Ruiz: You think they wanted us to get Joe?

Dr. Edwards: Maybe. Don't you think it's odd that a secretive biomancer who's been avoiding us for over a year just happened to get spotted wandering around a town?

[Both sit in silence for a moment.]

Dr. Ruiz: Well, even if you're right, it doesn't really change anything, does it?

Dr. Edwards: No, it doesn't.

[Both sit in silence for a moment.]

Dr. Ruiz: Alright, I need to run this by some people. I'll try to get back to you before the end of the week.

Dr. Edwards: That works for me. Let me know if you need any more information about the process.

[END TRANSCRIPTION]

Footnote: Proposal 9886-XLJ-E was approved on 16/09/2025.

Meeting 9886-B

This meeting transcription is currently being recorded live by Junebug.aic and cannot be edited until the meeting is finished. If you need to edit it immediately, please contact your supervisor.
Foreward: The following is a transcription of a meeting regarding the final decision made regarding SCP-9886.
Participants:

  • Dr. Carlos Ruiz: Research Lead assigned to SCP-9886
  • SCP-9886-1: Participating from their cell via a secure terminal
  • Junebug.aic: Artificially intelligent conscript responsible for automatic transcription

[BEGIN LIVE TRANSCRIPTION]
Dr. Ruiz: How are you holding up, Joe?

SCP-9886-1: I've been-

[SCP-9886-1 gasps and grabs their chest. Dr. Ruiz frowns.]

SCP-9886-1: I've been better.

Dr. Ruiz: Sorry. Is this a bad time?

[SCP-9886-1 shakes their head.]

SCP-9886-1: Let's just get it over with.

Dr. Ruiz: Alright. We have an update on your condition; the Sarkic team has been working with your pals at the thaumaturgy department, and they think they might have a way to get you back to normal. I don't really get most of the details, but my understanding is that they think they can use the clone to get a copy of your old body.

SCP-9886-1: Huh. Like, decompiling it?

Dr. Ruiz: I think they mentioned that, yes.

SCP-9886-1: That's…hmm. Did the Ethics Committee approve it?

Dr. Ruiz: Yes. They definitely took their time on it, though. Is there a problem? I can get a meeting set up if you want to discuss the details.

SCP-9886-1: No, it's just…from what I remember, decompilation has only been used on a biological construct once.

Dr. Ruiz: Yeah? What happened?

SCP-9886-1: No idea. Everyone involved requested amnestics, the results got classified, and the Ethics Committee has shut down every attempt since. Except this one, I guess.

Dr. Ruiz: Oh.

[Both sit silently.]

Dr. Ruiz: Well, it's not like you particularly like the thing.

SCP-9886-1: I don't know. I…it still feels weird as hell whenever I think of it living in my house, talking to all of you…but…it feels… I don't know. It feels wrong, I guess. To just…kill it.

[Both pause. SCP-9886-1 abruptly coughs heavily for several seconds before reaching into its mouth and removing a thin needle made from bone. It places it on a nearby tray which contains a small pile of similar needles.]

[SCP-9886-1 sighs.]

SCP-9886-1: This fucking sucks.

Dr. Ruiz: Yeah? Is that your official position on the matter?

SCP-9886-1: Yes. Write that in the report: SCP-9886-1 considers the situation to be "complete dogshit."

[Both laugh, then sit quietly for a moment.]

SCP-9886-1: By the way, I thought of something a little while ago. You said that you blocked my account from opening the document, right?

Dr. Ruiz: Yeah. Is that a problem? If you need access, we can figure something out.

SCP-9886-1: No, that isn't-

[SCP-9886-1 coughs violently for several seconds.]

SCP-9886-1: Sorry. It's just…it might be able to get into the real document.

[Dr. Ruiz leans forward.]

Dr. Ruiz: Oh. How?

SCP-9886-1: Do you know Mira? Dr. Talwar?

Dr. Ruiz: I believe so. She led your research team at the TCZ, correct?

SCP-9886-1: Yes. During the outbreak, I needed to set up a transmission connection to sterilize the virus over the entire village. Any ritual that large requires specific runes, and I didn't have the clearance for them. Mira was already handling the bio-cage, so she decided to give me her login credentials.

Dr. Ruiz: Hmm. It could use those to get around the account block, then.

SCP-9886-1: Yes. I don't know why it would think to use them, but it's possible.

[Both sit silently for a moment. Dr. Ruiz rubs chin with his hand.]

Dr. Ruiz: I'll try to figure out a good solution to that, but a bandaid fix should work for now; Junebug, lock Dr. Mira Talwar from accessing document SCP-9886, version CLO-02.

Junebug.aic: Done. Should I also close the currently active viewer?

Dr Ruiz: Sure, I- wait, what do you mean?

Junebug.aic: Dr. Talwar is currently reading SCP-9886 on secure terminal #762.

[Both participants freeze.]

Dr. Ruiz: Is that the terminal in Dr. Hadley's office?

Junebug.aic: Yes.

SCP-9886-1: Shit.

Dr. Ruiz: Junebug, close the viewer and Error: Exiting to Command Line

SCP-9886 is physically identical to Dr. Joseph Hadley, with the exception of several modifications: * The epidermis of the subject is more elastic than that of a normal human, resulting in skin folds resembling the effects of cutis laxa. The skin also lacks many sensory neurons, including nocireceptors. * Needle-like protrusions extend from the bones of the subject. These protrusions break through the skin of the subject in several locations around its body, including the hands, forearms, ribcage, and spine, and it has been observed using them as weaponry. The average bone density of the subject is also abnormally high, resulting in greater overall durability. * The subject has displayed an anomalously rapid healing response; all observed flesh wounds have scarred in less than two seconds, and any skeletal damage has been repaired in less than four minutes. SCP-9886 has never displayed any capacity for communication or emotion during containment. A temporary containment zone, designated as TCZ-648, was established under the control of MTF Beta-7[[footnote]] Maz Hatters [[/footnote]] in order to determine the threat posed by the sect and prepare for permanent containment. A research team, led by Dr. Mira Talwar, was also assigned to the zone to assist the task force. This team was composed of anomalous virologists, experts in Sarkic anomalies, and thaumaturgic specialists, including Dr. Joseph Hadley. > @@ @@ > Shortly after a squad from MTF Beta-7 entered the village, PoI-5329 released several hundred vermin from multiple buildings around the village, including rats, mice, rabbits, crows, and nutria; these animals were suspected and later confirmed to have been infected with the anomalous virus. The animals attempted to exit the village and spread into the surrounding woodlands, with several members of the team commenting that they appeared to be moving in the general direction of nearby population centers. Through a joint effort between MTF Beta-7 and several members of the research team, the operatives were able to thaumaturgically contain the infected animals while Dr. Joseph Hadley enacted a ritual to eradicate the virus from all subjects in the containment zone. > @@ @@ > After the village was sterilized, the inhabitants were investigated for connections to GoI-28 and amnestics were administered. The surveillance team was ordered to keep watch over the building and report any movements while a strike team from MTF Beta-7 was organized to enter the property and secure PoI-5329. > **10/07/2025:** After the surveillance team confirmed that PoI-5329 had not been seen leaving the building, the strike team entered the property. They noted that there were signs of occupation on the ground floor, including recently used bedding and multiple statuettes of mutated animals made from bone. Upon entering the basement, the team reported that the ground under the building was composed of an organic substance resembling intestinal lining, and that a cyst-like structure, approximately 3 meters in diameter and filled with a light-yellow liquid, grew from the floor in the center of the basement. After the team moved closer to investigate, SCP-9886 forced open the cyst from the inside and moved to attack the closest team member. SCP-9886 was able to pierce the team member's protective gear and inflicted fatal puncture wounds to their chest and throat before being sedated by the rest of the team. After a complete search of the property, PoI-5329 could not be located. The strike team incinerated the building following the operation. The first item tested/destroyed by the NUMA.

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: SCP-9888 is to remain out-of-bounds to all personnel and foreign entities. To this end, the room containing SCP-9888 (3-5-20 Persistence Wing, Site-512, retroactively demarcated as CC-9888) has been clearly marked as a restricted zone, with biometric locks in place requiring at least three personnel with LEVEL 4 clearance or above to be present. In addition, a Foundation standard RS3 Vault Door has been installed to deter unauthorised entry.

Prior to the formation of SCP-9888, the attached annex to CC-9888 was a designated living space for Experimentation & Paratechnology (E&P) researchers. Rations for two individuals are to be delivered daily to that annex via the Site-512 internal chute system.

There are no special containment procedures for SCP-9888-1 instances, due to their inability to leave CC-9888.

There are no special containment procedures for SCP-9888-2.

DESCRIPTION: SCP-9888 is a 10.0m x 15.7m x 5.2m region of blank space. Any physical objects placed within SCP-9888 experience metastructural fission; their metastructures are torn apart, as the various composite meta-substructures of the objects are forcibly separated from the physical structures they were attached to, before dispersing throughout the surroundings. Prior to Incident 9888-B, this process was believed to invariably cause hyper-accelerated degradation of the respective physical structures.

SCP-9888, before the occurrence of Incident 9888-A, was the Nye-Uchiyama Metastructure Atomiser (NUMA), a piece of paratechnology developed by E&P. Further information on the NUMA can be found in ADDENDA I and II.

SCP-9888-1 instances are the surviving physical remnants of metastructural fission. The exact mechanism of their survival is unclear; due to their origin, only their external, physical characteristics are accessible, and even then unusable. Both SCP-9888-1 instances are housed within CC-9888.

SCP-9888-2 refers to the persistent metaphysical corruption of CC-9888, detailed in ADDENDUM 9888.XIV.

ADDENDUM 9888.I: NUMA Proposal Cover

PROPOSAL 23.5.97 ("NUMA")

EXPERIMENTATION & PARATECHNOLOGY, SITE-512

COMMISSIONED BY: Practician (O5-4)
SUPERVISED BY: Dr. Wayland Laurence Pan

17/09/23
Dr. Uchiyama Aiko
Senior Researcher, Metaphysics, E&P, Site-512

Forward: Metaphysical messes have always been a headache to manage. The dual challenge of dealing with the physical in conjunction with the metaphysical has often led to a paradox in containment: the latter renders containing the former impossible, while the former provides severe challenges in reining in the effects of the latter.

Abstract: The Nye-Uchiyama Metaphysical Atomiser (NUMA) is a proposed piece of paratechnology that could greatly aid in the containment and/or decommissioning of metaphysical anomalies. Through atomisation of their metastructure, we can contain their physical structures prior to their gradual metaphysical regeneration. In addition, this proposed paratechnology could lead to significant advancements in our understanding of metaphysics, specifically in the fields of conceptual attachment, perceptual characteristics, ontological structures, and parasemantics.

The NUMA is theoretically sound. It operates through the rapid delivery of multiple concentrated bursts of metaphysical energy, calculated precisely in order to just overcome the meta-binding energies without leading to physical damage. In order to prevent re-attachment to the physical object, following their separation, the relevant meta-substructures are accelerated temporally, leading to their natural dispersion and disintegration, in accordance with Thien's Law. The energy released in this disintegration will be recaptured by the NUMA, both in order to prevent metaphysical pollution of the surroundings, and to offset the energy usage of the machine.

The NUMA has been designed with utmost practicality in mind. Its volume has been kept, non-anomalously, under 900 cubic meters, and its emergency cutoff system ensures that in the event of a catastrophic failure, the NUMA will absorb the resultant metaphysical explosion into the metastructure of its metaphysical cladding, followed by its own metastructure, shielding the surroundings from any contamination. The NUMA’s mechanisms are metaphysically isolated from the machine itself, ensuring minimal disruption to its functioning.
