SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Extensive knowledge and access to SCP-9931 objects and media is restricted to personnel of Clearance 4/9931 or above. All personnel of Clearance 5/9931 report to the office of O5-10 directly.

Pertinent knowledge of SCP-9931 will be issued to operatives of Mobile Task Force Phi-2 "Clever Girls" below Clearance 4/9931 at the discretion of appropriate superiors. As of 20 September 2045, three (3) embedded field agents are assigned to the search and retrieval of any further SCP-9931 objects at the following Locations of Interest: #401829, #401830, #45068.

SCP-9931-1, -2, and -3 are contained in Medium Security Archeological Storage at CASKSK-Site-65. Accompanying documentation is to refer to these items collectively as Anomalous Object #1829.

SCP-9931-4a though -4o are in a medium security storage locker at USCASC-Site-15. Duplicated files are stored on Server 181519520201 for review and deciphering by artificial intelligence constructs Bouchard.aic, Champollion.aic, and Dr. Benson Roth, D.C.Sc (all Clearance 5/9931).

DESCRIPTION: SCP-9931 is a series of pre-Anthropocene technofossils excavated from siltstone strata in the Scollard Formation at Alberta, Canada. Location of discovery extended a depth of 72.19 to 73.18 meters below surface, just under the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary.

SCP-9931 violates the law of superposition. Reliable radiometric dating methods on SCP-9931 and layers of strata adjacent to discovery place both at an age of 66.46 million years BP;1 Despite this, the layers of strata are in order with the rest of the excavation site, showing no signs of a hole being excavated and filled back in.

  • V — SCP-9931-1 through -4
  • V — SCP-9931-4 Examples

V-Appendix 9931.Inv.13

SCP-9931-1
SCP-9931-1 is a cylindrical concrete container, with rough exterior dimensions of 99.28 × d 64.26 cm and interior of 79.31 × d 46.19 cm. Concrete had cracked and through this exposure iron rebar had corroded almost entirely, but SCP-9931-1 retained general structure. Exterior surface indicates SCP-9931-1 was not cast in the ground.

Lid was pinned with rebar and sealed with concrete. Interior was divided into three sections by grates composed of a bronze alloy, since corroded into copper and tin minerals.2 Despite the resulting loss of material strength and damage sustained to the upper grate, both were found intact. (See Dossier: SCP-9931-1 for detail.)

All other SCP-9931 objects were recovered inside.

SCP-9931-2
SCP-9931-2 is the fragmentary remains of what was once a presumably functional electronic device affixed to the interior face of the lid of SCP-9931-1 when it was sealed. Item had fallen to the floor of the first chamber and was neutralized, but it is indeterminable if this occurred before discovery or during transport.

Metal components had degraded into bornite and similar decomposite ores an unknown magnitude of time before discovery. Stable carbon isotopes, silicates, and some polymer components have not degraded, notably among them a hermetically sealed vial found to contain permineralized neural tissue, interfaced with the remains of a microelectrode array. It is believed that SCP-9931-2's intended purpose was to extend the longevity of SCP-9931, shielding the items from interferences with local reality and/or retroactive causality. (See Dossier: SCP-9931-2 for detail.)

SCP-9931-3
SCP-9931-3 is a box comprised of carbon and metallic ore, approximately 37.52 × 20.04 × 16.67 cm, found in good condition. The metal base was constructed from bronze alloy, also corroded. Carbon fibers lining the exterior and interior of SCP-9931-3 have largely preserved its structural integrity, unlike SCP-9931-2.

Pitting found on the width of the container and lid indicate SCP-9931-3 locked or latched closed mechanically, but the exposed mechanisms have deteriorated completely. Contents of SCP-9931-3 were found partially embedded in a plastiglomerate compiled at the basin of the container. This plastiglomerate is believed to have been a polyurethane-based foam meant to insulate or cushion SCP-9931-4. (See Dossier: SCP-9931-3 for detail.)

SCP-9931-4
SCP-9931-4 is the collection of fifteen (15) digital storage devices found contained within SCP-9931-3. All instances are the same design of nanoshuttle memory device,3 operating off of iron nanoparticles inside of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNT). Each SCP-9931-4 is comparable in complexity and design to civilian nanotech advancements of the late 2020s, and has a storage capacity of 187.5 terabytes. (See Portal:SCP-9931-4 for full archive.)

Character encoding is represented by variable-length 3-bit or 5-bit code units, as opposed to 4-bit multiples. Decoding of contents has supplied audio and visual media, including a character set of 78,320 characters, comprising eleven (11) different writing scripts (not including an ideographic text markup), corresponding to eleven or potentially more (11+) languages.

As of 20 September 2045, these languages have not been fully deciphered, but from structure and associated recordings of phonetics, their scripts are logographic and either syllabic, semi-syllabic, or alphasyllabic; and are read top-down progressing right. Typography is comprised primarily from linear strokes, arced strokes, and simple diacritics, with little use of loops or counters. Photos indicate these characters originated as a form of inscription using teeth and claws. Due to their use in the computer language, the numerals, text markup, and order in the character set is the most that has been discerned. Most context derived from SCP-9931-4 has been through photo, video, and mathematical equations. (See Linguistic Analysis: Cretaceous Language Family (GoI-9931) for detail.)

Contents of SCP-9931-4 indicate that SCP-9931 originated from an advanced society of Late Cretaceous dinosaurs, comparable in technology to humanity, and was utilized by a research organization of unknown directive or operation. For purposes of clarity, this society has been provided the tentative name of the "Anomalous Campanian Culture Group" (ACCG; Group of Interest #9931), and this organization the "ACCG Organization" (Group of Interest #9931-A). (See Group of Interest Dossier: GoI-9931 and subfolders for detail.)

The majority of files on SCP-9931-4 consist of visual and auditory documentation from the ACCG Organization, but cultural media presumed to originate from a larger cosm of the culture group are also included in substantial amount. Photography and videography depicts at least six species of civilized dinosaurs, prominent pictured among the ACCG Organization is a species of pachysaurid undiscovered to civilian paleontology and has yet to be found in the stratigraphic record.4

V-Appendix 9931.4Ex.7

As of 20 September 2045, Over 2.4 million files across 84 different files types have been compiled from automated review of SCP-9931-4 and converted into standards used by Foundation operating systems. These files total 166.53 TB of an estimated 173 TB.

All contents of SCP-9931-4a through -4n have been duplicated and converted. Assigned artificial intelligence constructs Bouchard.aic and Champollion.aic project review of SCP-9931-4o at 56% complete.

Below varied example size of individual or series of photos, videos, and audios:

SCP-9931-4 Converted file name(s)
Description of contents
SCP-9931-4a [4A-FolderA1A] ACG438 dinosaur scholarship (1–12).9931fmt3 (image format)
Three (3) bipedal dinosaurs of different species (an oviraptorid, a pachysaurid, and a troodontid) clothed in tunics standing in an office. The instances are varyingly pictured shaking hands, vocalizing, and writing on paper or dry-erase board.
SCP-9931-4b [4B-FolderD2] ACG438 album (13).9931fmt6 (audio-video format)
Video consists of a still image, an album cover of a Velociraptor in a cocktail dress, singing on stage with fireworks. The number "4500" in title is prominent, presumably representing a calendar year. Audio is of a musical performance utilizing 2/4 and 4/4 time signatures. Vocalist sings in soprano with frequent trills at the end of a lyric. Instrumental consists of string, percussion, and occasional brass instruments.
SCP-9931-4c [4C-FolderG1B] AccompanyingAudio.9931fmt2 (audio format)
[4C-FolderG1B] Nedoceratops wall pyroclastic (1–6).9931fmt5 (image format)
An enclosed concrete room with the severed charred head of a ceratopsid5 mounted on wall. Floor and wall is littered with ashes, soot, and small debris. Mouth is open to varying degrees across photos. An audio file of throat singing with intermittent redactions was recovered in the same folder.
SCP-9931-4e [4E-FolderA1] Eutricondont w typewriter (1).9931fmt11 (audio-video format)
An unidentified eutriconodont is introduced to a typewriter and an empty planter box. After apparent instruction by the recorder and despite its size, the mammal shows proficient skill as a typist while an unidentified eudicot rapidly grows and spouts. Subject stops to consume the bright purple, fleshy fruits borne from the plant.
SCP-9931-4h [4H-FolderE5E] SatCalc65MYA (1–30).9931fmt58 (text format)
Collection of 30,000 sets of measurements and calculations attributed to "alpha"-numeric designations, detailing the trajectories of extraterrestrial or extrasolar objects. The moon, all major planets from Mercury to Neptune, and the dwarf planet Ceres have been identified through comparison to projections of their locations 65 MYA. 451 projected trajectories have a ≥1% risk of collision with the Earth, 36 in the century of calculation.
SCP-9931-4i [4I-FolderC1] ACG438t sauropod mountain grazing.9931fmt3 (image format)
Scan of photograph. Pictures a quadrupedal sauropod6 grazing on unknown vegetation. Sauropod is not clothed, and does not appear to acknowledge the photographer. Climate and mountain range at horizon appear to correspond to a section of Appalachian Plateau overlooking the Ariondack Mountains.
SCP-9931-4k [4K-FolderB2N1] SoI-82025 arthropod fibrous (1–10).9931fmt5 (image format)
Deceased specimens of unknown terrestrial arthropods. Texture appears woody and fibrous. Ruler for scale inserted post-photography indicates specimens to range between 3 and 8 units of measurement.
SCP-9931-4m [4M-FolderA5] Tyranosaurus text.9931fmt31 (text format)
Single page text document. Page border is solid black with the number "1273" at left-hand header. Contents consists solely of anomalous text-based visual art of an indistinct tyrannosaurid. Graphic is animate and responds with hostility to computer cursor, despite no code corresponding to animation or cursor position tracking. If the graphic "consumes" the cursor, all associated graphics and drivers to the cursor will be deleted from the host computer.
SCP-9931-4o [4O-FolderF4C] LoI05 (1–34).9931fmt4 (image format)
[4O-FolderF4C] LoI05IR (1–29).9931fmt8 (image format)
Visible and infrared photography. Passageway approximately 2–2.5 meters in height carved through limestone cave. Pillars, arches, and antechamber are ornate but uneven. Recently deceased dromaesaurids,7 flowering vines, and cloth tapestries found throughout location.
SCP-9931-4o [4O-FolderI7A] ACG438 tech schema 1204.9931fmt15 (multimedia format)
201-page schematic for a compact device with an internal power source. Exact composition and function of the device is uncertain, but determined to be SCP-9931-2 or a prototype. Diagrams for a primary battery, nanoshuttle switches, a tachyonic field emitter, and an inorganic-organic interface with dense neural cell cultures have been identified.

(See Portal:SCP-9931-4 for full archive of summaries and front-facing documents.)

HISTORY: SCP-9931 was discovered 21 June 2045 by coal miners at the Rumsey Quarry, located southeast of the Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park in Alberta, Canada (since designated Location of Interest #45068). Embedded webcrawlers were flagged to correspondence between paleological associates and Korite & Westmoreland International detailing SCP-9931-1. Mobile Task Forces Phi-2 "Clever Girls" and Sigma-66 "Steel Veil" were dispatched to secure SCP-9931, amnesticize civilians, and expunge correspondences.

SCP-9931-1 was designated SCP-9931 on 22 June. Efforts to open SCP-9931-1 was authorized the same day, leading to the discovery and catalogue of the contents with their current designations. Safe containment, Dark disruption, and Notice risk classification were assigned by O5-10, overseer of SCP-9931 activities. The Reverse Engineering and Application Division, Department of Informational Technologies (READ, DIT) was assigned with designing a device to interface with SCP-9931-4.

The first functional device was brought online on 5 August to attempt interface with SCP-9931-4a. When the non-standard format of SCP-9931-4 was confirmed, the Artificial Intelligence Applications Division (AIAD, DIT) assigned Bouchard.aic under supervision of Dr. Benson Roth, D.C.Sc, both trained in deciphering esoteric coding languages. On 13 August, a newly brought online artificial intelligence construct, Champollion.aic, was given inaugural assignment in translating the character languages. This process is ongoing.

As of 20 September 2045, an estimated 96.26% of SCP-9931-4 contents have been parsed and archived in Foundation standards. Files are expected to be fully compiled by October 2045.

(1) Message from Champollion.aic (1)

@Champollion.aic
ver1.0.5 Gen(IV)
Lv.5/9931 Clearance

Hello, Overseer. You are as pertinent as ever.

At 07:57:43 UTC, Bouchard.aic flagged a folder on SCP-9931-4o containing files of note. He positively identified the presence of Latin script characters originating from the device, as further confirmed by myself and Dr. Roth. Enclosed in this message, I've sent the initial flagged file.

I'm not authorized to tell you or the Council what to think after reading it, but I will assure: with this translation, I will have Linear 9931-c and Linear 9931-d scripts cracked in time for Christmas.

  • 4O-FolderF4C DoC TNWD A350 (EN).9931f3

Department of Civiology, Temperate-New-West Division

#350 "Future Fossil"

Artifact #350

This artifact was recovered second hand by a Raving sect in the Olar Peninsula. Its initial provenance has been lost, but the item found secondary context as an idol of a doomsday cult.

Artifact #350 is the complete skull of an unknown synapsid, weighing 10.2 cupra. At rest, the item occupies a volume of 5.15 × 7.74 × 6.04 digits, and the cranial circumference measures 18 even. The cranial cavity is a sizeable volume of 2,450 millicanteens.

The foramen magnum is located at the bottom of the skull, indicating a severely vertical posture. The facial bones are astoundingly flat. The jaws hold an omnivorous array of 32 incisor and molar teeth and show signs of having been given dentalcare in life.

#350 has shown these notable properties:

  1. Viewing between the jaws from the front reveals soft tissue of the mouth, including the tongue and the throat. These tissues and they space they occupy exists separate from the view of the back and underside. Muscles do not respond to stimuli, have not dried out, and have not decomposed.

    Any items inserted into the throat beyond sight are lost. This has included food provided as tribute and over 1 reach of endoscope.
  2. A unique genome has been identified in samples taken from the tongue and bone marrow. Mapping has found that the #350 genome is most comparable to small, habitually arboreal mammals of the taxon Euarcharbor. Greatest similarity (56.1%) has been found with the Armesian shrubrunner (Eua. vellicodens armesii), Bowedclaw's shrubrunner (Eua. ve. boweclawii), and ahwa nester (Eua. auanidor ruber). These fauna are not known to live in the Temperate-New-West continent.

    Degradation of DNA has been minimal. Estimates place death at 50 – 60 years before discovery, and an apparent phylogenetic age of 70 – 95 million years from the Euarcharbor or related ancestor. Whether the artifact is the remains of an contemporaneous but undiscovered species, a product of genetic engineering, or a time-traveling species has not been determined.
  3. Physical documents pressed against the artifact will become irreversibly changed. In a span of moments, all writing, print, or engravings in any non-pictographic language will change to form symbols of a previously unknown language read horizontally rather than vertically. Consistent results indicate that #350 is translating to this language, with translation depending on the context or intent of the writer. For example, the sentence "Aya has red feathers and yellow feathers" will consistently convert into the same characters, but the same homophones vary in different contexts.

    It has been found this a phonemic language, but some characters do not have definite correlations to the Iyanna or Srir phonetic characters . By converting dictionaries, a lexicon of over 80,000 words has been observed. A copy of this document has been transformed by #350 and indexed with this document as an extensive example.

Artifact #350 was recovered by the Department of Field Action on Year 4503 Day 243, in a raid on a Raving commune residing in caves of the Olar Hills, north of Halay, Guey. The a'Halay chapter of the Raving, self-identified as "the Old One's Ears" and "Hympsie Speakers", expressed the belief that #350 is the remains of an individual that was a member of a civilization that preexisted the sapient theropods, and that the artifact's properties were a means of posthumous communication. The detained oracle, "Rhythm-of-Dripping-Water", has provided several reverent epithets for the artifact, which he and surviving followers attest had been in the chapter's possession for fifty years.

Dr. Noreano (Year 4503 Day 260) — Genetic testing indicates subject is a descendant of Paupa Reddew, also known as "Drum-of-Wet-Fronds", a Ranter revolutionist that went into hiding in Year 4461. "Rhythm-of-Dripping-Water" is presumably the subject's only name, having hatched to Ranters outside of larger society.

Appended is the transcript of the first interrogation of Rhythm-of-Dripping-Water, who Artifact #350 was seized from (Year 4503 Day 245).

Dr. Noleano Do
State your name for the record.

Noleano
Your cooperation would be appreciated. We may even reconsider your flower privileges, depending on how you do.

Rhythm-of-Dripping-Water
The flowers. My sinuses close up without them!

Noleano
I will give you some if you answer my questions today. Who are you?

Rhythm
I am Rhythm-of-Dripping-Water, Speaker of the Mouth,
Hand to the Elder's Voice.

Noleano
The Elder's Voice. This is the idol of worship to your followers, correct?

Rhythm
To the followers left, you killers.

Noleano
Tell me more about this Elder. What do they do?

Rhythm
What does the Elder do? The Elder inscribes with the tongue of the old ones! A fine, so refined, clawrighting that swirls like water and sharpens like glass.

Noleano
Stop. You said of "old ones". Which pantheon you are talking about?

Rhythm
Who knows? The Elder knows. Their fellows are dead, but their mind stayed to remember them.

Noleano
You mean the skull.

Rhythm
Left it for us. To guide nestlings after they've long gone. Unheard for so long. But my clan writes to the Elder, to the departed with them, and they write us back.

Noleano
How do you read the writing? It is unlike any script my coworkers and I have seen.

Rhythm
Perseverance and patience, thickheaded one. Pay heed and you will bear their message.

Noleano
Have patience for me. What is the Elder's message?

Rhythm
The Elder's kind, their time is gone. Brought to an end when the old sun fell and the rain turned to ash. They made way for us. Now it is ours. Soon our time will be gone. But we must make time for another!

Rhythm
The next of kin will rise from the oceans and find the ground barren and white! We must leave them a spark of life to start anew!

Noleano
Calm down! Calmly explain what you believe will happen.

Rhythm
Do not play with me! You know as well as I that the waters have been rising by the summer! The ice lands cover your ancestor's nesting ground, pachycephalosaur! The small fliers herald the earth and times coming!

Noleano
He's noncompliant. Bring him back to his cell.

Rhythm
It's calamity! Calamity! They grow worse, each one that comes!

Dr. Noreano (Year 4503 Day 245) — The comments from Rhythm-of-Dripping-Water and the other detainees indicate that this sect is mistaken on the effects of oracle roses, as their hallucinations provide visions of future events and not past ones. The recent blizzards and growth of the polar caps are a mild concern, but its a natural glacial period. Even if it was an existential threat, the solution to that problem is not to huff pollen and feed a skull roses and frogs.

Dr. Sleekclaw (Year 4503 Day 258) — Tests prove that no, the members of the Raving cannot read Script #350. The a'Halay belief Dripping-Water can is a product of mass hysteria and his authority as the cult's leader.

Dr. Omma (Year 4504 Day 38) — From extensive review, there seems to be an absence of a dinosaur presence in Script #350. There are no distinct words between sapient and non-sapient dinosaurs, the closest hypernym is for the bipedals as a whole. The translated names for dinosaurs use morphemes visually related to more common ones, likely coming from an ancestral or descendant language, similar to our own practices of taxonomic nomenclature. No common names, as far as my team can tell.

Further, there is a sense of enmity in these words, as literal translations are compounds such as "terrible lizards" and "beast feet". My own race, who pride ourselves on family, has the slanderous name of "egg thief". Considering the phylogenetic evidence, I am willing to agree Artifact #350 came not from an isolated contemporary of ours, but a successor. In what regard, I cannot say. I have informed the Temporal Department on Lingusitics' theory.

All personnel of Clearance 5/9931 report to the office of [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/o5-command-dossier|O5-10]]] directly. Pertinent knowledge of SCP-9931 will be issued to operatives of [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/task-forces#phi-2|Mobile Task Force Phi-2 "Clever Girls"]]] below Clearance 4/9931 at the discretion of appropriate superiors. As of 20 September 2045, three (3) embedded field agents are assigned to the search and retrieval of any further SCP-9931 objects at the following Locations of Interest: #401829, #401830, #45068. SCP-9931-1, -2, and -3 are contained in Medium Security Archeological Storage at [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/welcome-to-wonderful-site-65|CASKSK-Site-65]]]. Accompanying documentation is to refer to these items collectively as Anomalous Object #1829. SCP-9931-4a though -4o are in a medium security storage locker at [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/aiad-homescreen|USCASC-Site-15]]]. Duplicated files are stored on Server 181519520201 for review and deciphering by artificial intelligence constructs Bouchard.aic, Champollion.aic, and Dr. Benson Roth, D.C.Sc (all Clearance 5/9931). ------ **DESCRIPTION:** SCP-9931 is a series of pre-Anthropocene technofossils excavated from siltstone strata in the Scollard Formation at Alberta, Canada. Location of discovery extended a depth of 72.19 to 73.18 meters below surface, just under the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary. SCP-9931 violates the law of superposition. Reliable radiometric dating methods on SCP-9931 and layers of strata adjacent to discovery place both at an age of 66.46 million years BP;[[footnote]] Both towards the tail end of the Late Cretaceous period (100.48–66.46 MYA). These dates correspond to the Campanian age (83.55–72.12 MYA), the penultimate division of the period, preceding the Maastrichtian (72.12–66.46 MYA), which ended with the [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/a-fancy-dinosaur|Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event]]]. [[/footnote]] Despite this, the layers of strata are in order with the rest of the excavation site, showing no signs of a hole being excavated and filled back in. [[tabview]] [[tab V — SCP-9931-1 through -4]] [[div style="background: rgb(238, 242, 241); padding: 10px;"]] ++++ V-Appendix 9931.Inv.13 **__SCP-9931-1__** SCP-9931-1 is a cylindrical concrete container, with rough exterior dimensions of 99.28 × //d// 64.26 cm and interior of 79.31 × //d// 46.19 cm. Concrete had cracked and through this exposure iron rebar had corroded almost entirely, but SCP-9931-1 retained general structure. Exterior surface indicates SCP-9931-1 was not cast in the ground. Lid was pinned with rebar and sealed with concrete. Interior was divided into three sections by grates composed of a bronze alloy, since corroded into copper and tin minerals.[[footnote]] Primarily bornite, malachite, and cassiterite. [[/footnote]] Despite the resulting loss of material strength and damage sustained to the upper grate, both were found intact. [[size 75%]](See __Dossier: SCP-9931-1__ for detail.)[[/size]] All other SCP-9931 objects were recovered inside. **__SCP-9931-2__** SCP-9931-2 is the fragmentary remains of what was once a presumably functional electronic device affixed to the interior face of the lid of SCP-9931-1 when it was sealed. Item had fallen to the floor of the first chamber and was neutralized, but it is indeterminable if this occurred before discovery or during transport. Metal components had degraded into bornite and similar decomposite ores an unknown magnitude of time before discovery. Stable carbon isotopes, silicates, and some polymer components have not degraded, notably among them a hermetically sealed vial found to contain [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-8373|permineralized neural tissue]]], interfaced with the remains of a microelectrode array. It is believed that SCP-9931-2's intended purpose was to extend the longevity of SCP-9931, shielding the items from interferences with local reality and/or retroactive causality. [[size 75%]](See __Dossier: SCP-9931-2__ for detail.)[[/size]] **__SCP-9931-3__** SCP-9931-3 is a box comprised of carbon and metallic ore, approximately 37.52 × 20.04 × 16.67 cm, found in good condition. The metal base was constructed from bronze alloy, also corroded. Carbon fibers lining the exterior and interior of SCP-9931-3 have largely preserved its structural integrity, unlike SCP-9931-2. Pitting found on the width of the container and lid indicate SCP-9931-3 locked or latched closed mechanically, but the exposed mechanisms have deteriorated completely. Contents of SCP-9931-3 were found partially embedded in a plastiglomerate compiled at the basin of the container. This plastiglomerate is believed to have been a polyurethane-based foam meant to insulate or cushion SCP-9931-4. [[size 75%]](See __Dossier: SCP-9931-3__ for detail.)[[/size]] **__SCP-9931-4__** SCP-9931-4 is the collection of fifteen (15) digital storage devices found contained within SCP-9931-3. All instances are the same design of nanoshuttle memory device,[[footnote]] A highly compact, nonvolatile storage device utilizing molecular machines. Binary data is stored by shuttling molecules or ions between two states along another molecule it is either mechanically interlocked around (a "molecular shuttle") or inside of (a "nanoparticle shuttle"). Depending on composition and conditions, a nanoshuttle memory device can last up to tens of millions of years without corruption of the stored data. [[size 65%]]Further reading: __Begtrup, G. E.; Gannett, W.; Yuzvinsky, T. D.; Crespi, V. H.; et al. (13 May 2009). "[[[https://web.archive.org/web/20120119124854/http://www.physics.berkeley.edu/research/zettl/pdf/363.NanoLet.9-Begtrup.pdf|Nanoscale Reversible Mass Transport for Archival Memory]]]". //Nano Letters//. 9 (5): 1835–1838.__[[/size]][[/footnote]] operating off of iron nanoparticles inside of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNT). Each SCP-9931-4 is comparable in complexity and design to civilian nanotech advancements of the late 2020s, and has a storage capacity of 187.5 terabytes. [[size 75%]](See __Portal:SCP-9931-4__ for full archive.)[[/size]] Character encoding is represented by variable-length 3-bit or 5-bit code units, as opposed to 4-bit multiples. Decoding of contents has supplied audio and visual media, including a character set of 78,320 characters, comprising eleven (11) different writing scripts (not including an ideographic text markup), corresponding to eleven or potentially more (11+) languages. As of 20 September 2045, these languages have not been fully deciphered, but from structure and associated recordings of phonetics, their scripts are logographic and either syllabic, semi-syllabic, or alphasyllabic; and are read top-down progressing right. Typography is comprised primarily from linear strokes, arced strokes, and simple diacritics, with little use of loops or counters. Photos indicate these characters originated as a form of inscription using [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-1472|teeth and claws]]]. Due to their use in the computer language, the numerals, text markup, and order in the character set is the most that has been discerned. Most context derived from SCP-9931-4 has been through photo, video, and mathematical equations. [[size 75%]](See __Linguistic Analysis: Cretaceous Language Family (GoI-9931)__ for detail.)[[/size]] Contents of SCP-9931-4 indicate that SCP-9931 originated from an advanced society of Late Cretaceous dinosaurs, comparable in technology to humanity, and was utilized by a research organization of unknown directive or operation. For purposes of clarity, this society has been provided the tentative name of the "Anomalous Campanian Culture Group" (ACCG; Group of Interest #9931), and this organization the "ACCG Organization" (Group of Interest #9931-A). [[size 75%]](See __Group of Interest Dossier: GoI-9931__ and subfolders for detail.)[[/size]] The majority of files on SCP-9931-4 consist of visual and auditory documentation from the ACCG Organization, but cultural media presumed to originate from a larger cosm of the culture group are also included in substantial amount. Photography and videography depicts at least six species of civilized dinosaurs, prominent pictured among the ACCG Organization is a species of pachysaurid undiscovered to civilian paleontology and has yet to be found in the stratigraphic record.[[footnote]] //Pachycephalosaurus ectostratus// ([[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/two-time|Moira & Smith]]], 2031), designated Species of Interest #317. Type specimen is designated [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-317|SCP-317-1]]] ##grey|(neutralized)##. [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] [[size 75%]](See __Portal:SCP-9931-4__ for full archive of summaries and front-facing documents.)[[/size]] [[/div]] [[/tab]] [[/tabview]] ------ **HISTORY:** SCP-9931 was discovered 21 June 2045 by coal miners at the Rumsey Quarry, located southeast of the Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park in Alberta, Canada (since designated Location of Interest #45068). Embedded webcrawlers were flagged to correspondence between paleological associates and Korite & Westmoreland International detailing SCP-9931-1. Mobile Task Forces Phi-2 "Clever Girls" and Sigma-66 "Steel Veil" were dispatched to secure SCP-9931, amnesticize civilians, and expunge correspondences. SCP-9931-1 was designated SCP-9931 on 22 June. Efforts to open SCP-9931-1 was authorized the same day, leading to the discovery and catalogue of the contents with their current designations. Safe containment, Dark disruption, and Notice risk classification were assigned by O5-10, overseer of SCP-9931 activities. The Reverse Engineering and Application Division, Department of Informational Technologies (READ, DIT) was assigned with designing a device to interface with SCP-9931-4. The first functional device was brought online on 5 August to attempt interface with SCP-9931-4a. When the non-standard format of SCP-9931-4 was confirmed, the Artificial Intelligence Applications Division (AIAD, DIT) assigned Bouchard.aic under supervision of Dr. Benson Roth, D.C.Sc, both trained in deciphering esoteric coding languages. On 13 August, a newly brought online artificial intelligence construct, Champollion.aic, was given inaugural assignment in translating the character languages. This process is ongoing. As of 20 September 2045, an estimated 96.26% of SCP-9931-4 contents have been parsed and archived in Foundation standards. "We need a number that keeps counting even when the universe won't."

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9933 must continuously broadcast a signal to the SCiP-net relay every second. Under the 2010 Austria Accords, this time signal is also relayed in real-time to all signatory Groups of Interest. As signal loss could be misinterpreted as a temporal destabilization event, the signal must reside on triple-redundant systems.

The central anomaly must be contained within its dedicated measurement apparatus at all times, supported by multiple independent backup power sources. The apparatus must maintain a stable connection to SCiP-net, even during transportation and field deployment.

As the sole authoritative reference for Foundation Standard Time, SCP-9933 is to be protected at all costs. Since concealing a device required to continuously transmit a signal is impossible, security teams must possess sufficient firepower to repel counterattacks1. During deployment, it must be escorted by a sufficient number of Mobile Task Force units to counter all known Groups of Interest operating within the surrounding area2.

Due to the inclusion of DELTA as a standard tool in field kits, Procedure 9933-ICARUS is to be conducted on a monthly schedule to replenish available units.

One-year visualization of SCP-9933's morphic state isolated within the temporal field.

Description: SCP-9933 is an extradimensional spatial anomaly that morphs its physical geometry3 at a perfectly constant rate. Due to its design, it is immune to all known forms of time manipulation, including timeline resets or reality bending.

The anomaly is deterministic and follows an infinite series of unique4 shapes. Every second, the monitoring array measures the anomaly's current shape and cross-references with where it appears on the pre-calculated sequence5. Using this and the constant rate of change, the computer can determine exactly how much time has elapsed.

Since this count cannot be altered by any reality benders, Foundation Standard Time (FST) is used by the anomalous community as the only objective method to measure time.

Human time is a headache. Between time zones, leap years, and daylight savings, it’s all circumstantial. Programmers fixed this with UNIX time: a single, growing number that counts seconds from a fixed point in 1970.

The anomalous world is worse. To a reality bender, 'Tuesday' is just an opinion. We need a clock that doesn't rely on regular physics. We need a number that keeps counting even when the universe won't.

- Excerpt from the Project EPOCH proposal

Project EPOCH

SCP-9933 was initially proposed by Director Maria Jones as a definitive record-keeping instrument for RAISA. After the O5 Council recognized its potential for tracking temporal anomalies, the project was approved.

Initial development with the Department of Esoteric Physics attempted to recreate the atomic clock, but with temporal shielding. However, despite theoretically shielding the atom from temporal anomalies, researchers could not establish a method for tracking elapsed time and therefore could not prove its success.

Without proof of progress and with increasing costs, Project EPOCH was under threat of cancellation.

Transcript from the Foundation Research Conference

Dr. Adrian Parker

Parker: Director Jones?

Jones: Yes?

Parker: Dr. Adrian Parker. I was interested in your Epoch project, but I think you need to pivot.

Jones: Excuse me?

Parker: Your clock relies on a repeating cycle. No matter how fast or slow, the atom always returned to the same states, so there was no way to tell how much time had passed between measurements. So, a magician can speed up time between measurements, but as long as it ends up in the same place again, you can't see anything different.

Jones: Yes, the project stalled due to that issue.

Parker: Then you shouldn't use something that repeats. You need a deterministic mathematical anomaly that will never form any repeating pattern. That way, even if the magician speeds up time, it can never return to where it should be.

*Director Jones ponders for a second.*

Jones: What's your name again?

2D mathematical representation of the sequence. Note how no path is ever repeated.

Dr. Adrian Parker joined the team and led the pivot toward the artificial creation of a mathematically irrational anomaly. Early stabilization attempts revealed issues arising from the anomaly’s higher-order dimensional structure, producing discontinuities when projected into three-dimensional space. These errors compounded over time, threatening long-term determinism.

Dr. Parker conducted an extended review of Foundation archives, surveying several thousand records related to dimensional projection anomalies. He subsequently conducted further research on SCP-045, examining its stability as a lower-dimensional projection of a higher-dimensional structure. From this, he derived a projection framework that eliminated cumulative error in SCP-9933’s morphic encoding.

Adoption of this framework proved instrumental, and Project EPOCH was completed in 2009. Subsequent analysis confirmed the sequence to be deterministic, allowing its forward progression to be reverse-engineered and pre-calculated. Backtracking the sequence, however, remained infeasible.

Maria Jones
MJ

SCP-9933 has passed all testing, and Project EPOCH has successfully concluded. The Foundation Timestamp has been formally defined and activated. As the sequence is infinite, RAISA has arbitrarily set it to the number of seconds since the beginning of 2010.

What began as an internal recordkeeping initiative has become something far larger. I do believe this will be a pivotal moment for many of you.

I am currently coordinating with Overwatch Command regarding external presentation of this achievement to the anomalous community. With this in mind, I am requesting the team’s recommendation for who should present and publish this breakthrough. However, I suspect I already know the answer.

Adrian Parker
AP

I’ve been informed of the team’s decision.

I don’t know how to adequately thank you for the confidence you’ve placed in me. This project represents a defining breakthrough in my career, and being trusted to represent it makes every hour spent on EPOCH feel justified.

Thank you for choosing me.

Overwatch Command
O5

Your proposal for Dr. Adrian Parker to be the presenter is denied.

The Department of External Affairs has decided that you will present in his place.

Maria Jones
MJ

To be clear, my role in Project EPOCH was simply administrative. I am not a scientist, and the technical substance of EPOCH is more appropriately represented by my team.

The Project EPOCH staff expressed strong support for Dr. Parker, and he has already accepted the role.

Overwatch Command
O5

Dr. Parker lacks the diplomatic clearance required for this level of classified engagement. Individuals will be present whom he is not authorized to encounter or even made aware of.

The Austria Accords constitute a major multilateral diplomatic event. As a director, your established reputation carries institutional authority. The presenter is expected to represent the weight of the Foundation as a whole.

This decision is non-negotiable.

2010 Austria Accords in ██████ Building, Austria.

The 2010 Austria Accords were attended by the Global Occult Coalition and most members of the Council of 108, who all agreed on the established Foundation Standard Time. Additional Groups of Interest later adopted Foundation Standard Time independently, including many hostile ones. However, SCP-9933 itself remained exclusively under Foundation control.

Excerpt from the 2010 Austria Accords Proceedings

GOC: This is absurd. A standard cannot exist if it is wholly controlled by a single organization.

Foundation: Foundation Standard Time is being shared in real time. You are receiving the signal without restriction.

GOC: Then let me be precise. We are all relying on a single centralized dependency. If it fails, the entire world goes dark.

Foundation: Rest assured, SCP-9933 is maintained on triple-redundant systems, with continuous monitoring and-

GOC: That is not what I meant, and you know it. If the Foundation is unwilling, then we will pursue our own implementation. You previously indicated that your lead researcher intended to publish his work.

*Audible whispering among Foundation delegation*

Foundation: The Foundation will not be publishing any papers relating to the creation of SCP-9933.

GOC: What?

Maria Jones: What? Dr. Parker never agreed to-

Foundation: Dr. Parker- the Foundation retains discretion over what is disclosed and when. I am aware the Coalition has many secrets of its own.

GOC: You are looking down on us. We can recreate it with or without the research.

A petition by both Dr. Parker and the GOC to the Foundation Ethics Committee received no response. Dr. Parker then submitted additional requests to continue SCP-9933-related research and publish works unrelated to its creation. However, Director Jones had already formally concluded the project, citing completion of all objectives. Dr. Parker was privately commended for his contributions and reassigned to unrelated projects.

During a system blackout in 2012, the timestamp suddenly jumped forward ██ years. While initially attributed to technical issues6, a thorough internal audit of the deepwell revealed [REDACTED] caused by a failure of [REDACTED], leading to initialization of Protocol 2000-Ganymede. All details of the timeline reset were then wiped by the order of O5-█. Upon this revelation, the O5 Council has decided to omit the first few digits from the publicly available timestamp.

Coalition Memorandum to the Foundation

The Coalition formally objects to the removal of digits from Foundation Standard Time. The Austria Accords contain no provision permitting the redaction of temporal data of this significance.

We further note that omission of the number of elapsed years does not conceal the existence of a temporal discontinuity. Such a discontinuity admits only a narrow range of plausible explanations. The Coalition requests clarification on whether this measure reflects an unresolved systemic failure or acknowledgment of an uncontained temporal event.

Foundation Response to the Memorandum

The Foundation acknowledges the Coalition’s position and appreciates its continued attention to chronological integrity.

The Foundation further notes that during prototype testing in 2009, a similar displacement was recorded. This was initially attributed to prototype instability and caused confusion with our development team. With the recent context, the Foundation has looked into your previous records. Your declassified reports from the same period document experimentation involving temporal eigenweapons, which you later stated were never deployed and were safely decommissioned.

Protests from the GOC subsequently ceased. While other parties voiced objections, no organization was able to propose a verifiable alternative.

Project ICARUS

A section of the containment unit of SCP-9933 being transported for ICARUS experimentation.

After the 2012 incident, the O5 Council declared a new goal of backtracking the sequence to get a more accurate analysis of previous time jumps. Dr. Parker was recruited back into a newly formed 9933 team and assigned to Project ICARUS to analyze SCP-9933 to find further uses and back-track the sequence.

In Experiment ICARUS-1508, the 9933 team successfully entangled the state of SCP-9933 into a sealed containment unit. Upon opening it and measuring, the state collapses to match "SCP-9933 Prime" at the moment of observation. By using the "collapsed" state, a computer can accurately determine exactly how much time has passed relative to the Foundation's baseline without requiring the original SCP-9933 instance. This was then compressed into a portable device called "Deviation from Epoch, Local Time Analyzer" (DELTA).

While DELTAs are pivotal for field agents to determine if they are subjected to localized temporal dilation, it has limitations. DELTAs are non-recoverable once activated and cannot be recalibrated or reused. Therefore, it can provide a one-time "check-in" but cannot continuously measure the fluctuations in reality. SCP-9933 itself is still transported to various anomalies to accurately analyze the temporal geometry.

Transcript from the ICARUS-1508 post-meeting

Jones: The experiment worked, but it was risky. You came close to destabilizing SCP-9933. I need to be clear: its value is that it’s a stable clock.

Parker: It’s not just a clock. It’s a true constant, more constant than the speed of light. I’m not pushing it for nothing. This is the first thing I’ve worked on that actually matters.

Jones: Adrian, you have contributed to a groundbreaking project, much younger than most.

Parker: But a much bigger name is attached to the project, director. Barely anyone’s even heard of me, and if they have, they just think I made a clock.

Jones: That’s not how the Foundation sees it.

Parker: Maybe. But history won’t. This is a bigger discovery than e, pi, or any other irrational number. Yet I’ll still end up buried in some secret file cabinet. Now I’m close to an even bigger thing. Closer than I’ll ever be to something like this again.

Jones: Using the anomaly like this isn’t relevant to recordkeeping.

Parker: It never was for me.

Jones: That’s not what you said when you approached me about EPOCH.

Parker: I know. I lied. I needed an opening, and feigning interest was harmless enough to get me in.

Jones: I appreciate the honesty, but RAISA is vital.

Parker: Not to me. I don't care about filing. I cared about being attached to something that couldn’t be ignored. Something permanent. I was ready too, but those bureaucrats blocked it. Now I’m standing in front of time itself. I’m not letting it go again.

After many disagreements, a procedure for the creation of DELTA was approved by RAISA to be within acceptable safe limits. Procedure 9933-ICARUS has been added to the special containment procedures.

Transcript from the Project ICARUS Status Review

O5-7: Congratulations on Project ICARUS. It is a rare privilege to design a Foundation-made SCP that functions as intended without inadvertently destroying the world.

Jones: Thank you. As for the secondary objective-

O5-7: No. ICARUS was successful. The project is being closed.

Jones: What? Dr. Parker is still working on-

O5-7: The project was a charade. We needed the team to give us leverage against the Coalition. Whether that leverage manifested as a usable tool or information about their cover-ups was irrelevant.

Jones: Why?

O5-7: Our intelligence indicates the GOC is approaching an independent implementation. I remember the degree of control orbital eigenweapons once afforded us. Now we possess control over the definition of time itself, and we cannot allow the Coalition to approach parity. With DELTA, we can convince the Coalition to drop its development in exchange for giving them access to the tools.

Jones: You’re reducing DELTA to a pawn. It has fundamentally altered field operations. The idea that any operative can see their time dilation is revolutionary.

O5-7: His work was always intended to be a pawn. We simply did not anticipate it being this effective. This Dr. Parker is intelligent, isn't he?

Jones: Yes, I believe all he wants is recognition. Your actions in 2010-

O5-7: How is progress on the other objective?

Jones: Well, limited. Even though I provided RAISA supercomputers, we are basically brute-forcing guesses of temporal jumps with low confidence. We need more data on previous states.

O5-7: Is that an issue of his capability, or of available technology?

Jones: Technology.

*O5-7 pauses*

O5-7: That is fixable. Finding the GOC cover-ups could be vital for future bargaining. Perhaps he can be made aware of our more classified technology.

Internal Memorandum

We would like to acknowledge the success Dr. Parker has achieved with SCP-9933.

However, his OMPHALOS proposal is incredibly unethical. We are talking about a large sacrifice just to check our math. While our brute forcing attempts have been so far unsuccessful, that is simply the nature of brute forcing. It can be any day now that we will suddenly crack the code.

This has gone far from the goal of SCP-9933. If we are continuing with this, I will openly resign from the team.

Sincerely,

RAISA Director Maria Jones

BY ORDER OF OVERWATCH COMMAND

Project OMPHALOS has been accepted.

Dr. Parker's research has concluded the infeasibility of brute forcing. We understand the controversy, but it is nonetheless your team's failure in brute-forcing that led to this as the only outcome.

.

.

Project OMPHALOS

Due to early research into Project ████████, technology that can ██████████████████████ was made available to the 9933 team. Project OMPHALOS was initiated to use this technology to create 9933-Ω in which previous states of the SCP-9933 sequence could be directly observed. Dr. Parker claims that access to this historical data would enable the identification of temporal discrepancies resulting from anomalous activity or Groups of Interests.

The remaining team was relocated to Site-███ to use their technology to create 9933-Ω.

Phase I

Phase I used ████████ and a temporal acceleration field derived from SCP-155, adapted by Dr. Parker to artificially advance the creation. Its history was initialized to begin exactly one year prior to our Foundation’s creation of SCP-9933. Through controlled intervention, they were guided to independently develop their own instance of SCP-9933.

Measurement of the simulated SCP-9933 concluded two things:

1. While the temporal field accelerated their entire reality by 400%, their SCP-9933's morphic rate remained the same as ours. The inhabitants perceived the morphic rate as normal, unknowingly defining their 'second' to match the accelerated timeframe. This confirms the rate as constant across all realities.

2. Due to more data and the relatively short sequence length, backtracking their sequence was trivial. This prompted the discovery that the sequence was not infinite but instead terminates at an "origin state", a zero point of the sequence. The total elapsed time since the origin state perfectly matched the total elapsed time of the simulated sub-reality.

With a new understanding of the start of the sequence, backtracking the sequence became feasible using Foundation Supercomputers.

Despite observing the psychological outcome of his simulated counterpart, Dr. Adrian Parker formally requested continuation into Phase II. He stated that every version of himself would understand his reasons and that he was willing, along with all others, to sacrifice himself for another version of himself.

However, the simulation's "Phase II Incident" prompted significant hesitation among our own 9933 team over measuring our reality's lifespan. The O5 Council is currently in deliberation.

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9935 is contained at its time and place of origin, at the site of Bruce Park in Indianapolis, Indiana, USA circa 1889 - near the corner of East 22nd St. and North College Avenue in the modern day. A perimeter has been established around the field and no civilians are to be permitted beyond the perimeter. Any persons who attempt to access the East 22nd St. site are to be given a Class-C amnestic and remanded to local police. Ongoing containment of this perimeter is under the purview of MTF Delta-23 "Batboys".

Due to the ongoing temporal anomaly present at the site, no additional obfuscation assets are necessary - it is impossible to see the site of SCP-9935 until one crosses the boundary of the temporal anomaly.

Hoosiers second baseman Charley Bassett being tagged out at home by Nationals catcher Tom Daly. Image taken during the bottom of the 21,015th inning.

Description: SCP-9935 is a baseball game between the Indianapolis Hoosiers and Washington Nationals that has been played continuously since it originally began on the 5th of October, 1889. As no rule exists that declares a baseball game concluded after a set period of time if the score is tied, and as neither team has broken the tie since the game began, it has run uninterrupted for over 135 years.

The unusual nature of the game in question has resulted in a region of altered temporal state surrounding the ball field that affects both the persons who inhabit the region, and persons from outside the region who cross into it. Crossing over the anomaly's threshold during the course of the game will find the affected persons shifted temporally to the 5th of October, 1889 - as determined by the positions of stellar objects within the region and without. Persons looking at the altered region from the outside will see a flat patch of dirt in a vacant lot on East 22nd Street, while persons within the altered region will see the city of Indianapolis as it existed in 1889 when looking out from within it.

The altered region is only accessible during the hours in which the game is being played - starting roughly two hours before 14:00 EST and lasting between 4-5 hours in duration. Shortly after the conclusion of the period of play, the altered region will demanifest until the start of the next period. The game is played every day except Sunday and any of the eleven major American federal holidays.

Map of the city of Indianapolis circa 1889 and 2025. Relative location of Bruce Park added - relative location of anomaly threshold demarcated in red.

The area within the boundary is roughly 19,000m2, and begins roughly six meters from the back fence of the Bruce Park field, extending down both sidelines towards the grandstand, from which it extends out ten meters past the grandstand behind home plate. This threshold is not static, and has been known to shift back and forth up to 1.2m. The day-night cycle within roughly matches the same cycle outside of it, though the interior cycle does not experience seasonal shift, as every day within the boundary is the 5th of October, 1889.

SCP-9935 is inhabited primarily by players and spectators who were present at the start of the game in 1889. These persons do not grow old, nor do they seem to be otherwise adversely affected by the altered temporal topography of SCP-9935. They are capable of passing the threshold of SCP-9935, but only on the 1889 side - the same (but in reverse) as individuals who enter SCP-9935 from the modern day. Persons within SCP-9935 are aware of the anomalous nature of the game, and have commented on it when questioned by Foundation personnel (see Addendum 9935.6 for more details).

It is currently uncertain whether SCP-9935 exists as a temporal loop perpetuated by the innately arcane nature of the game of baseball (in which the persons within SCP-9935 are those who were there the day of the game), or a parallel timeline extracted from consensus reality in which the game never ended (in which the persons within SCP-9935 are not from the "consensus" timeline, but instead originated because of the unusual nature of the game). This question arises from a potential misinformation campaign that would have arisen shortly after the original published end of the game; one of the organizations that acted as a precursor to the modern Foundation, the Wabash Theological Seminary, was aware of the anomalous nature of SCP-9935 and worked to supress knowledge of it at the time, but their work did not begin until several months after the supposed end of the game.

Whether the original game ended as published (a 15-6 win for Indianapolis) and the persons involved lived out the rest of their lives naturally (and therefore SCP-9935 is a branch timeline) or whether the published end result was misinformation on the part of the Wabash Theological Seminary (and the inhabitants of SCP-9935 are the original players stuck in a temporal loop) is unknown, as no records have been recovered from the Seminary's archives that indicate either as truth.

Addendum 9935.1: History

SCP-9935 began on the 5th of October 1889 at roughly 14:00 Eastern Standard Time. The game was played at Bruce Park in Indianapolis, Indiana, United States, and was the third game in a three-game series between the host Indianapolis Hoosiers and the visiting Washington Nationals1. Both teams were at the end of losing seasons - Indianapolis would finish the season with a record of 59-75, while Washington would finish with a record of 41-83. They would finish 7th and 8th in the National League, respectively, and both teams would fold before the start of the next season2.

According to gamekeeper Martin Van Dijk, the game sat at 15-6 going into the 7th inning, at which point Washington scored five runs on Indianapolis pitcher Amos Rusie off strong hitting by batters Tom Daly, Arthur Irwin, and Billy Hoy. The Hoosiers were held scoreless in the 7th and both teams were unable to score in the 8th, leading to a 15-11 9th inning start. Nationals second baseman Sam Wise then proceeded to get on base, steal second, and was promptly batted in by Arthur Irwin who, along with his brother John Irwin, scored on a Walt Wilmot double to bring the game within a run, 15-14. Tom Daly later hit a single that scored Ed Beecher from second, tying the game at 15. The Hoosiers were held scoreless at the bottom of the 9th, leading to the first extra innings period.

The unusual properties of SCP-9935 became apparent quickly, as neither team managed to score a run for the next twelve innings. Indianapolis shortstop and player manager, Jack Glasscock, described the revelation as such:

Jack "Pebbly Jack" Glasscock, player manager for the 1889 Indianapolis Hoosiers.

"It must’ve been somewhere ‘round the twentieth inning when we first began to realize how queer the whole affair had grown. By then we were plumb wore out, the sun had long since gone down, and the lamps out in the field were no help at all, faint little glimmers that scarcely lit the grass. We’d been told a storm was bound to roll in that evening, yet it never did, and still we played on. Felt like hours piled atop hours, each of us praying one side or the other might finish it off so we could all go home, but neither club could manage the winning stroke."

"Me and John3 went out to speak with Bill4 about stoppin’ things, for we were all bone-tired, but he just shook his head and said the game had to be played out, no matter the hour. It was, I reckon, the top of the thirty-fifth when the next run came across. We sat in the dugout before takin’ our turn at bat, and I told Jerry5 it was no shame if he wanted to lay down his arms and call it a night. But Jerry snapped right back at me: “Jack, I ain’t goin’ into the record books as the fellow who stood idle while his nine lost the longest game ever played.” Sure enough, he steps up and drops a little bounder past second, then Emmett sends him along with a fly out to right, and the lad comes home on a passed ball. All square again."

"At length we struck a bargain with Bill to call a halt after the forty-first, so’s everyone could steal away for some rest. I swear I never slept so sound in all my life. Come the next morning, we tramped back to the park, and someone remarked how the weather was the selfsame as the day before - mighty strange, we all thought, seeing as how we’d braced for rain the previous night. The crowd was back too, same faces and same hollers, eager to see how the thing might end. That’s when it struck me how peculiar it all was. Near everything stood just as it had the day before - the sky, the people, even the sun breaking through the fog at dawn. The only thing different was the number painted up on the scoreboard."

-Jack Glasscock

After the second day of play with no score increase, a pre-game meeting was called between managers Jack Glasscock and John Morrill, and umpires Bill Krieger, Tad Renshaw, and Buck Halstead. In Morrill's account of that meeting:

John "Honest John" Morrill, manager for the 1889 Washington Nationals.

"You’d reckon I’d have put it clear out of mind by now, but truth be told it feels as though it might’ve been yesterday. At the outset, we all figured this contest was either a sorry exhibition of baseball, or else the greatest match ever, which just so happened to be played betwixt two of the sorriest clubs ever to set foot upon a diamond. Whichever way it turned, we knew it would be remembered. Old Bill Krieger asked us plain what our course should be if the affair spilled into a third day. Seems comical now, but in that moment all we thought on was getting home and finding work, for the club was about to fold."

"I went into that parley certain he meant to tell us there existed some forgotten rule or obscure by-law that would let us call the game as it stood. We were already in the forty-sixth inning, no nearer to a decision than the day prior. But he said no such statute was writ, the game must be seen to its close. Still, he wished to strike an agreement should we march into day three. “Nine innings a day only,” says he, “with fresh pitchers each morn. We’ll play every day save the Sabbath, so the Lord’s rest be not disturbed, and we keep at it until the matter is settled or heaven itself descends to call time.” We’d already spoken as a team, and the lads were set to see it through. Those with wives had ‘em brought ‘round, for all knew this would be the last match we’d play, and there was one of those new Bell switchboards down at the station if a fellow had to ring his folks."

"We all supposed the end must come within a day or so. Funniest thing, I recollect Ed6 remarkin’ on the weather, saying how fair it had been these past few days. “Just the same fine day as it was yesterday,” he says, plain as you please."

-John Morrill
